howItWorks.title: How it works
items: Time zone conversion uses the browser's IANA time zone database (Intl API) directly. No offsets are hard-coded, so DST start and end dates stay correct every year.
Timestamp units are inferred from the digit count: up to 11 digits = seconds, 12–14 = milliseconds, 15–17 = microseconds, 18–19 = nanoseconds.

A time skipped when DST starts (e.g. New York 2026-03-08 02:30) is pushed one hour later; a time repeated when DST ends (e.g. New York 2026-11-01 01:30) uses the first occurrence. A warning is shown in both cases.
'+1 day' follows the calendar, so on a DST change day it can be 23 or 25 real hours. Use the 'hours' unit for exactly 24 hours.
Adding 1 month to January 31 gives the last day of February (29 in leap years, 28 otherwise).

whatIs.title: What is the Time Converter?
whatIs.description: Convert between Unix timestamps and dates, and see one moment in several countries at once. Search zones by city name (Seoul, New York, London, Sydney) or IANA name (Asia/Tokyo); daylight saving time is applied automatically from the browser's time zone data. Copy ISO 8601, RFC 2822 or SQL formats, add or subtract time, and get the difference and business days between two times on one screen.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Paste a timestamp or date into the top box. The format and unit (seconds, ms, µs, ns) are detected automatically, even inside a log line.
Dates without a time zone are read in the base time zone. Change it by searching a city, country or IANA name.
Copy Unix seconds/ms, ISO 8601, RFC 2822 or SQL from 'Developer formats'.
Add cities under 'In other time zones' to see the same moment's local time, offset, DST status and day change.
Use 'Add or subtract time' and 'Between two times' for N days later, N business days later, or the gap between two times. 'Copy link' shares the current view.

tips.title: Tips
items: New York is 14 hours behind Korea, 13 hours during DST (March 8 – November 1, 2026).
JavaScript Date.now() is milliseconds (13 digits), most server/DB Unix time is seconds (10 digits), Go/Rust UnixNano is nanoseconds (19 digits).
Store ISO 8601 with an offset (e.g. 2026-10-01T12:00:00+09:00) or UTC in APIs and databases to avoid DST confusion.
For exactly 24 hours later, add 24 hours rather than 1 day — they differ on DST change days.
To schedule across countries, use the World Clock meeting planner to find overlapping work hours.

items.q: What's the time difference between Korea and the US?
items.a: New York is 14 hours behind Korea and Los Angeles 17 hours. During DST (March 8 – November 1 in 2026) it's 13 and 16 hours.

items.q: What is a Unix timestamp?
items.a: The number of seconds since January 1, 1970 00:00:00 UTC. It's a single zone-independent number, widely used in servers and databases. Some systems use milliseconds (13 digits) or nanoseconds (19 digits), so this tool infers the unit from the digit count.

items.q: What is DST?
items.a: Daylight saving time moves clocks forward one hour in summer. The US and Canada observe it from the second Sunday of March to the first Sunday of November, Europe from the last Sunday of March to the last Sunday of October, and southeastern Australia from the first Sunday of October to the first Sunday of April. Korea, Japan and China don't use it.

items.q: What happens with a time that doesn't exist, like 2026-03-08 02:30 in New York?
items.a: When DST starts, clocks jump from 02:00 to 03:00, so that time never happens. The tool moves it one hour later (03:30) and shows a warning. A time that occurs twice when DST ends uses the first occurrence.

items.q: How are business days counted?
items.a: Weekends and Korean public holidays (including substitute holidays and election days) are excluded, counting from the day after the start through the end date. Lunar holidays are covered for 2024–2030; temporary holidays only once designated by the government.

whatIs.title: What is the Salary Take-Home Calculator?
whatIs.description: The Salary Take-Home Calculator shows you exactly how much you'll actually receive each month after deducting the four major insurances (National Pension, Health Insurance, Employment Insurance, Long-term Care Insurance), income tax, and local income tax from your gross annual salary. It's especially useful for job seekers, professionals negotiating a job offer, or anyone comparing compensation levels. The calculator uses the latest 2025 rates for accurate results.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Enter your gross annual salary (total yearly pay before deductions).
2. Enter the number of dependents (including yourself) and the number of children under 20.
3. If you receive non-taxable allowances (meal allowance, car maintenance, etc.), enter the monthly amount.
4. Click Calculate to see your monthly take-home pay with a full breakdown of each deduction.

tips.title: Tips
items: Meal allowance (up to ₩200,000/month) and car maintenance allowance (up to ₩200,000/month) are non-taxable — be sure to enter these if they apply. They can increase your take-home pay by tens of thousands of won.
When negotiating a salary, compare take-home amounts rather than gross figures to get a true picture of your compensation.
Income tax deductions vary by number of dependents, so recalculate whenever your family situation changes.

items.q: What rates does the calculator use?
items.a: It applies the 2026 rates: National Pension 4.75% (9.5% total after the 2025 pension reform, monthly income cap ₩6.59M), Health Insurance 3.595% (7.19% total), Long-term Care Insurance 13.14% of health insurance premium, and Employment Insurance 0.9%.

items.q: What are common non-taxable allowances?
items.a: The most common non-taxable items are the meal allowance (up to ₩200,000/month), self-driving subsidy (up to ₩200,000/month), and childbirth/childcare allowance (up to ₩200,000/month).

items.q: Why might the result differ from my actual paycheck?
items.a: Each company handles fringe benefits and additional deductions differently, which can cause minor discrepancies. For the exact figure, refer to your pay stub.

loan.description: See your monthly payment instantly. Compare equal installment, equal principal and bullet repayment, add a grace period, reverse-calculate the max loan from a monthly budget, and check rate changes and DSR.

whatIs.title: What is the Loan Calculator?
whatIs.description: Enter the loan amount, rate and term to compare monthly payments and total interest across equal installment, equal principal and bullet repayment. You can also add a grace period, find the maximum loan for a monthly budget, see how payments move with rate changes, and run a quick DSR check.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Enter the loan amount, annual rate and term — results appear immediately.
2. Pick a repayment method (equal installment / equal principal / bullet) and a grace period.
3. In the 'Monthly → max loan' tab, enter what you can pay each month to see the maximum you can borrow.
4. Use the comparison table, rate-change table and DSR check below; open the repayment schedule calculator for the full month-by-month table.

tips.title: Pro Tips
items: Even 0.1%p matters: for KRW 300M over 30 years (equal installment, around 4%), total interest differs by about KRW 6M, so compare lenders.
Equal principal has the lowest total interest but higher early payments — choose it if you have room in your early budget.
Manage your credit score (no late payments, moderate card utilization) to lower the spread on your rate.
If you choose a variable rate, check the 'What if the rate changes?' table to make sure you can handle a 1–2%p rise.
Prepaying early saves the most interest. Prepayment fees usually stop after 3 years.

items.q: Equal installment or equal principal — which is better?
items.a: Equal principal costs less total interest but has higher early payments. Choose equal principal if you have early cash flow, or equal installment for a steady monthly payment.

items.q: What is a grace period loan?
items.a: You pay only interest for a set period, then repay principal and interest over the remaining term. It lowers early payments but increases total interest because principal is repaid later.

items.q: If I can pay KRW 1.5M a month, how much can I borrow?
items.a: Use the 'Monthly → max loan' tab. For example, at 4.5% over 30 years with equal installment it is about KRW 296M. Actual limits can be lower due to DSR/LTV rules and bank review.

items.q: What is DSR and how does the 40% rule apply?
items.a: DSR is the ratio of annual principal + interest on all loans to annual income. When total loans exceed KRW 100M, banks cap it at 40% and non-bank lenders at 50%, and variable-rate loans are assessed with an added stress rate. The DSR here is for reference only.

items.q: How do LTV and DTI affect a loan?
items.a: LTV limits the loan relative to collateral value; DTI limits annual repayment relative to income. Lower ratios mean higher limits and better rates.

items.q: When is the prepayment fee waived?
items.a: Most prepayment fees are waived 3 years after the loan starts. Government policy loans may differ, so check with your bank.

policy.title: 2026 policy products (confirmed)
items: Youth Future Savings: launched June 2026. Ages 19-34, personal income up to KRW 60M and household up to 200% of median income. Up to KRW 500k/month, 3-year term, government match 6% (standard) or 12% (preferred), tax-free interest.
Youth Leap Account: new sign-ups closed in December 2025. Existing holders keep the match and tax exemption until their 5-year maturity.

Government matching contributions are not included in the interest here; they are added separately at maturity.

taxRules.title: Tax on interest
items: Standard 15.4% = income tax 14% (Income Tax Act Art. 129) + local income tax 1.4%, withheld by the bank.

Co-op deposits (up to KRW 30M): income tax exempt, 1.4% rural special tax. Exemption kept through 2028 for total salary up to KRW 70M; higher-income associate members pay 5% separate tax in 2026-2028 and 9% from 2029.
Preferential 9.5% = income tax 9% + rural special tax 0.5%; new general tax-preferred accounts are no longer offered.
Interest and dividends above KRW 20M a year are subject to comprehensive financial income taxation.

savings.title: Savings Calculator
savings.description: Calculate maturity amounts and pre/after-tax interest for installment savings and fixed deposits, the same way banks do. Standard 15.4%, preferential and tax-free, effective yield, 3-product comparison and goal reverse calculation.

howItWorks.title: How it is calculated
items: Savings, simple: pre-tax interest = monthly × rate/12 × n(n+1)/2, the method used by the FSS comparison site and bank apps.
Savings, monthly compound: each payment grows by (1 + rate/12)^k for its remaining k months.
Deposit, simple: principal × rate × months/12; monthly compound: principal × ((1 + rate/12)^months − 1).
Tax = pre-tax interest × tax rate (truncated to the won). Standard 15.4%, preferential 9.5%, co-op 1.4%, tax-free 0%.
Effective yield = after-tax interest ÷ total principal ÷ years. A savings rate r equals a deposit rate of r × (n+1)/(2n) (about 0.54× for 12 months).

comparison.title: Savings vs deposit, simple vs compound
items: If you have a lump sum, a deposit pays more unless the savings rate is nearly double.
If you don't, save monthly first and move the matured amount into a deposit.
Simple vs monthly compound: a 1-2% difference over 12 months, larger over 3+ years.
High-rate special savings often cap monthly payments (e.g. KRW 300k), so total interest can be smaller than it looks.

whatIs.title: The one thing to know
whatIs.description: In installment savings each monthly payment earns interest for a different length of time: the first for n months, the last for one. Simple-interest savings therefore earn monthly × rate/12 × n(n+1)/2. KRW 1M/month for 12 months at 5% earns KRW 325,000 before tax and KRW 274,950 after the 15.4% tax, a little over half of the KRW 600,000 a 12M deposit at 5% would earn. A 5% savings plan equals roughly a 2.7% deposit.

howToUse.title: How to use
items: Choose installment savings (monthly) or fixed deposit (lump sum).
Enter the monthly amount (or principal), annual rate, term in months and simple/monthly compound. Most bank products use simple interest.
Pick the interest tax type; pre/after-tax interest and the maturity amount update instantly.
Use the effective-yield card to compare with a deposit (or savings), and the 3-product table to compare different rates, terms and taxes.
Use the goal reverse calculation to see how much to save each month, and share results by link or image.

tips.title: Tips
items: Compare after-tax interest. Co-op (1.4%) and tax-free products give 15%+ more after-tax interest at the same rate.
If you can't meet bonus-rate conditions you only get the base rate, so calculate with it too.
Ages 19-34: check Youth Future Savings first (6-12% government match, tax-free).
Early-termination rates are far below the contract rate; keep an emergency fund and set a comfortable monthly amount.
Compare bank rates on the FSS comparison site (finlife.fss.or.kr).

items.q: How much interest for KRW 1M/month for a year at 5%?
items.a: With simple interest, KRW 325,000 before tax; minus 15.4% tax (KRW 50,050) leaves KRW 274,950, for a maturity amount of KRW 12,274,950. It is not 5% of 12M because each payment earns interest for a different period.

items.q: What deposit rate is a 5% savings plan equal to?
items.a: A 12-month 5% savings plan earns the same as about 2.71% on a 1-year deposit; about 2.60% for 24 months and 2.57% for 36 months (r × (n+1)/(2n)).

items.q: What if I terminate early?
items.a: You get the bank's early-termination rate instead of the contract rate (a fraction of the base rate depending on elapsed time, as low as about 0.1% early on). Check the product description.

items.q: When is interest paid?
items.a: Regular savings and deposits pay principal and interest at maturity, with tax withheld then. Some deposits pay interest monthly, which earns slightly less because there is no compounding.

items.q: Who can open tax-free comprehensive savings?
items.a: Available until end of 2028 with a KRW 50M principal limit across institutions. From 2026, new applicants aged 65+ must be basic pension recipients; disabled persons, independence patriots and basic livelihood recipients remain eligible (Restriction of Special Taxation Act Art. 88-2).

items.q: How much tax on co-op (Nonghyup, Shinhyup) deposits?
items.a: Up to KRW 30M per member, income tax is exempt and only 1.4% rural special tax applies. From 2026, associate members with total salary above KRW 70M pay a 5% separate tax (Art. 89-3).

retirement.title: Retirement Pay Calculator
retirement.description: Calculate statutory severance pay, retirement income tax under the 2023+ rules and your take-home amount.

howItWorks.title: How it is calculated
items: Average-wage period: the calendar days in the 3 months before the retirement date (89–92 days). Retiring on Oct 1 means Jul 1 – Sep 30, 92 days.
Average daily wage = (3-month wages + annual bonus × 3/12 + leave pay × 3/12) ÷ days in the period. If this is below the ordinary wage, the ordinary wage is used (Labor Standards Act Art. 2(2)).
Severance = average daily wage × 30 days × days of service ÷ 365. Days beyond full years are prorated.

Retirement tax: subtract the service-years deduction, multiply by 12 and divide by years of service to get converted pay. Apply basic rates (6–45%) to converted pay minus the converted-pay deduction, then divide by 12 and multiply by years of service.
Service-years deduction (2023+): up to 5 yrs 1M × years; up to 10 yrs 5M + 2M × (years−5); up to 20 yrs 15M + 2.5M × (years−10); over 20 yrs 40M + 3M × (years−20) KRW.
Converted-pay deduction: up to 8M in full; up to 70M 8M + 60% of excess; up to 100M 45.2M + 55%; up to 300M 61.7M + 45%; over 300M 151.7M + 35%. Local income tax is 10% of the retirement income tax.

whatIs.title: What is the Severance Pay Calculator?
whatIs.description: Calculates statutory severance and the daily average wage from your dates and last-3-month pay (using the ordinary wage if higher), then subtracts retirement income tax (2023+ deductions) and local tax to show take-home pay. It also shows how much an IRP pension saves in tax and how severance grows if you leave a few months later.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Pick your start date and retirement date (the day after your last working day). Under 1 year, it shows how many days remain and the expected severance at 1 year.
2. The default is 'Monthly pay': enter your average monthly pre-tax pay (base + fixed allowances) for the last 3 months.
3. If pay varied by month, choose '3-month detail'. The period is split into three monthly segments with day counts, and an optional monthly ordinary wage is compared against the average wage.
4. Add bonuses and annual-leave pay received in the last year, if any. Only 3/12 of each is added.
5. Review take-home pay, the tax steps, lump sum vs IRP and the 'leave later' table, then share or save the result.

tips.title: Pro Tips
items: Severance must be paid within 14 days of retirement; the parties may agree to extend this in special cases (Retirement Benefit Security Act Art. 9). Late payment accrues 20% annual interest (Labor Standards Act Art. 37).
For tax, any fraction of a year counts as a full year, so 5 years and 1 day is treated as 6 years, increasing the deduction.
If the last 3 months include business suspension, parental leave or probation, those days and wages are excluded (LSA Enforcement Decree Art. 2), so actual severance may be higher.
Taking IRP severance as a pension after 55 cuts the retirement tax by 30% (40% from year 11, 50% from year 21).

Under a DC pension plan the employer contributes at least 1/12 of annual pay and the result depends on investment returns, so it may differ from the statutory severance (severance/DB basis) shown here.

items.q: How long do I need to work to get severance?
items.a: At least 1 year of continuous service and an average of 15+ contractual hours per week over 4 weeks, regardless of full-time, contract or part-time status (Retirement Benefit Security Act Art. 4(1)). Even one day short of a year means no statutory severance.

items.q: Do workplaces with fewer than 5 employees have to pay severance?
items.a: Yes. The Act applies to every workplace with at least one employee (Art. 3). It has applied to workplaces with 4 or fewer since December 2010, in full since 2013. Only businesses employing just cohabiting relatives and domestic workers are excluded.

items.q: What if I work fewer than 15 hours a week?
items.a: Workers averaging under 15 contractual hours per week over 4 weeks are excluded (Art. 4(1) proviso). If actual hours average 15 or more, you may qualify, so keep records.

items.q: When must severance be paid?
items.a: Within 14 days of retirement, extendable by mutual agreement in special cases (Art. 9(1)). Late payment accrues 20% annual interest (Labor Standards Act Art. 37), and non-payment is punishable by up to 3 years in prison or a 30 million KRW fine (Art. 44). You can file a petition with the Ministry of Employment and Labor.

items.q: Is the retirement date my last working day?
items.a: No. It is the day the employment ends, usually the day after your last working day. If you worked through Sep 30, the retirement date is Oct 1 and the average-wage period is Jul 1–Sep 30 (92 days).

items.q: How is the average wage calculated?
items.a: Total pay for the 3 months before retirement plus 3/12 of last year's bonuses and annual-leave pay, divided by the calendar days in those 3 months (89–92) (Labor Standards Act Art. 2(1)6). Severance = daily average wage × 30 × service days ÷ 365 (Retirement Benefit Security Act Art. 8).

items.q: What if my ordinary wage is higher than my average wage?
items.a: If the daily average wage is lower than the daily ordinary wage, the ordinary wage is used (Labor Standards Act Art. 2(2)). For monthly pay, daily ordinary wage = monthly ordinary wage ÷ 209 hours × 8 hours (40-hour week).

items.q: How is retirement income tax calculated?
items.a: Subtract the service-years deduction, multiply by 12 and divide by service years to get converted pay; subtract the converted-pay deduction, apply the basic rates, divide by 12 and multiply by service years. Local tax adds 10% (Income Tax Act Art. 48, 55). The 2023 deductions remain unchanged in 2026.

items.q: Are bonuses and annual-leave pay included?
items.a: Yes. 3/12 of bonuses received in the last year and 3/12 of unused annual-leave pay that became payable in the last year are added to the 3-month total. Leave pay that arises only on retirement is excluded.

items.q: How is an IRP taxed?
items.a: Moving severance into an IRP defers the retirement tax entirely. Taken as a pension after 55, you pay 70% of the original tax (60% from year 11, 50% from year 21 starting 2026); withdrawing a lump sum early triggers the original tax (Income Tax Act Art. 129).

items.q: What is the difference between DB and DC pensions?
items.a: DB (defined benefit) guarantees at least the statutory severance and the employer bears investment risk. DC (defined contribution) means the employer deposits at least 1/12 of annual pay into your account each year (Art. 20) and the payout depends on your returns. DB suits steadily rising pay; DC suits returns above wage growth. This calculator uses the severance/DB basis.

items.q: Can I get an interim severance settlement?
items.a: Generally no, except for statutory reasons such as buying a home as a non-homeowner, a jeonse deposit (once per employment), 6+ months of medical care exceeding 12.5% of annual pay, bankruptcy or rehabilitation within 5 years, wage peak systems, reduced working hours, or disasters (Enforcement Decree Art. 3). Service years restart after settlement.

whatIs.title: What is the Tax Calculator?
whatIs.description: An all-in-one Korean tax calculator for income tax, VAT, and capital gains tax. It applies the latest NTS rates and deductions so you can accurately estimate your tax liability and identify tax-saving opportunities.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Select the type of tax: income tax, VAT, or capital gains tax.
2. Enter your income amount and applicable deductions.
3. Click 'Calculate' to see the tax amount, local income tax, and effective tax rate.
4. Review deduction breakdowns and tax-saving tips to plan your strategy.

tips.title: Pro Tips
items: Income tax uses progressive rates (6%–45%), so maximize deductions like personal exemptions and pension contributions.
Contributing ₩6M to pension savings and ₩3M to IRP yields up to ₩1.65M in tax credits annually.
Business owners should manage tax invoices carefully to utilize input VAT credits.
A single-household homeowner holding a property for 2+ years may be exempt from capital gains tax.
For complex tax situations, consult a certified tax accountant for legal optimization.

items.q: How are income tax rates determined?
items.a: Korea uses progressive rates from 6% to 45%: under ₩14M at 6%, ₩14M–50M at 15%, ₩50M–88M at 24%, above ₩88M from 35% to 45%.

items.q: General vs simplified VAT taxpayers?
items.a: Businesses over ₩48M annual revenue are general taxpayers (10% VAT). Below are simplified taxpayers (1–4% by industry) with limited input VAT credit.

items.q: Capital gains tax exemption conditions?
items.a: A single-household owner holding (and in designated areas, residing in) a home for 2+ years qualifies for exemption. Luxury homes (over ₩1.2B) are taxed on the excess.

items.q: Do I need to file local income tax separately?
items.a: No. Local income tax (10% of income tax) is automatically calculated and collected with your income tax return.

steps.title: When the money goes out
items: Contract day: pay the deposit (usually 10% of price). The deal must be reported within 30 days of the contract, usually by the broker.
Interim payment: pay the interim amount set in the contract (sometimes skipped).
Closing day: pay the balance (incl. the loan) and the brokerage fee, and pay the scrivener for the housing bond discount, stamp duty and registration.
Acquisition tax: report and pay within 60 days of acquisition (the earlier of closing or registration), usually together with registration.
After moving in: register your address. First-time buyer relief requires moving in within 3 months.

items.q: How much extra does buying a home cost beyond the price?
items.a: For a single home of 85㎡ or less, roughly 2–3% of the price. A ₩500M Seoul apartment costs about ₩5.5M in taxes, up to ₩2M brokerage (+₩200K VAT) and about ₩1.1M for bonds, stamp duty and scrivener — around ₩9M; a ₩700M home about ₩17M. Over 85㎡ adds 0.2% rural tax, and heavy multi-home rates of 8–12% raise it a lot.

items.q: What are the 2026 acquisition tax rates for homes?
items.a: For one home (or a 2nd home outside adjusted areas): 1% up to ₩600M, 1–3% between ₩600M and ₩900M (formula), 3% above ₩900M. Adjusted areas: 8% for a 2nd home, 12% for 3+. Non-adjusted: 8% for a 3rd home, 12% for 4+. Local education tax, and rural special tax over 85㎡, are added.

items.q: Why is there a housing bond cost?
items.a: Transfer registration requires buying Type-1 National Housing Bonds in proportion to the official value. Most buyers sell them back immediately and only bear the discount. The discount rate changes daily; here we assume an official value of 70% of price and a 5% discount. It is the 'bond discount' line in a scrivener's quote.

items.q: How much can I borrow?
items.a: The limit is the tighter of LTV (loan to price) and DSR (annual payments on all loans ÷ income). LTV and mortgage caps vary by region, number of homes, first-time status and price, and change with government measures — check with your bank. The bank DSR limit is 40%, and the stress DSR assumes a higher rate, which can lower the limit further.

items.q: Level payment or level principal?
items.a: Level payment keeps the same amount every month with a lower start. Level principal starts higher but pays down faster with less total interest, and gives a higher early DSR.

items.q: Do I have to pay the maximum brokerage fee?
items.a: No. The legal rate is a cap and can be negotiated. Sale caps: 0.6% under ₩50M (max ₩250K), 0.5% under ₩200M (max ₩800K), 0.4% under ₩900M, 0.5% under ₩1.2B, 0.6% under ₩1.5B, 0.7% from ₩1.5B, plus VAT (10% general, 4% simplified).

items.q: Where can the result differ from reality?
items.a: Bond discount rates (daily), scrivener quotes, negotiated brokerage and the actual official value can shift costs by hundreds of thousands of won. Loan stamp duty and loan fees, and the heavy-tax exemption for homes with official value ≤ ₩100M, are not included. Use the acquisition tax calculator for exact tax.

3. Use 'Minify' to produce a single-line optimized SQL string.
4. Copy the result or save to history for future reference.

tips.title: Pro Tips
items: Format SQL before submitting PRs — reviewers understand logic much faster.
Paste ORM-generated queries to quickly spot performance bottlenecks.
Large INSERT statements become easy to validate once VALUES rows are aligned.
Consistent keyword casing helps the team maintain SQL coding standards.
CTE and recursive queries are indented level by level, making debugging far easier.

items.q: Which database dialects are supported?
items.a: MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQL Server (T-SQL), Oracle (PL/SQL), and ANSI SQL standard. DB-specific syntax is recognized correctly.

items.q: Can it format nested subqueries?
items.a: Yes. IN, EXISTS subqueries and nested queries are indented by level. CTE and recursive queries are also structured.

items.q: What does minify do?
items.a: Removes unnecessary whitespace, line breaks, and comments to produce a compact single-line SQL string.

items.q: Window functions supported?
items.a: Yes. ROW_NUMBER(), RANK(), and GROUP BY ROLLUP, CUBE, GROUPING SETS are all formatted correctly.

principle.title: Why the file gets smaller
items: File size roughly follows pixel count. Halving width and height leaves 1/4 of the pixels.
JPG and WebP drop less-visible detail as quality goes down. 80–90% is usually hard to tell apart.
PNG is lossless with no quality setting. Shrink the dimensions or switch to JPG to save space.
Large reductions are done in half-size steps to avoid jagged edges and moiré.

formats.title: JPG vs PNG vs WebP
items: JPG: the standard for photos, accepted everywhere, small files. No transparency.
PNG: lossless with transparency. Good for logos, text-heavy images and screenshots.
WebP: usually smaller at the same quality and supports transparency. For official submissions, JPG is safer.

idPhoto.title: ID photo pixel math
items: Pixels = cm ÷ 2.54 × dpi, using 300dpi print quality.
Fill mode crops from the center, so use a photo with the face centered.
Passport photos also have rules on face size and background, and each organization sets its own pixel, file size and format limits. Check the submission notice first.

whatIs.title: What is this tool?
whatIs.description: Change a photo's pixel dimensions and file size. Fit ID-photo specs, social media sizes and "under XX KB" upload limits in one place. All processing happens in your browser, so photos never leave your device.

howToUse.title: How to use
items: Choose or drop photos. Multiple files work, and you can paste a copied image with Ctrl+V.
Pick a common size, or set the size by pixels, percent or long side.
If there is an upload limit, enter the KB value under Max file size.
Check the resulting size and file size, then download one by one or all as a ZIP.

tips.title: Tips
items: Enable aspect ratio lock to auto-calculate dimensions from one value.
WebP format is 25-35% smaller than JPEG at the same quality.
Use social media presets to prevent images from being cropped on platforms.

items.q: The site says "500KB or less". What do I do?
items.a: Enter 500 as Max file size and save as JPG. Quality is lowered first, then dimensions if needed. 1KB is counted as 1,000 bytes, so it passes even if the site uses 1,024. With an exact pixel size, only quality is adjusted.

items.q: How many pixels for an ID photo?
items.a: At 300dpi, 3×4cm is 354×472px and 3.5×4.5cm is 413×531px. If the organization specifies pixels, turn off the ratio lock and enter them as an exact size.

items.q: Are my photos uploaded?
items.a: No. Decoding, resizing and saving all happen with Canvas in your browser. Once the page is open, it works even offline.

items.q: Does enlarging a small photo make it sharper?
items.a: No. Enlarging invents pixels, so it gets blurry. That's why Long side mode never enlarges.

items.q: Will phone photos come out sideways?
items.a: No. The orientation stored in the photo (EXIF) is applied first. Metadata like location is not kept in the output.

rules.title: How we count
items: With/without spaces: counts visible characters (Unicode graphemes). Family emoji, flags and combining marks count as one.
Bytes (Korean = 2): same as the JobKorea/Saramin counters. Non-ASCII characters are 2 bytes; letters, digits, spaces and line breaks are 1 byte; emoji are 4 bytes.
UTF-8 bytes: Korean 3 bytes, ASCII 1 byte, emoji 4 bytes. Useful for server/database storage limits.
Sentences split after . ! ? … followed by a space or a line break (numbers like 3.14 are not split). Paragraphs are separated by blank lines.

Manuscript: simplified 200-cell Korean manuscript paper (20 × 10). Each line break starts a paragraph with one indent cell; two lowercase letters or digits share a cell. Fine rules such as end-of-line punctuation are skipped, so results may be off by a few cells.
Reading/speaking time: estimated at 500 / 250 Korean characters per minute and 238 / 150 English words per minute.
X weighted length: follows X's official twitter-text (v3) rules — Latin letters and digits 1, Korean/CJK and emoji 2, links starting with http 23. The limit is 280.

whatIs.title: What is the Character Counter?
whatIs.description: The character counter shows characters with and without spaces, bytes, words, sentences, paragraphs, lines, manuscript sheets and reading time as you type. howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Pick a question tab (Q1–Q5) and optionally give it a title.
2. Paste or type your text; counts, bytes and manuscript sheets update instantly.
3. Choose the counting rule (with/without spaces, bytes, X) and a target, or tap a common limit.
4. Click repeated words to find them, then tidy the text and run a spell check.

tips.title: Tips
items: Companies differ on with/without spaces or bytes. Match the target to the wording on the application form.
Byte limits usually count Korean as 2 bytes, so 1,000 bytes is about 500 Korean characters. ASCII letters, digits and spaces are 1 byte.
If lines broke when copying from a PDF or HWP file, use 'Join broken lines' to restore paragraphs.
A word used more than three times feels repetitive. Click it in the repeated-words list to see where it appears.

items.q: How are emoji counted?
items.a: This tool counts each emoji as one visible character (including family and flag emoji). JobKorea/Saramin count an emoji as 2 characters and 4 bytes and X counts it as 2, so when emoji are present we also show the site-style count.

items.q: Why do byte counts differ between sites?
items.a: Some count a Korean character as 2 bytes (JobKorea, Saramin, SMS) while UTF-8 uses 3 bytes. We show both so you can use whichever your destination requires.

items.q: Is my text saved or uploaded?

whatIs.title: What is the UUID Generator?
whatIs.description: A UUID (Universally Unique Identifier) is a 128-bit identifier guaranteed to be globally unique, widely used as database primary keys, API request tracking IDs, filenames, and more. This tool generates v1 (time-based), v4 (random), v7 (sortable time-based), and Nil UUIDs securely in the browser, with support for bulk generation and various output formats (with/without hyphens, uppercase, etc.).

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Select the UUID version: v1, v4, v7, or Nil.
2. Set how many UUIDs to generate (1 to 1,000).
3. Choose the output format (with hyphens, uppercase, with braces, etc.).
4. Click Generate, then copy the results or download as a file.

tips.title: Tips
items: For modern systems, prefer v7 over v4. Since v7 embeds a timestamp, it sorts chronologically and performs much better as a database index.
Storing UUIDs as 32-character strings without hyphens saves storage space when using them as database primary keys.
Use the bulk generation feature to produce hundreds of UUIDs at once for test data in SQL INSERT statements.

items.q: What is the difference between v4 and v7?
items.a: v4 is fully random with an extremely low collision probability. v7 embeds a millisecond-precision timestamp at the front, enabling chronological sorting and better database index efficiency.

items.q: Are generated UUIDs stored on a server?
items.a: No. All UUIDs are generated entirely in your browser and never sent to any server. The process is completely client-side.

items.q: Is there any risk of UUID collisions?
items.a: For v4 UUIDs, the probability of a collision is approximately 5.3×10⁻³⁶ — effectively zero for all practical purposes.

whatIs.title: What is the Cron Expression Tester?
whatIs.description: The Cron Expression Tester lets you validate and interpret cron schedule expressions used in Linux/Unix crontabs, AWS EventBridge, GitHub Actions, and similar systems — all in real time. It explains what a given expression means in plain language and shows a list of upcoming execution times, helping you catch scheduling mistakes before they happen.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Enter a cron expression in the input field (e.g., `0 9 * * 1-5`).
2. The tool immediately explains the schedule in plain English.
3. Review the list of upcoming execution times to verify the schedule is correct.
4. Select from preset buttons for common patterns.

tips.title: Tips
items: When using day-of-week ranges like `0 9 * * 1-5`, confirm whether your system uses 0–6 (Sun–Sat) or 1–7 (Mon–Sun) notation.
AWS CloudWatch Events / EventBridge supports an optional sixth field for the year.
Step intervals using `/` (e.g., `*/5 * * * *` for every 5 minutes) have varying support across systems — always test before deploying.

items.q: What is the difference between standard cron and Quartz cron?
items.a: Standard cron uses 5 fields (minute hour day month weekday). Quartz cron uses 6–7 fields (second minute hour day month weekday [year]). This tool is based on the standard 5-field format.

items.q: Are special characters like `L` and `W` supported?
items.a: L (last) and W (weekday) are Quartz-specific characters not supported by standard crontab. Check your runtime environment before using them.

items.q: The expression is correct but the times look off — what's wrong?
items.a: Cron runs on the server's system time. Make sure your server's timezone is set to the one you expect (e.g., Asia/Seoul for KST).

whatIs.title: What is the JWT Decoder?
whatIs.description: The JWT Decoder is a developer tool that Base64-decodes the three parts of a JWT (JSON Web Token) — Header, Payload, and Signature — and displays their contents for analysis. It's useful for debugging API authentication issues, checking token expiration, and inspecting claims. All processing happens in the browser, so you can safely analyze tokens without them ever leaving your device.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Paste your JWT token (without the Bearer prefix) into the input field.
2. The token is split into Header (algorithm, token type), Payload (claims data), and Signature.
3. Time-related claims like exp (expiration) and iat (issued at) are displayed as human-readable dates.
4. The tool automatically checks whether the token is still valid based on the current time.

tips.title: Tips
items: Production JWT tokens may contain personal or sensitive data. Never paste them into an untrusted online decoder. This tool processes everything locally in your browser with no server transmission.
JWT Payloads are only signed, not encrypted. Avoid storing sensitive information in the Payload.
Monitor token expiration (exp) regularly so you can design appropriate refresh cycles.

items.q: Can you verify the Signature?
items.a: Signature verification requires the server's secret key. Since this is a client-side tool, it doesn't accept secret keys for security reasons — it only provides structural analysis of the Header and Payload.

items.q: Can asymmetric algorithms like RS256 be decoded?
items.a: Yes — the Base64 decoding approach is the same regardless of algorithm. Header and Payload contents are accessible for any JWT algorithm.

items.q: Why does the tool say the token is invalid?
items.a: If the exp (expiration) timestamp is earlier than the current time, the token is shown as expired. If the token has a formatting error, a parsing failure message is displayed.

howToUse.title: How to use
items: Enter the car price (incl. VAT), options and discount to set the purchase price.

items.q: How is a balloon installment calculated?
items.a: You pay only interest on the balloon throughout the term and repay it in full at maturity; the rest is repaid in equal installments. Monthly payments drop but total interest rises. Whether the balloon can be refinanced at maturity depends on the lender.

items.q: Is there an early repayment fee?
items.a: The rate and period are set by your contract, and some products have none. Under Korea's Financial Consumer Protection Act, no early repayment fee may be charged once 3 years have passed since the loan (including installment finance) contract.

items.q: Installment finance vs auto loan?
items.a: With installment finance, a finance company pays the dealer and you repay it over time. With an auto loan you borrow from a bank or card company (or pay by card and split it). Pricing, liens and perks vary by product, so compare total interest for the same amount and term.

items.q: How much is acquisition tax?

items.q: What is a typical car installment rate?

items.q: Can I compare leases or rentals?

items.q: How much is car registration tax?
items.a: For passenger cars, acquisition tax is 7% (personal use) or 4% (commercial). Compact cars get a reduced rate of 4% with additional discounts.

items.q: What are EV tax benefits?
items.a: Through Dec 31, 2026, EVs get up to 1.4M KRW reduction in acquisition tax (1.0M from 2027). The hybrid reduction ended in 2024.

items.q: What is bond purchase?
items.a: A mandatory bond purchase when registering a vehicle. The rate varies by vehicle price, displacement, and region.

bogeumjariLoan.title: Bogeumjari Loan Calculator
bogeumjariLoan.description: Check eligibility and estimate monthly payments for the government-backed Bogeumjari housing loan

whatIs.title: What is Bogeumjari Loan?
whatIs.description: Bogeumjari Loan is a government-backed fixed-rate mortgage provided by Korea Housing Finance Corporation (HF). It offers more stable rates than variable-rate bank loans, with preferential terms for first-time buyers, newlyweds, and multi-child families.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Select loan type (general/first-time/newlywed/multi-child).
Enter property price and combined household annual income.
Choose loan term (10-50 years).
View eligibility, estimated loan limit, and monthly payment.

tips.title: Tips
items: First-time buyers get LTV up to 80% vs 70% for general type.
Newlywed type offers 0.3%p rate discount. Check if you married within 7 years.
Online-only (Akkim-e) version offers 0.1-0.2%p additional rate discount.

items.q: What are the eligibility requirements?
items.a: Combined household income under 70M KRW, property under 600M KRW, and homeownership restrictions apply.

items.q: What's the interest rate?
items.a: As of 2026, Akkim-e Bogeumjari rates are approximately 4.05-4.35% annually. Type-specific discounts apply additionally.

items.q: How does it differ from Didimddol Loan?
items.a: Didimddol has stricter income requirements but lower rates (2-3%). Bogeumjari has broader eligibility and higher loan limits. Compare both for your situation.

items.q: What are the eligibility requirements for first-time buyer (생애최초) type?
items.a: Both you and your spouse must have no history of owning property. Even if you're currently a non-homeowner, any past ownership disqualifies you. If either spouse has ever owned property, you must apply under the general type.

items.q: What is the interest rate for first-time buyer Bogeumjari Loan?
items.a: As of 2026, the first-time buyer type receives a 0.2%p rate discount on top of the base rate. For a 30-year term, the rate is approximately 4.05%. Combined with the newlywed discount (0.3%p), it can go as low as 3.75%.

items.q: What is the maximum loan amount for first-time buyer Bogeumjari Loan?
items.a: The maximum loan limit for first-time buyers is 420 million KRW. LTV is also expanded to 80% (vs 70% for general), allowing more borrowing against the same property. For a 500M KRW property, up to 400M KRW (500M × 80%) is possible.

whatIs.title: What is Median Income?
whatIs.description: The standard median income is the midpoint of national household income announced annually by the Ministry of Health and Welfare. It serves as the qualification threshold for various government welfare programs including basic livelihood benefits and housing support.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Select the year (2023-2026) to view median income data.
Review median income by household size (1-6 persons).
Check amounts at various percentage thresholds (32%-100%).
See which government welfare programs each threshold qualifies for.

tips.title: Tips
items: Livelihood benefits: 32%, medical: 40%, housing: 48%, education: 50% of median income.
Median income uses pre-tax income. The 'recognized income' calculation differs from simple salary.
Median income increases yearly - check again even if you didn't qualify last year.

items.q: What is the 2026 median income?
items.a: For 1-person households approximately 2.56M KRW/month, 4-person households approximately 6.49M KRW/month. About 6.4% increase from the previous year.

items.q: How is recognized income calculated?
items.a: Recognized income = Income assessment + Asset-to-income conversion. Use the Bokjiro (bokjiro.go.kr) simulation tool for precise calculation.

items.q: What benefits are available at 100% median income?
items.a: National Employment Support System, youth rent subsidy, and child tax credit may apply. Each program has additional requirements beyond income.

bmi.title: BMI Calculator
bmi.description: Calculate your Body Mass Index (BMI) to start healthy weight management

input.title: Body Information Input

howItWorks.title: How it's calculated
items: BMI = weight (kg) ÷ height (m)². Example: 170cm, 65kg → 65 ÷ 1.7² = 22.5
Classification uses the displayed value (rounded to one decimal). 22.96 shows as 23.0 and is classified as pre-obese.
Healthy weight range = height (m)² × 18.5 to 22.9, shown in 0.1kg steps that actually classify as normal when entered.
Standard weight = height (m)² × 22 (170cm → 63.6kg)
With a waist measurement, abdominal obesity is combined with your BMI category into the KSSO comorbidity risk.

comparison.title: Standards compared
items: KSSO (2022): <18.5 underweight, 18.5–22.9 normal, 23–24.9 pre-obese, 25–29.9 class 1, 30–34.9 class 2, 35+ class 3 obesity
WHO: 18.5–24.9 normal, 25–29.9 overweight, 30+ obese (classes at 30, 35, 40). The same person can be classified differently.
BMI vs body fat %: BMI can't separate muscle from fat. If you are muscular, check with the body fat calculator.
BMI 22 standard weight vs Broca ((height − 100) × 0.9): 63.6kg vs 63.0kg at 170cm — similar, but they diverge for very tall or short people.

meaning.0: BMI is an obesity index calculated from height and weight
meaning.1: Used as a reference indicator for overall health status
meaning.2: Has limitations as it doesn't reflect muscle mass, bone density, etc.
meaning.3: Observe weight changes through regular measurements

management.0: Balanced diet and regular exercise are important
management.1: Steady management is more effective than rapid weight changes
management.2: Consult with professionals considering individual differences
management.3: Stress management and adequate sleep are also necessary

whatIs.title: What is the BMI Calculator?
whatIs.description: The BMI (Body Mass Index) Calculator expresses your weight status as a number from height and weight. It classifies you as underweight, normal, pre-obese or obesity class 1–3 under the Korean KSSO 2022 standard (default) or WHO, and shows the healthy weight range for your height and how many kg you are from it. Add your waist to check abdominal obesity and comorbidity risk.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Enter height (cm) and weight (kg) to see your BMI and category instantly.
Check your healthy weight range, how many kg to lose or gain to reach normal, and the distance to adjacent categories.
Optionally enter your waist to see abdominal obesity and comorbidity risk.
Switch the standard to WHO for international comparison. Share the result as a link or image.
Tap 'Log today' to save on this device and see your BMI trend chart.

tips.title: Tips
items: BMI ignores muscle mass, so athletes and muscular people may be classified as pre-obese or obese. Use it with the body fat calculator.
Asians carry higher metabolic risk at the same BMI; the KSSO defines 23–24.9 as pre-obese and 25+ as obese.
A waist of 90cm or more for men and 85cm or more for women is abdominal obesity, which raises risk even with a normal BMI.
Weigh under the same conditions (morning, before eating) and watch the monthly trend rather than daily swings.

items.q: What is the normal BMI range?
items.a: 18.5–22.9 under the KSSO standard and 18.5–24.9 under WHO. Korean health check-ups and clinics use the KSSO standard.

items.q: Is a BMI of 23 obese?
items.a: Under the KSSO, 23–24.9 is 'pre-obese' (formerly called overweight). It is not obesity but the range where comorbidity risk starts to rise; under WHO it is normal.

items.q: Does it apply to children and teenagers?
items.a: The adult chart applies from age 19. Children and teens are assessed by BMI percentile for age and sex on the 2017 Korean growth charts (85th to <95th overweight, 95th+ obese). Consult a pediatrician if concerned.

items.q: Are the cut-offs the same for people 65 and older?
items.a: Yes, but older adults face greater risk from muscle loss and underweight, and many studies found the lowest mortality at a BMI slightly above the normal upper limit. Preserving muscle and nutrition matters more than aggressive weight loss.

items.q: Can a low BMI still indicate health problems?
items.a: Yes. A BMI below 18.5 can be associated with malnutrition, osteoporosis and weakened immunity. If you've lost weight rapidly, consult a doctor.

calorie.description: Use your BMR and maintenance calories (TDEE) to get daily calories for weight loss, the date you'll reach your target weight, and macros

formulas.title: How it's calculated
items: Mifflin-St Jeor (default): 10×weight + 6.25×height − 5×age + 5 (men) / −161 (women)
Harris-Benedict, 1984 revision: men 88.362 + 13.397×weight + 4.799×height − 5.677×age; women 447.593 + 9.247×weight + 3.098×height − 4.330×age
Katch-McArdle: 370 + 21.6×lean body mass (weight×(1−body fat))
Maintenance (TDEE) = BMR × activity factor 1.2 / 1.375 / 1.55 / 1.725 / 1.9
Target = TDEE ∓ pace (kg/week)×7,700÷7. Weight loss never goes below the higher of BMR and the sex minimum (1,200 women / 1,500 men kcal)

guide.sources: Sources: Mifflin MD et al., Am J Clin Nutr 1990 · Roza AM & Shizgal HM, Am J Clin Nutr 1984 · Frankenfield D et al., J Am Diet Assoc 2005 · Ministry of Health and Welfare & Korean Nutrition Society, 2020 Dietary Reference Intakes for Koreans.
guide.disclaimer: This calculator gives general estimates and is not a medical diagnosis or prescription. If you are pregnant or breastfeeding, have a condition such as diabetes or kidney disease, or have a history of eating disorders, consult a doctor or registered dietitian. The minimum calorie levels (1,200 women / 1,500 men kcal) are general guidance, not medical standards.
guide.title: Understanding Calories and Metabolism

bmr.0: The minimum energy required to sustain life
bmr.1: Used for heart beating, breathing, temperature regulation, etc.
bmr.2: Accounts for 60-70% of total energy expenditure
bmr.3: Decreases with age and lower muscle mass

calorie.0: About 7,700 kcal per kg of body weight is a common approximation (based on fat tissue; early weight loss is often faster due to water)
calorie.1: 0.5–1 kg per week (under 1% of body weight) is the usual recommended pace
calorie.2: Maintenance calories drop as you lose weight, so recalculate every 2–4 weeks
calorie.3: Combine diet with strength training to limit muscle loss

whatIs.title: What is the Calorie Calculator?
whatIs.description: The Calorie Calculator takes your gender, age, height, weight, and activity level to calculate your Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR) and Total Daily Energy Expenditure (TDEE). Using the Harris-Benedict or Mifflin-St Jeor formula, it recommends a daily calorie intake based on your goal — weight loss, maintenance, or gain.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Enter sex, age, height and weight, and pick your usual activity level.
2. Choose lose, maintain or gain, and a weekly pace (0.25–1 kg).
3. Enter a target weight to see how long it takes, the expected date and a weight chart.
4. If you know your body fat %, enter it to compare with Katch-McArdle, and check your macro targets.

tips.title: Tips
items: Eating 500 kcal below your TDEE typically results in about 0.5 kg of weight loss per week.
Eating far below your BMR can cause muscle loss and rebound weight gain (yo-yo effect).
When choosing your activity level, consider all daily movement — your job, commute, and lifestyle — not just exercise.

items.q: How many calories should I eat a day to lose weight?
items.a: Subtract about 550 kcal from your maintenance calories (TDEE) for 0.5 kg a week, or about 1,100 kcal for 1 kg a week (using 1 kg ≈ 7,700 kcal). General guidance is not to go below your BMR or 1,200 (women) / 1,500 (men) kcal, so this calculator uses that floor and shows the realistic pace instead.

items.q: What is the difference between BMR and TDEE?
items.a: BMR (basal metabolic rate) is the minimum energy your body uses at complete rest. TDEE (maintenance calories) is BMR multiplied by an activity factor (1.2–1.9) — what you actually burn in a day.

items.q: Which equation is more accurate?
items.a: For most adults Mifflin-St Jeor (1990) is rated closest to measured values, so it is the default. Harris-Benedict uses the 1984 revision of the 1919 original, and if you know your body fat % you can compare with the lean-mass-based Katch-McArdle.

items.q: I'm eating the calculated amount but not losing weight.
items.a: Results are estimates and individuals can differ by ±10% or more. Watch your 2–3 week average weight; if it isn't moving, cut 100–200 kcal a day or add activity.

bodyFat.title: Body Fat Calculator
bodyFat.description: Estimate body fat from neck, waist and hip tape measurements. Compare Navy, RFM, BMI-based and YMCA formulas side by side with error ranges, lean mass and a goal weight.

input.title: Body Information & Measurements
input.neckNote: Measure just below the Adam's apple
input.hipNote: Measure at the widest part of the hips

classification.title: Body Fat Classification Chart
classification.note: Ideal body fat ranges may vary by age group. Consult with a professional for accurate diagnosis.

howItWorks.title: How it works
items: US Navy: BF% = 495 ÷ (1.0324 − 0.19077·log₁₀(waist−neck) + 0.15456·log₁₀(height)) − 450 (men, cm). Women use waist+hip−neck with different coefficients.
RFM: 64 − 20 × height ÷ waist (women start at 76). Derived in 2018 from US NHANES DXA data.
BMI-based (Deurenberg 1991): 1.2 × BMI + 0.23 × age − 10.8 × sex (male 1, female 0) − 5.4.
YMCA: a quick formula using only waist (inches) and weight (lb).
Fat mass = weight × BF%, lean mass = weight − fat mass, target weight = lean mass ÷ (1 − goal BF%).

comparison.title: Which result to trust
items: With careful measurements, the Navy method is the safest choice; typical error is about ±3–4 points.
RFM needs only height and waist, and studies found it tracks body fat better than BMI.
BMI-based estimates overrate muscular people and tend to underrate Asians, who carry more fat at the same BMI.
Bioimpedance (InBody) is sensitive to hydration; DXA is accurate but needs a clinic.

measurement.0: Morning measurements on an empty stomach are most accurate
measurement.1: Place the tape measure lightly against the skin
measurement.3: Take multiple measurements and use the average

management.0: Balanced diet and regular exercise are fundamental
management.1: Strength training to increase muscle mass reduces body fat percentage
management.2: Aim for gradual changes rather than rapid weight loss
management.3: Adequate sleep and stress management are also important

whatIs.title: What is the Body Fat Calculator?
whatIs.description: It estimates the share of your weight that is fat, from tape measurements plus height, weight and age. It shows four formulas side by side (US Navy, RFM, BMI-based Deurenberg, YMCA) with each one's approximate error range, and calculates fat mass, lean mass and the weight matching a goal body fat.

howToUse.title: How to use
items: 1. Enter sex, age, height and weight.
2. Measure and enter neck and waist (women also hip). See the diagram below for where to measure.
3. Read the headline body fat with its error range, and compare formulas.
4. Move the goal slider to see target weight and fat to lose, and save entries to track change.

tips.title: Tips
items: Measure in the morning before eating, same posture and same spots, so entries are comparable.
Read the range across formulas, not one number. ±3–5 points of error is normal.
If weight stays the same but your waist shrinks, you likely lost fat and gained muscle.

items.q: Which formula is most accurate?
items.a: With careful measurements, the US Navy method is the most widely validated tape method, at about ±3–4 points. RFM does similarly with only height and waist. BMI-based estimates can't tell muscle from fat, so their error is larger.

items.q: Why does it differ from InBody?
items.a: InBody estimates fat via body water using bioelectrical impedance, so meals, exercise and hydration change the reading. A 3–5 point gap is common; measuring the same way over time matters most.

items.q: What is a healthy body fat?
items.a: Per Gallagher (2000), the healthy range at age 20–39 is 8–19% for men and 21–32% for women, rising slightly with age. ACE classifies 25%+ (men) and 32%+ (women) as obese.

items.q: Can body fat be too low?
items.a: Fat is needed for hormones, temperature and organ protection. ACE puts essential fat at 2–5% for men and 10–13% for women; going below that can cause health problems.

whatIs.title: What is the Work Hours Calculator?
whatIs.description: The Work Hours Calculator helps part-time workers, hourly employees, and contract workers estimate their wages. Based on the 2026 minimum wage, it automatically calculates base pay, night shift premium (10 PM – 6 AM), overtime pay, and weekly holiday pay. You can see a complete breakdown of deductions and your final take-home pay in one view.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Enter your hourly wage (or auto-fill the minimum wage).
2. Set your shift start/end times and work days.
3. Check the box if your shift includes night hours.
4. Click Calculate to see base pay, night premium, weekly holiday pay, estimated taxes, and take-home pay.

tips.title: Tips
items: Working 15 or more hours per week qualifies you for weekly holiday pay (주휴수당). It is calculated as: (scheduled weekly hours ÷ 40) × 8 × hourly wage.
Night shift premium applies to hours worked between 10 PM and 6 AM the following day — an additional 50% of ordinary wages.
If you receive a monthly salary, divide it by 209 hours to calculate your effective hourly rate.

items.q: What is the 2026 minimum wage?
items.a: The 2026 minimum wage is ₩10,320 per hour. Paying below this amount is a violation of the Minimum Wage Act.

items.q: Do premium allowances apply equally at workplaces with fewer than 5 employees?
items.a: Workplaces with fewer than 5 employees may be exempt from overtime, night, and holiday premiums (50% add-ons). However, the minimum wage and weekly holiday pay still apply.

items.q: Can daily workers claim weekly holiday pay?
items.a: Even daily workers can claim weekly holiday pay if they worked 15 or more hours per week at the same workplace for 4 consecutive weeks.

whatIs.title: What is Omok?
whatIs.description: Omok (Gomoku) is a strategy board game where two players take turns placing stones to be the first to line up 5 in a row — horizontally, vertically, or diagonally — on a 19×19 grid. Black plays first. Under Korean Renju rules, Black has forbidden moves: double-three (3-3), double-four (4-4), and overline (6+). The tool supports both AI and online P2P multiplayer.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: AI Game: Choose a difficulty (Easy/Normal/Hard) and click on the board to place your stone.
Online Game: Create a room or connect directly via Peer ID to play with a friend.
Hover over the board to preview stone placement. Click to confirm.
On mobile, tap to place stones. Keyboard navigation (arrow keys + Enter) is also supported.

tips.title: Strategy Tips
items: Place your first stones near the center for both offensive and defensive advantages.
Create an open three (unblocked on both ends) — the opponent cannot block both sides at once.
Forbidden move rules (3-3/4-4/overline) only apply to Black, so White can attack freely.
Always block the opponent's three-in-a-row immediately — a four-in-a-row cannot be stopped.

items.q: What are forbidden moves?
items.a: Restrictions that apply only to Black: double-three (creating two open threes simultaneously), double-four (creating two fours simultaneously), and overline (6 or more in a row) are forbidden.

items.q: How does online multiplayer work?
items.a: Create a room to get a Peer ID, then share it with your opponent. The game connects via WebRTC P2P for real-time play with no server lag.

items.q: What's the difference between AI difficulties?
items.a: Easy uses basic pattern recognition, Normal applies intermediate strategies, and Hard uses deep Minimax search with alpha-beta pruning. Start with Easy if you're a beginner.

whatIs.title: What is the Lotto Number Generator?
whatIs.description: A tool that automatically generates Lotto 6/45 numbers and analyzes historical winning statistics. It offers multiple generation modes: fully random, frequency-based (using commonly drawn numbers), and number exclusion. Note that lotto is a pure game of chance — every number combination has an equal probability of winning (approximately 1 in 8.14 million).

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Select a number generation mode: fully random, frequency-based, or with exclusions.
2. Set how many sets to generate (1–5).
3. Click Generate to get 6 numbers from 1 to 45.
4. Check the historical statistics section for number frequency and numbers that haven't appeared recently.

items.q: Does picking frequently drawn numbers improve my odds?
items.a: No. Each lotto draw is an independent event, so past frequency has no effect on future probabilities. The frequency-based mode is provided as a fun option, not a strategy.

items.q: Does buying the same numbers every week eventually guarantee a win?
items.a: The jackpot probability is the same every week regardless of whether you repeat numbers or change them (approximately 1 in 8,145,060). There is no mathematical difference.

items.q: Are the generated numbers truly random?
items.a: Yes — the browser's crypto.getRandomValues() API is used to generate cryptographically secure random numbers.

whatIs.title: What is the Ladder Game?
whatIs.description: The ladder game (사다리타기) is a traditional Korean random-draw method in which participants descend a ladder of vertical and horizontal lines to land on a result. This online tool lets you enter participant names and outcomes, then generates a fair ladder with a seeded algorithm. It supports direct position selection, blind mode, and reveal-one-by-one mode. Perfect for deciding order, assigning duties, drawing lots, or choosing prizes — and results can be shared via URL.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Enter participant names (separated by commas or line breaks).
2. Enter the result items (prizes, penalties, etc.).
3. Choose a game mode: position selection, blind, or reveal one by one.
4. Generate the ladder and select a starting column to see the result.

tips.title: Tips
items: Higher complexity makes the game more exciting with more participants.
Use blind mode to hide results for a surprise reveal effect.
Share results via URL so others can verify the same ladder.
Use presets (lunch menu, duty assignment, etc.) for a quick start.

items.q: Are the results fair?
items.a: A seeded random algorithm generates the ladder. The same seed always produces the same result, enabling URL sharing — and no one can predict the result in advance.

items.q: How many participants can join?
items.a: Up to 10 participants. The ladder width adjusts automatically to fit the number of participants.

items.q: Can results be saved or shared?
items.a: Yes — participant names, results, and the seed are encoded into the URL, so sharing the link reproduces the same ladder. You can also save the result screen as an image.

whatIs.title: What is the Regex Extractor?
whatIs.description: The Regex Extractor is a powerful developer tool for finding, extracting, and replacing patterns in text using regular expressions. Perform tasks like log file analysis, email/phone number extraction, code refactoring, and data cleaning in an intuitive GUI. Preset patterns for common use cases — email, phone number, URL, IP address — are also included.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Enter a regex pattern or pick a preset (email, phone number, URL, etc.).
2. Set the flags: g (global), i (case-insensitive), m (multiline).
3. Paste the text you want to analyze into the input area.
4. Matches are highlighted; in extraction mode you can copy the list of matches.

items.q: Is there a Replace function?
items.a: Yes — you can switch between extraction mode and replace mode. Capture groups in the replacement pattern are referenced as $1, $2, etc.

items.q: Does it work with Korean text?
items.a: JavaScript regex supports Unicode, so it works fine with Korean text. The Korean character range is expressed as [가-힣].

items.q: What do I do when I get a regex error?
items.a: An error message is displayed for invalid patterns. Check for mismatched parentheses and properly escaped special characters (e.g., `\.`).

howItWorks.title: How it works
items: Your input becomes a standard string: a web address, WIFI:T:WPA;S:name;P:password;H:false;;, vCard 3.0, SMSTO:number:message, mailto:, tel:, geo:, and so on.
The QR version (1–40) is chosen automatically from the data length and error correction level. Each version adds 4 modules per side (21 to 177).
Reed–Solomon error correction recovers about 7% (L), 15% (M), 25% (Q), or 30% (H) damage. Higher levels make the same data use a larger version.
Maximum capacity is 2,953 bytes at version 40, level L. Korean characters take 3 bytes each in UTF-8.
Everything runs in your browser; nothing you type is sent to a server.

realWorld.title: Common uses
items: Restaurant tables: menu or ordering URL and guest Wi-Fi, printed several per A4 sheet
Business cards: a vCard QR saves name, phone, and email at once
Posters and flyers: event page URL or store location (map link)
Bookings and inquiries: SMS (SMSTO) or email QR with recipient and message prefilled

comparison.title: Static vs dynamic QR
items: Static QR (this tool): the content is stored in the QR itself. No expiry, fees, or scan limits — but it can't be changed after printing.

Dynamic QR (paid services): the QR holds the service's short link and the destination is changed on their server. You get scan stats and editable targets, but the QR may stop working when the subscription ends.
Need to change the destination later? Put a page you control into a static QR and update that page instead.
Barcodes (1D) hold short, mostly numeric data; QR codes (2D) hold URLs and any text up to a few thousand bytes.

tips.title: Making QR codes that scan
items: For print, at least 2 cm per side is recommended; make posters scanned from afar larger (a common rule of thumb is about 1/10 of the scanning distance).
Use dark dots on a light background with contrast of 4:1 or more. Inverted colors fail on some scanners.
Keep logos under 30% of the QR width and use error correction H. Never cover the three large corner squares (finder patterns).
The standard recommends a 4-module quiet zone. Graphics touching the QR lower the scan rate.
Shorter URLs make simpler codes that still read when printed small.
Before printing, print at actual size and scan with at least two devices (iPhone and Android).

whatIs.title: What is the QR Code Generator?
whatIs.description: A free QR code generator that runs in your browser with no sign-up. It supports 8 types — URL, text, Wi-Fi, contact (vCard), SMS, email, phone, and location — with custom colors, error correction, margin, and a center logo. Save as PNG (up to 2048px) or SVG, or print many on one A4 sheet. These are static QR codes: the content lives in the image, so they never expire and have no scan limits.

howToUse.title: How to use
items: Pick a type from the tabs (with a tab focused, use the left/right arrow keys).
Type your content and the preview updates instantly, with QR version, module count, and data size below it.
Under Design, adjust dot and background colors, error correction, and margin, and add a center logo if needed.
Scan the preview with your phone's camera to confirm it opens correctly.
Save as PNG (choose a size) or SVG, copy the image, or print several on A4 for tables.

items.q: Do these QR codes expire?
items.a: No. Static QR codes store the content in the image itself, so there is no expiry and no scan limit. A URL code keeps working as long as the web address does.

items.q: Is my Wi-Fi password or contact info stored on a server?
items.a: No. QR codes are generated in your browser and nothing is sent. The share link only includes URL and text types — never Wi-Fi passwords or contacts. Anyone who scans a Wi-Fi QR can see the password, so a guest network is recommended.

items.q: Will a QR code with a logo still scan?
items.a: Error correction lets it read even with the center covered. Keep the logo under 30% of the QR width, use level H, and test-scan before saving. Never cover the three large corner squares.

items.q: What size and format should I use for print?
items.a: Use SVG for design tools and print shops since it scales without blur, and 2048px PNG for documents and banners. At least 2 cm per side is recommended; print denser codes larger.

items.q: Does a Wi-Fi QR connect on iPhone?
items.a: Recent iPhone and Android camera apps recognize Wi-Fi QR codes and offer to join. Behavior can vary by device, so scan it yourself before posting.

items.q: Can I use QR codes commercially?
items.a: Yes. QR Code is a registered trademark of DENSO WAVE, which does not exercise its patent rights, so anyone can create and use them freely. Images made here have no watermark.

whatIs.title: What is the Fuel Cost Calculator?
whatIs.description: An expense calculation tool for accurately computing fuel costs and depreciation for business vehicles. Enter the vehicle type (sedan / SUV / truck), fuel type (gasoline / diesel / LPG / electric), fuel efficiency, and mileage, and it calculates the deductible business expense based on your business-use ratio. Useful for accurately claiming vehicle-related expenses on personal income tax returns and corporate tax filings.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Select the vehicle type and fuel type.
2. Enter fuel efficiency (km/L) and monthly mileage (km).
3. Enter the fuel price (₩/L) and the business-use percentage (%).
4. Monthly and annual fuel costs, along with the deductible business amount, are calculated automatically.

items.q: What vehicle expenses can be claimed as business expenses?
items.a: Self-employed individuals can claim fuel costs, insurance premiums, depreciation, and repair costs in proportion to their business-use ratio. Keeping a mileage log makes it easier to substantiate the deduction.

items.q: Does it support electric vehicles?
items.a: Yes. For electric vehicles, the calculation is based on energy consumption (kWh/100km) and electricity rates (₩/kWh), equivalent to fuel costs.

items.q: How is depreciation calculated?
items.a: Annual depreciation is calculated by dividing the vehicle's acquisition cost by its useful life (e.g., 5 years for passenger cars, 4 years for trucks), then applying the business-use ratio.

tips.title: Tips
items: Keep a detailed mileage log for business vehicles to maximize tax deductions.
Use the real-time fuel price refresh feature for accurate current-rate calculations.
Adjust the depreciation coefficient (×1.0–1.5) to reflect your vehicle's age and condition.
Compare regional fuel prices to improve the accuracy of business trip expense reports.

whatIs.title: What is Base64?
whatIs.description: Base64 is an encoding scheme that converts binary data to ASCII strings. Widely used in email attachments, web image data URIs, and API communication.

useCases.title: Use Cases
items: Embed images directly in HTML/CSS (Data URI)
Encode API authentication tokens
Email attachment transmission
Text transmission of binary data

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. On the Encode tab, enter text or a file to convert it to a Base64 string.
2. On the Decode tab, enter a Base64 string to restore the original text or file.
3. Enable the URL-safe option if you need URL-safe Base64.
4. When encoding files, you can also output in data URI format (data:image/png;base64,...).

tips.title: Tips
items: Base64-encoding an image lets you embed it directly in HTML (``) or CSS (`background-image: url(data:...)`).
JWT tokens have Base64URL-encoded Headers and Payloads — use this tool to decode them easily.
Base64 increases data size by about 33%, so consider alternatives when file size matters.

items.q: What is the difference between Base64 and Base64URL?
items.a: Base64URL replaces `+` and `/` (which have special meaning in URLs) with `-` and `_`, and omits the `=` padding. It's used in JWTs, cookies, and URL parameters.

items.q: Is Base64 a form of encryption?
items.a: No. Base64 is an encoding scheme, not encryption. Anyone can decode it, so it must not be used for security purposes.

items.q: Can it encode Korean text?
items.a: Yes — any UTF-8 encoded text, including Korean and all Unicode characters, can be converted to Base64.

urlEncoder.title: URL Encoder/Decoder
urlEncoder.description: Safely encode URLs or decode encoded URLs back to original. Includes URL parameter analysis.

whatIs.title: What is URL Encoding?
whatIs.description: URL encoding (percent-encoding) converts characters that cannot be used in URLs to %XX format. Allows safe inclusion of special characters, spaces, and non-ASCII characters in URLs.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. On the Encode tab, enter a URL or query parameter to convert it to percent-encoding (%XX).
2. On the Decode tab, enter a percent-encoded URL to restore the original string.
3. Use the URL parameter parser to break a query string into key-value pairs.
4. Choose between encodeURIComponent and encodeURI depending on what you're encoding.

tips.title: Tips
items: Use encodeURIComponent when encoding individual query parameter values (not the full URL). encodeURI is intended for the full URL.
Korean characters in URLs can be handled differently by different browsers, so always transmit them in percent-encoded form for safety.
When debugging complex API requests, use the URL parameter parser to break the query string apart and quickly identify issues.

items.q: What is the difference between encodeURI and encodeURIComponent?
items.a: encodeURI preserves URL structural characters (`:`, `/`, `?`, `#`, etc.) and encodes the rest. encodeURIComponent also encodes those structural characters, making it suitable for individual parameter values.

items.q: Should spaces be encoded as `+` or `%20`?
items.a: In URL paths, `%20` is the standard. In HTML form data (application/x-www-form-urlencoded), spaces are encoded as `+`. Check the server specification when making API requests.

items.q: How do I put a password with special characters in a URL?
items.a: Values containing special characters like passwords must be encoded with encodeURIComponent. Characters like `@`, `:`, and `/` will cause URL parsing errors if included unencoded.

hashGenerator.title: Hash Generator
hashGenerator.description: Generate hash values for text or files. Supports MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-512 and more.

whatIs.title: What is a Hash?
whatIs.description: A hash function converts arbitrary data into a fixed-length value. Same input always produces the same hash. Used for file integrity verification, password storage, and more.

algorithms.title: Algorithm Descriptions
items: MD5: 128-bit, fast but not recommended for security
SHA-1: 160-bit, for legacy compatibility
SHA-256: 256-bit, current standard recommendation
SHA-512: 512-bit, highest security level

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Enter the string you want to hash in the Text tab.
2. Select a file in the File tab to generate a hash for integrity verification.
3. Choose an algorithm: MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, or SHA-512.
4. Copy the generated hash or compare it against a reference hash for verification.

tips.title: Tips
items: After downloading a file, compare its hash against the official hash to verify it hasn't been tampered with. Especially useful for verifying software distribution packages.
MD5 and SHA-1 are cryptographically weak for password storage. Use purpose-built algorithms like bcrypt or Argon2 for hashing passwords.
SHA-256 is the most widely used secure hash algorithm today, found in Git commit IDs, SSL certificates, and more.

items.q: Is MD5 still acceptable to use?
items.a: MD5 has known collision vulnerabilities and is not suitable for cryptographic security purposes. It is still used for non-security tasks like file integrity checksums.

items.q: Does the same input always produce the same hash?
items.a: Yes — hash functions are deterministic: the same input always produces the same output. Even a single character change results in a completely different hash.

items.q: Can the original text be recovered from a hash?
items.a: Generally, no. Hash functions are one-way by design — mathematically irreversible. Add a salt to passwords to protect against rainbow table attacks.

whatIs.description: A tool that compares two pieces of text or code side by side and color-codes additions, deletions, and changes. It's useful whenever you need to quickly spot differences between two texts — code reviews, configuration file changes, document version comparisons, and more. Like git diff, it supports line-by-line and word-by-word comparison.

tips.title: Tips
items: During code reviews, paste the before and after code to quickly gauge the scope of changes.
When comparing config files (JSON, YAML, ENV), use the ignore-whitespace option to focus on actual content changes rather than formatting differences.
Paste translation files (ko.json, en.json) side by side to spot any missing keys.

items.q: What is the difference between unified view and split view?
items.a: Unified view shows changed lines sequentially. Split view places the original on the left and the modified version on the right simultaneously — split view is generally better for understanding context.

items.q: Can it handle large amounts of text?
items.a: It can compare thousands of lines within browser memory limits. For very large files, it's recommended to compare only the relevant sections.

items.q: Can differences in whitespace or line breaks be ignored?
items.a: Enabling the ignore-whitespace option filters out indentation and trailing space differences so you can focus on meaningful content changes.
