tips.title: Tips
items: `hsl()` is intuitive in CSS: H (hue 0–360), S (saturation 0–100%), L (lightness 0–100%) make it easy to adjust colors.
Screen RGB colors don't print exactly as-is. Check the CMYK values and share them with your printer for accurate print colors.
For transparency (alpha channel), use #RRGGBBAA in HEX or rgba(r,g,b,a) in CSS.

items.q: What is the difference between 3-digit and 6-digit HEX codes?
items.a: #RGB is shorthand for #RRGGBB. For example, #F0A equals #FF00AA. The shorthand is only valid when each channel is a repeated pair of identical digits.

items.q: Does CMYK guarantee accurate print colors?
items.a: CMYK values from RGB conversion are approximate due to the difference between color spaces. For exact print colors, use a standard color matching system such as Pantone.

items.q: Why does the same HEX code look different across browsers?
items.a: Differences in monitor color profiles (sRGB, Display P3, etc.) and calibration can cause the same value to appear differently. Use a color management system (CMS) for design work that requires consistency.

notes.length: Inch, foot, yard and mile use the 1959 international definitions (1 in = 2.54 cm exactly). Ja = 10/33 m (≈30.3 cm).
notes.weight: 1 lb = 0.45359237 kg (exact). A geun depends on the item: 600 g for meat, 375 g for produce. 1 don = 3.75 g, 1 nyang = 10 don.
notes.area: 1 pyeong = 400/121 m² (≈3.3058 m²). Korea has required m² legally since 2007. 1 danbo = 300 pyeong, 1 jeongbo = 3,000 pyeong.
notes.volume: US gallon (3.785 L) and UK gallon (4.546 L) differ. Doe/hop/mal follow the traditional system (1 doe ≈ 1.804 L); market measures may differ.
notes.temperature: Temperatures are converted with formulas, not factors. Absolute zero = 0 K = -273.15 °C = -459.67 °F.
notes.speed: 1 knot = 1 nautical mile per hour = 1.852 km/h. 1 mph = 1.609344 km/h.
notes.data: KB, MB, GB are powers of 1000 (SI); KiB, MiB, GiB are powers of 1024 (IEC). That is why a 1 TB disk shows as about 931 GB in Windows. 100 Mbps = 12.5 MB/s.
notes.time: 1 month = 30.436875 days and 1 year = 365.2425 days (Gregorian averages). Use the D-Day calculator for actual date differences.
notes.pressure: Tire pressure 35 psi ≈ 241 kPa ≈ 2.46 kgf/cm². 1 atm = 101,325 Pa (exact).
notes.energy: Food kcal uses the thermochemical calorie: 1 kcal = 4.184 kJ. 1 kWh = 3.6 MJ.
notes.fuel: For L/100km, lower is better (it is the reciprocal). Korea uses km/L, Europe L/100km, the US mpg.
notes.cooking: A Korean recipe cup is 200 mL, a US cup about 236.6 mL (240 mL on nutrition labels), a metric cup 250 mL. Tablespoon 15 mL, teaspoon 5 mL.
notes.traditional: Traditional Korean units are not legal units since the 1961 Measures Act, but remain common for real estate (pyeong), gold (don) and meat (geun). Tap a row to open its category.
notes.css: rem is relative to the root (html) font size, em to the parent element. In CSS 1in = 96px and 1pt = 4/3px.

items.q: How many m² is one pyeong?
items.a: 1 pyeong = 6 ja × 6 ja with 1 ja = 10/33 m, so 400/121 m² ≈ 3.3058 m². m² to pyeong is × 0.3025.

items.q: Is 1 GB 1000 MB or 1024 MB?
items.a: SI: 1 GB = 1000 MB. IEC: 1 GiB = 1024 MiB. Drive makers use 1000; Windows shows 1024-based values labeled GB.

items.q: Why do meat and vegetable geun differ?
items.a: By custom, 1 geun of meat is 600 g and of produce 375 g (1/10 gwan). It has not been a legal unit since 1961.

items.q: How do I convert L/100km to km/L?
items.a: Divide 100 by it: 5 L/100km = 20 km/L. For US mpg, multiply by 0.4251 to get km/L.

howItWorks.title: How words are split
items: At separators such as space, _, -, . and /: user_id-name → user, id, name
At a lowercase-to-uppercase change: getUserName → get, User, Name
Runs of capitals (acronyms) stay together and split before the next capitalized word: XMLHttpRequest → XML, Http, Request
Digits stick to the preceding word: Request2Parser → request2, parser / HTML5Parser → html5, parser
Scripts without case (e.g. Korean) are kept as-is and split where they meet Latin letters: 주문Id → 주문, Id

The step tools below let you chain line sorting, de-duplication, empty-line removal, find & replace (regex), full/half-width conversion and SQL IN / JS array generation.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Paste your text into the input. Multi-line input is converted line by line.
In 'Every case at once', press the copy button next to the format you need.
For cleanup, press the buttons below to stack steps. Steps run in the order you add them and can be undone or removed individually.

tips.title: Tips
items: IDs copied from a spreadsheet → Trim → Remove empty lines → Remove duplicates → SQL IN gives you a ready-made WHERE id IN (...) clause.
Paste several snake_case API field names and copy the camelCase versions in one go.
Sorting is natural, so file2 comes before file10.
Use 'Line breaks → space' for text copied from PDFs, and 'Full-width → half-width' for ＡＢＣ１２３ from CJK documents.
With regex on (m flag), replacing ^ with '- ' turns every line into a bullet.

items.q: What is the difference between camelCase and PascalCase?
items.a: camelCase starts lowercase and capitalizes later words (myVariable). PascalCase capitalizes every word (MyClass). Variables and functions usually use camelCase; classes and components use PascalCase.

items.q: Does it work with Korean text?
items.a: Korean has no letter case, so characters are kept and only word separators change (사용자 이름 → 사용자_이름). Sorting follows Korean order, and character reversal works on whole graphemes so Hangul and emoji never break. For initial-consonant extraction or romanization, use the Korean initials / jamo / romanization tool.

items.q: What rules does Title Case follow?
items.a: Every word is capitalized except articles, short prepositions and conjunctions (a, an, the, and, or, of, to, in, on, at…) that are neither the first nor the last word. Words that already mix cases, like NASA or iPhone, are preserved unless most of the line is in capitals.

items.q: How are names with acronyms and numbers split?
items.a: XMLHttpRequest2Parser is split into XML / Http / Request2 / Parser, so snake_case gives xml_http_request2_parser. Digits stay attached to the preceding word.

items.q: Is my text sent to a server?
items.a: No. Everything runs in your browser, and shared links contain only the names of the selected steps, never your text.

howItWorks.title: How the Check Digit Works
items: The last digit of EAN-13, EAN-8, UPC-A and ITF-14 is a check digit computed from the others, so a single misread digit is rejected by the scanner.
Formula: starting from the digit just left of the check digit, multiply by 3, 1, 3, 1… moving left, add everything up, and subtract (sum mod 10) from 10. If the remainder is 0, the check digit is 0.
CODE128 embeds its own checksum character automatically, so you never add a check digit yourself.
2D codes like QR are not generated here. Use the QR code generator.

items: Store and warehouse inventory: CODE128 labels (e.g. A-0001) scanned at receiving and shipping

Shipping cartons: ITF-14 printed on the outside of the box

comparison.title: Format Comparison
items: CODE128 — letters, digits and symbols; the most compact for the same content. Default for internal use
CODE39 — uppercase, digits and a few symbols; longer than CODE128 for the same content. Legacy compatibility
EAN-13 — 13 digits, the global retail standard (Korea 880). Retail use requires an issued GS1 number
EAN-8 — 8 digits, for packages too small for EAN-13 (separate application to GS1 Korea)
UPC-A — 12 digits, US/Canada retail. North American scanners also read EAN-13, so Korean products usually keep EAN-13
ITF-14 — 14 digits, for cartons and other logistics units. Thick bars survive rough printing surfaces

Save a single barcode as PNG or SVG, or print many (or a serial range) on A4 label sheets. Everything runs in your browser; nothing is sent to a server.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Pick a format. Use CODE128 for internal inventory and EAN-13 (with an issued number) for retail products.
Enter one value, paste two columns (code, name) from Excel for many, or generate a serial range (prefix + start + count).
Adjust bar width, height, margin, font size and colors. You'll be warned if contrast is too low.

items.q: Can I make my own barcode and sell products with it?
items.a: Internal-use barcodes are fine, but EAN-13 numbers for retail (supermarkets, convenience stores, online malls) must be built from a company prefix issued by GS1 Korea. A made-up 880 number may collide with another company's product and can't be used for listing or distribution. Check fees at gs1kr.org.

items.q: How do I add the EAN-13 check digit?
items.a: Enter only the first 12 digits and the 13th is calculated for you. If you enter 13 digits, the last digit is verified and, if wrong, the correct number is shown with a Fix button.

items.q: Does starting with 880 mean made in Korea?
items.a: No. 880 means the number was issued by GS1 Korea, not the country of origin. Products made abroad by Korean companies can also start with 880.

items.q: Can a barcode contain Korean text?
items.a: 1D barcodes such as CODE128 hold only letters, digits and symbols. Print Korean product names as captions (second column in Bulk mode) under the barcode, or use a QR code if the text itself must be encoded.

items.q: My labels are misaligned when printed.
items.a: Set scale to Actual size (100%), margins to None and disable headers/footers in the print dialog. If it's still off, enter the top margin, side margin and gaps from your label pack, test on plain paper and adjust in 1 mm steps.

items.q: Should I save as SVG or PNG?
items.a: Use SVG for print and design tools (Illustrator, Figma), since it stays sharp at any size; use PNG for documents, spreadsheets and shop images. PNG is saved at 3× the preview resolution.

manager.title: Password managers & two-factor authentication
items: Store passwords in a password manager (built into your browser/phone, or Bitwarden, 1Password, KeePass, etc.) so you never have to memorize long random passwords.
You only need to remember the manager's master password — make that one a long passphrase.
Turn on two-factor authentication for important accounts (email, banking, portals). Authenticator apps or passkeys are safer than SMS.
Don't keep passwords in notes apps, messengers or screenshots.

nist.title: NIST SP 800-63B in brief
items: Services using a password as the only factor should require at least 15 characters; at least 8 when combined with multi-factor authentication.
Allow a maximum length of at least 64 characters, including spaces and Unicode.
Don't impose composition rules ("mix upper, lower, digits, symbols") — length and blocking breached passwords work better.
Don't require periodic password changes; require a change when there is evidence of compromise.
Check new passwords against lists of breached and common passwords, and allow pasting and password managers.
Many Korean sites still enforce composition rules, so presets are provided above.

tips.title: Password principles
items: Length matters most: 16+ characters for random strings, 6+ words for passphrases.
Use a different password for every site. One leak otherwise exposes every account sharing it (credential stuffing).
Birthdays, phone numbers, names, years and keyboard patterns (qwer1234) are the first things attackers try.
Rather than changing passwords on a schedule, change them immediately when a leak is suspected.
This generator uses the browser's cryptographic randomness (crypto.getRandomValues) without bias and never stores or sends results.

passphrase.title: Why passphrases work
items: Randomly chosen words joined together are long yet easy to remember, e.g. Ocean-Table-Frost-Lunar-Pilot-Grape.
The strength only holds when words are picked at random. Sentences, lyrics or proverbs you pick yourself are weak.
This tool's list has 819 words, about 9.7 bits per word: 6 words ≈ 58 bits, 8 words ≈ 77 bits.
If a site requires digits and symbols, turn on "Add one digit" and use the hyphen separator.

whatIs.title: What is the Password Generator?
whatIs.description: A security tool that generates strong, secure passwords and easy-to-remember passphrases. It provides random passwords combining upper/lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters, as well as EFF wordlist-based passphrases. A password strength analyzer shows the security level of the generated password. All processing happens entirely in the browser — nothing is sent to a server.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Select the mode: random characters or passphrase.
2. Set the length and character types to include (uppercase, lowercase, numbers, special characters).
3. Click Generate to create a cryptographically secure password.
4. Copy it to your clipboard and save it in a password manager.

items.q: Are generated passwords stored or sent anywhere?
items.a: No. They are created on your device with the Web Crypto API (crypto.getRandomValues) and are never sent to a server or saved to localStorage. Share links (URL) only contain settings such as length and character types.

items.q: Is it truly random?
items.a: It uses cryptographic randomness and discards out-of-range values so no character is favored by modulo bias. Results missing a required character type are regenerated entirely, so digits and symbols don't cluster in particular positions.

items.q: How are entropy and crack time calculated?
items.a: Entropy is log2 of the number of passwords the current settings can produce (accounting for required types and excluded characters). Crack time is the average time to try half of them at 10 billion guesses per second offline. Real-world time depends heavily on the site's hashing and login rate limits.

items.q: How long should my password be?
items.a: 16+ characters for random passwords (about 100 bits with all character types) or 6+ words for passphrases. If a site caps the length (e.g. 8–16), use the longest length allowed.

items.q: Is it safe to type my password into the strength checker?
items.a: Input is analyzed only on this page and is never stored or sent. If you're still worried, test an example with a similar shape instead of your real password.

whatIs.description: A single tool that covers D-Day countdown to a specific date, calculating the difference between two dates, and adding or subtracting days from a date. Handles everything date-related — exam prep, travel planning, event coordination, contract expiry tracking, and more. Includes Korean public holiday data and supports business day calculations.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: On the D-Day tab, enter a name and date or tap a preset (CSAT, Seollal, Chuseok, Christmas) to see days left plus business days, weekends and holidays.
Save several D-Days and pin one so it opens first on your next visit.
On the Anniversary tab, enter the day you started dating, got married or your baby was born to see 100-day and yearly milestones.
Use Date difference and Add/Subtract for the span between two dates or the date N (business) days later.
Share, save the image or copy the link; whoever opens it sees the same D-Day.

tips.title: Tips
items: Use business day mode for calculating contract review periods or legal filing deadlines.
Register important dates — probation end dates, visa expiry, insurance renewal — as D-Days and bookmark them for easy reference.
Share a project deadline countdown with your team using the URL sharing feature.

items.q: How are D-1 and D-Day defined?
items.a: The target date itself is D-Day, the day before is D-1 and the day after is D+1. Today is computed in Korea Standard Time. Couple anniversaries often count the first day as day 1, so the Anniversary tab lets you choose.

items.q: Which years of Korean holidays are supported?
items.a: 2024-2030, including Seollal/Chuseok, substitute holidays, Labor Day and Constitution Day (public holidays since 2026), election days and temporary holidays. New temporary holidays are added after they are designated.

items.q: Does it handle February 29?
items.a: Yes. One year after Feb 29 is Feb 28, and one month after Jan 31 is the last day of February.

whatIs.title: What is the percentage calculator?
whatIs.description: It answers the eight most common percent questions at once: B% of A, ratio, percent change, sale price, original price from a sale price, stacked discounts, percentage points, and VAT-inclusive to net. No mode switching: change a number and every card updates, each with its formula and a copy button.

howToUse.title: How to use
items: 1. Type a question in the top box, like '15% of 50000', '30000->40000' or '120000 30% off'. The matching card fills in and the answer appears right away.
2. Or type numbers directly into any card. Korean units like 5만 work too.
3. Choose decimal places (0-4) and Korean unit display, and toggle 'Show formula' to see the math.
4. Copy gives a plain number without commas, and the page URL reproduces your inputs when shared.

tips.title: Tips
items: To get the net amount from a VAT-inclusive price, divide by 1.1. That is not the same as subtracting 10% (× 0.9).
Reverse discount: 70,000 after 30% off means an original price of 70,000 ÷ 0.7 = 100,000.
For investment returns or raises, put the before and after values into the percent change card.
Differences between rates (interest, approval ratings) are best stated in percentage points.

items.q: Is a 20% discount followed by a 10% discount the same as 30% off?
items.a: No. 20% off then 10% off equals 0.8 × 0.9 = 0.72, which is a 28% discount. Sequential percentage discounts do not simply add up.

items.q: What is the difference between percentage points (%p) and percent (%)?
items.a: Going from 3% to 5% is a '2 percentage point increase' but also roughly a '67% increase.' %p expresses the absolute difference; % expresses the relative change.

items.q: How are decimal places handled?
items.a: Results are displayed to two decimal places by default. You can change the decimal precision setting if you need more precise results.

whatIs.title: What is the Age Calculator?
whatIs.description: Enter your date of birth to instantly see your international age (만 나이), Korean counting age (세는 나이), calendar-year age (연 나이), Chinese zodiac sign (12 animals), and star sign, all at once. Following the 2023 Civil Act amendment, the international age standard is now official in Korean public and legal contexts, making accurate age calculation essential for employment, insurance, medical care, and more.

tips.title: Tips
items: Since June 2023, the international age (만 나이) is the official standard for legal and public matters in Korea. Be careful not to confuse it with the traditional Korean counting age.
Use this calculator to accurately verify insurance product age criteria, mandatory retirement age (age 60), and National Pension eligibility ages (63–65).
Helpful for checking age-based policy eligibility — such as minor status (under 19) or 'youth' criteria (19–34) as defined by various government programs.

items.q: What is the difference between international age and Korean counting age?
items.a: International age (만 나이) increments by 1 after each birthday — the global standard. Korean counting age (세는 나이) starts at 1 at birth and adds 1 on every January 1st.

items.q: What is calendar-year age (연 나이)?
items.a: Current year minus birth year (e.g., 2026 - 2000 = 26). Even after the 2023 unification, the Juvenile Protection Act (alcohol/tobacco), Military Service Act and civil-service exam rules use it.

items.q: What is the international age if my birthday hasn't passed yet this year?
items.a: If your birthday hasn't occurred yet this year, your international age is (current year − birth year − 1). It increases by 1 on your birthday.

items.q: When do Feb 29 babies get older in common years?
items.a: Under the Civil Act (Art. 158, 160(3)) the period ends on the last day of February, so the age increases on March 1.

items.q: How are lunar birthdays calculated?
items.a: Each year the lunar month/day is converted to the solar calendar using the KASI almanac. Leap-month births use the regular month in years without that leap month; 30th-day births use the 29th in short months. International age uses the actual (solar) birth date.

items.q: Which scale should I use — 4.5 or 4.0?

howItWorks.title: How the draw works
items: The list is split by new lines and commas; a trailing "x number" is read as the ticket count (weight).
The seed string is hashed (cyrb128) to initialize a random generator (sfc32). The same seed always yields the same sequence.
One ticket is drawn from all remaining tickets, then all of that person's tickets are removed, repeated for each winner (weighted sampling without replacement).
With an empty seed, an unpredictable seed is created with crypto.getRandomValues.
Winners come out in draw order, so you can assign prizes from 1st place down.

whatIs.title: What is Random Picker?
whatIs.description: A draw tool for picking winners from a list: comment giveaways, group chat prizes, live stream viewer draws. It draws several winners without duplicates and supports ticket weights and excluding previous winners. Every draw records a seed and time and produces a verification link so participants can confirm they get the same result.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Paste the entrant list. New lines or commas separate names and the count updates instantly.
2. Choose the number of winners. Give extra chances with "Alex x3".
3. Press Draw winners: names spin and winners are revealed one by one. Use presentation mode on a big screen for live events.
4. Copy the announcement for your chat, or share the result card image and verification link.
5. For several prizes, keep "Exclude previous winners" on and draw another round.

tips.title: Tips
items: Publish the entrant list before the draw to avoid disputes about missing or added names.
Announce a seed in advance (e.g. the event date) and draw with it to prove the host could not choose the result.
Duplicates from pasting the list several times are cleaned up by duplicate removal. Turn it off to give one chance per comment.
Devices set to reduce motion, or "Show results instantly", skip the animation.

items.q: Is the draw really fair?
items.a: With an empty seed, an unpredictable seed is created with the Web Crypto API crypto.getRandomValues(), and every entrant gets equal odds per ticket. Anyone can recompute the same result with the verification link.

items.q: Can the same person win twice?
items.a: No. Within one draw each name wins at most once. With "Exclude previous winners" on, winners of earlier rounds are not drawn again.

items.q: Can I save or share results?
items.a: Draw history is saved in this browser, and you can share via the copied announcement, the result card image or the verification link. The link holds the list, winner count and seed, so opening it recomputes the same result.

howToUse.title: How to use
items: 1. On the Timer tab, press 1, 3, 5, 10, 15 or 30 min to start right away, or enter hours, minutes and seconds and press Start (or Enter).
2. While running, use +1 min to extend, Space to pause/resume and R to reset. The remaining time also shows in the browser tab title.
3. Press Fullscreen (F) for big digits. Space and R keep working during a class or talk; press Esc to exit.
4. On the Stopwatch tab, press Lap (L) to record splits. You'll see each split, the fastest and slowest laps and the average, and can copy them as CSV.
5. Copy the share link to get an address with the same timer ready (e.g. /timer/?m=10). Because of autoplay rules, the person opening the link presses Start.

tips.title: Tips
items: Bookmark a share link to open a '10-minute timer' in one click. Your last duration and alert settings are remembered in this browser.
For classes and meetings, turn on fullscreen and 'Keep screen on' so the laptop display doesn't go dark.
If you'll be working in another tab, enable browser notifications so a pop-up appears along with the sound.
To alternate focus and breaks use the Pomodoro timer; for per-section talk timing use the presentation timer.

items.q: Is it still accurate in a background tab?
items.a: Yes. Instead of subtracting one every second, the timer stores the end time and compares it with the current time, so browser throttling of background tabs can't make it drift. The alarm is also scheduled for the end time and fires within about a second. If the computer goes to sleep the browser pauses, and the timer finishes as soon as it wakes.

items.q: Why is there no sound?
items.a: Browsers block audio until you interact with the page (autoplay policy). The timer unlocks sound when you press Start, which is also why a shared link never starts on its own. Try 'Test sound'; if you hear nothing, check tab mute, system volume and your phone's silent mode (on iPhone, the silent switch mutes web audio).

items.q: How do I use fullscreen?
items.a: Press the Fullscreen button or F to fill the screen with the digits. Space (start/pause) and R (reset) still work, and Esc or F exits. On browsers without fullscreen support, such as Safari on iPhone, a large overlay covers the page instead.

items.q: What happens if I close the browser?
items.a: Closing the tab or browser stops a running timer. Only your last duration and alert settings are saved on this device, so you can start the same time again right away.

items.q: Can I set more than an hour?
items.a: Yes, up to 99 hours 59 minutes 59 seconds. Minutes or seconds over 60 are added up automatically (e.g. 90 minutes = 1 hour 30 minutes).

baseConverter.title: Base Converter
baseConverter.description: Convert binary, octal, decimal, hex and any base 2–36 at once — with fractions, two's complement, IEEE 754 and step-by-step work

howItWorks.title: How it works
items: Decimal → base N: divide the integer part by N repeatedly and read remainders bottom-up; multiply the fraction by N repeatedly and read integer parts top-down.
Base N → decimal: sum each digit × N^position. The first place after the point is N^-1.
Binary ↔ hex converts directly by grouping 4 bits, binary ↔ octal by grouping 3 bits.
Two's complement of a negative number = invert all bits (ones' complement) + 1. The n-bit range is −2^(n−1) to 2^(n−1)−1.
IEEE 754 float32 = 1 sign + 8 exponent (bias 127) + 23 mantissa bits; float64 = 1 + 11 (bias 1023) + 52 bits.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Type in any base field and all others update instantly. Negative numbers (-42), fractions (13.625), prefixes (0xFF, 0b1010) and separators (1010_1101) are accepted
'Step-by-step' shows the division, place-value and grouping methods for exams and classes
Pick 8/16/32/64 bits under 'Signed integers' to see two's complement, ones' complement, sign-magnitude and overflow; click bits to change the value
Enter a real number in the IEEE 754 section to see the float32/float64 sign, exponent, mantissa and exact stored value
Your inputs are saved in the page URL, so sharing the link opens the same view

tips.title: Notes
items: Binary: the 0-and-1 system computers actually use. One hex digit = 4 bits
Octal: used for Unix file permissions (chmod 755 = rwxr-xr-x)
Hexadecimal: used for color codes (#FF0000), memory addresses and byte dumps
Decimal 0.1 repeats forever in binary as 0.0(0011) — the source of floating-point error
The 8-bit two's complement range is −128 to 127; −128 cannot be written in ones' complement or sign-magnitude

whatIs.title: What is the Number Base Converter?
whatIs.description: A real-time converter between binary, octal, decimal, hexadecimal and any base from 2 to 36. It converts arbitrarily large integers and fractions (including repeating fractions) exactly, and shows two's/ones' complement and sign-magnitude, the IEEE 754 floating-point layout, by-hand solution steps and UTF-8 bytes of text on one screen.

items.q: Why is hexadecimal so common in computing?
items.a: One hex digit maps exactly to 4 binary bits, so memory addresses, color codes and hash values stay short. It uses digits 0–9 and letters A–F (10–15).

items.q: Are negative numbers and fractions supported?
items.a: Yes. Prefix a minus sign (-42) for negatives, and see 8–64-bit two's complement, ones' complement and sign-magnitude under 'Signed integers'. Fractions like 13.625 convert too; values that never terminate in binary, like 0.1, show the repeating part in parentheses: 0.0(0011).

items.q: How do I compute two's complement?
items.a: Invert every bit of the positive binary value (ones' complement), then add 1. e.g. 8-bit 5 = 00000101 → inverted 11111010 → +1 = 11111011 = −5. Try it in the bit view.

items.q: Why is 0.1 + 0.2 not 0.3?
items.a: 0.1 repeats forever in binary, so float64 stores the nearest value (0.1000000000000000055…). Enter 0.1 in the IEEE 754 section to see the exact stored value.

items.q: Can I convert an IP address to binary?
items.a: Enter each octet (0–255) into the decimal field to get its 8-bit binary form. e.g. 192 → 11000000, 168 → 10101000.

Use the pin icon to keep a note on top and the trash icon to delete. Deleted by mistake? Tap Undo in the message at the bottom

whatIs.title: What is the Notepad?
whatIs.description: A browser notepad that works instantly with no login or install. Notes are auto-saved only in this device's browser (localStorage) and never sent to a server. Manage multiple notes in a list, find & replace, count characters, and back up or restore everything. Handy for work notes, to-do lists, drafts, and code snippets.

items.q: Where are my notes stored?
items.a: In this browser's localStorage on this device. Nothing is sent to a server, so no one else can see them. Clearing the browser's site data deletes them, so back up anything important.

items.q: Can I see my notes on another device?
items.a: There is no automatic sync. Download a full backup (JSON) and use Import on the other device. If the same note exists in both, the more recently edited version is kept.

items.q: Is there a limit on notes or size?
items.a: You can store any number of notes up to the browser's storage quota (usually around 5 MB). Hundreds of plain-text notes fit easily, and you'll see a warning if storage runs out.

items.q: I deleted a note by mistake.
items.a: Tap Undo in the message that appears at the bottom right after deleting or replacing all. Once the message is gone it can't be undone, so restore from a backup file if you have one.

note.maturity: Tax at maturity: each row assumes the product matures at that point and subtracts tax on cumulative interest. Early termination of a real deposit pays a lower early-withdrawal rate.
note.yearly: Yearly tax: each year's interest is taxed and the remainder reinvested.

method.title: How it is calculated
items: Lump sum: principal × (1 + rate ÷ n)^(n × years), where n is the number of compounding periods a year (1, 2, 4, 12 or 365). Same as Excel =FV(rate/n, n×years, 0, -principal).

Monthly deposits: the rate is converted to an equivalent monthly rate (1 + rate ÷ n)^(n ÷ 12) − 1 and compounded monthly. Same as Excel =FV(monthly rate, months, -deposit, -principal, 1) (start of month; 0 for end).

Interest tax: standard 15.4% (14% income tax + 1.4% local tax), preferential 9.5% (9% + 0.5% special rural tax), tax-free 0%. Interest and dividend income above 20 million KRW a year is taxed with other income; this calculator applies the 15.4% flat rate only.
Annualized return: the annual rate (IRR) that matches your cash flows to the after-tax amount. For monthly deposits, later deposits compound for less time, so 'total return ÷ years' understates it.
Real value = after-tax amount ÷ (1 + inflation)^years; real return = (1 + annualized return) ÷ (1 + inflation) − 1 (Fisher equation).
Bank products truncate fractions and count days, so results may differ by a few to a few hundred won. Stock and fund returns vary year to year; results here assume the same return every year.

compoundCalculator.title: Compound Interest Calculator
compoundCalculator.description: Calculate lump-sum and monthly compound interest after tax, solve for a savings goal, and see the Rule of 72, simple vs compound and inflation-adjusted real returns in one place.

howItWorks.title: How it works
items: Lump sum future value = principal × (1 + r ÷ n)^(n × t), with r the annual rate, n compounding periods per year and t years.
10,000,000 KRW at 5% compounded yearly for 10 years becomes 16,288,946 KRW (6,288,946 interest before tax); simple interest would be 5,000,000.
At the same 5% compounded monthly, the effective annual rate is 5.12% and the result is 16,470,095 KRW.
With monthly deposits each payment compounds for its remaining time. 500,000 KRW a month at 5% monthly for 10 years (start of month) gives 60,000,000 principal and 17,964,644 pre-tax interest.

Korean deposits withhold 15.4% on total interest at maturity, so the 10M example pays 15,320,449 KRW after tax. If interest is paid and taxed every year and only the rest reinvested, you get 15,133,082 KRW.

comparison.title: Simple vs compound, lump sum vs monthly
items: Simple vs compound: small difference over 1–2 years, growing with time. 10M KRW at 5% for 10 years: 5.0M simple vs 6.29M compound interest.
Yearly vs monthly compounding: at the same stated rate, monthly earns slightly more, especially at higher rates and longer periods (12% → 12.68% effective).
Lump sum vs monthly: with the same total principal, monthly deposits earn less because later money compounds for less time, but you can start without savings and spread market entry.
Tax at maturity vs every year: paying tax later lets that money compound too. That is why tax-deferred accounts (pension savings, IRP, ISA) help long-term investors.

howToUse.title: How to use
items: Pick lump sum, monthly deposits or goal planner at the top.
Enter the principal (or monthly deposit), annual rate and period in years or months.
Choose the compounding frequency and deposit timing. Bank savings plans usually use start-of-month deposits.
Choose the interest tax and when it is withheld; the after-tax amount updates instantly.
Review the Rule of 72, simple vs compound, inflation-adjusted value, scenarios and the yearly table, then share as a link or image.

tips.title: Making compounding work
items: Time matters most. Starting 10 years earlier with the same monthly amount changes the result dramatically; check it with scenarios.
Compare bank products by after-tax amount or after-tax annualized return, not just the stated rate.
Stock and fund returns vary each year. Use conservative expected returns and check the low scenarios too.
If your return is below inflation, your balance grows but your purchasing power shrinks. Check the real return.

whatIs.title: What is this calculator?
whatIs.description: Compound interest earns interest on interest. This calculator covers lump sums, monthly deposits and a goal planner (how much per month, or what return, to reach a target), and applies Korean interest tax (15.4%, 9.5% or tax-free) and its timing (once at maturity or every year) so you see what you actually receive.

items.q: What is the Rule of 72?
items.a: Divide 72 by the annual return (%) to estimate the years needed to double your money: 6% → 12 years (11.9 exactly), 8% → 9 years. It works best around 6–10%; at 2% (36 vs 35 years) or 20% (3.6 vs 3.8) the error grows. This calculator shows the estimate, the exact value (ln 2 ÷ ln(1 + effective rate)) and the after-tax value.

items.q: Is tax deducted from compound interest every year?
items.a: Korean compound deposits and savings usually withhold tax once at maturity on the total interest (15.4% standard), so pre-tax interest keeps compounding. Products that pay interest yearly or funds taxed every year withhold tax annually and reinvest only the rest, so you receive a little less. Compare both under 'When tax is withheld'.

items.q: How much difference does monthly compounding make?
items.a: At the same stated rate, monthly compounding earns more: 5% becomes 5.12% effective, 12% becomes 12.68%. 10M KRW at 5% for 10 years: 16,288,946 yearly vs 16,470,095 monthly (pre-tax), about 180,000 KRW more.

items.q: How much must I save monthly to have 100 million KRW in 10 years?
items.a: At 5% compounded monthly, start-of-month deposits and 15.4% tax at maturity, about 664,911 KRW a month (641,317 tax-free). Use the goal planner to try other targets, periods and rates, or switch to 'Required return' if your monthly amount is fixed.

items.q: How is the real (inflation-adjusted) return calculated?
items.a: By the Fisher equation: real return = (1 + nominal) ÷ (1 + inflation) − 1. 'Nominal minus inflation' is an approximation. The calculator applies it to the after-tax annualized return and also shows the final amount in today's money (after-tax amount ÷ (1 + inflation)^years).

items.q: Why is the total return of monthly deposits lower than expected?
items.a: The last deposits barely compound, so total interest ÷ total principal is far below rate × years. The after-tax annualized return (IRR) reflects the timing of your deposits.

items.q: Why does my bank app show a slightly different amount?
items.a: Banks truncate fractions of a won, count interest by days, and apply product-specific bonus or early-termination rates, so results can differ by a few to a few hundred won. Interest and dividend income over 20 million KRW a year is subject to comprehensive taxation and may be taxed more.

electricityCalculator.title: Electricity Bill Calculator
electricityCalculator.description: Estimate this month's electricity bill from your kWh usage or appliance hours. Based on KEPCO residential progressive rates (Q4 2026), with tier breakdown, extra A/C cost and month-over-month comparison.

tiers.title: Where you are in the tiers

savingTips.title: How to lower your bill
items: If you are just above a tier boundary (200/400 kWh, or 300/450 kWh in July–August), a small cut avoids the higher unit rate and base fee.
For inverter air conditioners, keeping a moderate setting (around 26°C) is usually better than switching on and off repeatedly. Clean filters and shade the outdoor unit.
Heating appliances such as electric blankets, heaters and dryers draw a lot of power, so trimming their hours cuts usage quickly.
Switch off standby power with power strips, and replace old fridges and lighting with efficient models.
Check real-time usage in the KEPCO ON app and see whether you can join the energy cashback program.

structure.title: What makes up your bill
items: Base fee by tier: 910 / 1,600 / 7,300 KRW (high voltage 730 / 1,260 / 6,060).
Energy charge per tier: low voltage 120.0 / 214.6 / 307.3 KRW/kWh, high voltage 105.0 / 174.0 / 242.3.
Climate & environment charge: usage × 9.0 KRW.
Fuel cost adjustment: usage × quarterly rate; frozen at the +5.0 KRW cap for Q4 2026.
Plus 10% VAT and the 2.7% Electric Power Industry Fund.

calcOrder.title: Calculation order (same as the bill)
items: Electricity charge = base + energy + climate + fuel adjustment (each truncated to the won)
VAT = charge × 10% (rounded)
Fund = charge × 2.7% (truncated to 10 won)
Bill = total truncated to 10 won
Check: August 2024 (fund 3.2%), summer 363 kWh gives 63,610 KRW, matching KEPCO's reported household average that month.

welfare.title: Welfare discounts
items: Severe disability, veterans, basic livelihood/medical recipients: 16,000 KRW/month cap (20,000 Jun–Aug)
Basic housing/education: 10,000 (12,000 Jun–Aug); near-poverty: 8,000 (10,000 Jun–Aug)
Large families (5+), 3+ children, newborn households (3 years): 30%, 16,000 cap; life-support equipment: 30%
Apply via KEPCO (123) or KEPCO ON. This calculator subtracts the discount before VAT and the fund (approximation).

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Enter monthly electricity usage in kWh (check your bill)
Select the current season (summer/winter have different tiers)
The estimated bill is calculated based on progressive rates

rateInfo.title: Rate Structure
items: Korean residential electricity uses progressive pricing tiers
Summer (Jul-Aug) and winter (Dec-Feb) have adjusted tier ranges
Bill consists of base fee + usage fee + climate fee + fuel adjustment
VAT (10%) and Electric Industry Fund (3.7%) are added

whatIs.title: What is the Electricity Bill Calculator?
whatIs.description: A tool that calculates monthly electricity costs based on Korea Electric Power Corporation (KEPCO)'s progressive residential tariff system. It reflects all items appearing on an actual bill: basic charge, energy charge, climate environment charge, fuel cost adjustment, VAT, and the electricity industry promotion levy. Use it to estimate your bill before it arrives, or to simulate the cost of additional appliances like air conditioners or electric heaters.

tips.title: Tips to Reduce Your Electricity Bill
items: Know your progressive tiers (Tier 1: ≤200 kWh, Tier 2: ≤400 kWh). If you're near a tier boundary, cutting usage slightly can save a disproportionately large amount.
Summer (Jul–Aug) and winter (Dec–Feb) seasons have adjusted tier limits. Track your usage separately during these months to avoid unexpected jumps.
Combine air conditioning with a fan or circulator, adjust your refrigerator temperature, and eliminate standby power to save 10–30 kWh per month.
Installing a small rooftop solar panel reduces your net usage, potentially dropping you into a lower progressive tier for significant savings.

items.q: What are the progressive tiers?
items.a: For residential low voltage outside summer: up to 200 kWh is tier 1 (120.0 KRW/kWh), 201–400 kWh tier 2 (214.6), over 400 kWh tier 3 (307.3). In July–August the boundaries widen to 300/450 kWh. The base fee is 910, 1,600 or 7,300 KRW by tier (tariff effective 2023-11-09).

items.q: How much more if I run the A/C a few more hours a day?
items.a: A 1 kW air conditioner running 4 more hours a day for 30 days adds about 120 kWh. The extra cost depends on which tier that usage falls into, so use the A/C calculator above. Inverter units often draw less than their rated power on average.

items.q: What is the super-user rate?
items.a: In summer (Jul–Aug) and winter (Dec–Feb), usage above 1,000 kWh a month is charged 736.2 KRW/kWh (593.3 for high voltage). It does not apply in other months.

items.q: How are VAT and the fund calculated?
items.a: VAT is 10% of the electricity charge (rounded to the won) and the Electric Power Industry Fund is 2.7% (truncated to 10 won). The fund rate fell from 3.7% to 3.2% in July 2024 and to 2.7% in July 2025. The final bill is truncated to 10 won.

items.q: Why might my real bill differ?
items.a: If your meter is read mid-month, months that span a season change are prorated by days. Apartment bills depend on the complex's contract type. TV license fees and the extra deduction for welfare households using 200 kWh or less are not included. Check the KEPCO ON app or call 123 for the exact amount.

items.q: Is the essential-use deduction still available?
items.a: It was abolished for general households. It remains only as an additional reduction for welfare-discount households using 200 kWh or less a month.

terms.title: Key terms
items: Screen resolution (CSS pixels): screen.width × screen.height as reported by the browser. Layouts and media queries use this unit.
Physical pixels: screen resolution × DPR. If Windows at 150% shows 1280 × 720, the panel is about 1920 × 1080.
DPR (device pixel ratio): physical pixels per CSS pixel. Retina/high-res phones are 2–3; a typical FHD monitor at 100% is 1.
Viewport: the inner size of the browser window including scrollbars (innerWidth × innerHeight). Responsive breakpoints are based on it.
PPI: pixels per inch. Roughly 90–110 for desktop monitors, 140–230 for laptops, 400+ for smartphones.

whatIs.title: What is the screen resolution checker?
whatIs.description: Shows your screen resolution (CSS pixels), physical pixels, browser viewport, device pixel ratio (DPR), aspect ratio, estimated refresh rate, HDR/color gamut and input type (touch/mouse) at a glance. It also shows the active Tailwind/Bootstrap breakpoint, a PPI calculator and a reference table of common device resolutions. Everything is read in your browser and never sent to a server.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Open the page — the blue card at the top shows your screen resolution, physical pixels, viewport and DPR immediately.
2. Resize the window or rotate the device to see the viewport and breakpoints update in real time.
3. For your monitor's PPI, press 'Use my physical pixels' in the PPI calculator and enter the diagonal from the product spec.
4. For bug reports or support tickets, use 'Copy all (text)' or 'Copy JSON' and paste the environment info.

tips.title: Pro Tips
items: If Windows shows a smaller resolution than your monitor's spec, display scaling (125%, 150%) is the reason. The 'physical pixels' value is close to the panel resolution.
Browser zoom changes DPR and resolution. Reset to 100% with Ctrl+0 and refresh for an accurate reading.
On screens with DPR 2 or higher, serve images/icons at 2x (srcset, SVG) to avoid blurriness.
The refresh rate is an estimate. Power saving or background tabs can lower it — use 'Re-measure refresh rate' to check again.

items.q: My monitor is 1920×1080, so why does it show 1280×720 or 1536×864?
items.a: Browsers report resolution in CSS pixels. With 150% display scaling, 1920 ÷ 1.5 = 1280; at 125% it is 1536. DPR then reads 1.5 or 1.25, and resolution × DPR = physical pixels.

items.q: What is the difference between screen resolution and viewport size?
items.a: Screen resolution is the whole display; the viewport is the inside of the browser window, excluding the address bar, tabs and taskbar. Responsive layouts change based on viewport width.

items.q: Can it tell my exact refresh rate and screen size in inches?
items.a: No. Browsers don't expose refresh rate or physical size. The refresh rate is estimated from frame intervals, and inch-based size needs the diagonal from your product spec entered into the PPI calculator.

items.q: Is my device information sent to any server?
items.a: No. All information is read locally by JavaScript in your browser and is never transmitted or stored.

items.q: Why do some copied emojis look different or broken in other apps?
items.a: Emojis follow the Unicode standard, but Apple, Google, Samsung and Microsoft draw them differently. If the receiving OS or app does not support an emoji, it may show an empty box (□) or a separate skin-tone swatch.

whatIs.title: What is the Lunar-Solar Date Converter?
whatIs.description: A tool that converts between the Korean lunar calendar (lunisolar calendar) and the Gregorian solar calendar in both directions. Useful for finding the solar date of traditionally observed events like birthdays, memorial days, and Korean holidays (Seollal, Chuseok) that are tracked by the lunar calendar.

items.q: Why does the same lunar date fall on a different solar date each year?
items.a: The lunar calendar is based on the moon's cycle (~29.5 days), giving it about 354 days per year — 11 days shorter than the solar year. A leap month (윤달) is added every few years to realign them, which is why the solar equivalent of a lunar date shifts annually.

items.q: How are dates in a leap month (윤달) handled?
items.a: A checkbox is provided to indicate whether a date falls in a leap month. For example, '윤4월 15일' and '4월 15일' are different days. If your birthdate or anniversary falls in a leap month, be sure to select that option.

items.q: What year range does the converter support?
items.a: Conversion uses KASI (Korea Astronomy and Space Science Institute) data from 1900 to 2050. Korean dates can differ by a day from the Chinese lunar calendar in some months because of the time zone, so Korean data is used.

explain.public: Globally routable on the internet. Firewall allowlists use addresses like this.

whatIs.title: What is the IP Address Checker?
whatIs.description: A tool that instantly displays your public IP address along with geolocation data (country, city), ISP, ASN, and timezone — all in one place. Commonly used to verify VPN connectivity, check which region a streaming or gaming service sees you as, and quickly retrieve your IP for firewall whitelist configurations.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Your current public IP (IPv4 or IPv6) appears in the blue card as soon as the page opens. Copy it with the button next to it.
2. The location and network cards show country/city, ISP (ASN), the Cloudflare data center you hit, and HTTP/TLS versions.
3. Turn on your VPN and press Refresh to see the new IP and location, then run the WebRTC leak test to check for VPN bypass.
4. Enter another address in 'IP address check' to instantly see if it is valid, IPv4/IPv6, and private/public/CGNAT.
5. Press 'Copy all' to copy every item as text for support tickets or firewall requests.

tips.title: Pro Tips
items: When using a VPN or proxy, this tool lets you instantly verify whether your IP has changed and whether you are connected from the intended country.
Useful for confirming that region-locked content (streaming, gaming) is accessible from the correct geographic location.
Quickly copy your public IP for server configs, firewall rules, or remote access setups that require a fixed IP whitelist.

items.q: Does the IP location reveal my home address?
items.a: No. IP-based geolocation shows the region where your ISP has assigned that IP block, not your physical address. Accuracy is typically at the city level.

items.q: Will I see an IPv4 or IPv6 address?
items.a: Depending on your device and network setup, either IPv4 (e.g., 123.45.67.89) or IPv6 (e.g., 2001:db8::1) may be shown. Both versions are supported; the address displayed corresponds to the protocol used for the connection.

items.q: Will my IP look different on a corporate or school Wi-Fi?
items.a: Yes. Corporate and school networks use NAT, so all devices on the network share a single public IP. This tool will show the network's public IP, not your device's private IP.

items.q: Is a '30% off' deal or a 'buy one get one free' deal better?

items.q: Which is better: a 10% coupon or a flat ₩3,000 coupon?
items.a: At a purchase price of ₩30,000, they are equal. Above ₩30,000 the percentage coupon saves more; below ₩30,000 the flat coupon wins. Run both through the calculator to compare exactly.

items.q: Should I account for VAT when calculating discounts?
items.a: Some online shops display the discount based on the pre-tax price, but the final checkout amount includes 10% VAT. Confirm whether the listed price is tax-inclusive or exclusive to get an accurate final figure.

rules.title: How speed is counted
items: Korean speed = correct keystrokes (jamo) per minute, the same way Hancom Typing counts.
닭 = ㄷ·ㅏ·ㄹ·ㄱ is 4 keystrokes; double final consonants count as 2.
과 = ㄱ·ㅗ·ㅏ is 3 keystrokes; compound vowels count as 2.
Tense consonants (ㄲ ㄸ ㅃ ㅆ ㅉ) and ㅒ ㅖ count as 1 (Shift is not counted). Spaces and punctuation count as 1.
English WPM treats 5 correct characters as one word, per minute.
Accuracy counts every character you ever got wrong, even if you fixed it.
The syllable you are still composing is never marked wrong; it is shown with a blue underline.

howTo.title: How to use
items: Pick a mode: Daily text (changes every day), Short, Long, or Timed (30s/60s).
The timer starts the moment you type the first character. No start button.
Correct characters turn dark, errors get a red underline, and the syllable being composed gets a blue underline.
Finish the text or run out of time to see speed, accuracy, grade and most-missed keys.
Share the result as an image or link so friends can race on the same text.

Intermediate: 200-299 · 30-39 WPM (adult average about 250 · 40 WPM)
Advanced: 300-399 · 40-59 WPM

whatIs.title: What is the Typing Test?
whatIs.description: A tool to measure your typing speed (WPM or keystrokes per minute) and accuracy in both Korean and English, and to improve through repeated practice. You type the given text as it appears, and the tool records your speed, error rate, and elapsed time so you can track your progress over time.

tips.title: Tips to Improve Your Typing
items: Focus on accuracy before speed. Reducing typos leads to faster long-term improvement than rushing and hitting errors.
Maintain the home row position (Korean: ㅏ·ㅓ keys, English: ASDF·JKL;). Keeping fingers close to the home row reduces travel distance and naturally increases speed.
Practicing 10–15 minutes daily is more effective than a single long session. Muscle memory is built through consistent repetition.

items.q: What is the average Korean typing speed for an adult?
items.a: The average adult types around 200–300 keystrokes per minute (타수). Professionals in office roles typically aim for 350+ keystrokes/min, while fast typists reach 600+ keystrokes/min.

items.q: What is the difference between WPM and keystrokes per minute?
items.a: WPM (Words Per Minute) is an English-centric metric counting words (standardized to 5 characters). Korean typing is traditionally measured in keystrokes per minute. Roughly, 60 WPM in English feels similar in effort to about 300 keystrokes/min in Korean.

items.q: Are my results saved?
items.a: Recent results are automatically saved to your browser's local storage so you can compare them on future visits. No data is sent to any server and no personal information is collected.

whatIs.description: A tool that converts Arabic numerals into Korean Hangul monetary notation (e.g., '금 삼백만 원 정'). Essential for official documents such as checks, contracts, promissory notes, and receipts where amounts must be written in Korean to prevent fraudulent alteration.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Enter the number you want to convert in the input field. Commas are handled automatically.
2. The converted Korean text appears instantly in both colloquial form (e.g., '삼백이십만 오천 원') and formal document form (e.g., '금 삼백이십만 오천 원 정').
3. Click the copy button next to your preferred format to send it to the clipboard.

tips.title: Pro Tips
items: Checks in Korea require the format '일금 ○○원 정'. Use the formal document result directly and paste it into your document.
Contracts conventionally include both numerals and Korean text, e.g., '3,000,000원(삼백만 원)'. This dual notation helps prevent disputes.
Amounts in the hundreds of millions or even trillions are accurately converted, making this tool reliable for high-value documents such as real estate contracts.

items.q: Is there a standardized format for Korean monetary notation?
items.a: The official format is '일금 ○○원 정'. '금 ○○원 정' is also widely accepted. Required formats may vary by document type (check vs. contract), so confirm with the relevant party.

items.q: What is the maximum number that can be converted?
items.a: Conversion is supported up to 9,999조 9,999억 9,999만 9,999원 (quadrillions of won), which covers virtually any practical use case.

items.q: Is Chinese financial notation (壹, 貳, 參 etc.) supported?

law.title: Why m² instead of pyeong
items: Since July 2007, Korea's Measures Act requires legal units such as m² and g instead of non-legal units like pyeong or don in trade, advertising and official documents; violations can be fined.
That is why sales notices and real-estate statistics use m², and the press writes 'price per 3.3 m²' instead of per pyeong.
Saying 'how many pyeong' in conversation is fine, but check the official m² figures in contracts and ads.
National housing size is an exclusive area of 85 m² or less (100 m² in eup/myeon areas outside the capital region), used for subscription, tax and loan rules. That is why 84 m² units are so common.

what.title: What is Pyeong?
items: A pyeong is the area of a square 6 ja (尺) on each side. Since 1 ja = 10/33 m, 1 pyeong = (60/33)² = 400/121 m² ≈ 3.305785 m².
1 m² = 121/400 pyeong = 0.3025 pyeong, so m² × 0.3025 = pyeong and pyeong × 3.3058 = m².
The shortcut 'pyeong × 3.3' is off by about 0.6 m² per 100 pyeong. Use this calculator when you need exact values.
1 pyeong ≈ 35.58 ft², handy when comparing with listings abroad.

reference.title: Apartment Area Reference
items: Exclusive area: the living space inside the unit. Sales notices and transaction records use it, and type names like 59 m² and 84 m² are exclusive areas.
Supply area: exclusive + residential common (stairs, corridors, elevators). The customary '34-pyeong type' is based on supply area.
Contract area: supply + other common (underground parking, management office). More common for officetels and retail units than apartments.
Service area: space like balconies that is not counted in any of the above. Extending the balcony makes the usable area larger than the exclusive area.
Exclusive 84 m² is 25.4 pyeong, but on a supply basis it is about a 33–35-pyeong type, hence '34 pyeong'. Don't compare the two bases with each other.

whatIs.title: What is the Pyeong Calculator?
whatIs.description: A tool for converting between pyeong (坪), the traditional Korean area unit, and square meters (m²). Indispensable when browsing Korean real estate listings, planning home renovations, or evaluating apartment sizes. Also explains the difference between supply area (공급면적) and exclusive-use area (전용면적) commonly used in Korean property listings.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Pyeong → m²: Enter the number of pyeong and the equivalent square meters appear instantly. Example: 33 pyeong → 109.09 m².
2. m² → Pyeong: Enter square meters to convert to pyeong. Example: 84 m² → 25.41 pyeong.
3. Adjust the decimal precision setting to get the level of detail you need.
4. Refer to the reference table for common size thresholds: national housing standard (≤85 m²), and small/medium/large categories.

tips.title: Pro Tips
items: A '33-pyeong apartment' in listings refers to the supply area. The actual living space (전용면적) is typically 10–20% smaller. Always compare both figures when evaluating an apartment.
A quick mental shortcut: 1 pyeong ≈ 3.3 m². Multiply pyeong × 3.3 for a rough estimate, or use this calculator for precision.
For renovation material estimates, always measure the exclusive-use area (전용면적) and cross-check with physical measurements to minimize waste.

items.q: How many m² is exactly 1 pyeong?
items.a: A pyeong is a square 6 ja on each side (1 ja = 10/33 m), so exactly 400/121 m² ≈ 3.305785 m². Conversely, 1 m² is 0.3025 pyeong.

items.q: How many pyeong is an 84 m² apartment?
items.a: The 84 m² in sales notices is exclusive area, which is about 25.4 pyeong. It is called '34 pyeong' because that figure is based on supply area (about 110–115 m²), which adds residential common area. A 59 m² unit is about 17.8 pyeong exclusive, roughly a 24-pyeong type on a supply basis.

items.q: What efficiency ratio should I use?
items.a: Apartments are usually 70–80%; officetels are much lower at roughly 50–60%. For an exact value, divide exclusive area by supply area from the sales notice's area table.

items.q: Is an extended balcony counted in the pyeong figure?
items.a: No. Balconies are service area and are not included in exclusive, supply or contract area. Extending one increases the space you actually use, so two 84 m² units can feel different.

items.q: Is it illegal to use pyeong?
items.a: Since July 2007, Korea's Measures Act requires legal units like m² in trade and advertising. Saying 'pyeong' in conversation is fine, but official figures in contracts, ads and statistics are in m².

items.q: How do I convert price per pyeong to price per m²?
items.a: Price per m² = price per pyeong ÷ 3.3058. 40 million KRW per pyeong is about 12.1 million KRW per m². 'Price per 3.3 m²' in the news means the same as price per pyeong.

sources.title: Rules and sources (2026)
items: VAT rate 10%: VAT Act Art. 30
Fractions under 1 won: no statutory rule — VAT is supply × 10% in principle; round down or round per agreement
Simplified taxpayer threshold under 104M won prior-year sales (from Jul 1, 2024): VAT Enforcement Decree Art. 109
Payment exemption under 48M won: VAT Act Art. 69
Value-added rates 15–40%: Enforcement Decree Art. 111; tax computation: Act Art. 63
Card sales issuance credit 1.3%, 10M won/year (through Dec 31, 2026): VAT Act Art. 46
E-filing credit 10,000 won: Restriction of Special Taxation Act Art. 104-8
Deadline: 25th of the month after the period (Act Arts. 49, 67); moved to the next day if on a weekend or holiday (Framework Act on National Taxes Art. 5)

vatCalculator.title: VAT Calculator
vatCalculator.description: Calculate VAT (10%) from supply amount, or reverse-calculate from total amount.

howItWorks.title: How it works
items: Supply → total: VAT = supply × 10%, fraction rounded down (default) or rounded.
Total → supply: VAT = total ÷ 11, supply = total − VAT, so the amount received stays exact. When this differs from supply × 10% by 1 won, a note is shown.
Multiple items: each line is qty × unit price; supply and VAT are summed. Exempt lines carry no VAT and zero-rated lines carry 0 VAT, both totaled separately.
General taxpayer: output VAT − input VAT − card sales credit − e-filing credit. A negative result is a refund.
Simplified taxpayer: sales × value-added rate × 10% − purchases × 0.5% − credits. Under 48M won annual sales, payment is exempt; no refunds.

basic.title: What is VAT?
items: Value Added Tax (VAT) is a tax on the supply of goods and services
Korea's VAT rate is 10%
Supply Amount × 10% = VAT
Total = Supply Amount + VAT

reverse.title: Reverse VAT Calculation
items: From total: Supply Amount = Total ÷ 1.1
From total: VAT = Total ÷ 11
Tax invoices require separate supply amount and VAT
Simplified taxpayers have different VAT rates by industry (1.5%-4%)

whatIs.title: What is the VAT calculator?
whatIs.description: Adds 10% VAT to a supply value or splits a VAT-inclusive total into supply value and VAT. It also builds tax-invoice totals for multiple items (taxable, zero-rated, exempt) and estimates the VAT return and next filing deadline for general and simplified taxpayers — handy for small business owners, freelancers and online sellers.

howToUse.title: How to use
items: 1. Quick: choose supply → total, total → supply, or VAT → supply and enter an amount; results update instantly.
2. Match the VAT rounding rule (round down / round) with your counterparty. A note appears when there is a 1-won gap.
3. Multiple items: enter item, quantity, unit price and tax type to get taxable supply, VAT, exempt amount and total like a tax invoice. Pick "VAT included" for retail prices.
4. VAT return estimate: choose general or simplified, enter sales, purchases and card sales to see the estimated payable (or refund) and a D-day to the next deadline.
5. Copy for invoice, copy table (Excel) and copy link share the exact result; the link restores the same inputs.

tips.title: Tips
items: Always state "VAT excluded" or "VAT included" on quotes — for a 1.1M won quote it is a 100,000 won difference.
Simplified taxpayers are individual businesses with prior-year sales under 104M won (from July 2024; 48M won for real-estate rental and entertainment venues).
Individual businesses with lots of card/cash-receipt sales should claim the card sales credit (1.3%, up to 10M won/year, through 2026).
Exempt goods (unprocessed farm/fishery products, books, medical and education services) get a regular invoice, not a tax invoice.

items.q: Is 10% VAT based on supply value or total?
items.a: Supply value. Relative to the total it is 1/11 (about 9.09%). Example: supply 1,000,000 won → VAT 100,000 → total 1,100,000.

items.q: How are fractions under 1 won handled on tax invoices?
items.a: There is no statutory rounding rule; VAT is supply × 10% in principle and fractions follow the parties' agreement (rounding down is common). When reversing from a total, compute VAT = total ÷ 11 first and supply = total − VAT so the total matches exactly.

items.q: How much VAT does a simplified taxpayer pay?
items.a: Sales incl. VAT × value-added rate by industry (15–40%) × 10%, minus 0.5% of purchases and other credits. Under 48M won annual sales, payment is exempt but filing is still required.

items.q: When is the VAT filing deadline?
items.a: Individual general taxpayers file by July 25 (Jan–Jun) and January 25 of the next year (Jul–Dec). Simplified taxpayers file the full year by January 25. If the date falls on a weekend or holiday, it moves to the next business day.

alcoholCalculator.title: Blood Alcohol Calculator
alcoholCalculator.description: Estimate blood alcohol concentration (BAC) using the Widmark formula.
alcoholCalculator.warning: This is a statistical Widmark estimate. Body type, food, liver function, medication and sleep can change the real value a lot, and it cannot be used as evidence for a breath test or legal judgment. If you drank, do not drive.

formula.title: Widmark Formula
items: BAC(%) = alcohol(g) / (weight kg x r x 10) - beta x hours elapsed
Alcohol(g) = volume(ml) x ABV x 0.789 (e.g. one soju bottle 360ml at 15.7% = about 44.6g)
r (distribution factor): men 0.68-0.70, women 0.55-0.60. This tool uses the low end to estimate high
beta (elimination): average 0.015%/h, 0.010-0.020% by person. Time to 0% uses the slow 0.010%

factors.title: Influencing Factors
items: Higher body weight results in lower BAC
Drinking on an empty stomach increases absorption and BAC
Women have lower body water ratio, resulting in higher BAC for same intake
Fatigue and medication can affect alcohol metabolism rate

whatIs.title: What is the Blood Alcohol Calculator?
whatIs.description: Estimates blood alcohol concentration (BAC) with the Widmark formula. Enter sex, weight, drinks (soju, beer, somaek, wine, makgeolli, liquor, highball) and times to see your current estimate, the individual range, the estimated time to 0%, and a BAC timeline. Korean thresholds for license suspension (0.03%) and revocation (0.08%) are shown too.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Enter sex and weight. The Widmark r value depends on sex.
2. Set the start time and add what you drank. Build somaek from a soju:beer ratio.
3. Edit count, ABV and time in the list; results update instantly.
4. Check the estimated time to 0% and do not drive before then. Share via link or image.

tips.title: Important Tips
items: This calculator provides an estimate based on average alcohol metabolism. Actual BAC varies significantly with individual health, fasting state, medications, and other factors.
Drinking on an empty stomach speeds alcohol absorption by 2–3×, causing BAC to rise much faster. Eating food and drinking water slows absorption.
Hangover remedies and coffee do not speed up alcohol metabolism. Only time breaks down alcohol — consult the calculator's estimated clearance time before driving.

items.q: What BAC does one bottle of soju give?
items.a: For a 70 kg man, one bottle (360ml, 15.7%) is about 44.6g of alcohol, an estimated 0.094% right after, above the 0.08% revocation line. Reaching 0% takes about 6 hours on average and over 9 hours if elimination is slow.

items.q: Can I use this to decide whether I can drive?
items.a: No. The Widmark formula is a statistical estimate with large individual variation. The only safe BAC for driving is 0%. If you drank, do not drive.

items.q: Why do women get a higher BAC from the same amount?
items.a: Women have less body water per kg, so a smaller Widmark r (women 0.55-0.60, men 0.68-0.70). The same alcohol spreads into less water, giving a higher BAC.

license.title: License — can I use these commercially?
items: All 38 fonts in the list are under the SIL Open Font License (OFL 1.1). You can use them for free in websites, apps, ads, print, video and logos, including commercial work.
Embedding as a web font or bundling in PDFs and apps is allowed.
Not allowed: selling the font files by themselves, or distributing modified versions under the original (reserved) font name.
License info was checked against the Google Fonts repository (ofl folder) and each vendor's repository. Re-check the latest terms on each card's official page before use.

usage.title: How to Use
items: Type your copy or pick a sample (Ga-na-da, greeting, numbers & Latin, paragraph).
Adjust size, weight, line height, letter spacing and the preview background. Fonts without the chosen weight use the closest one, noted on the card.
Narrow down by category (gothic, myeongjo, handwriting, display, coding) or search, and star favorites (saved in this browser).
Pin up to 4 fonts to compare them side by side at the top.
Use 'Copy CSS' for the <link>, @import and font-family code, and 'Official page' to download.
'Copy share link' keeps your text, size and pinned fonts in the URL.
Drop your own font file (ttf/otf/woff/woff2) to preview it with the same settings. The file is never uploaded.

tips.title: Font Selection Tips
items: Body text: multi-weight gothics like Pretendard, Noto Sans KR or Nanum Gothic. Around 16px, line height 1.6–1.8 and letter spacing -1 to -2% suit Korean body text.
Headlines and banners: bold display faces like Black Han Sans, Do Hyeon or Jua, paired with a gothic for body text.
Emotional or brand copy: use myeongjo (Gowun Batang, Hahmlet) or handwriting fonts for short headlines only.
Code and tables: monospace fonts like D2Coding or Nanum Gothic Coding keep digits aligned.
On the web, load only the weights you use. Each weight adds hundreds of KB.

whatIs.title: What is the Font Preview Tool?
whatIs.description: A tool for designers and marketers choosing a Korean font for banners, product pages and websites. Preview 38 commercially free (SIL OFL) Korean fonts with your real copy, adjust size, weight, line height, letter spacing and light/dark background, and compare them side by side. Only fonts on screen are loaded, subset to the characters you typed, so the page stays light.

items.q: Can I use the font on my website right away?
items.a: Yes. 'Copy CSS' copies a <link> tag, an @import rule and the font-family declaration. Put the <link> in your HTML <head> or the @import at the top of your CSS, then set font-family.

items.q: Can I use these fonts commercially?
items.a: All fonts in the list are SIL OFL 1.1, free for commercial use in ads, print, web and video. Selling the font files by themselves and distributing modified versions under the original name are not allowed. Check the latest terms on each card's official page.

items.q: Where do I download the font files?
items.a: Each card's 'Official page' button opens the Google Fonts specimen page or the vendor repository (Pretendard, D2Coding).

items.q: I chose weight 900 but the text looks thin.
items.a: If the font has no 900 weight, the closest available weight is used. The 'Weights' line on the card shows available and applied weights.

items.q: Is my own font file uploaded to a server?
items.a: No. It is read locally with the browser FontFace API and never sent anywhere. It is gone when you close the page.

items: Korea (KST) is UTC+9

whatIs.title: What is the World Clock?
whatIs.description: A tool that displays the current local time in major cities around the world in real time, all on one screen. Compare Seoul, New York, London, Tokyo, Sydney, and many more time zones at a glance — ideal for scheduling international meetings, timing calls to friends abroad, or checking stock exchange and crypto trading hours.

items.q: Is Daylight Saving Time (DST) automatically applied?
items.a: Yes. DST rules for each country and region are applied automatically. Countries observing DST (such as the US and Europe) will show times shifted forward by one hour during the applicable months.

items.q: What if the city I need is not in the list?
items.a: You can add a city by searching for its IANA timezone name (e.g., America/Chicago, Asia/Kolkata). Your custom city list is saved in your browser for future visits.

items.q: How is the International Date Line handled?
items.a: Locations east of the Date Line (e.g., Hawaii) are one calendar day behind, while locations to the west (e.g., Fiji) are one day ahead. The date is shown alongside each city's time so the difference is clear.

rentConverter.rateInfo: Based on Bank of Korea base rate, typically 4-6%

what.title: What is Rent Conversion?
items: Converting a jeonse deposit into monthly rent, or monthly rent into a jeonse deposit
Rates vary by contract; regional market rates are published by the Korea Real Estate Board (R-ONE)
Under the Housing Lease Protection Act the conversion rate is capped at the lower of 10% and the BOK base rate + 2%p

example.title: Calculation Example
items: Jeonse 300M → Monthly (deposit 50M, rate 5%): (300M-50M) × 5% ÷ 12 ≈ 1.04M KRW
Monthly 1M (deposit 100M, rate 5%) → Jeonse: 100M + (1M × 12 ÷ 5%) = 340M
Higher conversion rate means higher monthly rent for the same Jeonse amount

whatIs.title: What is the Jeonse/Wolse Conversion Calculator?
whatIs.description: A tool for converting between jeonse (전세, lump-sum deposit lease) and wolse (월세, monthly rent) using the legal conversion rate. Compare the true monthly cost of each arrangement — including the opportunity cost of a locked-up deposit — to decide which option is financially better for your situation.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Jeonse → monthly: enter the jeonse amount and the deposit to keep; the rent on the remainder is shown instantly.
2. Monthly → jeonse: enter deposit and rent to get the equivalent jeonse amount.
3. The rate defaults to the legal cap (base rate + 2%p). Edit the base rate if it changes, or type your contract's actual rate.
4. Use the deposit slider for a semi-jeonse deposit, then enter loan/savings rates and salary to compare total costs and the breakeven rate.
5. For renewals, check the maximum deposit or rent allowed under the 5% cap.

tips.title: Pro Tips
items: The legal cap on the jeonse-to-wolse conversion rate is 'base rate + 2%' (Housing Lease Protection Act). If a landlord demands a higher rate, you have grounds to object.
Don't forget the opportunity cost of a jeonse deposit. A ₩200M deposit at 4% annual interest is ₩670,000/month you're forgoing in deposit interest.
Non-financial factors — jeonse insurance availability, lease fraud risk, and moving costs — should also factor into your jeonse vs. wolse decision.

items.q: What is the jeonse-to-wolse conversion rate?
items.a: The annual interest rate applied when converting part or all of a jeonse deposit into monthly rent. At 5% conversion rate, ₩10M of deposit converts to approximately ₩41,000/month (₩10M × 5% ÷ 12).

items.q: Is a contract that exceeds the legal maximum rate invalid?
items.a: The portion exceeding the legal cap is void. Overpaid monthly rent can be claimed back, so always verify the legal ceiling at the time of signing.

items.q: What is the difference between ban-jeonse and regular monthly rent?
items.a: Ban-jeonse (반전세) combines a high deposit — close to a full jeonse — with a smaller monthly payment. Regular wolse has a much lower deposit and higher monthly rent. Use this calculator to compare the actual monthly cost of both arrangements.

whatIs.title: What is the Water Bill Calculator?
whatIs.description: Estimates your bill from household size and monthly usage (㎥): base fee, water usage, sewerage and the water use levy. Seoul and Busan use official 2026 tariffs; for other regions enter the rates from your bill. Water bills are VAT-exempt.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Choose your region. Outside Seoul/Busan, choose 'Custom' and enter the rates from your bill.
2. Pick household size to fill in the average usage.
3. Adjust usage with the slider or input; the bill updates instantly. If billed every 2 months, enter half.
4. Check the comparison with average households and savings per tip, then share as an image or link.

tips.title: Water-Saving Tips
items: Replacing a standard shower head (10–15 L/min) with a water-efficient model (3–5 L/min) can cut shower water use by more than 50%.
Placing a water-filled plastic bottle in the toilet tank saves about 1–1.5 L per flush — roughly 1–2 m³/month for a family of four.
Always run the washing machine with a full load. Doing one full load uses 30–40% less water than two half-loads, and washing in cold water saves energy too.

items.q: Why do water rates differ by region?
items.a: Each local government sets its own rates by ordinance. In 2026 Seoul charges flat 580 won (water) and 480 won (sewerage) per ㎥, while Busan charges 920 won for water with tiered sewerage rates.

items.q: How much water does a family of four use?
items.a: Seoul and Busan use about 6㎥ per person per month as the reference, so about 24㎥ for four people — roughly 30,600 won in Seoul.

items.q: Why can sewerage cost more than water?
items.a: Sewerage fees cover sewer pipes and treatment plants, and many cities are raising them to replace aging facilities. Seoul will raise them every year for five years from 2026.

whatIs.title: What is the CSS Gradient Generator?
whatIs.description: A developer tool that lets you visually configure gradient colors, direction, and type (linear/radial/conic) and instantly generates the corresponding CSS code. No need to memorize complex CSS gradient syntax — design the effect you want through an intuitive UI and copy the ready-to-use code directly into your project.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Select the gradient type: linear, radial, or conic.
2. Add color stops and set each color (using the HEX, RGB, or HSL color picker) and its position (%).
3. For linear gradients, adjust the angle (0–360°) or click a direction shortcut button (top, bottom, left, right, diagonal).
4. Confirm the result in the live preview box, then click the CSS copy button to save the generated code to your clipboard.

items.q: Will the generated CSS work in all browsers?
items.a: `linear-gradient` and `radial-gradient` are supported in all modern browsers including IE11. `conic-gradient` requires Chrome 69+, Firefox 83+, or Safari 12.1+ and is not supported in IE11.

items.q: Can I create gradients with transparency (alpha)?
items.a: Yes. Use the rgba() color input or the opacity slider in the color picker to add transparent color stops. This is useful for creating semi-transparent overlays on top of images.

items.q: How do I combine a gradient with a background image?
items.a: Use CSS multiple backgrounds: `background: linear-gradient(...), url(image.jpg);` — separate values with a comma. Adapt the generated code to layer a gradient overlay on top of your image.

For personal names, separate surname and given name with a space.
