whatIs.title: What is the PDF Tools?
whatIs.description: PDF Tools is an all-in-one browser-based utility for editing PDF files without any additional software. It offers four core functions: merging multiple PDFs, splitting out specific pages, rotating pages, and converting images to PDF. All processing is local — files are never uploaded to a server, keeping your documents private.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Select the operation you need (Merge / Split / Rotate / Image to PDF) from the tabs.
2. Upload or drag and drop your PDF files or images.
3. Merge: reorder files. Split: specify page numbers to extract. Rotate: choose pages and angle. Image to PDF: arrange image order.
4. Click the process button and the output file will download automatically.

tips.title: Pro Tips
items: Use 'Image to PDF' to combine multiple scanned images into a single PDF document.
Use 'Split' to extract specific pages from contracts or reports.
Processing time may increase for very large PDF files due to browser memory constraints.

items.q: Is there a file size limit?
items.a: Processing is limited by browser memory. Files up to several dozen MB generally work fine. Very large files may slow down processing.

items.q: Can I process password-protected PDFs?
items.a: Password-protected PDFs must be unlocked first. Password removal is not currently supported.

items.q: Will quality be degraded during conversion?
items.a: Merge, split, and rotate operations preserve original data with no quality loss. Image-to-PDF conversion retains the original image resolution.

whatIs.title: What are PDF Tools?
whatIs.description: Merge PDFs, split or extract pages, delete/rotate/reorder pages, and convert images (JPG, PNG) to PDF on one screen. Most online PDF sites upload your file to a server; this tool processes it inside your browser, so the file never leaves your device.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Merge: add several PDFs, set the order by dragging (or with the up/down buttons), then press "Merge PDFs". The result is saved as "firstfile_merged.pdf".
Split: add one PDF and pick a method. For a range type "1-3, 5, 8-" (8- = page 8 to the end); "Every N pages" and "Each page" download several files as one ZIP.
Organize pages: every page has move earlier/later, rotate and delete buttons, and you can drag to reorder. Press "Save changes" to create the new PDF.
Image→PDF: add photos and choose the paper (A4, Letter, original size), orientation and margin. Each image becomes one page.

tips.title: Tips
items: Scans named scan_1, scan_2… can be put in order at once with "Sort by name" (numbers sorted numerically).
To get each range as its own file, turn on "Save each range as a separate file" under Split → Page Range.
Phone photos that used to come out sideways are straightened automatically using their EXIF orientation.
Merge, split and organize copy the original pages as-is, so text and image quality are unchanged.

items.q: Are my files uploaded to a server?
items.a: No. Files are read and processed only in this browser's memory and are never sent to any server. They disappear when you close the page.

items.q: Can I process password-protected PDFs?
items.a: PDFs with an open password or editing restrictions cannot be processed. Open the file in a PDF viewer with the password and save a copy with "Print to PDF", then use that copy.

items.q: Is there a file size limit?
items.a: There is no fixed limit, but processing uses browser memory, so files of several hundred MB may be slow or fail. A desktop can handle larger files than a phone.

items.q: Does quality drop?
items.a: Merge, split and organize copy pages without re-rendering, so quality is unchanged. Image→PDF embeds JPG and PNG originals as-is; only photos that need orientation correction and WebP/GIF images are re-saved as high-quality JPG.

items.q: How is page rotation saved?
items.a: It changes the page rotation value in the PDF, so the content is untouched and other PDF viewers show the same orientation.

items.q: Can I convert PDF to JPG?
items.a: Only image→PDF is supported at the moment.

whatIs.title: What is Tetris?
whatIs.description: Tetris is the iconic block-stacking puzzle game created by Alexey Pajitnov in 1984 and one of the best-selling games of all time. Tetromino pieces fall from above — rotate and place them to complete horizontal lines and clear them from the board. This version features hold, next-piece preview, ghost piece, and a level progression system.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Click the Start button or press any key to begin.
2. Use the left/right arrow keys to move pieces, the up arrow to rotate, and the down arrow for soft drop.
3. Press the spacebar for an instant hard drop to the bottom.
4. Press C to hold the current piece and swap it with your stored piece.

tips.title: Pro Tips
items: Watch the ghost piece (translucent preview) to see exactly where your piece will land.
Save the I-piece (long bar) for a Tetris — clearing four lines at once — for maximum points.
Keep your stack as flat as possible; irregular peaks make it increasingly hard to place pieces as speed increases.

items.q: How does the hold feature work?
items.a: Press C to store the current piece in the hold slot and bring out the next piece. You can swap again by pressing C, but only once per piece.

items.q: What is a T-Spin?
items.a: A T-Spin involves rotating the T-piece into a tight gap. A T-Spin Double clears two lines with a high bonus, making it a favorite advanced technique.

items.q: How do I pause the game?
items.a: Press P or Escape to pause. The board is hidden during pause so you can't plan ahead.

stats.title: Statistics

rules.title: Game Rules
items: Guess a secret number made of distinct digits (daily puzzle: 4 digits, 1–9)
Right digit in the right spot is a strike (S); right digit in the wrong spot is a ball (B)
No shared digits at all is an out
Practice mode lets you pick 3/4/5 digits, whether 0 is used, and a try limit
After 3 guesses you can see how many candidates remain, or spend one try to reveal a possible candidate

example.title: Example
items: If answer is 1-2-3 and you guess 1-3-5: 1S 1B 1O
1 is in the correct position → Strike
3 is in the number but wrong position → Ball
5 is not in the number → Out

tips.title: Strategy Tips
items: Use two non-overlapping guesses first (e.g. 1234, 5678) to find which digits are in
Mark every digit from an out with ❌ in the notepad
Never put a ball digit back in the same spot — that spot is ruled out
When stuck, check the remaining candidate count and pick a guess that splits them best

whatIs.title: What is Number Baseball?
whatIs.description: Number Baseball is a brain game where you deduce a hidden 3–4 digit number (all digits unique) through Strike, Ball, and Out feedback. A Strike means a digit is correct and in the right position; a Ball means correct digit but wrong position; an Out means the digit doesn't appear at all. Find the number within limited attempts using logical reasoning.

items.q: What is the best first guess?
items.a: Starting with non-repeating digits like '1234' is a common strategy. The first result tells you which digits are and aren't in the answer, setting up efficient follow-up guesses.

items.q: Can 0 appear in the first digit?
items.a: By default, 0 does not appear in the first position. All digits in the answer are unique.

items.q: How many guesses is considered good?
items.a: A 4-digit game can always be solved in 7 guesses or fewer. Solving in 5 or fewer is considered excellent.

items.q: When does the daily puzzle change?

items.q: Can 0 be used?

items.q: How many guesses is good?
items.a: A good player usually cracks a 4-digit (1–9) number in 5–6 guesses, and around 7 at most. Solving in 5 or less is excellent.

contrastChecker.title: Contrast Checker
contrastChecker.description: Check WCAG contrast ratio between text and background colors for accessibility compliance.
contrastChecker.textarea: Type text here to preview readability

preview.title: Preview
preview.normalText: Normal text (16px) preview. Check readability according to WCAG standards.

wcag.title: WCAG Standards
items: AA: Normal text 4.5:1 or higher, Large text 3:1 or higher
AAA: Normal text 7:1 or higher, Large text 4.5:1 or higher
Large text: 18pt (24px)+ or 14pt (18.67px) bold
UI components and graphics require 3:1 minimum

tips.title: Accessibility Tips
items: Don't convey information through color alone (use icons, patterns)
Always verify contrast between text and background
Avoid red-green combinations for color-blind users
Maintain sufficient contrast in dark mode too

whatIs.title: What is the Contrast Checker?
whatIs.description: The Contrast Checker calculates the luminance contrast ratio between text and background colors and verifies compliance with W3C Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG 2.1). It helps designers and developers ensure their color choices are readable by everyone, including users with low vision. Essential for public sector and enterprise web services with accessibility requirements.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Enter the foreground (text) color and background color using the color picker or HEX code.
2. The contrast ratio is calculated and displayed automatically.
3. Check WCAG AA compliance (4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text) and AAA (7:1 and 4.5:1).
4. If the ratio fails, receive alternative color suggestions that meet the standard.

items.q: What is the difference between WCAG AA and AAA?
items.a: AA is the minimum standard covering most legal requirements. AAA is a stricter level ensuring optimal readability for all users. AA compliance is the practical target for most projects.

items.q: What counts as 'large text'?
items.a: WCAG defines large text as 18pt (approximately 24px) or larger, or 14pt (approximately 18.67px) bold or larger. A relaxed contrast ratio applies to large text.

items.q: Do logos and decorative text need to meet contrast requirements?
items.a: No — logos and purely decorative text are exempt under WCAG. However, all text conveying information must comply.

whatIs.title: What is Korean Wordle?

items.q: Can I only play once a day?

items.q: What do the hint colors mean?

items.q: Can I share my results with friends?

boxShadow.title: CSS Box Shadow Generator
boxShadow.description: Visually create multi-layer box-shadow CSS code

basics.title: box-shadow Syntax
items: box-shadow: [inset] x-offset y-offset blur spread color
X Offset: positive=right, negative=left shadow direction
Y Offset: positive=down, negative=up shadow direction
Blur: shadow blur amount (0=sharp, higher=softer)
Spread: shadow expand/shrink size
Multiple shadows can be stacked separated by commas

tips.title: Design Tips
items: For natural shadows, set Y offset larger than X offset
Blur value about 2x the offset looks natural
Using colors with transparency (rgba) gives a more refined effect
Multiple layers can express depth perception
Neumorphism effect combines light/dark two shadows

whatIs.title: What is the CSS Box Shadow Generator?
whatIs.description: The CSS Box Shadow Generator is a developer tool for visually designing box-shadow CSS properties and instantly copying the code. Adjust horizontal/vertical offsets, blur radius, spread radius, color, opacity, and inset/outset with sliders and see a live preview in real time. Stack multiple shadow layers to create complex, polished effects.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Use sliders to adjust horizontal offset (X), vertical offset (Y), blur, and spread.
2. Set the shadow color and opacity.
3. Check the inset checkbox to create an inner shadow.
4. Click 'Add Layer' to stack multiple shadows, then copy the generated CSS code.

items.q: Can I apply multiple shadows simultaneously?
items.a: Yes. CSS box-shadow supports multiple comma-separated values. This tool's multi-layer feature generates that code automatically.

items.q: What is an inset shadow?
items.a: Adding the inset keyword creates a shadow inside the element rather than outside. Great for pressed button effects or inner depth.

items.q: Can I get Tailwind CSS class equivalents?
items.a: The tool generates standard CSS, and suggests the closest Tailwind shadow utility class as a reference.

flexboxGuide.title: Flexbox Basics
items: flex-direction sets the main axis direction (row/column)
justify-content aligns items along the main axis
align-items aligns items along the cross axis
flex-wrap controls whether items wrap to new lines
gap sets spacing between items

gridGuide.title: Grid Basics
items: grid-template-columns defines the column structure
grid-template-rows defines the row structure
fr unit sets proportional sizes
grid-column/grid-row specifies item span
gap sets spacing between cells

tips.title: Usage Tips
items: Flexbox is ideal for 1D layouts (row or column), while Grid excels at 2D layouts (rows and columns)
Select a preset then customize properties to quickly build your desired layout
Use responsive preview to check how it looks on desktop, tablet, and mobile
Copy the generated CSS code and apply it directly to your project

whatIs.title: What is the CSS Flexbox & Grid Generator?
whatIs.description: The CSS Flexbox & Grid Generator is a developer tool that lets you visually design layouts using CSS Flexbox and Grid, generating ready-to-use CSS code in real time. No need to memorize complex property names — use buttons and dropdowns to set up your layout and copy the code directly into your project.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Select the Flexbox or Grid tab.
2. Configure container properties (flex-direction, justify-content, align-items, grid-template, etc.) using the controls.
3. Add or remove items and adjust individual item properties (flex-grow, grid-column, etc.).
4. Check the live preview on the right and copy the generated CSS code.

items.q: When should I use Flexbox vs Grid?
items.a: Flexbox is best for one-dimensional layouts (a row or a column). Grid excels at two-dimensional layouts (rows and columns simultaneously). Use Flexbox for navbars and card rows; use Grid for full-page layouts.

items.q: Does the generated code work in all browsers?
items.a: Flexbox and Grid are fully supported in all modern browsers. IE11 has partial Flexbox support and requires legacy Grid syntax.

items.q: Can I create responsive Grid layouts?
items.a: Yes. The tool supports auto-fill/auto-fit with minmax() for responsive grids that adapt without media queries.

whatIs.title: What is the SVG Editor & Optimizer?
whatIs.description: The SVG Editor & Optimizer is a developer tool for editing SVG (Scalable Vector Graphics) code directly and reducing file size by stripping unnecessary metadata and empty elements. A live preview lets you see changes instantly as you edit. You can also export optimized SVG or convert it to PNG or JPEG raster images.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Upload an SVG file or paste SVG code directly into the editor.
2. View the live SVG rendering in the preview panel on the right.
3. Click Optimize to generate a cleaned, smaller SVG.
4. Download the optimized SVG or convert it to PNG/JPEG.

items.q: How much can optimization reduce file size?
items.a: Depending on SVG complexity, exports from Illustrator or Figma can often be reduced by 20–70%. Files with heavy metadata and extra layers benefit the most.

items.q: Is animated SVG supported?
items.a: You can edit CSS or SMIL-based SVG animation code. Whether the animation plays in the preview depends on browser support.

items.q: Can I specify the output dimensions for PNG conversion?
items.a: Yes. Enter a custom width and height before converting to PNG and the output will match your specified dimensions.

cors.description: This tool runs in the browser, so access to some API servers may be restricted by CORS policy. If you encounter CORS errors, use a proxy server or check the API server's CORS configuration.

whatIs.title: What is the API Tester?
whatIs.description: The API Tester lets you send HTTP requests to REST API endpoints directly from your browser — no separate client installation needed. Configure HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, etc.), request headers, query parameters, and request body (JSON or form data). It provides Postman-like functionality entirely within your browser.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Select the HTTP method (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, etc.).
2. Enter the API endpoint URL.
3. In the Headers tab, add headers like Authorization and Content-Type as needed.
4. For POST/PUT requests, switch to the Body tab, enter JSON or form data, then click Send.

items.q: What should I do about CORS errors?
items.a: Browsers block cross-origin API requests under the CORS policy. The server needs to include proper CORS headers, or you can route requests through a CORS proxy in development.

items.q: How do I pass an authentication token?
items.a: In the Headers tab, add 'Authorization: Bearer {token}' for bearer token auth, or use the header name required by your API for API key authentication.

items.q: Are my request histories saved?
items.a: Yes. Recent requests are automatically saved so you can quickly reuse them. Bookmark frequently used requests for even faster access.

accounts.title: What is the 4-account method?
items: Spending everything from one account hides how much is left. Split accounts by purpose and each balance becomes your remaining budget.
Fixed-cost (salary) account: rent, utilities, phone, insurance and subscriptions leave by auto-debit.
Living account: for variable costs like food, transport and leisure. Link a debit card and spend only its balance.
Emergency account: keep 3–6 months of essential costs in an instant-access (parking) account.
Investment account: savings plans, pension accounts (IRP), ISA and other long-term assets. Auto-transfer on payday: pay yourself first.

usage.title: How to Use
items: Enter monthly take-home pay, or switch to 'From salary' to convert an annual salary to take-home
Pick a budget rule (50/30/20, 4 accounts, first job) and auto-split, or edit each category
Check the savings-rate verdict and how much you'll save in a year on the blue card
Log actual spending per month to see what's left and your daily allowance; past months show a summary
Your budget and log are saved in this browser. Export CSV or share a link to move them

rule.title: What is the 50/30/20 Rule?
items: Needs (50%): housing, food, transport, phone, insurance, medical: hard-to-cut costs
Wants (30%): leisure, clothing, social events, education: adjustable spending
Savings (20%): emergency fund, savings, investing. Extra loan principal payments count here too
Popularized by Elizabeth Warren's "All Your Worth" (2005). In high-rent areas needs often exceed 50%, so some use 60/20/20

tips.title: Saving Tips
items: Cutting fixed costs (phone, insurance, subscriptions) pays off every month. Start with budget carriers, duplicate insurance and unused subscriptions
Don't save what's left; auto-transfer savings on payday first
Divide yearly costs (holidays, gifts, car tax) by 12 and budget them monthly so no month goes into deficit
Overspend one day and the remaining daily allowance shrinks automatically. Checking once a day is enough
20% is a common savings-rate guideline. If that's hard, start at 10% and raise it each year

whatIs.title: What is the Budget Calculator?
whatIs.description: The Budget Calculator is a personal finance tool for tracking monthly expenses by category — housing, food, transportation, communication, leisure, and more — to calculate total spending and monitor your budget at a glance. Guided by the 50/30/20 budgeting rule, it helps you understand your spending patterns and identify areas where you can save.

items.q: What is the 50/30/20 rule?
items.a: A simple personal finance guideline: allocate 50% of after-tax income to needs (housing, food, transport), 30% to wants (leisure, shopping), and 20% to savings and debt repayment.

items.q: Will my data be saved between visits?
items.a: Yes. Budget items are stored in browser localStorage, so they persist when you reload the page.

items.q: Can dual-income households calculate combined budgets?
items.a: Yes. Enter the combined household income and all shared household expenses in the respective fields.

whatIs.title: What is the Budget Calculator?
whatIs.description: This budget calculator helps you decide where each paycheck should go. Enter your income (monthly take-home or annual salary), pick a rule (50/30/20, 4 accounts or first job) and compare each category against the target ratios with a savings-rate verdict. Log actual spending each month to see what's left and your daily allowance, plus when you'll reach your emergency fund goal.

items.q: What is the 50/30/20 rule?
items.a: A simple guideline: allocate 50% of after-tax income to needs (housing, food, transport), 30% to wants (leisure, shopping), and 20% to savings and investing.

items.q: Is my data saved between visits?
items.a: Yes. Your budget and monthly log are saved automatically in this browser (localStorage) and never sent to a server. Clearing browser data deletes them, so export a CSV backup.

items.q: How is the daily allowance calculated?
items.a: This month's variable living budget (food, transport, medical, leisure, clothing, social events, other) minus what you've spent, divided by the remaining days including today. Fixed costs (housing, phone, insurance, education) and savings are excluded.

items.q: Does sharing reveal my amounts?
items.a: By default only your savings rate and ratios are shared. Turn on 'Include amounts' to share amounts and a link with your budget.

items.q: Can dual-income households calculate combined budgets?
items.a: Yes. Enter the combined household income and all shared household expenses.

whatIs.title: What is the Loan Repayment Scheduler?
whatIs.description: The Loan Repayment Scheduler generates a full month-by-month repayment table showing principal, interest, and remaining balance for your loan. It supports equal principal+interest (annuity), equal principal, and deferred repayment structures, and lets you simulate the interest savings from early repayment. Essential for planning mortgages, auto loans, or personal loans.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Enter the loan principal, annual interest rate, and loan term (in months).
2. Select a repayment method (equal principal+interest / equal principal / deferred).
3. Enter the loan start date and payment dates will be generated automatically.
4. Review the monthly schedule showing principal, interest, and balance — export to Excel if needed.

items.q: Which repayment method is better: equal P+I or equal principal?
items.a: Equal principal repayment results in less total interest and decreasing monthly payments but has higher initial payments. Equal P+I offers predictable monthly payments, making budgeting easier.

items.q: How much interest can I save with early repayment?
items.a: Enter a lump-sum early repayment at a specific month to simulate the interest savings and how much the loan term shortens.

items.q: Can it handle variable rate loans?
items.a: The calculator uses a fixed rate. For variable rate loans, recalculate the remaining schedule each time the rate changes.

whatIs.title: What is the Loan Repayment Scheduler?
whatIs.description: The Loan Repayment Scheduler generates a full month-by-month repayment table showing principal, interest, and remaining balance for your loan. It supports equal principal+interest (annuity), equal principal, and deferred repayment structures, and lets you simulate the interest savings from early repayment. Essential for planning mortgages, auto loans, or personal loans.

howToUse.title: How to use
items: 1. Choose principal (x10,000 KRW), annual rate, term and method (equal payment, equal principal, bullet, graduated). Results appear right away with defaults.
2. Enter a grace period in months if any — only interest is paid during it.
3. For hybrid loans, set the fixed period and the new rate under 'Rate change'.
4. Enter amount, timing and fee rate under 'Prepayment' to compare shortening the term vs lowering the payment.
5. Click a year to expand monthly rows, then download CSV, copy for Excel or print. Share the URL to reopen the same scenario.

items.q: Equal payment or equal principal?
items.a: Equal principal has the lowest total interest and shrinking payments but a higher start. Equal payment keeps every month the same. The 'methods compared' table shows the difference for your exact terms.

items.q: After prepaying, shorten the term or lower the payment?
items.a: For the same amount, shortening the term saves more interest; lowering the payment eases monthly cash flow. In Korea prepayment fees usually apply only within 3 years, pro-rated by the remaining period, and were cut to actual cost for contracts from 2025-01-13.

items.q: Can it handle variable rates?
items.a: Yes. Under 'Rate change', set the fixed period (e.g. 5 years) and the later rate; payments for the remaining term are recalculated from that point. Try a few expected rates to compare scenarios.

items.q: Why does it differ from my bank by a few won?
items.a: This tool accrues interest monthly (annual rate ÷ 12) and truncates below one won. Banks accrue daily, so each payment may differ slightly, and the last payment settles the remainder.

sources.title: Sources & notes
items: Moving prices are set freely by companies, not by government tariff. Figures are estimates based on 2025-2026 published quote ranges from moving platforms/companies, not official rates.
Son-eomneun days: lunar days ending in 9 or 0 (9, 10, 19, 20, 29, 30). Lunar conversion follows KASI.
KFTC standard terms for moving cargo: deposit, cancellation and damage compensation rules
Korea Consumer Agency Consumer24 (consumer.go.kr) and the 1372 hotline: moving disputes
Resident Registration Act Art. 16: move-in report within 14 days of moving
Housing Lease Protection Act: opposability from 0:00 the day after handover + move-in report; priority repayment with a fixed date stamp

Basis: within 20km, elevator, off-peak weekday

tips.title: Money-Saving Tips
items: Weekdays that avoid son-eomneun days, weekends and month end are cheapest. Pick low-% days on the calendar.
March and September are peak months and cost about 20% more. Aim for Jun-Aug or Nov-Jan if you can.
Get 3+ on-site (or video) quotes to avoid same-day extra charges.
Getting rid of furniture beforehand can drop the truck size a step (5t to 2.5t).
AC relocation and move-in cleaning are often cheaper when quoted separately.
Write in the contract whether ladder truck, elevator, crew size and packing materials are included.

whatIs.title: What is the Moving Cost Calculator?
whatIs.description: The Moving Cost Calculator estimates your total moving expenses based on the move type (full-service packing, semi-packing, or basic transport), home size, distance, and timing (peak vs. off-peak season). It incorporates the latest 2025–2026 market rates and includes optional costs for ladder trucks, storage moves, and appliance reinstallation.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Enter your current home size (pyeong or number of rooms) and select the move type.
2. Enter the origin and destination addresses or estimated distance.
3. Choose your preferred moving date — peak season and weekend surcharges apply automatically.
4. Check any add-ons (ladder truck, storage, AC reinstallation, etc.) to see the total estimated cost.

items.q: When is moving peak season?
items.a: March–April (spring) and September–October (fall) are peak seasons, with prices typically 20–30% higher. Month-end and weekends are also in high demand and may include surcharges.

items.q: What's the difference between full-service, semi, and basic moves?
items.a: Full-service includes packing, transport, and unpacking by the movers. Semi-service has movers pack large furniture/appliances only. Basic service covers transport only — you pack everything yourself.

items.q: Will the estimate match the actual quote?
items.a: This calculator uses average market rates as a reference. Actual costs depend on item types, access conditions, and the specific company. Always get at least 3 quotes to compare.

whatIs.title: What is the Moving Cost Calculator?
whatIs.description: Enter home size (amount of stuff), moving type, distance, floors with elevator/ladder truck and the date to estimate a min-typical-max moving cost. Moving prices are not government-regulated, so these figures are estimates based on 2025-2026 market quote ranges. Use it to budget before getting quotes and to check whether quotes are reasonable.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Pick your home size (pyeong or m²) to see the typical truck size (1 ton to two 5-ton trucks).
2. Choose the moving type (small truck/regular/semi-packed/full-packed) and storage days if needed.
3. Set distance, origin/destination floors and elevator/stairs/ladder truck.
4. Pick a date on the calendar to apply son-eomneun day, weekend, month-end and season surcharges. Lower % days are cheaper.
5. Enter received quotes in 'Compare quotes' and track tasks with the checklist.

items.q: What is a son-eomneun day, and is it really pricier?
items.a: Lunar days ending in 9 or 0 (9, 10, 19, 20, 29, 30) are traditionally considered free of spirits and good for moving. Demand concentrates, so prices run about 10% higher or bookings fill early. The calendar marks them with 'S'.

items.q: When is peak moving season?
items.a: March and September peak, with February, April and October also busy. Weekends/holidays and month end are pricier too. This calculator applies estimated surcharges of 5-30% (season), 5-20% (weekend/holiday), 5-20% (son-eomneun day) and 0-10% (month end), multiplied when they overlap.

items.q: How do small truck, regular, semi-packed and full-packed moves differ?
items.a: Small truck: a 1-ton driver mainly hauls. Regular: you pack, the mover hauls and places. Semi-packed: the mover packs kitchen/furniture/appliances, you pack clothes and small items. Full-packed: the mover does everything. A storage move keeps items in a warehouse between dates, adding another loading round and a storage fee.

items.q: What about deposits and cancellations?
items.a: The KFTC standard terms for moving cargo set compensation rules (forfeiting or doubling the deposit, etc.) depending on timing and who cancels. Check whether the mover uses the standard terms and confirm deposit, balance and extra charges in the contract.

items.q: What if something gets damaged?
items.a: Photograph furniture before work and report damage or loss immediately. Under the standard terms, the mover's liability may lapse if not notified within 30 days of delivery. If unresolved, call the 1372 consumer hotline.

items.q: Why do real quotes differ from this estimate?
items.a: Actual volume, access and parking, crew size, packing materials and local prices all matter. Get at least 3 quotes and compare them here. Quotes far below the estimated minimum often add same-day charges.

whatIs.title: What is the Car Maintenance Cost Calculator?
whatIs.description: The Car Maintenance Cost Calculator computes the total annual and monthly cost of owning a vehicle, covering insurance, vehicle tax, fuel, routine maintenance, and depreciation — all in one place. Enter your car model, year, fuel type, mileage, and fuel efficiency to get a realistic picture of total ownership costs. Useful for car purchase decisions and cost-reduction planning.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Enter vehicle details: model type, engine displacement (or EV), and model year.
2. Input annual mileage, fuel efficiency (or electricity consumption), and current fuel price.
3. Enter insurance type, estimated premium, and periodic service costs.
4. Review the breakdown of annual costs per category and the per-km cost.

tips.title: Pro Tips
items: EVs have lower fuel and maintenance costs, but factor in the higher purchase price and potential battery replacement costs for a full TCO comparison.
Vehicle tax in Korea is charged at ₩180–220 per cc of displacement (approximately ₩520,000/year for a 2,000cc sedan), payable in June and December.
Drivers with under 10,000 km/year can save on insurance premiums with a low-mileage special policy.

items.q: Why is the actual cost higher than expected?
items.a: Commonly overlooked costs like depreciation, car washes, parking fees, highway tolls, tire replacements, and unexpected repairs significantly inflate the real total. This calculator includes these items for a realistic figure.

items.q: Are EVs actually cheaper to own?
items.a: EVs are clearly cheaper in fuel and maintenance, but the higher purchase price, depreciation, and post-warranty battery replacement mean total cost of ownership (TCO) varies by model.

items.q: Does it support business vehicle expense calculations?
items.a: Yes. Business vehicles can deduct up to ₩15 million per year in expenses. Enter fuel usage and mileage to see the deductible amount based on business use percentage.

whatIs.title: What is the Tile Matching Game?
whatIs.description: The Tile Matching Game (Memory Game) is a concentration and memory training game where you flip cards to find matching pairs. Flip two cards at a time — if they match, they're removed; if not, they flip back. The goal is to clear all pairs with as few attempts as possible. Great for improving cognitive skills in players of all ages.

tips.title: Pro Tips
items: In the early game, flip cards freely while actively memorizing their positions — that stored knowledge is your greatest asset later.
Try to remember card positions using mental grid coordinates (row, column) for efficient recall.

whatIs.title: What is the Salary Comparison Tool?
whatIs.description: The Salary Comparison Tool lets you compare two or more salary conditions side by side, showing the exact difference in national pension, health insurance, employment insurance, and income tax deductions — and the resulting monthly take-home pay. When negotiating a job offer or comparing compensation packages, this tool shows you exactly how much pre-tax salary differences translate to in actual monthly income.

items.q: How much does a ₩5M salary difference translate to in take-home pay?
items.a: It varies by bracket, but for mid-range salaries (₩30M–50M), a ₩5M annual difference typically means about ₩300,000–400,000 more per month after taxes. The difference changes near tax bracket thresholds.

items.q: How are non-taxable items handled?

items.q: Does the number of dependents affect the tax?

whatIs.title: What is the YAML ↔ JSON Converter?
whatIs.description: The YAML ↔ JSON Converter is a developer tool that transforms YAML and JSON between each other in real time. Configuration files for tools like Kubernetes, Docker Compose, and GitHub Actions use YAML, while API responses use JSON — this tool bridges the gap seamlessly. File upload/download and key sorting are also supported.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Paste your YAML or JSON text into the input field, or upload a file.
2. Select the conversion direction (YAML → JSON or JSON → YAML).
3. Optionally enable 'Sort Keys' to receive alphabetically ordered output.
4. Copy the converted result or download it as a file.

items.q: What happens to YAML comments when converting to JSON?
items.a: JSON does not support comments, so all YAML comments (lines starting with #) are removed during conversion. They cannot be recovered if you convert back to YAML.

items.q: Are nested structures and arrays converted correctly?
items.a: Yes. YAML's indentation-based nesting and array notation (dash syntax) are accurately converted to JSON objects and arrays.

items.q: Are YAML anchors (&) and aliases (*) handled?
items.a: Yes. Anchors and aliases are resolved to their actual values before conversion, since JSON has no equivalent concept.

deadline.yearlyGift: Over 20M KRW, you may pay in annual installments for up to 5 years with collateral (interest added).
deadline.yearlyInherit: Over 20M KRW, you may pay in annual installments for up to 10 years (longer for family businesses) with collateral (interest added).
deadline.late: Missing the deadline loses the 3% filing credit and adds a non-filing penalty (generally 20%) and late-payment penalty (0.022% per day).

gift.title: Gift tax: the essentials
items: Gift deductions (10-year total): spouse 600M; parents/grandparents → adult child/grandchild 50M (minor 20M); child → parent 50M; other relatives (blood relatives within 6th degree, in-laws within 4th) 10M; none otherwise.
The limit is per receiver: gifts from father, mother and grandfather share one 50M limit per 10 years.
Gifts from the same giver (a parent/grandparent and their spouse count as one) within 10 years are added together for the rate, and gift tax already paid is credited.

Marriage/childbirth deduction: from 2024-01-01, an extra 100M for gifts from parents/grandparents within 2 years before/after marriage registration or within 2 years of a child's birth/adoption. Lifetime 100M combined, so up to 150M with the basic deduction.
Gifts that skip a generation (grandparent → grandchild) add 30% to the calculated tax, or 40% if the grandchild is a minor receiving over 2B. No surcharge if the parent has died.
Rates run in 5 brackets from 10% (tax base ≤100M) to 50% (over 3B); filing on time gives a 3% credit.

inheritance.title: Inheritance tax: it's all about deductions
items: Taxable value = estate − debts/dues − funeral costs + gifts to heirs within 10 years (5 years for non-heirs).

You get the larger of a 500M lump sum or 200M basic + personal deductions (50M per child, 10M per year until 19 for minors, 50M for those 65+, 10M per year of life expectancy for the disabled). A spouse inheriting alone cannot use the lump sum.
Spouse deduction: what the spouse actually receives, capped at the statutory share and 3B, with a 500M minimum even if they receive less. So with a spouse and children, usually up to 1B is tax-free.
Financial asset deduction: 20% of net financial assets (all if ≤20M, min 20M, max 200M).
Co-residence home deduction: a single home lived in with the deceased for 10+ years, inherited by a homeless child, up to 600M (net of mortgage).
Funeral costs: 5M without receipts, up to 10M with receipts, plus up to 5M for a columbarium/natural burial.
With prior gifts, deductions are capped at taxable value minus the prior gifts' tax base. Gift tax paid on them is credited.

burden.title: Gifts with debt (loan or lease deposit assumed)
items: If a home is gifted together with its loan or lease deposit, gift tax applies only to the value minus that debt.
The debt part is treated as a sale by the giver, so the giver owes capital gains tax on it. Favorable if the home qualifies for the one-home exemption; multi-home owners should check surcharges.
Between family members, the debt transfer must be proven. The receiver has to pay the interest and principal, and the NTS checks the source of repayment.
Acquisition tax is also split: purchase rates for the debt part, gift rates for the rest. This calculator covers only the gift tax part.

tips.title: Tax-saving tips
items: The gift deduction renews every 10 years: 20M at birth, then the limit at 10 and 20, can pass over 100M tax-free by age 30 (if the law stays the same).
Splitting the same amount among several people lets each use their own deduction and lower brackets.
If a marriage or birth is coming up, use the 100M marriage/childbirth deduction within the window.
Gifts made more than 10 years before death are not added back to the estate. Assets likely to appreciate are best gifted early.
Even with no tax due, keep transfer memos and a gift contract and file a return; it helps if the source of funds is questioned later.

items.q: How much can parents give a child tax-free?
items.a: 50M KRW per 10 years to an adult child, 20M to a minor, combined across all lineal ascendants. Within 2 years of marriage registration or a child's birth, the 100M marriage/childbirth deduction raises this to 150M.

items.q: How do I get the marriage/childbirth deduction?
items.a: Gifts from parents/grandparents on or after 2024-01-01 received within 2 years before/after marriage registration or within 2 years of a child's birth/adoption get an extra 100M deduction. Lifetime limit 100M combined; claim it on your gift tax return.

items.q: Do gifts from mom and dad get two deductions?
items.a: No. The deduction is per receiver and shared by all lineal ascendants (50M per 10 years). Parents are also treated as one giver for 10-year aggregation.

items.q: Up to what amount is there no inheritance tax?
items.a: With a spouse and children, the 500M lump sum plus the 500M minimum spouse deduction usually make 1B tax-free. With children only, 500M; a spouse inheriting alone gets 200M basic plus the spouse deduction (min 500M). Funeral, financial asset and co-residence home deductions may add more.

items.q: Was the child deduction raised to 500M?
items.a: No. The 2024 government bill (500M per child, 40% top rate) was voted down in the National Assembly on 2024-12-10, and the 2025 regular session did not pass any inheritance tax deduction/rate reform. As of October 2026, 50M per child, a 500M lump sum and 10–50% rates still apply.

items.q: Does gifting early reduce inheritance tax?
items.a: Gifts within 10 years of death (5 years for non-heirs) are added back at their value when gifted, with the gift tax paid credited. Gifts older than 10 years are not added back, so earlier is better.

items.q: When must I file?
items.a: Gift tax: within 3 months from the end of the month of the gift. Inheritance tax: within 6 months from the end of the month of death (9 months if living abroad). Filing on time gives a 3% credit; late filing adds penalties. You can file on Hometax.

items.q: Is it worse for grandparents to give directly to grandchildren?
items.a: Skipping a generation adds 30% (40% for a minor receiving over 2B). But going through the parent means paying gift tax twice, so giving directly is often cheaper. Compare both in the scenarios above.

tips.title: Tax Saving Tips
items: Utilize the 10-year gift deduction cycle to significantly reduce taxes over the long term.
Start gifting to children early for compound growth benefits and tax savings simultaneously.

Real estate is assessed at official price rather than market value, which may affect the actual burden.

It applies available deductions — basic deduction, spouse deduction, dependent deduction, and financial asset deduction — to calculate the final tax liability. It also helps you understand the tax rate structure and legitimate tax-reduction strategies.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Select the Inheritance Tax or Gift Tax tab.
2. Enter the total inherited or gifted asset value (broken down by real estate, financial assets, and other assets if applicable).
3. Check applicable deductions (spouse deduction, child deduction, financial asset deduction, etc.) and confirm the deductible amounts.
4. The taxable base, applicable tax rate, and final payable tax (after 3% filing deduction) are calculated automatically.

items.q: What is the inheritance tax filing deadline?
items.a: Inheritance tax must be filed and paid within 6 months from the end of the month in which the death occurred. If the deceased or heirs lived abroad, the deadline extends to 9 months.

items.q: What are the gift tax exemption limits?
items.a: Over a 10-year period: ₩600M from a spouse, ₩50M (adults) or ₩20M (minors) from lineal ascendants (parents/grandparents), ₩50M to lineal descendants (children), and ₩10M from other relatives.

items.q: Can inheritance and gift taxes overlap?
items.a: Yes. Gifts made to heirs within 10 years before death are added back into the taxable estate for inheritance tax purposes. Any gift tax already paid on those amounts is credited against the inheritance tax.

guide.title: Freelancer income tax essentials

withholding.title: 3.3% is prepaid tax
items: When business (personal service) income is paid, 3% income tax plus 0.3% local tax is withheld (Income Tax Act Art. 129).
In May of the next year you file and settle: overpaid tax is refunded, underpaid tax is due.
Lower income and more dependents make a refund more likely.
Income tax and local tax are each truncated below 10 KRW.

rates.title: Simple rate · Standard rate · Books
items: Personal services (940xxx) use the simple rate if last year's income was under 36M KRW, otherwise the standard rate. New businesses use the simple rate while this year's income is under 75M KRW.
Simple rate: income × rate counts as expenses; income above 40M uses a lower excess rate.
Standard rate: documented major expenses + income × standard rate, capped at 2.8× the simple-rate income (3.4× for double-entry filers).
Books (simplified ledger): real expenses count. With last year's income of 48M KRW or more, filing without books incurs a penalty.

deductions.title: Deductions
items: Basic deduction: 1.5M KRW per person including yourself.
Pension deduction: all national pension paid as a regional subscriber.
Yellow Umbrella: up to 6M (business income ≤40M), 4M (≤100M), 2M (>100M) from 2025 contributions.
Tax credits: 70K standard credit if you have no wage income; children 8–20: 250K for one, 550K for two, +400K each from the third.
Regional health insurance is not an income deduction; it is an expense when filing with books.

filing.title: Deadline and filing
items: File last year's income May 1–31. If the 31st is a weekend or holiday, the next business day.
File on Hometax or Sontax; simple-rate filers can use the pre-filled return.
Refunds usually arrive about a month after filing.
Late filing adds a 20% non-filing penalty plus late-payment interest.

guide.sources: Sources: Income Tax Act Arts. 55, 129, 59-2, 59-4, 81-5; Enforcement Decree Arts. 143, 145; Restriction of Special Taxation Act Art. 86-3; NTS 2025 standard/simple expense rate notice (Hometax business code lookup).

withholding.title: What is 3.3% Withholding?
items: When freelancers receive payment, 3% income tax + 0.3% local tax = 3.3% is withheld at source.
This is a 'prepaid tax' that gets settled during the annual tax filing in May.
If withholding > actual tax, you get a refund. If less, you pay the difference.
Income received without withholding must also be reported in the annual filing.

expenseRates.title: Expense Rate Selection Guide
items: Simple rate: Available if prior year revenue was under 24M KRW (non-professionals).
Standard rate: Applied to businesses above a certain size or those required to keep double-entry books.
Actual expenses: Enter real expenses with supporting documents for more accurate calculation.
Rates vary significantly by industry and are based on National Tax Service standards.

tips.title: Tax Saving Tips
items: Keep receipts for business expenses (transport, communication, equipment) to help reduce taxes.
National pension and health insurance are fully deductible - always include them in your filing.
If annual revenue exceeds 48M KRW, consider double-entry bookkeeping even if not required.
Freelancers can get up to 7M KRW tax credit through IRP (Individual Retirement Pension) contributions.

whatIs.title: What is the Freelancer Tax Calculator?
whatIs.description: A tool that calculates your actual comprehensive income tax from 3.3% withholding income, helping you predict whether you'll receive a refund or owe additional tax at year-end. It supports both standard expense rates (by industry) and actual documented expenses, so you can compare tax strategies. Use it before filing to avoid surprise tax bills.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Enter your total annual income (before withholding).
2. Select the expense input method — standard expense rate (auto by industry), standard flat rate, or enter actual expenses directly.
3. Enter personal deductions: number of dependents, spouse deduction, etc.
4. Click 'Calculate' to see estimated income tax, withheld amount (3.3%), and net refund or additional payment.

items.q: What is the 3.3% withholding tax?
items.a: It's a combined withholding rate of 3% income tax + 0.3% local income tax. The client (payer) deducts this before paying you.

items.q: Which is better: standard expense rate or actual expenses?
items.a: If your income is modest and actual expenses are low, the standard rate is easier. If you have high verifiable expenses, claiming actual costs often reduces your tax more. Use this calculator to compare both scenarios.

items.q: Do I have to file a comprehensive income tax return in May?
items.a: Yes. Freelancers with income must file a comprehensive income tax return in May each year, even if tax was already withheld. The May filing is the final reconciliation.

items: CGNAT (RFC 6598): 100.64.0.0/10 — carrier NAT space. Looks private but can collide if used internally.
Loopback 127.0.0.0/8, link-local 169.254.0.0/16 (self-assigned when DHCP fails)

vlsm.title: VLSM & summarization tips
items: Allocate the largest requirement first so every block lands on its boundary with no gaps.
Pick the smallest power-of-two block holding hosts + 2 (network and broadcast). 60 hosts → /26 (62).
Router-to-router links use /30 (2 hosts) or an RFC 3021 /31.
Use the minimal aggregate for exact route summaries; check the extra addresses before using a single supernet.

basics.title: Subnet Basics
items: A subnet divides a larger network into smaller segments.
The subnet mask separates the network portion from the host portion of an IP address.
The network address is the first address in the subnet (all host bits are 0).
The broadcast address is the last address in the subnet (all host bits are 1).
Usable hosts = total addresses - 2 (network + broadcast), except /31 = 2 (RFC 3021) and /32 = 1.

cidr.title: CIDR Notation
items: /24 = subnet mask 255.255.255.0 (254 hosts)
/8 = subnet mask 255.0.0.0 (~16.7 million hosts)
Higher numbers mean smaller networks; lower numbers mean larger networks.

It's used by network engineers, server admins, and students to quickly validate IP designs and subnetting. Also useful when configuring AWS VPC CIDR blocks or firewall rules.

tips.title: Pro Tips
items: /24 gives 256 IPs (254 usable), /16 gives 65,536 IPs — commonly used in cloud VPC design.
Always verify CIDR rules before entering them in AWS or GCP security groups to avoid unintended IP access.
/26 (62 hosts) or /27 (30 hosts) are typical for per-department VLAN segmentation.

items.q: What is CIDR?
items.a: CIDR stands for Classless Inter-Domain Routing. It represents an IP address and network size in the format '192.168.1.0/24'. A larger number after the slash means a smaller network.

items.q: Can I use the network or broadcast address for hosts?
items.a: No. The first IP (network address) and last IP (broadcast) in each subnet cannot be assigned to hosts. The usable host count is total IPs minus 2.

items.q: Does this support IPv6?
items.a: Currently only IPv4 is supported. For IPv6 subnetting, use a dedicated tool or refer to RFC 4291.

items.q: What is CIDR?
items.a: Classless Inter-Domain Routing writes an address and its network size as '192.168.1.0/24'. The larger the number after the slash, the smaller the network.

items.q: Can the network and broadcast addresses be used?
items.a: In a normal subnet the first (network) and last (broadcast) addresses can't be assigned to hosts, so usable hosts = total - 2. Exceptions: a /31 uses both addresses (RFC 3021) and a /32 is a single host.

htmlEntityConverter.title: HTML Entity Converter
htmlEntityConverter.description: Encode HTML special characters to entity codes or decode entities back to original characters.

what.title: What are HTML Entities?
items: HTML entities are escape codes used to safely represent special characters in HTML.
Characters like & < > " ' must be encoded as they conflict with HTML syntax.
Encoding user input is critical for preventing XSS (Cross-Site Scripting) attacks.

formats.title: Encoding Format Comparison
items: Named: © — Human-readable but only supports predefined characters
Decimal: © — Unicode code point in decimal, supports all characters
Hex: © — Unicode code point in hexadecimal, supports all characters
Named format only covers about 250 predefined entities.

usage.title: Usage Tips
items: Encoding is needed when embedding special characters in JavaScript or CSS within HTML.
Named entities have the best compatibility in HTML email templates.
When embedding HTML in JSON, also escape " and \ characters.
In RSS/XML feeds, & < > " ' are the 5 mandatory encoding targets.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Select the conversion direction — 'Characters → Entities (encode)' or 'Entities → Characters (decode)'.
2. Paste the text you want to convert into the input field.
3. Check the output field and use the copy button to save to clipboard.
4. Use 'All characters' or 'Special characters only' options to adjust the conversion scope.

tips.title: Pro Tips
items: Always encode user-supplied content before inserting it into HTML templates to prevent XSS attacks.
The 5 characters <, >, &, ", and ' must always be escaped as HTML entities.
Converting special characters to entities in HTML email bodies improves compatibility across email clients.

items.q: How is HTML entity encoding different from URL encoding?
items.a: HTML entities (e.g., &) represent special characters within HTML documents. URL encoding (e.g., %26) safely encodes special characters in URLs. They serve different contexts.

items.q: What's the difference between numeric (&#number;) and named (&) entities?
items.a: Both work the same way. Named entities (e.g., &) are more readable. Numeric entities (e.g., &) can represent any Unicode character, useful when no named entity exists.

items.q: Can Korean characters be converted to entities?
items.a: Yes, Korean characters can be expressed as numeric Unicode entities (e.g., 한). However, with modern UTF-8 encoding being standard, converting Korean to entities is rarely necessary.

guide.title: How it works
guide.formula: Average pace (seconds/km) = finish time (seconds) ÷ distance (km), and speed (km/h) = 3,600 ÷ pace (seconds/km). To calculate time from pace, multiply distance by pace.
guide.splits: Each split is calculated from the unrounded time and distance, rather than from the displayed rounded pace. The final row shows the exact finish distance once.

exerciseCalorie.source: MET source: 2024 Compendium of Physical Activities (code {code})

eq.title: In food terms (approx.)
eq.note: Food calories are rough per-serving values and vary widely by product and recipe. MET estimates are for an average adult; individual results can differ by ±20% or more.

adv.show: + Adjust for sex, age and height (advanced)
adv.note: Estimates your resting metabolic rate (RMR) with the Harris-Benedict equation to compute a corrected MET and your personal net burn.
adv.explain: Standard METs assume a resting rate of 3.5 ml/kg/min. If your actual RMR is lower (common for women, older adults and heavier people), the same activity is a higher intensity for you (corrected MET), and the calories burned on top of rest are closer to gross burn minus your own RMR.

steps.note: Stride = height × 0.415 (men) / 0.413 (women); time = distance ÷ {kmh} km/h; calories = MET {met} × weight × time. Real stride varies with speed, leg length and terrain, and pedometers also count slow everyday steps, so this can overestimate.

howItWorks.title: How it works
items: Gross calories (kcal) = MET × weight (kg) × time (h). 1 MET is the energy of sitting quietly (3.5 ml O₂/kg/min, about 1 kcal/kg/h).
MET values come from the 2024 Adult Compendium of Physical Activities (Herrmann et al., 2024). E.g. running 8 km/h (12030) 8.5, brisk walking (17200) 4.8, rope skipping (02068) 11.0.
Net burn = (MET − 1) × weight × time: the extra calories on top of what you would have burned at rest.
Advanced: your resting rate is estimated with Harris-Benedict and corrected MET = MET × 3.5 ÷ your RMR (ml/kg/min), following the Compendium's 'Corrected METs' method.
Steps mode estimates stride from height (height × 0.415), derives distance and time, then applies the walking MET for the chosen pace.

comparison.title: Versus smartwatches and gym machines
items: Smartwatches use heart rate, age and sex, so values for the same workout can differ; heart-rate data reflects your condition better.
Treadmill/bike displays use a default weight unless you enter yours, so they can be far off.
MET estimates are a standard anyone can use without a device — good for comparing activities and planning.

formula.title: Calorie Formula
items: Calories (kcal) = MET × weight (kg) × time (hours)
Example: 70kg, 30min jogging (MET 7.0) → 7.0 × 70 × 0.5 = 245kcal
1kg body fat ≈ 7,700 kcal (basis for fat conversion)
1 bowl of rice ≈ 300 kcal

tips.title: Effective Exercise Tips
items: High-intensity exercises (running, jump rope) burn more calories in the same time.
Strength training increases metabolic rate even after exercise (EPOC effect).
Combining cardio and strength training is effective for weight loss and muscle maintenance.
Fasted cardio may help fat burning, but high intensity risks muscle loss.

whatIs.title: What is the Exercise Calorie Calculator?
whatIs.description: A tool that calculates precise calorie burn by inputting your body weight and exercise duration, using the MET (Metabolic Equivalent of Task) formula. It supports 40+ exercises including walking, running, swimming, and cycling, and accounts for how heavier individuals burn more calories for the same activity. Use it for diet planning or tracking daily activity levels.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Enter your body weight (kg) — heavier people burn more calories for the same exercise.
2. Select or search for the exercise type (e.g., walking, running, swimming, yoga).
3. Enter the duration in minutes.
4. View the calorie burn result and the estimated fat burned (in grams).

items.q: What is a MET value?
items.a: MET stands for Metabolic Equivalent of Task. Resting energy expenditure (3.5 ml O₂/kg/min) is defined as 1 MET. Light walking is about MET 3.5; running at 10 km/h is about MET 10.

items.q: Why does the result differ from my smartwatch?
items.a: Smartwatches incorporate heart rate, age, gender, and proprietary algorithms. MET-based calculations are standardized estimates with ±10–15% variance.

items.q: How much exercise is needed to burn 1 kg of fat?
items.a: 1 kg of fat equals approximately 7,700 kcal. For example, a 70 kg person running (burning ~6 kcal/min) would need about 21 hours. Combining exercise with dietary control is far more efficient.

whatIs.title: What is the Exercise Calorie Calculator?
whatIs.description: A tool that estimates calories burned from your weight and exercise time using the MET formula. MET values come from the 2024 Adult Compendium of Physical Activities and cover 70+ activities: walking and running by speed, cycling, swimming strokes, gym work, ball sports, dance and housework. It also shows how long it takes to burn off a food, converts steps to distance and calories, and totals a weekly plan with a body-fat estimate.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Enter your body weight (kg) — heavier people burn more for the same activity.
2. Search or use the category chips to pick an activity, then set the time with the slider. Results update instantly.
3. In 'Burn this food', pick a food (or enter kcal) to compare the time needed per activity.
4. 'Steps' estimates stride from height and converts steps to distance, time and calories.
5. 'Weekly plan' totals several sessions into weekly and monthly burn plus a body-fat estimate. Share via link or image.

items.q: What is a MET value?
items.a: Resting oxygen use (3.5 ml/kg/min) is defined as 1 MET, and activity intensity is expressed as a multiple of it. In the 2024 Compendium, moderate walking (4.5–5.5 km/h) is 3.8, running at 10 km/h is 9.3 and rope skipping is 11.0.

items.q: Why does the result differ from my smartwatch?
items.a: Smartwatches use heart rate, age and sex and apply their own algorithms. MET estimates are for an average adult and can differ by about ±20%. Turn on the advanced adjustment (sex, age, height) to see net burn based on your own resting rate.

items.q: How much exercise does it take to lose 1 kg of fat?
items.a: 1 kg of body fat is roughly 7,700 kcal. A 70 kg person running at 8 km/h (MET 8.5, about 9.9 kcal/min) would need about 13 hours. Real-world loss is often smaller due to appetite and metabolic adaptation, so combine exercise with diet.

how.title: How to use
items: Press Start and allow microphone access. Noise is measured every 0.1 s.
The average is the equivalent level (Leq), an energy average, the same method legal limits use.
Choose the Neighbor noise tab to compare against the day/night limit for the current time and log every exceedance automatically.
Stop to save or share a result card, and export the exceedance log as CSV.

tips.title: Measuring accurately
items: Place the phone in the middle of the room, away from walls and the ceiling, not on the floor or furniture. For floor noise, use the room where the upstairs noise is loudest.
Make sure the case doesn't cover the microphone, and switch off nearby fans or air conditioners.
For overnight logging, keep the charger connected, the screen on (wake lock is applied automatically) and the browser in the foreground. Most phones stop the microphone when the screen locks.
If you have a sound level meter or a trusted app, calibrate once with Microphone calibration to make later readings far more reliable.

whatIs.title: What is the Noise Meter?
whatIs.description: A tool that measures ambient noise levels in real-time in decibels (dB) using your smartphone or PC microphone. No app installation required — works directly in the browser. Use it for checking everyday noise levels, assessing work environments, measuring floor-noise complaints, or monitoring background noise in music practice rooms, libraries, and offices.

items.q: Is microphone permission required?
items.a: Yes, microphone access is needed for measurement. Click 'Allow' when the browser requests permission. You can revoke the permission in browser settings after use.

items.q: Can the result differ from a professional sound level meter?
items.a: Yes. Smartphone microphones are less precise than professional meters and have different frequency response characteristics. Use this tool for relative noise assessment and everyday checks. For legally required measurements, use calibrated professional equipment.

items.q: What dB level counts as noisy?
items.a: Below 40 dB is quiet (library-like); 60 dB is normal conversation; 80 dB is a loud office; 90 dB+ risks hearing damage. Korean apartment noise standards are 43 dB (daytime) / 38 dB (nighttime).

whatIs.title: What is the Noise Meter?
whatIs.description: A tool that measures ambient noise levels in real-time in decibels (dB) using your smartphone or PC microphone. No app installation required — works directly in the browser. Use it for checking everyday noise levels, assessing work environments, measuring floor-noise complaints, or monitoring background noise in music practice rooms, libraries, and offices.

items.q: How accurate is a phone noise meter?
items.a: Phone microphones vary in sensitivity and frequency response, so uncalibrated readings can be off by ±5–10dB. Comparing readings from the same device (last night vs tonight) works well, but absolute values are estimates. If you have a sound level meter, use Microphone calibration to match it.

items.q: What are the Korean floor-noise limits?
items.a: Under the Rules on the Scope and Standards of Floor Noise in Apartment Buildings (effective Jan 2, 2023), impact noise (footsteps, jumping) is limited to a 1-minute Leq of 39dB by day and 34dB at night, and a maximum level of 57dB by day and 52dB at night. The maximum limit counts as exceeded when it is crossed 3 or more times in an hour. Airborne noise (TV, audio) uses a 5-minute Leq of 45dB day / 40dB night. Buildings approved before June 30, 2005 add 2dB from 2025.

items.q: Can I use this log for an official complaint or lawsuit?
items.a: Phone measurements are not legal evidence. For official measurement use the Floor Noise Neighbor Center (1661-2642), your local government's meter lending, or an accredited firm. A log of when and how often noise occurred (CSV) plus clips can still help explain the situation to building management or counselors.

items.q: How is Leq different from a normal average?
items.a: Decibels are logarithmic, so a plain average understates loud moments. Equivalent level (Leq) averages sound energy: half 60dB and half 70dB gives about 67.4dB, not 65dB. Legal limits use this method.

items.q: What does dB(A) mean?
items.a: Human ears are less sensitive to low and very high frequencies. A-weighting models that, and most noise regulations use dB(A). This tool applies an A-weighting filter to the microphone signal.

items.q: Is audio recorded or uploaded?
items.a: No. Everything is computed in your browser. Only when you enable clip recording in neighbor-noise mode are short clips kept in this device's memory, and they become files only when you press Save.

noiseMeter.disclaimer: Readings are uncalibrated phone/PC microphone estimates, not legal measurements. For official assessment of floor-noise disputes, contact the Floor Noise Neighbor Center (1661-2642) or an accredited measurement firm.

calibration.title: How to Calibrate
items: Every phone sensor has its own offset of about 0.5–2°, so calibrate once for precise work.
Place the phone in the position you will measure in (flat or standing on an edge) and tap 'Calibrate'.
Turn the phone 180° in the same spot and tap 'Second reading'. The average of the two is the sensor offset, so it works even if the surface is not level.
Calibration is saved on this device separately for flat and upright positions; clear it with 'Reset calibration'.
Check: after calibrating, turning the phone 180° in the same spot should show the same angle with only the high side swapped.

level.title: Using the Level
items: Surface: lay the phone screen-up on the surface. Like a real bubble, it moves to the high side, and the high side is also shown in text.
Edge: stand the phone up and hold an edge against a shelf, frame or door frame. Portrait/landscape is detected automatically.
Within ±0.2° the display turns blue and says 'Level'; Android phones also give a short vibration.
Slope (%) is tan(angle)×100 and rise per meter (mm) is tan(angle)×1000. Example: 1° ≈ 1.7% ≈ 17.5 mm/m.
To measure a ramp or roof angle, lay the phone on it in Surface mode, read 'Total tilt', and use 'Hold' to read it after lifting the phone.

compass.title: Compass Usage
items: Hold the phone flat to see the heading and direction the top of the screen points to.
The blue N mark and needle point to magnetic north.
Browsers that do not provide a true-north heading show a notice instead of a heading.
Keep away from magnets, metal and electronics for accuracy.

whatIs.title: What is the Spirit Level & Compass?
whatIs.description: A tool that uses your smartphone's built-in gyroscope, accelerometer, and magnetometer to measure tilt angle (level/plumb) and compass bearing in real-time. No separate tool needed — just use your smartphone for everyday DIY tasks like assembling furniture, hanging picture frames, installing shelves, or leveling a camera.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Place your smartphone flat and the tilt angle is shown in real-time.
2. When perfectly level, the bubble in the center turns green.
3. Switch to the compass tab to view current bearing (N/S/E/W) and angle.
4. If calibration is needed, slowly move the phone in a figure-8 motion.

tips.title: Pro Tips
items: Keep the compass away from metal objects and electronics for more accurate bearing readings.
Thick phone cases or cases with magnets may reduce compass accuracy.
Use the level while taking photos to get a straight horizon without tilted shots.

items.q: Does it work on both iOS and Android?
items.a: Yes, it works on most smartphones with a gyroscope and magnetometer. Some budget devices may lack sensors, limiting compass functionality.

items.q: How accurate is the level reading?
items.a: Typically ±1–2 degrees depending on the device. Sufficient for DIY tasks; use a professional laser level for precision construction work.

items.q: What if the sensor gives erratic readings?
items.a: Refresh the page or place the phone on a flat surface and restart. For compass errors, calibrate by slowly rotating the phone in a figure-8 pattern.

items.q: Does it work on both iOS and Android?

items.q: How accurate is the level reading?
items.a: It displays 0.1° steps, but without calibration phones can be off by 1–2°. Reversal calibration (two readings in the same spot, turned 180°) usually brings this within 0.5°. Use a professional level for precision construction.

items.q: What if the sensor gives erratic readings?
items.a: Refresh the page and start again. If level readings look off, use Calibrate; for compass errors, slowly move the phone in a figure-8 to recalibrate the phone's own compass.

metronome.title: Metronome
metronome.description: An accurate metronome for piano, guitar, drums and choir. Time signatures, subdivisions, per-beat accents, tap tempo, speed trainer and random mute.

howToUse.title: How to use
items: Start/stop with the play button or the Space key.
Change BPM with ±1/±5, the slider or ↑↓ (Shift for ±5). Changes apply instantly while playing.
Tap along 4+ times with Tap Tempo (T key) to get the average BPM. Pausing 2 seconds starts a new measurement.
Pick a time signature and subdivision (8ths, triplets, 16ths, swing), then tap beat dots to set accent/normal/mute.
In Practice tools, enable the speed trainer, random mute or auto stop, and add a count-in bar.

howItWorks.title: Accuracy and how it works
items: A 25 ms timer schedules clicks due in the next ~0.1 s on the AudioContext clock (the A Tale of Two Clocks pattern).
Click timing comes from the audio hardware clock, so rendering or other work cannot shift the intervals.
The beat display is drawn when the click is actually heard (output latency compensated).
While playing it requests a screen wake lock, and extends the schedule window to 1.5 s when the tab is in the background.

how.title: How to Use
items: Press the play button to start the metronome.
Use +/- buttons or the slider to adjust BPM.
Tap the Tap Tempo button rhythmically to auto-detect BPM.
Select a time signature (2/4, 3/4, 4/4, 6/8) to change the beat pattern.
Enable vibration feedback on mobile devices for haptic beats.

tempos.title: Classical Tempo Markings
items: Grave: ~40 BPM - Very slow, solemn
Largo: ~50 BPM - Slow, broad
Adagio: ~66 BPM - Slow, comfortable
Andante: ~76 BPM - Walking pace
Moderato: ~108 BPM - Moderate speed
Allegro: ~132 BPM - Fast, lively
Vivace: ~160 BPM - Lively, fast
Presto: ~184 BPM - Very fast

whatIs.title: What is the Metronome?
whatIs.description: An online metronome that provides a steady beat for music practice. Adjust BPM (beats per minute), set time signatures like 4/4 or 3/4, and use the tap function to measure the tempo of any song. Works for all instruments — piano, guitar, drums, voice, and dance practice. No installation required; runs directly in your browser.

tips.title: Pro Tips
items: When learning a new piece, start at 70–80% of your target BPM and gradually increase as accuracy improves.
Use the tap tempo feature to measure the BPM of any song you want to play along with.
Use accent settings to emphasize backbeats (beats 2 and 4) for a more natural groove feel.

items.q: The metronome seems to drift — is this normal?
items.a: With many open browser tabs or high system load, timing can become slightly irregular. Close unnecessary tabs or enable vibration mode for a more consistent beat feel.

items.q: What BPM range is supported?
items.a: Generally 20 BPM (very slow Largo) to 240 BPM (very fast Prestissimo).

items.q: What are the BPM ranges for classical tempo markings?
items.a: Largo (40–60), Adagio (66–76), Andante (76–108), Moderato (108–120), Allegro (120–156), Presto (168–200) are the commonly accepted BPM ranges.

whatIs.title: What is a metronome?
whatIs.description: A practice tool that clicks at a steady tempo. This metronome schedules clicks ahead on the audio clock, so timing stays steady even if the page stutters. Time signatures, subdivisions, per-beat accents, a speed trainer and random mute cover piano, guitar, drums and choir practice.

tips.title: Tips by instrument
items: Piano: start new pieces at 60-70% of the target tempo and let the speed trainer add 2-4 BPM every 4 bars.
Guitar: turn on 16ths and match each alternate pick stroke to a click for an even picking hand.
Drums: mute beats 1 and 3 to feel the backbeat, and use random mute to hold time on your own.
Choir: add a one-bar count-in, and turn on screen flash to share the beat without sound.

items.q: What does BPM count in 6/8?
items.a: The note value in the bottom number. In 6/8 each click is an eighth note, with accents on 1 and 4. For dotted quarter = 60, set 180 BPM.

items.q: No sound on iPhone
items.a: iOS silences web audio when the ring/silent switch is on. Turn silent mode off and press play again.

items.q: Does it keep playing in another tab?
items.a: In most browsers, yes. Power saving or browser policies may delay tempo changes or pause it in the background, so keep this tab in front for the most accurate practice.

items.q: Can I save or share settings?
items.a: Settings are saved automatically in this browser. The share link contains BPM, time signature, accents, subdivision and trainer settings so students or choir members get the exact same setup.

benefits.title: Benefits of White Noise
items: Masks ambient noise to improve sleep quality
Helps improve focus and productivity
Used for baby sleep and tinnitus relief

tips.title: Tips for Effective Use
items: Pink/brown noise is more effective for sleep than white noise.
Keep volume below conversation level (~60dB).
Set a sleep timer to avoid playing all night.

whatIs.title: What is the White Noise Generator?
whatIs.description: A browser-based tool that generates background sounds to aid sleep, focus, and meditation. It offers white noise along with brown noise, rain, waves, and other nature sounds. A sleep timer lets it stop automatically after a set period. Using earphones enhances the ambient noise-masking effect.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Select your preferred sound type (white noise, brown noise, rain, ocean waves, etc.).
2. Adjust the volume slider to a comfortable level.
3. For sleep use, set a timer for auto-stop.
4. Press play. Using earphones is recommended for best results.

items.q: What's the difference between white, pink, and brown noise?
items.a: White noise has equal energy across all frequencies (like TV static). Pink noise emphasizes lower frequencies naturally (wind, waterfall). Brown noise is deeper and bass-heavy (thunder, ocean waves).

items.q: Which noise type is best for sleep?
items.a: Individual preference varies, but research suggests brown noise and rain sounds tend to be effective for sleep induction. Try different types to find what works best for you.

items.q: Is long-term use safe for hearing?
items.a: At moderate volume (below 60–70 dB) it's safe. Keep the volume low, especially with earphones. Prolonged exposure above 85 dB carries a risk of hearing damage.

pensionCalculator.title: National Pension Calculator
pensionCalculator.description: Estimate your Korean National Pension (NPS) monthly benefit, total contributions, and income replacement rate.
pensionCalculator.notice: This calculator provides estimates based on 2024 Korean NPS guidelines. Actual benefits may vary based on contribution history, credits, and other factors.

formula.title: Pension Calculation Formula
items: Basic Pension = 1.2 × (A + B) × (contribution months / 480)
A value = average income of all subscribers in the 3 years before pension eligibility (~2.86M KRW in 2024)
B value = average standard monthly income during your contribution period
5% additional payment for every 12 months beyond 20 years of contributions
This calculator assumes your current income remains constant throughout

contribution.title: Contribution Rate Guide
items: Total contribution rate: 9% of income
Employee share: 4.5%
Employer share: 4.5%
Self-employed pay the full 9%
2024 upper income limit: 6.17M KRW per month

tips.title: How to Maximize Your Pension
items: Longer contribution periods increase your benefit (minimum 10 years, up to 40 years)
Voluntary or continued voluntary enrollment can extend your contribution period
Use the retroactive payment system to pay premiums for exemption periods

whatIs.title: What is the National Pension Calculator?

items: 1. Enter your current age and enrollment start year (or total contribution period).

items.q: Why is the pension age rising?
items.a: Those born before 1953 receive benefits from age 60. Those born 1969 or later receive benefits from age 65, with gradual phase-in in between. This is a financial stability measure due to aging demographics.

items.q: How much is deducted for early pension?
items.a: Each year you claim early, benefits are permanently reduced by 6%. Claiming 5 years early means a 30% reduction for life.

items.q: What happens if I stop paying?
items.a: Your eventual benefit decreases. You must contribute for at least 10 years (120 months) to receive pension payments. Otherwise, a lump-sum refund is given.
