cssUnitConverter.inputHint: You can type the unit too, e.g. 24px or 1.5rem. ↑/↓ ±1, Shift ±10, Alt ±0.1
cssUnitConverter.inputError: Enter a number or number + unit (e.g. 24px).
cssUnitConverter.physicalNote: In CSS, 1in is always exactly 96px. It may not match a ruler held to your screen; it matches real size only in print.
cssUnitConverter.approxNote: ch and ex depend on the font and can't be computed exactly, so they use the CSS spec fallback (0.5em). % is relative to font-size.
cssUnitConverter.bulkDesc: Paste CSS to convert px values to rem based on a {root}px root font size. Values inside comments, url() and strings are left untouched.
cssUnitConverter.bulkNote: rem/em inside media queries use the browser's default font size (usually 16px), not the html font size. If you changed the root font size, keeping @media lines in px is safer.
cssUnitConverter.clampDesc: Builds a clamp() expression that is the min size at the min viewport and the max size at the max viewport, scaling linearly in between. It mixes in rem so user font-size preferences still apply.
cssUnitConverter.clampError: Sizes must be greater than 0 and the max viewport width must exceed the min viewport width.
cssUnitConverter.tableDesc: Common px values converted to rem. Click a cell to copy the rem value. The table follows the root font size setting.
cssUnitConverter.title: CSS Unit Converter
cssUnitConverter.description: Convert a value to 16 CSS units at once (px, rem, em, vw, vh, pt, cm and more), bulk-convert CSS px→rem, and generate clamp() fluid type.
cssUnitConverter.quickRefDesc: Quick reference table for frequently used CSS unit conversions.
quickRefRows: min rem, intercept rem + slope vw, max rem
guideAbsoluteItems: px (pixels): A CSS pixel is a 'reference pixel', not a device pixel. On retina screens 1px is drawn with 2–3 physical pixels.
in / pt / pc: 1in = 96px = 72pt = 6pc, so 1pt = 4/3px (≈1.333px) and 1pc = 16px, always.
cm / mm / Q: Based on 1in = 2.54cm, so 1cm ≈ 37.795px, 1mm ≈ 3.78px, 1Q = 0.25mm. Mostly used in print CSS (@media print).
guideRelativeItems: rem: Relative to the root (<html>) font size, usually 16px by default. Scales with the user's font settings — good for accessibility.
em: Relative to the element's own font size (for font-size itself, the parent's). Compounds when nested — use carefully.
% (percent): The reference depends on the property: font-size uses the parent font size, width uses the containing block width. This tool's % is font-size based.
ch / ex: Based on the width of '0' and the x-height. They vary by font, so this tool approximates with the spec fallback (0.5em). Handy for line length (max-width: 65ch).
guideViewportItems: vw / vh: 1% of viewport width/height. 100vw includes the vertical scrollbar, which can cause horizontal scrolling.
vmin / vmax: 1% of the smaller/larger side. Useful to keep proportions regardless of orientation.
svh / lvh / dvh: Fix the mobile address bar issue where 100vh is taller than the visible screen. Prefer 100dvh (or 100svh) for full-screen sections.
Sizing text with vw alone ignores user zoom and font settings. Mix in rem, e.g. clamp(min rem, rem + vw, max rem).
guideTipsItems: Font sizes: Use rem — respects user browser settings and improves accessibility.
Responsive font sizes: Use the clamp() generator to scale smoothly between a min and max size without media queries.
Porting px designs: Paste CSS into the bulk tab and keep the 1px option on for borders.
Component inner spacing: Use em — scales with the component's font size.
Media query breakpoints: Use px or em — em follows user font preferences but ignores the html font size.
Print CSS: Use pt, cm, mm — guarantees physical dimensions when printed.

u.targetPost: If you already have diabetes, the target (Korean Diabetes Association): below {a} {u} 2 hours after meals

u.diagNote: Diabetes is never diagnosed from a single reading. It must be confirmed by a repeat test or another test, and home meters are meant for monitoring. If you are worried, talk to a clinician.

hypo.title: Treating a low: the 15-15 rule
steps: Take 15 g of sugar: about 1/2–3/4 cup (120–175 mL) of juice or regular soda, 1 tablespoon of sugar or honey, or 3–4 hard candies.
Recheck after 15 minutes.
If it is still below 70 mg/dL (3.9 mmol/L), repeat once more.
Once recovered, eat a snack if your next meal is a long way off, to prevent another low.
hypo.emergency: If the person is confused or cannot swallow, do not force food — call emergency services right away. Repeated lows without diabetes should be checked by a doctor.

a1c.title: HbA1c result and average glucose
a1c.label: HbA1c
a1c.crit: Cutoffs: normal below 5.7% · prediabetes 5.7–6.4% · diabetes 6.5% or higher
a1c.formula: eAG (mg/dL) = 28.7 × HbA1c − 46.7 (ADAG study). Reflects average glucose over the past 2–3 months.
a1c.target: If you already have diabetes, a typical target is below 6.5% (Korean Diabetes Association, type 2) or below 7% (ADA), individualized by your clinician based on age and hypoglycemia risk.

u.tirNote: 70–180 mg/dL is the continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) target range for people with diabetes; spending 70%+ of time in it is the international consensus goal. For fingerstick logs, use it only as a reference.

g.title: Blood sugar cutoffs at a glance
g.tableUnit: Units: mg/dL. Divide by 18.016 for mmol/L (e.g. 126 mg/dL ≈ 7.0 mmol/L).
diagItems: Without symptoms, one reading is not a diagnosis. A repeat test on another day, or a second test, must also be over the cutoff.
A random glucose of 200 mg/dL or higher with strong thirst, frequent urination or unexplained weight loss meets the criteria on its own.
Under ISO 15197, a home meter passes if 95% of results fall within ±15% of the true value (±15 mg/dL below 100 mg/dL), so diagnosis uses lab tests.
Prediabetes carries a high risk of progressing to diabetes, but weight loss, exercise and diet changes can cut that risk substantially.
hypoItems: Below 70 mg/dL is hypoglycemia (level 1); below 54 mg/dL needs immediate action (level 2).
Common symptoms are cold sweat, shaking, a pounding heart, hunger and dizziness; severe lows can cause confusion.
Take extra care with insulin or sulfonylureas, and discuss any low with your clinician to find the cause.
tipsItems: Measure fasting glucose after at least 8 hours without food, usually before breakfast.
Measure post-meal glucose 2 hours after you started eating.
Wash and fully dry your hands first — leftover sugar such as fruit juice can raise the reading.
Note food, exercise and medication alongside each reading to spot patterns.
Export to CSV and show it to your clinician.
sources: Korean Diabetes Association, 2023 Clinical Practice Guidelines for Diabetes (diagnosis, glycemic targets, hypoglycemia)
American Diabetes Association, Standards of Care in Diabetes — Diagnosis and Classification / Glycemic Goals and Hypoglycemia
Nathan DM et al., Diabetes Care 2008 (ADAG: HbA1c → estimated average glucose)
Battelino T et al., Diabetes Care 2019 (international consensus on CGM time in range)

whatIs.title: What is the Unicode Text Styler?
whatIs.description: A tool that converts regular English text into various Unicode styles — mathematical symbols, double-struck, fraktur, bold, italic, and more. Since it uses actual Unicode code points rather than font changes, you can copy and paste the styled text into any platform that renders Unicode: Instagram, X (Twitter), KakaoTalk, LinkedIn profiles, and game nicknames.

items.q: Why doesn't Korean text convert?
items.a: This tool only supports Latin (English) character conversion. The Unicode mathematical character blocks are only defined for Latin letters. For Korean text decoration, use emojis or dedicated font apps.

items.q: The converted text looks broken on some platforms
items.a: If a platform or device doesn't include fonts covering the Unicode mathematical symbol range, characters may display as □ or ?. Modern iOS, Android, and Windows 10+ environments generally display them correctly.

items.q: Will search engines recognize this styled text?
items.a: Search engines often don't recognize Unicode mathematical symbols as regular text. Avoid using styled text for SEO content — it's best for visual design purposes only.

whatIs.title: What is the Unicode Text Styler?

Since it uses actual Unicode code points rather than font changes, you can copy and paste the styled text into any platform that renders Unicode: Instagram, X (Twitter), KakaoTalk, LinkedIn profiles, and game nicknames.

items.q: Can I style Korean text?
items.a: Font styles like bold or script exist in Unicode only for Latin letters and digits, so Korean stays as is. The Korean tab (jamo split, initials, circled initials, hearts between) and the Frames tab (꧁ ꧂, ★彡 彡★) work with Korean.

items.q: The text looks broken on some platforms
items.a: If the device or app font lacks those characters they show as □ or ?. Squared styles are most affected on older devices, and 🅰🅱🅾🅿 may render as emoji. Check the note on each card.

items.q: How are Instagram / KakaoTalk limits counted?
items.a: This tool counts visible characters (code points). Styled letters may take two units internally, so some platforms count them as longer; leave some room.

vs.title: Comparing lump sum vs DCA with the same total amount

concepts.title: Key Concepts
items: CAGR: Compound Annual Growth Rate, assumes steady annual growth
Lump Sum: Investing all money at once for long-term holding
DCA: Dollar Cost Averaging, investing fixed amounts monthly
Real Return: Actual purchasing power return after deducting inflation

formulas.title: Formulas
items: Lump sum: FV = PV × (1 + r)^n (annual return basis)
Monthly (paid at start of month): FV = PMT × ((1+i)^N − 1) / i × (1+i), i = monthly rate
Monthly rate i: annual basis (1+r)^(1/12) − 1, monthly compounding r/12
Real value = nominal ÷ (1 + inflation)^n

tips.title: Investment Tips
items: Lump sum tends to outperform DCA over longer periods
DCA reduces risk by averaging out market volatility
Consider inflation rate of 2-3% for realistic projections
Actual returns should account for taxes and fees

whatIs.title: What is the Investment Return Calculator?
whatIs.description: An investment analysis tool that calculates CAGR (Compound Annual Growth Rate), lump-sum vs. installment investment comparisons, and inflation-adjusted real returns in one place. You can back-calculate the required monthly contribution to reach a target amount, simulate compound growth, and clearly see the difference between nominal and real returns. Use it to compare stocks, ETFs, funds, and deposits over the long term.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Select the calculation type — CAGR, compound growth simulation, target amount back-calculation, etc.
2. Enter initial investment, monthly contribution (optional), annual return rate, and investment duration.
3. To account for inflation, enter the annual inflation rate for inflation-adjusted real return.
4. Review the result graph showing principal vs. gains and year-by-year portfolio growth.

items.q: What's the difference between CAGR and simple return?
items.a: Simple return compares only start and end values. CAGR expresses the compound annual growth rate — how much the investment grew per year on average. CAGR becomes more meaningful over longer investment periods.

items.q: Why does real return matter?
items.a: A 7% nominal return with 3% inflation means only ~4% actual purchasing power growth. Long-term investment performance must always be evaluated using real (inflation-adjusted) returns.

items.q: Which is better: lump-sum or installment investing?
items.a: Lump-sum generally outperforms in steadily rising markets; installment investing (dollar-cost averaging) is advantageous in volatile markets. Compare both directly with this calculator.

items.q: What does 500k KRW a month for 20 years become?
items.a: At a steady 7% a year, 120M KRW of principal grows to about 260M KRW. At 4% it is about 180M; at 10% about 360M.

items.q: ISA or pension savings first?
items.a: Pension savings/IRP give a 13.2–16.5% tax credit up front but must be drawn as a pension after 55. ISA needs only a 3-year hold and gains up to 2M KRW (4M low-income) are tax-free. Check the after-tax table.

items.q: Why does real return matter?
items.a: A 7% nominal return with 2% inflation is about 4.9% in purchasing power. 260M KRW in 20 years is about 170M in today's money.

items.q: What is the 4% rule?
items.a: A rule of thumb from past US data: withdrawing 4% of assets in year one, then adjusting for inflation, historically lasted about 30 years. Not a guarantee.

whatIs.title: What is the Image Compressor?
whatIs.description: A browser-based image optimization tool that reduces file size for JPG, PNG, and WebP images. All processing happens on your device — images are never uploaded to a server, protecting your privacy. Use it for web image optimization, reducing email attachment sizes, pre-processing SNS uploads, and batch compressing multiple images at once.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Drag and drop image files or click 'Select Files' to upload (multiple files supported).
2. Adjust the compression quality (0–100%) — around 80% is a good balance of quality and size.
3. Select the output format (keep original, convert to WebP, etc.).
4. Click 'Compress', review the before/after results, and download.

items.q: Is WebP supported in all browsers?
items.a: Most modern browsers support WebP — Chrome, Firefox, Edge, and Safari 14+. IE and some older browsers don't support it. For public websites, consider providing JPG fallbacks.

items.q: Can I restore the original after compression?
items.a: Lossy compression (JPG, WebP) is irreversible. Always keep a backup of originals before compressing important files.

items.q: Which compresses better: PNG or JPG?
items.a: For photos, JPG/WebP compress much smaller. For images with text, logos, or transparent backgrounds, PNG preserves quality without loss. Choose the right format for your use case.

whatIs.title: What is the Image Compressor?

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Drop photos, click to choose, or paste with Ctrl+V (multiple files supported).

3. Optionally change the output format and max size (long edge). Changes re-compress instantly.
4. Check quality with the before/after slider, then save one by one or all as a ZIP.

items.q: How do I get a photo under 500KB?
items.a: Choose 'Target file size' → 500KB and add your photo. It finds the highest quality that fits and lowers the resolution step by step if quality alone isn't enough. Keep the output as JPG if the site requires it.

items.q: Are my photos uploaded to a server?
items.a: No. Everything runs inside your browser and nothing is sent anywhere.

items.q: Is EXIF (location) data removed?
items.a: Yes. The image is redrawn and re-encoded, so GPS location, camera model and capture time are not kept. Orientation is applied from EXIF so the photo stays upright.

items.q: My iPhone HEIC photo won't open.
items.a: Chrome, Edge and most Android browsers can't open HEIC. Open this page in Safari on your iPhone to compress HEIC straight to JPG, or set Settings > Camera > Formats > Most Compatible.

items.q: The compressed file got bigger.
items.a: Re-saving an already compressed photo at high quality, or saving a photo as PNG, can increase size. Lower the quality, choose JPG/WebP, or reduce the resolution.

items.q: Are recordings saved to a server?

items.q: Can I record system audio (video/game sound)?

whatIs.title: What is the Nutrition Calculator?

Enter your daily meals to see total nutritional intake and how it compares to recommended daily allowances. Use it for diet management, muscle building, or dietary control for conditions like diabetes and hypertension.

items.q: What are the recommended macronutrient ratios?
items.a: For average adults: carbohydrates 50–60%, protein 15–20%, fat 20–30%. Adjust protein higher for muscle gain and reduce carbohydrates for weight loss.

items.q: What if a food isn't in the database?
items.a: Substitute with a similar food or manually enter nutritional values from the product label. For branded processed foods, check the manufacturer's website for exact figures.

items.q: What is the daily calorie recommendation?

whatIs.title: What is the Presentation Timer?
whatIs.description: A professional countdown timer optimized for presentations, lectures, and meetings. Features include color-changing visual warnings as time runs low, full-screen mode, and a last-minute alert. Works for solo presentation practice or as an MC tool to manage multiple speakers' time.

items.q: Can I hide the timer from the audience?
items.a: In full-screen mode on a dual-monitor setup, the presenter can see the timer while the audience sees only the presentation. Alternatively, open the timer on a separate smartphone screen for personal monitoring.

items.q: What happens when time runs out?
items.a: The display turns red and begins counting up (overtime), showing how much over time you've gone. Useful for tracking how long over schedule a presentation runs.

items.q: Are sound alerts supported?
items.a: Yes, sound alerts can be set for remaining time milestones (e.g., 5 minutes, 1 minute). During a live presentation, visual warnings or vibration are recommended to avoid disrupting the audience.

whatIs.title: What is the Presentation Timer?
whatIs.description: A professional countdown timer optimized for presentations, lectures, and meetings. Features include color-changing visual warnings as time runs low, full-screen mode, and a last-minute alert. Works for solo presentation practice or as an MC tool to manage multiple speakers' time.

items.q: Can I keep the timer hidden from the audience?
items.a: Open speaker mode on a laptop or phone in front of you. The audience sees only your slides while you see the time left in large type.

items.q: What happens when time runs out?
items.a: The screen turns red and keeps counting overtime like +01:23. When you stop, it shows your result, e.g. '+1m 23s vs target'.

items.q: Does it have sound alerts?
items.a: Yes. It chimes at the warning point, section changes and the end, and vibrates on phones. If sound would distract, turn it off and rely on vibration and color.

steps.title: How to apply
items: Check on Work24 that your employer filed the separation certificate and loss-of-coverage report, and that the reason code matches.
Register as a job seeker on Work24 (work24.go.kr).
Complete the online orientation for benefit applicants on Work24.
Visit your local job center with ID and apply for eligibility.
The first 7 days are an unpaid waiting period; attend the 1st recognition date set by the center.
Then report job-search activity about every 4 weeks (online available) and get paid within a few days.

know.title: Key facts
items: Daily benefit = 60% of the average wage over the last 3 months. 2026 cap 68,100 KRW, minimum 66,048 KRW (8 h).
Benefit days range from 120 to 270. Those 50+ or disabled get 30 more days with 1+ year of coverage.
You need 180 insured days within 18 months; multiple jobs are combined.
The benefit period is 12 months from the day after leaving; applying late loses remaining days.
Job-seeking benefits are not subject to income tax.

extended.title: Additional benefits
items: Early re-employment allowance: half of remaining benefits if re-employed with half or more left and kept 12 months
Training extension: up to 2 years at 100% during job-center-directed training
Individual extension: up to 60 days at 70% for severe hardship
Special extension: up to 60 days at 70% when designated by the Minister during mass unemployment
Wide-area job search and relocation expenses

caution.title: Cautions
items: Report any part-time or short-term work at recognition. Hiding it is fraud: repayment plus up to a 5x surcharge and criminal penalties.
Those newly hired after age 65 (unless continuously employed since before 65) are not covered.
Dismissal for serious misconduct may restrict benefits.
Reductions for repeat recipients (3+ claims in 5 years) are a pending bill and not in effect as of October 2026.
This calculator is for reference; the job center's decision is final.

items.q: Can I get benefits after a recommended resignation?
items.a: Yes, if it was due to business reasons such as downsizing. Check that the separation reason code is 23 (business necessity/downsizing, incl. dismissal and recommended resignation). Resignation or dismissal due to your own fault (26) may be restricted.

items.q: Where can I see my separation reason code?
items.a: Log in to Work24 and check your insured-status history. Common codes: 11 personal reasons, 12 quit due to changed conditions or unpaid wages, 22 closure, 23 business necessity, 26 dismissal for fault, 31 retirement age, 32 contract end. If incorrect, ask the employer to correct it or submit proof to the job center.

items.q: Who files the separation certificate?
items.a: The employer files it with the job center within 10 days of the center's request. Asking your employer to file early speeds things up.

items.q: Am I eligible when my fixed-term contract ends?
items.a: Yes, contract expiry is involuntary. But refusing a renewal offer on equal or better terms may be treated as voluntary.

items.q: Do I need to apply right away?
items.a: The benefit period is 12 months from the day after leaving. Days not received within it are forfeited, so apply as soon as possible.

items.q: Has the repeat-recipient reduction started?
items.a: A bill to cut benefits by up to 50% for 3+ claims in 5 years is pending but had not passed as of October 2026.

Enter your average salary before leaving, insured period, and age to get daily benefit amount and total benefit duration. Use it during job transition planning to budget for living expenses.

howToUse.title: How to Use

tips.title: Pro Tips
items: Voluntary resignation is generally ineligible, but exceptions exist (workplace harassment, wage theft, etc.).
Applications must be filed within 12 months of leaving — delays may reduce total benefit days.

items.q: How is the benefit duration determined?

items.q: Is there a daily benefit cap?

items.q: What happens to remaining benefit days after reemployment?
items.a: If you have 50% or more of your benefit days remaining upon reemployment, you may apply for the Early Reemployment Allowance. The faster you find a job, the more you receive.

calc.title: How it is calculated
items: Weekly contract hours = sum of (daily hours − break). Hours over 8 a day are overtime and excluded; max 40
Holiday hours = contract hours ÷ 40 × 8 (only if 15+ hours, max 8)
Holiday pay = holiday hours × hourly wage. e.g. 20 h/week at KRW 10,320 → 4 h × 10,320 = KRW 41,280
Monthly pay = wage × (weekly hours + holiday hours) × 365÷7÷12. 40 h/week → 209 h → KRW 2,156,880
Effective hourly = (weekly base + holiday pay) ÷ hours worked — about 1.2× the wage at 15+ hours

notes.title: Good to know
items: Holiday pay applies regardless of workplace size (incl. under 5 employees), industry or probation
Eligibility is based on contracted hours. Under 15 h/week on a 4-week average means no holiday pay (Art. 18(3))
You must attend all scheduled days that week. Lateness or leaving early is not an absence
50% overtime/night/holiday-work premiums apply only to workplaces with 5+ employees; holiday pay applies to all
Unpaid holiday pay can be claimed within 3 years (Art. 49). MOEL hotline 1350

items.q: How many hours do I need for holiday pay?
items.a: 15 contracted hours a week or more. 15 h → 3 holiday hours (15÷40×8), 20 h → 4 h, 40 h or more → the maximum 8 h.

items.q: Do I get holiday pay in a week I was absent?
items.a: No. If you miss any scheduled day, that week's holiday pay is not earned (Enforcement Decree Art. 30(1)). You are still paid for the days worked. Approved leave such as annual leave is not an absence.

items.q: Do I get holiday pay for my last week before quitting?
items.a: Yes, possibly. Since an August 2021 change in MOEL's interpretation, holiday pay is owed if the employment lasts the full week (7 days) and you attended all scheduled days, even with no work planned the next week. If employment ends on Friday, it is not earned.

items.q: Is a 14-hour contract to avoid holiday pay legal?
items.a: A contract under 15 hours is not illegal in itself, but if you actually work 15+ hours regularly, you can claim holiday pay based on actual hours. See the comparison above.

items.q: Is an hourly wage 'including holiday pay' a minimum wage violation?
items.a: For 40 h/week, the wage including holiday pay must be at least KRW 12,384 (10,320 × 1.2). Anything less means the base wage falls below the minimum.

items.q: Do part-timers taxed at 3.3% get holiday pay?
items.a: If you work set hours under the employer's direction, you may be an employee despite 3.3% withholding, and entitled to holiday pay and severance. Employee status depends on how you actually work, not the contract label.

info.title: What is Weekly Holiday Pay?

Holiday hours = (total weekly hours ÷ 40) × 8 hours (max 8 hours)
Holiday pay = hourly wage × holiday hours
Applies regardless of social insurance enrollment if 15+ hours per week
Failure to pay holiday pay constitutes wage theft

items: Total weekly hours = daily hours × working days
Holiday hours = (weekly hours ÷ 40) × 8, max 8 hours
Holiday pay = hourly wage × holiday hours
Monthly pay = (weekly base + holiday pay) × 4.345
Annual pay = monthly pay × 12

Freelancers and self-employed are not eligible (based on employment contract)

whatIs.title: What is the Weekly Holiday Pay Calculator?
whatIs.description: A tool that automatically calculates the mandatory weekly holiday allowance (주휴수당) owed to workers who work 15 or more hours per week under the Labor Standards Act. Enter your hourly wage and weekly hours to get weekly holiday pay, total weekly pay including holiday pay, monthly salary, and annual salary. Useful for part-time and hourly workers checking they're paid correctly.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Enter your hourly wage (KRW).
2. Enter your actual weekly working hours (e.g., 5 hours/day × 5 days = 25 hours).
3. See the weekly holiday pay (equivalent to 1 day's pay) and effective hourly rate including holiday pay.
4. Monthly and annual salary are automatically calculated based on 4.345 weeks/month.

tips.title: Pro Tips
items: Weekly holiday pay does not apply to workers under 15 hours/week — employers sometimes intentionally schedule below this threshold.
Weekly holiday pay must be paid separately — job ads claiming hourly wages 'including holiday pay' may actually be below legal minimum.
Always confirm weekly holiday pay is listed as a separate line item on your pay stub.

items.q: Are part-time convenience store workers entitled to weekly holiday pay?
items.a: Yes, any worker who works 15 or more hours per week is entitled to weekly holiday pay regardless of industry or employer size.

items.q: Does being late or leaving early affect holiday pay?
items.a: Weekly holiday pay requires full attendance during the scheduled workweek. Unauthorized absences in the same week may result in forfeiture of that week's holiday pay.

items.q: How do I report unpaid weekly holiday pay?
items.a: File a complaint with the Ministry of Employment and Labor or call 1350. Unpaid wages from the past 3 years are eligible for claims.

guide.title: Guide to Korean quotations and statements

sections.title: Which document?
items: Quotation: states price and terms before a deal. Adding validity, delivery and payment terms prevents disputes.
Transaction statement: confirms items, quantities and amounts on delivery. The receiver's signature makes it proof of delivery.
Bill: requests payment. Always include the due date and bank account.
This tool does not issue tax invoices. Corporations and sole proprietors with prior-year supply value of KRW 80M+ must issue e-tax invoices via Hometax or similar.

sections.title: How VAT is calculated
items: VAT excluded: unit price is the supply value; VAT = supply value × 10%, rounded down to the won.
VAT included: VAT = amount ÷ 11 (rounded down), supply value = amount − VAT.
Rounding of fractions is not set by law and follows the parties' agreement; most businesses round down.
Rounding per line can come out a few won lower than calculating once on the total. 'Once on the total' puts the difference on the largest line so the sums match.
Untick 'Taxable' for VAT-exempt items such as unprocessed farm/fishery products or medical and educational services.

sections.title: What to include
items: Supplier: trade name, business registration number, representative, address, business type/item, contact
The business registration number is checked against the NTS check-digit rule as you type. Use the business number lookup tool to check registration status.
The total is also written out in Korean (e.g. 금 일백일십만원정) to prevent tampering.
Document numbers follow date-serial (e.g. 20261001-001) and increase by one for each new document.

sections.title: PDF, printing and saving
items: Download PDF captures the preview as an A4 image, so Hangul never breaks.
Print prints only the document. Choosing 'Save as PDF' in the print dialog gives a PDF with selectable text.
Seal images have white backgrounds made transparent and are placed on the representative's (seal) mark.
Your details and draft are saved only in this browser; after a PDF or print, the customer is added to Recent clients. Nothing is sent to a server.

whatIs.title: What is the Invoice / Tax Invoice Generator?
whatIs.description: A tool for freelancers and small business owners to quickly create professional invoices and tax invoices and export them as PDF. Enter your business info, client details, line items and amounts, and VAT (10%) is automatically calculated with a total sum. No accounting software needed — generate and email or print the PDF directly.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Enter the issuer information (business name, registration number, address, etc.).
2. Enter the client information (company name, contact, email, etc.).
3. Add line items with quantity and unit price — subtotal and VAT (10%) are auto-calculated.
4. Click 'Save as PDF' to generate the print-ready document.

tips.title: Pro Tips
items: Save frequently used line items as templates for recurring clients to speed up the process.
For tax invoices, clearly distinguish between the supply date and the invoice issue date (legally important).
After issuing a quote, convert the same content to a tax invoice upon order confirmation for consistency.

items.q: Can I issue legally valid electronic tax invoices here?
items.a: Legally valid e-tax invoices must be issued through the National Tax Service's Hometax. This tool generates document-format invoices for sharing with clients. Use Hometax for official tax reporting.

items.q: Can tax-exempt businesses use this?
items.a: Yes, set VAT to 0% for tax-exempt transactions. Tax-exempt businesses should issue a 'bill of supply' (계산서) without VAT rather than a tax invoice.

items.q: Can I save client information for reuse?
items.a: Frequently used info is saved via browser localStorage and can be reloaded. Enter regular clients once and reuse conveniently.

whatIs.title: What is the Invoice / Tax Invoice Generator?
whatIs.description: Make a Korean quotation (견적서), transaction statement (거래명세서) or bill (청구서) in the standard Korean layout — supplier/customer boxes and the total written out in Korean — and download it as an A4 PDF. Choose VAT excluded, included or none and the supply value and VAT are calculated with won-level rounding down. Your business details and seal are saved in the browser and prefilled for the next document.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Enter the issuer information (business name, registration number, address, etc.).
2. Enter the client information (company name, contact, email, etc.).
3. Add line items with quantity and unit price — subtotal and VAT (10%) are auto-calculated.
4. Click 'Save as PDF' to generate the print-ready document.

tips.title: Pro Tips
items: Save frequently used line items as templates for recurring clients to speed up the process.
For tax invoices, clearly distinguish between the supply date and the invoice issue date (legally important).
After issuing a quote, convert the same content to a tax invoice upon order confirmation for consistency.

items.q: Can this replace a tax invoice?
items.a: No. A tax invoice is a statutory record issued via Hometax or similar. Quotations, statements and bills document the deal; the tax invoice must be issued separately.

items.q: Does a transaction statement need a seal?
items.a: It isn't a statutory form, so no. Many clients still ask for a sealed document, so uploading a seal image once is handy. The receiver signs the receipt line to confirm delivery.

items.q: With VAT included, the VAT is off by 1 won.
items.a: Included VAT is amount ÷ 11 rounded down. Rounding each line can differ from the total by a won or so. Switch VAT calculation to 'Once on the total' to match the total.

items.q: How do VAT-exempt or simplified taxpayers use it?
items.a: Set VAT to 'None' to show amounts without a VAT column. Simplified taxpayers who issue tax invoices (prior-year turnover KRW 48M+) can use 'Excluded' like general taxpayers.

items.q: Where is my data stored?
items.a: Only in this browser's localStorage — nothing is sent to a server. It won't appear on other devices or browsers, so keep important documents as PDFs.

whatIs.title: What is Coin Flip?
whatIs.description: A fair 50:50 random decision tool with 3D flip animation. Features streak tracking, statistics, and best-of-N match mode for various decision-making scenarios.

howToUse.title: How to Use

howItWorks.title: How It Works
items: When you click the button, Math.random() generates a number between 0-1, determining heads or tails at the 0.5 threshold.
CSS 3D transform (rotateY) renders the coin flip animation.
Each result is recorded in history, with heads/tails ratio updated in real-time.
In best-of-N mode, the winner is automatically determined when a majority is reached.

realWorld.title: Real-World Uses
items: Choosing offense/defense before sports matches (soccer, cricket, etc.)
Quick decisions among friends for bets or turn order
Demonstrating the law of large numbers in probability classes
Fast binary decisions when you can't make up your mind

comparison.title: Compared to Other Tools
items: Coin flip vs Dice: Coin for 2 choices, dice for 6+ options
Coin flip vs Roulette: Roulette supports 3+ custom items for diverse selections
Coin flip vs Lottery draw: Lottery allows adjustable win/lose ratios for unequal probabilities

tips.title: Tips
items: Great for quick binary decisions.
Best-of-N mode increases decision reliability.
Use statistics to demonstrate probability concepts.

items.q: Is it truly fair?
items.a: Yes, it uses Math.random() for a 50:50 probability. The more you flip, the closer the ratio converges to 50%.

items.q: Can the same side come up multiple times?
items.a: Yes, each flip is independent. Even after 10 heads in a row, the next flip is still 50:50.

crontabGenerator.title: Crontab Generator

format.title: Cron Expression Format
items: Minute(0-59) Hour(0-23) Day(1-31) Month(1-12) Weekday(0-7)
* = every, */n = interval, n-m = range, n,m = specific values
Weekday: 0 and 7 are Sunday, 1=Mon, 2=Tue, ..., 6=Sat

examples.title: Common Examples
items: * * * * * → Every minute
0 9 * * 1-5 → Weekdays at 9 AM
0 0 1 * * → 1st of every month at midnight
*/10 * * * * → Every 10 minutes

whatIs.title: What is the Crontab Generator?
whatIs.description: A tool that helps you easily generate crontab expressions for Linux/Unix scheduled task automation using a visual UI. Click sliders and checkboxes for minute, hour, day, month, and weekday fields to auto-generate the cron expression, with plain-language descriptions and a preview of the next execution times. Set up schedules intuitively without knowing cron syntax — useful for developers and server administrators alike.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Select a recurrence preset — 'Every minute', 'Hourly', 'Daily', 'Weekly', 'Monthly', etc., or
2. Fine-tune each field (minute, hour, day, month, weekday) by clicking or typing directly.
3. Copy the generated cron expression (e.g., 0 9 * * 1).
4. On the server, run `crontab -e` and paste the expression followed by your command.

tips.title: Pro Tips
items: Daily at 9 AM: `0 9 * * *` — commonly used for batch jobs and report emails.
*/5 means 'every 5 minutes', 1-5 means '1 through 5', 1,3,5 means '1, 3, and 5' — combine ranges and lists.
Before editing, run `crontab -l` to review existing schedules and avoid duplicates.

items.q: Can I use crontab on Windows?
items.a: Windows doesn't have crontab. Use Windows Task Scheduler, or run cron inside WSL (Windows Subsystem for Linux) or a Docker container.

items.q: How can I see cron job execution logs?
items.a: Append `>> /var/log/mycron.log 2>&1` to your cron command to log stdout and stderr to a file. Also check `/var/log/syslog` or `/var/log/cron` for execution history.

items.q: Can I run jobs with sub-minute (second) precision?
items.a: Standard cron has a 1-minute minimum interval. For sub-minute execution, use a loop inside the cron job, or switch to `systemd timer` or language-specific scheduler libraries.

whatIs.title: What is the .env Editor?
whatIs.description: A developer tool for editing .env files in the browser and converting them to various formats: dotenv, JSON, YAML, and shell export. Manage KEY=VALUE environment variables in a convenient table view, mask sensitive values to prevent accidental exposure during screen sharing, and compare or convert between different environment configs (dev/staging/production).

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Paste .env file contents into the text input, or drag and drop the file.
2. Edit, add, or delete key-value pairs in the table view.
3. Select the output format (dotenv, JSON, YAML, shell export, etc.).
4. Copy the converted result or download it as a file.

tips.title: Pro Tips
items: Mask API keys and passwords using the masking feature to keep them hidden during screen sharing.
When creating .env.example files, use empty values with descriptive comments and verify the format here.
Convert to Docker Compose environment variable format to use directly in your docker-compose.yml.

items.q: Are entered environment variable values sent to a server?
items.a: No. All processing happens in the browser only — nothing is transmitted to any server. Sensitive values like API keys and passwords can be handled safely.

items.q: How are comments (lines starting with #) handled?
items.a: Lines starting with # are recognized as comments and displayed separately. Comments are excluded in JSON conversion but preserved in dotenv conversion.

items.q: Are multiline values (containing newlines) supported?
items.a: Yes, multiline values enclosed in quotes (e.g., PEM certificates) can be parsed. However, newline handling may differ across output formats — verify after conversion.

items.q: What is Markdown?
items.a: A lightweight markup language that formats text with simple symbols like #, * and -. It is widely used on GitHub, Notion, Slack and many blogs.

items.q: Is my writing saved automatically?

items.q: Can I add images?

items.q: Is my text sent to a server?
items.a: No. Rendering, saving and exporting all happen in your browser. The preview is rendered safely, blocking scripts and dangerous links such as javascript:.

items.q: Line breaks look different from GitHub.
items.a: This preview turns every single line break into a new line, like a blog or notes app. In a GitHub README, separate paragraphs with a blank line or end a line with two spaces to force a break.

whatIs.title: What is GIF Maker?
whatIs.description: A tool that creates animated GIFs from multiple uploaded images. All encoding is done directly in the browser using the GIF89a format — no external server needed, keeping your images private. Use it for simple animations, meme creation, and frame sequence compositing. Adjust frame rate and loop count to create different effects.

tips.title: Pro Tips
items: Short frame intervals (under 100ms) create smooth animations; longer intervals (500ms+) produce a slideshow effect.
GIFs are limited to 256 colors, so simple images (logos, illustrations) render better quality than photos.
Large images produce large GIF files — resize to under 500px width before converting for easier sharing.

items.q: How many images can I add?
items.a: You can add images up to your browser's memory limit. Staying under 30–50 frames is generally stable. More frames mean larger file sizes, which can be inconvenient to share.

items.q: Can I make a GIF with a transparent background?
items.a: Using PNG images with transparent backgrounds preserves transparency in the GIF. Note that GIF only supports fully transparent or fully opaque — semi-transparency cannot be accurately represented.

items.q: Where can I use the created GIF?
items.a: Use on any platform that supports GIF: KakaoTalk, email, Slack, websites. Great for social media memes, product demo animations, and sticker creation.

backgroundRemover.title: Background Remover
backgroundRemover.description: Remove solid backgrounds — white product shots, ID photos, logos, green screens — to a transparent PNG or a new color. Nothing is uploaded.
backgroundRemover.preview: Background removed preview will appear here
backgroundRemover.clickToSelect: Picking color — click on background area...

howItWorks.title: How it works
items: The most common color along the edges becomes the background color. You get a warning if the edges are not uniform.
Each pixel's difference from the background is measured as ΔE in CIE Lab color space, which matches human perception better than RGB distance.
'From edges' mode flood-fills from the borders through connected background only, so matching colors inside the subject are kept.
Pixels just outside the tolerance become semi-transparent and the mixed-in background color is subtracted (defringe) to reduce halos.
Brush edits live in a separate mask, so they persist when you move the sliders.

realWorld.title: Good for
items: Turning white-background product shots into transparent PNGs for online stores
Changing ID photo backgrounds to white, light blue or blue
Putting paper stamps, signatures or white-background logos into documents and slides
Replacing green-screen backgrounds

comparison.title: Versus AI background removers
items: AI tools (e.g. remove.bg) recognize people and objects and can handle busy backgrounds, but often require uploading your photo.
This tool only looks at color, so on solid backgrounds it is fast and precise, and your photo never leaves the device.
Busy backgrounds or subjects that match the background color are beyond this tool — use an AI tool or Photoshop for those.
Upload or paste (Ctrl+V) a photo. The edge color is detected and removed right away.
If some background remains, use 'Pick bg' and tap it to add that color.
Adjust Tolerance for how much color is removed and Edge softening for smoother outlines.
Touch up with the Erase and Restore brushes. Ctrl+Z undoes.
Choose a new background (transparent, white, light blue…) and format (PNG/JPG), then save. Saving recomputes at the original resolution.
howToUse.title: How to Use
steps: Upload your image by dragging it onto the upload area or clicking to browse.
Click the 'Pick Background Color' button, then click on the background in the original image.
Adjust the tolerance slider — higher values remove more similar colors.
Use edge softening to smooth out the edges of the cutout.
When satisfied, click 'Download Transparent PNG' to save your result.

tips.title: Tips for clean cutouts
items: When shooting, make the subject and background clearly different and light evenly to avoid shadows on the background.
If white shirts or white products disappear, make sure 'From edges' is selected and lower the tolerance.
If holes inside letters (like O) remain, tap inside them with 'Pick bg' or switch to 'All matching'.
For green screens, raise tolerance to 25–40 and keep color fringe removal on.
The checkerboard in the preview means transparency; the PNG itself has no background.

limitations.title: Limitations & Notes
items: Gradient or patterned backgrounds are difficult to remove completely.
Color-based removal may accidentally remove parts of the subject if it shares colors with the background.
Large high-resolution images may take a few seconds to process.
Unlike AI-based tools (remove.bg), this uses simple color comparison and works best on uniform backgrounds.

whatIs.title: What is Background Remover?
whatIs.description: A browser-based tool that makes image backgrounds transparent using color-based chroma key technology. Unlike AI-powered background removal, you specify the color range directly — making it very effective for solid-color backgrounds (white, green screen, etc.). Images are never uploaded to a server, protecting your privacy. Download as a PNG with transparent background.

items.q: How is this different from AI background removal?
items.a: AI tools automatically detect object/person edges and can handle complex backgrounds but may be inaccurate. This tool uses chroma key — specialized for solid-color background removal with fine control over tolerance/range.

items.q: What if the background color is similar to the subject?
items.a: Lower the tolerance setting to minimize removal of subject areas that match the background color. For precise work, professional editing software like Photoshop is recommended.

items.q: Can it remove gradient or complex backgrounds?
items.a: Chroma key is optimized for solid-color backgrounds. It has limitations with gradients or complex patterns. For complex backgrounds, use an AI-specialized service like remove.bg.

whatIs.title: What is solid background removal?
whatIs.description: This tool detects the background color from the photo edges and makes similar colors transparent. It judges the background by color difference rather than AI recognition, so it works best when the background is a single color: product shots on white, ID photos, logos and green screens. Save a transparent PNG or put in a new background color — everything runs in your browser and the photo is never uploaded.

items.q: Is my photo uploaded?
items.a: No. Loading, removing and saving all happen inside your browser.

items.q: Can I change my ID photo background?
items.a: Changing only the background color is usually accepted, but passport photos require white and facial retouching is not allowed. Always check the requirements.

items.q: Hair edges look messy.
items.a: Increase edge softening and keep fringe removal on. Photos with lots of fine hair hit the limits of color-based removal; an AI tool will do better.

items.q: Does it handle large photos?
items.a: The preview is downscaled for speed, but saving recomputes at the original resolution (up to about 12.5 megapixels).

Change the canvas ratio (1:1, 4:5, 9:16...) and layout as you like.
Drag inside a cell to reposition, wheel or pinch to zoom. Drop onto another cell to swap.
Set gap, corners, background and footer text, then save as JPG/PNG or tap Share.

whatIs.title: What is Photo Collage?
whatIs.description: A browser-based collage tool that combines multiple photos into a single image using various grid layout templates. Choose from 5 layout templates, adjust photo order, set gaps between images, and download the finished collage. Perfect for SNS posts, photo memory organization, and product comparison images.

tips.title: Pro Tips
items: Photos with similar color tones or mood placed together create a cohesive, unified collage.
For Instagram posts, save in square (1:1) or portrait (4:5) ratio for optimal display.
Setting the gap (spacing) to 0 creates a seamless, clean grid-style result.

items.q: How many photos can I combine?
items.a: Depending on the layout, 2–6 photos can be combined. For more photos, create multiple collages and combine them in a subsequent step.

items.q: What resolution is the output?
items.a: The original photo resolution is maintained in the composite. Using high-resolution photos produces a collage suitable for printing.

items.q: Can I add text or stickers to the collage?
items.a: Currently only photo composition is supported. For text or sticker additions, do further editing in an image editor after exporting the collage.

items.q: Are my photos uploaded?
items.a: No. Loading, composing and saving all happen in your browser. Nothing is sent anywhere, and photos are gone when you close the page.

items.q: Part of my photo is cropped. Can I choose what shows?
items.a: Each cell is filled edge to edge, so photos are cropped to fit. Drag inside a cell to move the photo, and use the mouse wheel or pinch to zoom. Tap a cell for a zoom slider.

items.q: How do I reorder photos?
items.a: Drag a photo onto another cell to swap them. Made a mistake? Press Undo (Ctrl+Z).

items.q: What resolution is saved?
items.a: The long side is 2160px: 2160×2160 for square, 1728×2160 for 4:5. Choose JPG for smaller files or PNG for lossless output.

items.q: Can I make a photo booth strip?
items.a: Press 'Photo booth strip' next to Layout to set a 4-cut strip, 1:3 ratio, black background and footer text in one click. You can edit the caption and date.

items.q: My iPhone HEIC photo won't open.
items.a: HEIC opens only in Safari. In other browsers, share it as JPG from Photos, or set Settings > Camera > Formats to 'Most Compatible'.

fifteenPuzzle.title: 15 Puzzle
fifteenPuzzle.description: Slide numbered tiles to arrange them in order.

rules.title: Rules
items: Click a tile next to the empty space to slide it
Arrange numbers 1 to N in order to win
Try to finish in the fewest moves possible

whatIs.title: What is the 15 Puzzle?
whatIs.description: A classic sliding puzzle game where you push numbered tiles (1–15) into the empty space on a 4×4 grid to arrange them in order. Invented in the 1880s, this puzzle develops spatial reasoning and logical thinking. Choose grid sizes from 3×3 (8-puzzle) to 5×5, and challenge yourself to solve it in the fewest moves.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Select difficulty — 3×3 (easy), 4×4 (medium), 5×5 (hard).
2. Click or drag a tile adjacent to the empty space to slide it in that direction.
3. You win when all numbers are in order (1–15) with the empty space in the bottom-right.
4. Minimize your move count and time to set a new best record.

tips.title: Pro Tips
items: The basic 'row/column' strategy: complete the top row first (1,2,3,4), then the first column.
The final 2×2 corner (13,14,15) requires a special rotation technique — look up a 15-puzzle tutorial on YouTube.
If more than half the tiles appear severely scrambled, the puzzle might seem unsolvable — but this game only generates solvable configurations.

items.q: Can an unsolvable configuration appear?
items.a: No. This game only generates solvable configurations using a parity-checking algorithm to filter out impossible arrangements.

items.q: How do I find the optimal (minimum move) solution?
items.a: The optimal solution for 15-puzzle can be found with A* or IDA* algorithms, but the computation is very complex. Under 80–100 moves is generally considered a skilled solve.

items.q: Can I play with the keyboard?
items.a: Yes, use arrow keys (↑↓←→) to slide tiles adjacent to the empty space. Keyboard control can be faster and more precise than clicking.

rules.title: Controls
items: Click/tap to make the bird fly up
Pass through pipes to score points
Hit a pipe or the ground and it's game over!

whatIs.title: What is Flappy Bird?
whatIs.description: A one-tap arcade game where tapping the screen makes the bird flap upward, and releasing causes it to fall with gravity. Each time you pass through the gap between pipes, you score a point. Touching a pipe or the ground ends the game. Simple but intensely addictive, this reaction-speed game will keep you coming back for a higher score.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Click the screen or press Space bar to start the game and make the bird flap.
2. Each pipe gap you pass through scores 1 point.
3. Touching a pipe or falling to the ground is game over — click to restart.
4. Tap in a rhythmic pattern to maintain a consistent altitude.

tips.title: Pro Tips
items: Aim for the middle of each pipe gap — this gives you equal margin above and below.
Flying too high or too low is dangerous — practice staying in the middle third of the screen.
A steady, consistent tap rhythm is more stable than rapid bursts.

items.q: What score is considered good?
items.a: 10+ is intermediate, 30+ is advanced, 50+ is highly skilled. Even 5 points can be challenging at first — don't give up!

items.q: Does it work on touchscreen devices?
items.a: Yes, touch input is supported. Play on smartphones or tablets by tapping the screen.

items.q: Is my high score saved?
items.a: Yes, your best score (Best Score) is saved in browser localStorage. It persists between sessions so you can track your improvement.

hangman.title: Hangman
hangman.description: One Korean word a day, the same for everyone — guess it jamo by jamo.

rules.title: Rules
items: Guess the hidden Korean word
Press consonant and vowel buttons to select letters
Wrong guesses reduce your remaining tries
Guess the word before running out of tries

whatIs.title: What is Hangman (Word Guessing)?
whatIs.description: A traditional word-guessing game where you reveal a hidden Korean word one character (jamo) at a time. Each wrong guess adds a piece to the gallows drawing, and you must complete the word before the figure is fully drawn. The game uses correct Korean jamo (consonant/vowel) decomposition to handle Korean script properly, making it a fun way to build vocabulary.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. When the game starts, the hidden word is shown as blank spaces indicating its length.
2. Click consonant/vowel buttons on screen or type a character on the keyboard.
3. Correct characters appear in their position; wrong guesses add to the gallows drawing.
4. Keep guessing until you complete the word or fail 7 times.

tips.title: Pro Tips
items: In Korean, frequently occurring jamo like 'ㅇ', 'ㄴ', 'ㅣ', 'ㅏ' are good first guesses.
Use the word length and revealed characters to guess the part of speech (noun, verb, etc.).
When a category hint (food, animals, countries) is shown, focus guesses on vocabulary from that category.

items.q: How do I adjust word difficulty?
items.a: In practice mode choose Easy (9 lives), Normal (7) or Hard (5). The daily word always gives 7 lives.

items.q: How many wrong guesses are allowed?
items.a: The daily word and Normal allow 7 wrong guesses, Easy 9, Hard 5.

items.q: Can I see the correct answer after losing?
items.a: Yes, the answer is revealed after game over. Use it as a natural vocabulary learning opportunity.

pacMan.title: Pac-Man
pacMan.description: Classic arcade maze game eating dots and avoiding ghosts.

rules.title: Controls
items: Use arrow keys to move Pac-Man
Eat all dots to clear the level
Getting caught by ghosts costs a life
Eat power pellets to temporarily eat ghosts

whatIs.title: What is Pac-Man?
whatIs.description: The classic arcade game developed by Namco in 1980, where you navigate a maze eating dots while evading 4 ghosts. Eating a power pellet (large dot) lets you turn the tables and eat the ghosts. Each of the 4 ghosts (Blinky/Pinky/Inky/Clyde) uses a different AI strategy, and understanding their patterns is key to achieving high scores.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Use arrow keys (↑↓←→) or WASD to control Pac-Man. On mobile, swipe to change direction.
2. Eat all dots (·) in the maze to advance to the next stage.
3. Eat a power pellet (●) in the corners to turn ghosts blue and eat them.
4. Touching a ghost loses one life; losing all 3 lives is game over.

tips.title: Pro Tips
items: Ghosts predict Pac-Man's direction at intersections — unpredictable direction changes are effective.
Power pellet effects are short, so eat them when multiple ghosts are clustered together for combo points.
Using the maze edge tunnels makes it easier to lose pursuing ghosts.

items.q: How are the 4 ghosts' AI strategies different?
items.a: Blinky (red) directly chases Pac-Man. Pinky (pink) targets 4 tiles ahead. Inky (cyan) uses a complex calculated path. Clyde (orange) chases from far away but retreats when close.

items.q: How does the game get harder as stages progress?
items.a: Ghost movement speed and aggression increase, and power pellet effect duration shortens. At high stages, power pellets barely affect the ghosts.

items.q: Is my high score saved?
items.a: Yes, the high score is saved in browser localStorage and persists after closing the page.

items.q: Are the token counts exact?
items.a: They are heuristic estimates by character type; Korean in particular is shown as a range. Use each vendor's token counting API for exact numbers and enter them manually.

items.q: How do I pick a cache hit rate?
items.a: If requests with the same prefix keep arriving within the cache lifetime (5 minutes by default on Anthropic), most will hit. Use a lower rate for sparse traffic. Misses are billed at the cache write rate.

items.q: How current are the prices?
items.a: They were checked on each vendor's official pricing page on the date shown in the price table. Prices change often, so re-check the linked page before committing.

whatIsToken.title: What is a token?
items: The unit LLMs split text into; API pricing is per token
In English, roughly 4 characters make 1 token
The same text gives different counts with different tokenizers
For exact counts, use each vendor's token counting API or the usage field in responses

koreanTokens.title: Korean tokens
items: Hangul takes about 0.5–1.3 tokens per character, more than English
Tokenizers differ a lot on Korean, so the same text gives different counts per model
Claude 4.7+ models use a new tokenizer that yields about 30% more tokens (per Anthropic)
If cost matters, count real prompts and use Enter manually

costTips.title: Cost-saving tips
items: Put fixed system prompts and documents first and use prompt caching to cut input cost
Use the Batch API for non-urgent work to get 50% off input and output
Output costs 4–6x input, so cap responses with max_tokens
Long-context prices apply above 272K input on OpenAI and 200K on Gemini 3.1 Pro

whatIs.title: What is the LLM Token Calculator?
whatIs.description: The LLM Token Calculator estimates how many tokens your text consumes when processed by AI language models like ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini, and calculates the resulting API call cost. It helps developers and businesses forecast costs before building AI-powered applications and budget projects accordingly. Compare pricing across different models at a glance to choose the most cost-effective option.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Paste or type the text you want to tokenize into the input box.
2. Select the AI model (GPT-4o, Claude 3.5, Gemini, etc.) you plan to use.
3. Set the ratio of input (prompt) tokens to output (completion) tokens.
4. Enter your expected number of API calls to see the estimated monthly cost.

tips.title: Pro Tips
items: Non-English languages (Korean, Japanese, Chinese) are less token-efficient than English. Korean text typically uses 1.5–2× more tokens for the same content.
System prompts are sent on every API call. Keeping them concise can significantly reduce your monthly bill.
Lightweight models like GPT-4o mini or Claude Haiku are 10–20× cheaper and sufficient for simple tasks.
Output tokens usually cost 2–3× more than input tokens. Use max_tokens to cap response length.

items.q: How accurate is the token estimate?
items.a: The tool provides estimates. Actual token counts depend on the model's specific tokenizer (e.g., tiktoken) and may vary by ±10%.

items.q: What is a context window?
items.a: The maximum number of tokens a model can process at once. GPT-4o supports 128K and Claude 3.5 supports 200K tokens. Content exceeding this limit gets truncated.

items.q: Can I calculate embedding token costs too?
items.a: Embedding APIs use a separate pricing structure. This tool calculates costs for text generation (Chat Completions) API calls only.

nginx.title: Nginx Tips
items: Save config files in /etc/nginx/conf.d/ or /etc/nginx/sites-available/
After changes, run nginx -t to validate, then systemctl reload nginx
Adjust worker_connections and worker_processes based on server specs
Get free SSL certificates with Let's Encrypt (use certbot)

caddy.title: Caddy Tips
items: Caddy has automatic HTTPS by default — minimal SSL config needed
Caddyfile goes in /etc/caddy/Caddyfile
After changes, run systemctl reload caddy
Use reverse_proxy directive for simple proxy setup

security.title: Security Best Practices
items: Always use HTTPS and set up HTTP→HTTPS redirects
Add security headers (X-Frame-Options, CSP) to prevent XSS, clickjacking
Use server_tokens off to hide server version (Nginx)
Block unnecessary HTTP methods (TRACE, DELETE, etc.)

whatIs.title: What is the Web Server Config Generator?
whatIs.description: The Web Server Config Generator automatically creates Nginx and Caddy configuration files using best-practice presets for common use cases. Generate reverse proxy, SSL/TLS, static file serving, and security header configurations in just a few clicks. Even developers unfamiliar with server configuration can instantly obtain safe, optimized settings.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Select your web server type (Nginx or Caddy).
2. Choose your use case (reverse proxy, static files, PHP, Node.js, etc.).
3. Enter basic information such as domain name and port number.
4. Copy the generated configuration file and paste it into your server's config directory.

tips.title: Pro Tips
items: Caddy automatically provisions and renews Let's Encrypt SSL certificates. For small projects, Caddy is the simpler choice.
In Nginx reverse proxy configs, the presence or absence of a trailing slash in proxy_pass significantly affects URL routing. Always review the comments in the generated config.
Security headers (X-Frame-Options, CSP, HSTS, etc.) are included by default. Adjust the CSP policy to match your service's requirements.
Always validate your configuration with nginx -t before applying changes.

items.q: Should I choose Nginx or Caddy?
items.a: Choose Nginx for high traffic and fine-grained control. Choose Caddy for quick setup and automatic SSL. Nginx has a larger ecosystem, but Caddy's configuration is significantly simpler.

items.q: Is it safe to use the generated config as-is?
items.a: The config reflects security best practices, but production environments may need additional tuning. Especially CSP, CORS, and rate limiting should be customized for your service.

items.q: How do I enable HTTP/2 or HTTP/3?
items.a: For Nginx, add listen 443 ssl http2; to your config. Caddy supports both HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 automatically by default.

rules.title: Homeless period (max 32)
items: Counted from your 30th birthday, or from marriage registration if you married before 30
Single and under 30: 0 points; homeowners: 0 points
Under 1 year 2 points, +2 per year, 15+ years 32 points
If you sold a home, counting restarts from the date you became homeless (whole household)

rules.title: Dependents (max 35)
items: Excluding you: 0 = 5 points, +5 each, 6+ = 35 points
A spouse counts even with a separate registration
Parents/grandparents (incl. in-laws) count if you are head of household and share the registry for 3+ years; excluded if either owns a home
Unmarried children count; those 30+ need 1+ year on the same registry

rules.title: Account period (max 17)
items: Under 6 months 1, 6–12 months 2, then +1 per year, 15+ years 17
50% of the spouse's period adds up to 3 points (17 cap, since 2024-03-25)
Converted legacy accounts keep the original opening date
Up to 5 years opened as a minor are recognized (2024 change)

items.q: When does the homeless period start?
items.a: On your 30th birthday, or on the marriage registration date if you married earlier. If you sold a home, the later of that date and the date you became homeless applies. It is judged for the whole household.

items.q: Is it really 0 points if I'm single and under 30?
items.a: Yes. It starts at 2 points on your 30th birthday and rises 2 points a year.

items.q: How do parents count as dependents?
items.a: You must be head of household and share the resident registry with them for 3+ consecutive years. If either parent owns a home, both are excluded. Health insurance usage records may be required to prove actual residence.

items.q: Does my spouse's account count?
items.a: Since 2024-03-25, 50% of the spouse's period is converted and added up to 3 points, capped at 17 in total. E.g. own 5 years (7) + spouse 4 years (3) = 10.

items.q: Does a small home count as homeless?
items.a: For private general supply only, one home of 60㎡ or less valued at KRW 160M or less (capital region) or KRW 100M (elsewhere) is treated as homeless. Not for special supply.

items.q: What happens on a tie?
items.a: Since 2024-03-25, the longer account holder wins; if still tied, a lottery decides.

items.q: Does public housing use points?
items.a: No. National housing general supply uses deposit amount/count, not points. Points apply to private housing.

items.q: Where can I see cutoffs?
items.a: Applyhome (applyhome.co.kr) shows competition rates and winning scores by complex.

pay.title: 2026 enlisted pay
pay.note: Monthly pay is paid each month. The government savings match equals what the soldier saves in the Soldier Tomorrow Savings (up to KRW 550,000/month) and is paid at discharge. The often-quoted 'KRW 2.05M for sergeants' is KRW 1.5M pay plus the KRW 550K match. Source: MND 2026 budget.

ruleItems: Service counts from the enlistment date (day 1).
Discharge date is the day before the same date N months later. e.g. Army enlisted Mar 10, 2026 → Sep 9, 2027
If that date doesn't exist (e.g. Feb 31), the last day of that month is the discharge date (Civil Act Art. 160).
Progress = days served ÷ total days; 100% on discharge day.
Minimum time in grade: PVT 2, PFC 6, CPL 6 months, so sergeant in month 14.

faq.q: Does final leave move the discharge date earlier?
faq.a: No. The discharge date stays the same; leave taken right before it just means leaving the unit earlier.

faq.q: What if discharge falls on a weekend or holiday?
faq.a: The service end date follows the calendar and is not shifted. Ceremony times vary by unit.
Base pay is KRW 1.5M in 2026. Adding the savings match (max KRW 550K/month) gives 2.05M, but the match is paid at discharge and only for what was saved.

faq.q: What if a promotion is delayed?
faq.a: Enlisted promotions are reviewed, so a delay pushes the date and pay back. This tool assumes on-time promotions.

guide.lthdNote: The 1-house rate (holding + residence, up to 80%) applies to homes over ₩1.2B held 3+ and lived in 2+ years; otherwise the general rate (up to 30%). No deduction for surcharged homes or pre-sale rights.
guide.shortTitle: Rates by holding period and asset (Income Tax Act Art. 104)
guide.shortNote: When two rates apply, the higher tax wins. Unregistered transfers: 70%. Local income tax of 10% is added.

items.q: When must I file?
items.a: Within two months from the end of the month of sale (earlier of balance payment or registration). E.g. a March 15 closing is due May 31 (next business day if a holiday). Multiple sales in a year are combined in the May final return.

items.q: What are the 1-house exemption rules?
items.a: The household owns only one home on the sale date and has held it 2+ years; 2 years of residence are also required if it was in an adjusted area when bought (after 2017-08-03). Up to ₩1.2B fully exempt; above that only (price − ₩1.2B) / price of the gain is taxed.

items.q: I briefly own two homes while moving. What is the deadline?
items.a: Buy the new home at least 1 year after the old one and sell the old home within 3 years of buying the new one. Since 2026-10-01 it is 2 years if both homes are in adjusted areas and the new home was acquired on or after 2026-08-04 (contracts by 2026-08-03 keep 3 years).

items.q: Is the multi-home surcharge applied now?
items.a: Yes. The deferral ended on 2026-05-09, so from 05-10 adjusted-area sales get +20%p (2 houses) or +30%p (3+) and no long-term deduction. Contracts signed by 05-09 and closed within 4 or 6 months are excepted. The 2026 reform bill proposes temporary relief for 2027–2028 but has not passed.

items.q: Which expenses count?
items.a: Acquisition tax, brokerage, legal fees and capital improvements such as window frames, balcony extension or built-in AC. Repairs like wallpaper, flooring or boiler fixes do not count. Keep receipts.

items.q: Who gets the 80% long-term deduction?
items.a: Owners of a 1-house-exempt home over ₩1.2B held 3+ and lived in 2+ years: 4% per year held (max 40%) + 4% per year lived (8% for 2–3 years, max 40%).

items.q: How is the holding period counted?
items.a: From acquisition (earlier of balance payment or registration) to sale. Selling on the same date 2 years later counts as 2 years. Inherited homes count from the decedent's purchase for rate purposes; gifted homes from the gift registration.

items.q: What about joint ownership?
items.a: Each owner is taxed separately. Split prices and expenses by share and calculate each. Each owner also gets the ₩2.5M basic deduction.

whatIs.title: What is the Average Calculator?
whatIs.description: The Average Calculator computes all four types of averages—arithmetic, weighted, geometric, and harmonic—along with basic statistics like standard deviation, variance, median, and mode in one place. It is useful for grade calculations, investment return analysis, speed averaging, and many other real-world scenarios. The tool also helps you decide which type of average is appropriate for your data.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Enter numbers separated by commas, spaces, or line breaks.
2. For weighted average, also enter corresponding weights for each number.
3. Select the average type (arithmetic, weighted, geometric, or harmonic).
4. View the calculated result along with additional statistics like standard deviation and median.

tips.title: Pro Tips
items: Use weighted average when items have different importance, such as course grades weighted by credit hours.
Geometric mean is the right choice for averaging ratios and growth rates, such as compound annual growth rates (CAGR).
Harmonic mean is correct for averaging rates with an inverse relationship, such as speed, unit prices, or resistance.
When outliers are present, the median is more representative than the arithmetic mean.

items.q: Which is more accurate: arithmetic mean or median?
items.a: If the data has no extreme values, arithmetic mean works well. For skewed distributions like income or real estate prices, the median is more representative.

items.q: When should I use geometric mean?
items.a: Use it for investment returns, population growth rates, or any continuous change expressed as ratios or multiples over time.

items.q: Can I calculate with negative numbers or zeros?
items.a: Arithmetic and weighted averages work with negatives and zeros. Geometric mean requires positive numbers only. Harmonic mean cannot be calculated if zero is included.

whatIs.title: What is the Grade/Rank Calculator?
whatIs.description: The Grade/Rank Calculator automatically computes your Korean school grade (1st through 9th) and percentile from your rank and total number of test-takers. It is ideal for high school GPA management, university admissions planning, and analyzing relative performance on norm-referenced tests. It also reverse-calculates the rank range needed to reach a target grade.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Enter your rank (position in class or exam).
2. Enter the total number of students or test-takers.
3. Click Calculate to instantly see your grade and percentile.
4. Use the reverse calculation to find what rank you need for a target grade.

tips.title: Pro Tips
items: Grade 1 is the top 4%, Grade 2 is 4–11%, and Grade 3 is 11–23% by percentile cutoff.
When multiple students share the same score, they receive the same rank. The worst-case rank is used for grade boundary calculation.
CSAT (수능) grades use standard scores and percentiles, which differ from the school GPA grade method used here.
If you only know your score, not your rank, you can estimate your percentile using the class average and standard deviation.

items.q: Can I compare grades between subjects with different class sizes?
items.a: Since grades are determined by relative percentage, the same grade represents the same relative standing regardless of class size. Percentile provides the most intuitive comparison.

items.q: How do school grades affect university admissions?
items.a: Grade-based admissions use the average grade across subjects. Each university has different subject weighting policies, so check each school's admissions criteria.

items.q: Where exactly is the boundary between Grade 1 and Grade 2?
items.a: The top 4% earns Grade 1. For example, ranks 1–4 out of 100 students are Grade 1, ranks 5–11 are Grade 2. Fractional boundaries are rounded up.

items.q: Who uses the 5-tier system?
items.a: All students entering high school from the 2025 school year. Students who entered in 2024 or earlier keep the 9-tier system until graduation.

items.q: How are ties graded?
items.a: The grade uses the mid-rank percentile, where mid-rank = rank + (tied - 1)/2, and all tied students get the same grade. Example: 7 students tied for 1st out of 96 → mid-rank 4 (4.17%) → grade 2 on the 9-tier scale.

items.q: Where exactly is the grade 1 cutoff?
items.a: You get a grade when your mid-rank percentile is at or below its cumulative ratio. On the 9-tier scale with 100 students, ranks 1–4 are grade 1; on the 5-tier scale with 150 students, ranks 1–15 are. Small classes may have no grade 1.

methods.title: Why do the methods differ?
methods.ratio: Proportional: your GPA ÷ your max × target max. Consistent across scales, but ignores grade bands.
methods.band: Grade-band: first maps your GPA to a letter grade (A+~F), then to that grade's typical percentile range (or GPA). Values jump at grade boundaries, and bands vary by school.
methods.official: If the institution you apply to specifies a conversion formula, or your transcript states an official percentage, that value takes precedence.

whatIs.title: What is the GPA Converter?
whatIs.description: The GPA Converter converts grades between 4.3 and 4.5 GPA scales and also converts them to a 100-point percentage scale. It is useful when applying to graduate schools, studying abroad, or applying for jobs that require a different grading scale. It supports both letter grades (A+, A0, B+) and numeric GPA input.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Select your current GPA scale (4.3 or 4.5 maximum).
2. Enter the GPA as a number (e.g., 3.8) or letter grade (e.g., A+).
3. View the converted GPA in the other scale and the equivalent 100-point score.
4. For batch conversion, enter multiple course grades to get an overall converted GPA.

tips.title: Pro Tips
items: The 4.3 scale uses A+(4.3), A0(4.0), B+(3.3), while 4.5 uses A+(4.5), A0(4.0), B+(3.5). Differences appear at A0 and below.
Many US graduate programs use a 4.0 scale. A rough 4.5→4.0 conversion can be done by multiplying by 4.0/4.5.
Each institution has its own 100-point conversion table. Check the scale on your official transcript and disclose it to the receiving institution.
Highlighting strong grades in core major courses can strengthen your application even if your overall GPA is moderate.

items.q: Is a 4.3-scale 3.5 the same level as a 4.5-scale 3.5?
items.a: No. A 3.5 on a 4.3 scale is about 81.4%, while 3.5 on a 4.5 scale is about 77.8%. The same number means different things depending on the scale.

items.q: How are Pass/Fail courses handled?
items.a: P/F courses are typically excluded from GPA calculation. They are recorded as completion only and do not affect the grade average.

items.q: Is there an internationally recognized conversion standard?
items.a: There is no single universal standard. Services like WES (World Education Services) provide internationally recognized conversions. For important applications, using an official credential evaluation service is recommended.

whatIs.title: What is the PC Electricity Cost Calculator?
whatIs.description: The PC Electricity Cost Calculator estimates monthly and annual electricity bills by inputting the power consumption (watts) of each PC component—CPU, GPU, memory, storage, and more. It applies Korean residential and commercial electricity rate tiers to produce estimates close to your actual bill. It is also useful for calculating savings when upgrading to more energy-efficient components.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Enter the power consumption (W) for each PC component: CPU, GPU, motherboard, etc.
2. Set the average daily usage hours and load profile (regular use, gaming, rendering, etc.).
3. Select residential or commercial electricity rate plan.
4. View the estimated monthly and annual electricity cost along with total kWh usage.

tips.title: Pro Tips
items: The GPU is the largest power consumer in a gaming PC. A high-end GPU under full load can draw more power than all other components combined.
Real-world power draw is often lower than the TDP rating. Use monitoring tools like GPU-Z or HWiNFO64 to measure actual consumption for greater accuracy.
Korean electricity uses a tiered (progressive) rate. Exceeding 200 kWh/month significantly increases the per-unit rate, so be sure to check your billing tier.
Standby power consumption also adds up to thousands of won per year. Get into the habit of using sleep mode or full shutdown when not in use.

items.q: Is the PSU wattage rating the same as power consumption?
items.a: No. The PSU's rated wattage is the maximum it can supply. Actual consumption is the sum of what components are drawing at any given moment. Use the sum of component TDPs as your baseline.

items.q: Does the result include VAT?
items.a: Yes. Results include the climate and fuel adjustment charges, 10% VAT and the 2.7% power industry fund.

items.q: Can I calculate electricity costs for a crypto mining rig?
items.a: Yes. Set usage to 24 hours a day at full load to simulate mining conditions. Also check whether a commercial electricity plan applies to your situation.
