tips.title: 6 Tax-Saving Strategies
tips.subtitle: Review these items before filing — they can legally reduce your tax bill.

t1.title: Maximize Pension Savings & IRP Deductions
t1.desc: Combine pension savings fund (up to 6M KRW/yr) and IRP (up to 3M more) for a maximum 9M KRW tax credit at 16.5% rate.

t2.title: Document All Business Expenses
t2.desc: Equipment, transportation, communications, books, and business meals can all be claimed as expenses. Keep tax invoices and card receipts.

t3.title: Compare Simple vs Standard Expense Rates
t3.desc: If your income is below the threshold, the simple expense rate (60–90% by industry) lets you reduce income without receipts. Actual expenses may be higher.

t4.title: Yellow Umbrella Deduction for SMEs
t4.desc: Small business owners can deduct Yellow Umbrella (노란우산) contributions (up to 5M KRW) from income — a powerful tax reducer.

t5.title: Keep Financial Income Under 20M KRW
t5.desc: Once combined interest and dividends exceed 20M KRW, they enter global taxation at higher rates. An ISA account helps manage this threshold.

t6.title: Check All Available Tax Credits
t6.desc: Youth employment at SMEs (90% reduction), startup SME credits, e-filing credit (20K KRW), and medical/education/donation credits are easy to miss.

e1.title: Filing Season Opens

e2.title: General Filing & Payment Deadline

e3.title: Installment Payment 1st Due
e3.desc: If tax owed exceeds 10M KRW, pay 50% by this date. The remaining 50% can be paid by June 30.

e4.title: Diligent Filing Confirmation Deadline
e4.desc: High-revenue business owners must file with a CPA verification letter by June 30.

e5.title: Installment Payment 2nd Due

timeline.penaltyDesc: Missing the deadline incurs a 20% non-filing penalty (40% for fraudulent non-filing) plus a daily late payment surcharge of 0.022%. Always file on time.

q1.q: When is the global income tax filing period?
q1.a: Every year from May 1 to May 31. Diligent filing confirmation subjects have until June 30. File electronically via Hometax (hometax.go.kr) or the mobile Son-Tax app.

q2.q: I'm an employee — do I need to file?
q2.a: If you only have wage income and completed year-end tax adjustment, you do not need to file. However, if side income exceeds 3M KRW, you worked at multiple jobs, or your financial income exceeds 20M KRW, you must file.

q3.q: I already had 3.3% withheld — do I still need to file?
q3.a: Yes. The 3.3% withholding is a provisional payment, not the final tax. You settle the actual amount through the May global income tax filing. You may receive a refund or owe additional tax.

q4.q: When will I receive my tax refund?
q4.a: Refunds are issued within 30 days of filing. Register your bank account on Hometax for automatic deposit. Check refund status via the 'Refund Inquiry' feature on Hometax.

q5.q: Can I file without a tax accountant?
q5.a: Freelancers and business owners with simple income structures can use Hometax's pre-filled (모두채움) or simple filing feature. Complex situations (multiple income types, rental income, etc.) warrant professional advice.

whatIs.title: What is Comprehensive Income Tax?
whatIs.description: Comprehensive income tax is filed every May by individuals with income beyond employment (business, freelance, interest/dividend, pension, or other income), covering the previous year's combined income.

tips.title: Tips

infoPanel.title: Understanding Color Vision Deficiency
infoPanel.whatIsText: Color vision deficiency (CVD) occurs when one or more types of cone cells in the eye are absent or have reduced function, making it difficult to distinguish certain colors. It is often X-linked and therefore more common in males (~8%) than females (~0.5%).
designTipItems: Don't rely on color alone — use icons, patterns, and text labels to convey information
Ensure sufficient luminance contrast so color-blind users can still perceive content
For red-green CVD, prefer blue and orange as your primary contrast pair
Use CVD-friendly palettes (e.g., Okabe-Ito) for data visualizations

q1.q: What is the difference between color blindness and color weakness?
q1.a: Color blindness (dichromacy) means a specific cone type is completely absent, so the person cannot distinguish that color at all. Color weakness (anomalous trichromacy) means the cone is present but has reduced sensitivity. Color weakness is far more common than color blindness.

q2.a: The simulator uses color transformation matrices based on the Brettel/Viénot algorithm to approximate color-blind vision. While individual variation means it cannot be perfectly accurate, it is widely used for design accessibility reviews.

q3.q: Is my uploaded image sent to a server?
q3.a: No. All image processing is done entirely in your browser using the Canvas API. Your images are never uploaded to any server.

q4.a: Congenital color blindness has no known cure. Specialty lenses (e.g., EnChroma glasses) can improve color discrimination for some people, but effectiveness varies. Consult an ophthalmologist if you suspect a color vision deficiency.

howItWorks.title: How It Works
items: Protan, deutan and tritan simulation uses the physiologically based matrices of Machado, Oliveira & Fernandes (2009), published in 10% severity steps; values in between are linearly interpolated.
Matrices are applied in linear RGB, not to gamma-encoded sRGB values — applying them directly to sRGB distorts dark colors.
Achromatopsia is approximated by discarding color and keeping only lightness (linear luminance Y).
The palette check converts simulated colors to CIELAB, computes CIEDE2000 differences and flags pairs below 10 as confusable.
Everything runs in your browser; images are never sent to a server.

whatIs.title: What is this tool?
whatIs.description: This simulator shows how images and colors appear to people with color vision deficiency. It covers protan, deutan and tritan deficiencies plus achromatopsia with a 0–100% severity control, and automatically checks whether your chart/UI palette stays distinguishable. To check your own color vision, try ToolHub's Color Blind Test.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Pick a sample (chart, traffic light, color wheel) or upload an image. You can paste a screenshot with Ctrl+V.
Choose a color vision type and adjust severity. 100% is dichromacy ("color blind"); lower values are anomalous trichromacy ("color weak").
Use the compare slider to overlay the original, or "All types" to view every type at once.
Paste your chart HEX colors into the palette check to see confusable pairs and their color difference (ΔE) per type.
Settings and palette are stored in the URL, so copy the link to share with your team. Save the simulated image as PNG.

tips.title: Tips
items: Don't encode status (success/failure) with red vs. green alone — add icons, text or patterns.
Use a CVD-friendly palette such as Okabe-Ito for charts, or keep a large lightness difference between colors.
Most people with CVD are color weak, so also check at 50–70% severity, not only 100%.
Check text/background contrast against WCAG (4.5:1 for body text) with the Contrast Checker.

items.q: What is the difference between color blindness and color weakness?
items.a: Dichromacy ("color blindness") means one of the three cone types does not work; anomalous trichromacy ("color weakness") means a cone type's sensitivity is shifted. Color weakness is far more common. Here, 100% severity corresponds to dichromacy and anything lower to anomalous trichromacy.

items.q: How accurate is the simulation?
items.a: The Machado 2009 model is widely used in research and accessibility tools, but actual perception varies between individuals and depends on your monitor's color settings. Treat it as an approximation for design review.

items.q: Can this tell me if I am color blind?
items.a: No — it only shows how things look. Try ToolHub's Color Blind Test for a quick screening, and see an ophthalmologist for a proper diagnosis.

items.q: Are uploaded images stored on a server?
items.a: No. Images are processed only in your browser and never sent anywhere.

Retina distance is where one pixel subtends 1 arcminute (1/60°, the limit of 20/20 vision); beyond it pixels can't be told apart. Scaling is estimated Windows-style (96 PPI = 100%) so the effective PPI is 120 or less, and can be changed per screen. Workspace is the area multiple of FHD (1920×1080 at 100%).

guide.title: Screen Size Comparison Guide

whatIs.title: Why inches alone don't tell you the size
whatIs.description: Screen size in inches is the diagonal, so screens with different aspect ratios have different widths, heights and areas even at the same size. This tool turns diagonal and resolution into real width and height (cm), area difference, PPI, scaled workspace and recommended viewing distance, and draws every screen to the same scale.

formulas.title: How it's calculated
items: Width = diagonal × width px ÷ √(width px² + height px²), height likewise (1 inch = 2.54 cm). A 27" 16:9 screen is 59.8 × 33.6 cm.
Area grows with the square of the diagonal. At 16:9, a 32" screen is (32 ÷ 27)² ≈ 1.40×, i.e. 40% larger than 27".
PPI = √(width px² + height px²) ÷ diagonal (in), pixel pitch (mm) = 25.4 ÷ PPI.
Workspace = resolution ÷ scaling. A 32" 4K at 125% gives 3072×1728, about 2.56× the content of FHD at 100%.
At the same diagonal, wider ratios like 21:9 or 32:9 are shorter and have less area. A 34" 21:9 is about 33.4 cm tall — almost the same as a 27" 16:9 (33.6 cm).

distance.title: Reading the viewing distances
items: SMPTE 30°: the screen width fills 30° of your view — a common TV guideline. About 2.7 m for a 65" 16:9.
THX 40°: a more immersive, cinema-like distance. About 2.0 m for a 65" 16:9.
Retina distance: where one pixel subtends 1 arcminute (the 20/20 limit). You need to sit closer than this to notice the extra resolution. About 1.3 m for a 65" 4K, about 80 cm for a 27" QHD.
Monitors are usually viewed at 60–80 cm, so a 27" QHD (retina ≈ 80 cm) is borderline while a 27" 4K (≈ 54 cm) shows no visible pixels.

tips.title: Buying tips
items: Going from 27" QHD to 32" 4K gives 40% more area and 27% higher PPI. At 125% scaling you also get 1.44× the workspace.
For a TV, measure the distance to your sofa and pick a size between the SMPTE and THX distances. At 2.5 m that's roughly 60–80".
For phones the aspect ratio matters more than inches. A 6.3" 19.5:9 phone (iPhone 17) is only about 6.7 cm wide.
Use Rotate to compare portrait monitors or phones, and share the link to reopen the exact same comparison.

guide.ppiNote: Perceived sharpness depends on distance. For 20/20 vision, pixels disappear at about 290 PPI for a phone (~30 cm), 110–145 PPI for a monitor (60–80 cm), and only about 30 PPI for a TV at 3 m.

items.q: 27" QHD vs 32" 4K — which is bigger and sharper?
items.a: The 32" 4K is 70.8 × 39.8 cm, about 40% more area than the 27" QHD (59.8 × 33.6 cm). Its PPI is also higher (138 vs 109), so text looks sharper at the same distance. A 4K screen is usually used at 125–150% scaling for comfortable text size.

items.q: How big is a 65" TV really?
items.a: A 16:9 65" panel is about 143.9 cm wide and 80.9 cm tall, excluding bezels. The SMPTE 30° viewing distance is about 2.7 m, the THX 40° distance about 2.0 m, and 4K pixels stop being distinguishable at about 1.3 m.

items.q: Is a screen twice the inches twice as big?
items.a: No. At the same ratio, area grows with the square of the diagonal, so twice the inches means four times the area. Going from 55" to 65" is 18% more diagonal but about 40% more area.

items.q: Why do two 34" screens differ in size?
items.a: Aspect ratio. A 21:9 34" (3440×1440) is 79.7 × 33.4 cm — wider but shorter than a 16:9 34" (75.3 × 42.3 cm), with about 17% less area.

items.q: Why does scaling matter?
items.a: High-resolution screens at 100% make text tiny, so they're used at 125–200%. The visible workspace then becomes resolution ÷ scaling. A 27" 4K at 150% gives 2560×1440 — the same workspace as a 27" QHD, just sharper.

whatIs.title: What is Crossword?
whatIs.description: Crossword is a classic puzzle game where you fill in Korean words based on across and down clues. It helps expand vocabulary and general knowledge across a wide range of topics. Multiple difficulty levels are available, with hint and answer-reveal functions to help when you get stuck.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Read the across and down clues and type your answers into the corresponding numbered squares.
2. Click a square or use the arrow keys to navigate; type to enter letters.
3. When all squares are filled, the puzzle automatically checks your answers.
4. Use the hint button for an extra clue, or reveal a single letter if you're stuck.

tips.title: Pro Tips
items: Use intersections strategically: letters shared between across and down words narrow down possibilities for both answers simultaneously.
Start with the shortest words (2–3 letters). Filling them first reveals crossing letters that unlock longer words.
Re-read clues multiple times. Meanings that seem obscure at first often click after you've filled in some crossing letters.
For specialized terms and proper nouns, think of the most well-known term in that field first.

items.q: How do I correct a wrong answer?
items.a: Click the square and press Delete or Backspace to erase the letter, then retype. The reset button clears the entire puzzle.

items.q: Do new puzzles become available?
items.a: A new numbered daily puzzle is released every midnight (KST). You can also play the last 7 days and unlimited practice puzzles.

items.q: Can I play on mobile?
items.a: Yes. Tapping a square brings up the keyboard automatically. Touch navigation between squares is also supported.

howItWorks.title: How It Works
items: The characters from both names are arranged alternately
Each character's consonants/vowels are converted to ㅇ and ㅎ
Stroke counts are calculated (ㅇ=1, ㅎ=3)
Adjacent numbers are summed down to single digits for the final score

tips.title: Good to Know
items: Name compatibility is meant for fun
Only Korean names are supported (2-5 characters)
Save the result card as an image or share via link
Same names always produce the same result

whatIs.title: What is the Name Compatibility Test?
whatIs.description: The Name Compatibility Test analyzes the stroke count, phonetics, and consonant/vowel composition of two Korean names to produce a fun compatibility score and personality pairing description. It combines traditional Korean naming science (성명학) with statistical patterns to evaluate romantic, friendship, and professional relationships. Results are shareable as an image card for social media.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Enter the first person's name in Korean.
2. Enter the second person's name in Korean.
3. Select the relationship type (romantic, friend, or business).
4. View the compatibility score, pairing description, and advice—then share the result.

tips.title: Pro Tips
items: This is a fun tool, not a scientific assessment. Enjoy it lightheartedly and don't read too much into the results.
Save the result image and share it on KakaoTalk or Instagram for a fun conversation starter with friends.
Results may differ depending on whether you include the family name. Try both full name and given name only for comparison.
Compare multiple name combinations to find which pairing produces the highest score—it's a fun challenge.

items.q: Is name compatibility scientifically supported?
items.a: No. Name compatibility is based on traditional Korean naming philosophy but has no scientific validation. Use it purely for entertainment.

items.q: Can I use English names?
items.a: The analysis is designed for Korean names. You can transliterate English names into Korean phonetics and enter them to get a result.

items.q: Should I be concerned if I get a low score?
items.a: Not at all. Actual relationship quality depends on personality, shared values, and communication—factors far more significant than name compatibility.

whatIs.title: What is the Personal Color Self-Assessment?
whatIs.description: The Personal Color Self-Assessment analyzes your physical characteristics—skin tone, eye color, hair color—through 12 questions to identify which of the four seasonal color palettes (Spring Warm, Summer Cool, Autumn Warm, Winter Cool) suits you best. howToUse.title: How to Use

2. Answer all 12 questions about your skin, eyes, hair, and veins honestly.
3. Your seasonal color type (Spring Warm / Summer Cool / Autumn Warm / Winter Cool) is revealed.
4. Review the recommended and unflattering color palettes for your season.

tips.title: Pro Tips
items: Self-assessment has limitations. A professional colorist's draping test is most accurate. Use this tool to understand your general direction.
Spring Warm: bright warm tones (peach, coral, golden yellow). Summer Cool: soft cool tones (lavender, pink, sky blue).

items.q: How do I tell if I'm warm or cool tone?

ovulationCalculator.title: Ovulation Calculator
ovulationCalculator.description: Calculate your ovulation day, fertile window and next period from your last period and cycle length, shown on a 6-month calendar
ovulationCalculator.disclaimer: This calculator gives estimates based on an average cycle. It is not a medical diagnosis or a method of birth control. See a gynecologist if your cycles are shorter than 21 or longer than 45 days, you have had no period for 3+ months, or you have been trying to conceive for a year (6 months if 35 or older).

howItWorks.title: How it works
items: Next period = last period start + average cycle length.

Ovulation = next period − luteal phase (default 14 days). Cycle length differences mostly come from the pre-ovulation (follicular) phase, so we count back from the next period. In a 28-day cycle that is around day 14 after your period starts.
Fertile window = 5 days before ovulation to the day after. Sperm can survive up to 5 days; the egg lives 12–24 hours after ovulation.
The most fertile days are the 2 days before ovulation and ovulation day (Wilcox, NEJM 1995: about 10% five days before, about 33% on ovulation day).
For irregular cycles the calendar (rhythm) method is used as a reference: day (shortest cycle − 18) to day (longest cycle − 11).

tips.title: Good to know
items: Normal cycles usually last 21–35 days (24–38 days per FIGO 2018), and varying by a few days is common.
Stress, rapid weight change, poor sleep, breastfeeding and illness can shift ovulation. Treat calendar dates as approximate.
For more accuracy combine ovulation tests (ovulation 24–36 hours after the LH surge), basal body temperature (rises 0.3–0.5°C after ovulation) and cervical mucus (clear and stretchy).
If trying to conceive, having sex every 1–2 days during the fertile window works well — consistency matters more than precise timing.
Do not use this for contraception. With typical use, up to 23 in 100 people relying on fertility awareness methods get pregnant in a year (US CDC).

whatIs.title: What is the Ovulation Calculator?
whatIs.description: The Ovulation Calculator predicts your ovulation date, fertile window, and next expected period by entering your last menstrual period start date and average cycle length, displayed visually on a calendar. It is used by couples planning to conceive to time intercourse and as a reference for natural family planning. A cycle-tracking feature helps you monitor your own patterns over time.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Enter the start date of your last menstrual period.
2. Enter your average cycle length in days (typically 21–35 days).
3. Optionally adjust the luteal phase length (default: 14 days).
4. View the predicted ovulation date, fertile window start/end, and next expected period on the calendar.

tips.title: Pro Tips
items: The fertile window spans roughly 6 days: from 5 days before ovulation through ovulation day. The 1–2 days just before ovulation carry the highest conception probability.
For irregular cycles, using the average of at least 3 months of data produces more reliable predictions.
More precise ovulation tracking methods include: basal body temperature (rises 0.3–0.5°C after ovulation), LH test strips (ovulation predictor kits), and cervical mucus observation.
This tool is for reference only and should not be relied on for contraception. The typical failure rate of the natural family planning method is about 20–25%.

items.q: My cycle isn't 28 days. Can I still use this?
items.a: Yes. You enter your actual cycle length, so any cycle between 21 and 35 days is supported. 28 days is just a statistical average—normal cycles range from 21 to 35 days.

items.q: Can stress or dieting affect my ovulation date?
items.a: Yes. Extreme stress, rapid weight changes, and excessive exercise can shift ovulation timing earlier or later. Consult a gynecologist if your cycle suddenly changes significantly.

items.q: Can I use this calculator to confirm pregnancy?
items.a: No. This tool only estimates ovulation. Pregnancy must be confirmed with a home pregnancy test or medical examination. Use a test if your period is more than two weeks late.

whatIs.title: What is an ovulation calculator?
whatIs.description: Enter the first day of your last period and your average cycle length to estimate your next period, ovulation day and fertile window on a 6-month calendar. It relies on the fact that ovulation happens about 14 days (the luteal phase) before the next period. Logging several recent periods calculates your average cycle, and for irregular cycles it also shows a possible range based on your shortest and longest cycles. It is for planning only and must not be used for birth control.

howToUse.title: How to use
items: Pick the first day of your last period (the first day of bleeding).
Enter your average cycle and period length. If unsure, keep the defaults (28 and 5 days).
Log two or more recent start dates to apply your average cycle; if cycles vary by 8+ days, an irregular range is shown.
If you know your luteal phase from ovulation tests or temperature charting, adjust it between 10 and 16 days.
Check the calendar and the next 6 cycles, and export an .ics file to your phone calendar if you like.

items.q: Isn't ovulation always on day 14?
items.a: Only in a 28-day cycle. Ovulation happens about 14 days before the next period, so in a 35-day cycle it is around day 21 and in a 24-day cycle around day 10. That is why this calculator subtracts the luteal phase from your next expected period.

items.q: How long is the fertile window?
items.a: About 7 days: from 5 days before ovulation to the day after. The 2 days before ovulation and ovulation day are the most fertile.

items.q: What if my cycles are irregular?
items.a: Log several recent start dates (ideally 6 or more). The average is used for predictions, and if your shortest and longest cycles differ by 8+ days a possible range is shown with a dashed outline. The wider the range, the less reliable a calendar is — use ovulation tests too. See a doctor if cycles are shorter than 21 or longer than 45 days.

items.q: When should I take a pregnancy test?
items.a: Tests are most reliable after your period is due (about 2–3 weeks after sex). Testing too early can give a false negative, so if it is negative and your period is still late, retest in a few days or see a doctor.

items.q: Can I use this for birth control?
items.a: No. Ovulation can vary from cycle to cycle even in the same person, and a calendar cannot identify 'safe days'. Use proven methods such as condoms or the pill.

items.q: Where is my data stored?
items.a: Your inputs and period records are saved only in this browser's local storage. They are never sent to a server or added to the link (URL). You can delete them anytime with 'Clear all saved records'.

csatGrade.title: CSAT Grade Calculator
csatGrade.description: Enter raw scores for Korean, Math, English, Korean History and Inquiry to see estimated grades, your average grade and whether you meet minimum CSAT requirements
csatGrade.subject: Select Subject
csatGrade.disclaimer: Cutoffs are the confirmed 2026 CSAT (held Nov 2025) cutoffs; this year's real cutoffs depend on difficulty. Check the official KICE score report for your results.

grading.title: Grading Method
items: Korean, Math and Inquiry are graded relatively by standard score: top 4% = Grade 1, 11% = 2, 23% = 3, 40% = 4, 60% = 5, 77% = 6, 89% = 7, 96% = 8, the rest = 9.

Integrated CSAT: Korean (Speech & Writing / Language & Media) and Math (Probability & Statistics / Calculus / Geometry) are graded on one standard-score scale regardless of elective, so raw-score cutoffs differ by elective.
English is graded absolutely out of 100: 90+ = Grade 1, then every 10 points (80 = 2, 70 = 3 … 20 = 8, below 20 = 9).
Korean History is mandatory and graded absolutely out of 50: 40+ = Grade 1, then every 5 points (35 = 2 … 5 = 8, below 5 = 9). Skipping it voids the whole CSAT score report.
Up to two Inquiry subjects (50 points each). The current elective system continues through the 2027 CSAT; from the 2028 CSAT electives are removed.

tips.title: Notes
items: Grades, standard scores and percentiles shown here are estimates based on the confirmed 2026 CSAT cutoffs. Real grades depend on that year's score distribution.
KICE does not publish raw-score cutoffs. Score reports list only standard scores, percentiles and grades; widely shared raw cutoffs are private-institute estimates.
Minimum CSAT requirements differ by university (areas counted, best one vs. average of two Inquiry subjects, Korean History rule). Always check the admission guide.
Inquiry cutoffs vary a lot by subject, so only an average-level estimate for Social Studies / Science is provided.
Regular admissions use standard scores, percentiles and university-specific converted Inquiry scores rather than grades.

whatIs.title: What is the CSAT Grade Calculator?
whatIs.description: The CSAT Grade Calculator instantly displays your estimated grade by subject using the latest grade cutoff data after you enter your raw scores. It supports all subjects including Korean, Math, English, Social Studies, Science, Vocational Education, and second foreign languages. Full grade cutoff tables are provided to help you set target scores and plan your study strategy.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Select the exam year (academic year).
2. Select a subject and enter your raw score.
3. Your corresponding grade is displayed instantly.
4. Review the full grade cutoff table to identify the score needed for your target grade.

tips.title: Pro Tips
items: Grade cutoffs change every year. Prior-year cutoffs are reference data only—always check the official KICE score report after the actual exam.
English is graded on an absolute scale: 90+ = Grade 1, 80+ = Grade 2, etc.—unlike the relative-scale subjects.
Exploratory subject (탐구) cutoffs vary by selected elective. The same raw score may earn different grades in different subjects.
Mock exam (모의고사) cutoffs differ from actual CSAT cutoffs due to different test-takers and difficulty levels.

items.q: Can the same raw score earn different grades in different years?
items.a: Yes. CSAT uses relative grading (except English), so the same raw score can land in different grade brackets depending on that year's score distribution. Standard scores and percentiles are what actually determine university admissions.

items.q: Which side of a grade cutoff boundary counts as which grade?
items.a: The cutoff is the minimum score for that grade. For example, if Grade 1 cuts at 91, a score of 91 is Grade 1 and 90 is Grade 2.

items.q: How do I compare scores across different exploratory electives?
items.a: Universities use standard scores and percentiles to compensate for difficulty differences between electives. A lower raw score in a harder subject may produce a higher standard score.

whatIs.title: What is the CSAT Grade Calculator?
whatIs.description: Enter raw scores for Korean, Math, English, Korean History and Inquiry at once to see estimated grades per subject, estimated standard scores and percentiles, your average grade and whether you meet minimum CSAT requirements. It also shows the countdown to the 2027 CSAT (Nov 19, 2026). Relatively graded subjects use estimates based on the confirmed 2026 CSAT cutoffs.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Choose your Korean/Math electives and Inquiry areas (Social Studies / Science).
2. Enter raw scores; grades update instantly.
3. Check your average grade and best-3 sum in the blue card.
4. Enter a university's minimum requirement (e.g. best 3 sum ≤ 7) to see if you meet it.
5. Share an image or link; the link restores your scores.

items.q: When is the 2027 CSAT?
items.a: It is scheduled for Thursday, November 19, 2026. Check KICE announcements for the official schedule and score release date.

items.q: Can the same raw score earn different grades?
items.a: Yes. Korean, Math and Inquiry are graded relatively, so grades depend on that year's distribution. English and Korean History use fixed absolute cutoffs.

items.q: Why do Calculus and Probability & Statistics give different grades for the same raw score?
items.a: The integrated CSAT grades by a standard score adjusted using the common section. Because elective groups differ in ability, the same raw score can map to different standard scores and grades.

items.q: What does a 'best 3 sum of 7' requirement mean?
items.a: The sum of your three best grades among Korean, Math, English and Inquiry must be 7 or less, e.g. grades 2, 2, 3. Universities differ on whether Inquiry counts your best subject or the average of two.

items.q: Which grade is a score exactly on the cutoff?
items.a: A cutoff is the minimum score for that grade. If Grade 1 cuts at 92, then 92 is Grade 1 and 91 is Grade 2.

whatIs.title: What is the Lotto Tax Calculator?
whatIs.description: The Lotto Tax Calculator computes the tax withheld on Korean lottery winnings and shows your actual take-home amount. Prizes over 200,000 KRW are subject to 22% withholding (20% income tax + 2% local income tax); amounts exceeding 300 million KRW are taxed at 33% (30% + 3%). Use it to plan your finances if you win.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Select your prize tier or enter a custom prize amount.
2. View the withholding tax amount and net take-home figure.
3. Calculate combined winnings if you won multiple tiers simultaneously.
4. Annuity lottery options can also be calculated to show the after-tax monthly payout.

tips.title: Pro Tips
items: Lotto jackpot prizes are already net of 22% withholding when you collect from Dong Haeng Bokwon. No separate tax filing is required.
Lottery winnings are classified as other income (기타소득). If total other income is 3 million KRW or less annually, withholding is final. Above that, comprehensive income tax filing may be required.
For annuity lotteries, the monthly payment exceeding 200,000 KRW is subject to 22% withholding. Calculate the total 20-year tax burden as well.
Overseas lottery winnings may trigger Korean tax reporting obligations. Consult a tax accountant before collecting.

items.q: If I share winnings with family, is gift tax triggered?
items.a: Yes. Giving money to family members triggers gift tax. Spouses are tax-free up to 600 million KRW over 10 years; adult children up to 50 million KRW. Amounts above those thresholds require a gift tax filing.

items.q: Can I choose between lump sum and annuity?
items.a: Standard Lotto (6/45) pays only as a lump sum. Pension Lottery 720+ offers a choice: 7 million KRW/month for 20 years, or a lump sum (approximately 50–60% of total annuity value).

items.q: Is the take-home amount final, or are there additional taxes later?
items.a: The tax on the winnings themselves is fully settled at the time of collection. Subsequent investments or purchases may generate their own taxes (capital gains, acquisition tax, etc.) separately.

q1.question: How much tax do I pay on a Lotto 1st prize?
q1.answer: Based on an average 1st prize of ~2B KRW: 22% on the first 300M (66M tax) and 33% on the remaining 1.7B (561M tax), totaling ~627M in taxes. Take-home is approximately 1.373B KRW.

q2.question: Do I need to file income tax separately?
q2.answer: No. Lottery winnings are subject to separate taxation, so the withholding tax at source completes your tax obligation. No additional filing is needed.

q3.question: Can I share my winnings with family?
q3.answer: Yes, but gift tax applies. Spouses can receive up to 600M KRW tax-free, adult children up to 50M KRW. Amounts beyond these thresholds are subject to 10-50% gift tax.

detail.title: How it's calculated
detail.a: A value (2026, average income of all insured)
detail.credit: Credits (birth at A, military at A/2)
detail.formula: Monthly pension ≈ Σ(year factor × (A + B) × months) ÷ 240 ÷ 12 + dependent pension. Factor: 2.4 for 1988–1998 (B weighted 0.75), 1.8 for 1999–2007, 1.5 in 2008 falling 0.015/yr to 1.245 in 2025, 1.29 from 2026
detail.cpi: All amounts are in 2026 money. Pensions rise every January by last year's CPI ({p}% in 2026).

guide.title: National pension in a nutshell
guide.source: Sources: National Pension Act (effective 2026-01-01, Act No. 20903), Art. 63-2 (effective 2026-06-17), 2026 A value 3,193,511 KRW, dependent pension (spouse 306,630, child/parent 204,360 KRW per year). Laws: law.go.kr.

formula.title: How the amount is set
items: Basic pension = factor × (A + B) × (1 + 5% per year over 20). With 10–20 years you get 50% plus 5% per year over 10, so the pension is almost proportional to months contributed.
A is the average monthly income of all insured over the 3 years before you claim (3,193,511 KRW for 2026). It is the same for everyone, so lower earners get more per won paid.
B is your own average income revalued to today. This calculator treats your input as B, capped at 6.59M and floored at 0.41M KRW.
The factor depends on when you contributed. As a 40-year replacement rate: 70% for 1988–1998, 60% for 1999–2007, 50% in 2008 falling 0.5%p a year to 41.5% in 2025, and 43% from 2026.
Contribution rate: 3% (1988–92), 6% (1993–97), 9% (1998–2025), 9.5% in 2026 rising 0.5%p a year to 13% in 2033. Employees split it with the employer.

reform.title: What changed with the 2026 reform
items: 43% replacement rate for periods from 1 Jan 2026; earlier periods keep their old rates.
Contribution rate 9% → 9.5% in 2026, +0.5%p a year to 13% in 2033 (employee share 4.75% in 2026).
Birth credit: for children from 2026, 12 months each for the 1st and 2nd child and 18 months for each from the 3rd, with no 50-month cap. Credited at the A value, to one parent or split.
Military credit: up to 12 months of actual service for those discharged from 2026 (was 6). Credited at half the A value.
State guarantee: the state's duty to ensure stable, continuous payment is written into law (Art. 3-2).

timing.title: Early, normal or deferred
items: Early pension: up to 5 years early, −6% per year (0.5%/month), 70% for life at 5 years. Requires 10+ years and no income-earning work; payment stops if you start earning.
Deferred pension: up to 5 years, +0.6% per month (7.2%/yr), 136% at 5 years. You can also defer 50–90% only.
Versus normal, 5-year early breaks even around 77 and 5-year deferral around 84 (pension age 65).

boost.title: Ways to increase your pension
items: Catch-up payment: pay later for exempt or career-break periods, up to 119 months, at the current premium (instalments allowed).
Voluntary enrollment: people aged 18–59 not required to join (homemakers, students) can join.
Continued enrollment: keep contributing from 60 until 65.
Repayment: return a past lump-sum refund with interest to restore that period.
Credits: claim birth/military credits with your pension; an unemployment credit covers 75% of premiums while on job-seeking benefits.

work.title: Working while receiving
items: From 17 Jun 2026, no reduction if monthly earnings (after deductions) are below A + 2M KRW (about 5.19M).
Excess = earnings − A. 2M–3M: 150k + 15% over 2M; 3M–4M: 300k + 20% over 3M; 4M+: 500k + 25% over 4M. Capped at half the pension; dependent pension is not reduced.
The reduction applies only for up to 5 years after the pension starts.

items.q: What if I don't reach 10 years?
items.a: No old-age pension; at 60 you get a refund of contributions (incl. employer share) plus interest. Reaching 10 years via continued enrollment or catch-up payment usually pays off far more.

items.q: Why does NPS show a different amount?
items.a: NPS revalues each year's actual income and knows your exempt periods and credits. This tool assumes a constant average income, so check NPS for the exact figure.

items.q: Does the pension rise with inflation?
items.a: Yes, every January by last year's CPI (2.1% in 2026). Amounts here are in today's money; the nominal amount uses the growth rate you pick.

items.q: Is the pension taxed?
items.a: Only the part from contributions paid since 2002. After pension income and personal deductions, tax is small without other income; NPS withholds monthly and settles in January.

items.q: Can both spouses receive it?
items.a: Yes, each receives their own pension. If one dies, the survivor chooses between their own pension and the survivor's pension; choosing their own adds 30% of the survivor's pension.

items.q: Will I get nothing if the fund runs out?
items.a: The 2025 reform wrote the state's duty to guarantee payment into law (Art. 3-2), so pensions continue from contributions and state responsibility.

whatIs.title: What is the National Pension Calculator?
whatIs.description: The National Pension Calculator estimates your expected monthly National Pension benefit based on years of contribution and average monthly income, using 2025 rules. Compare three scenarios—early collection (up to 5 years early, 6% reduction per year), standard collection (age 63), and deferred collection (up to 5 years delayed, 7.2% increase per year)—to find the optimal claiming strategy.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Enter your total years of National Pension contributions.
2. Enter your average monthly income during the contribution period (based on actual premiums paid).
3. Select your intended collection timing (early, standard, or deferred).
4. View the estimated monthly benefit, annual total, and the break-even points for early vs. deferred collection.

tips.title: Pro Tips
items: The minimum contribution period is 10 years. Below that, you receive a lump-sum refund instead of a monthly pension. You can use voluntary continued enrollment to reach 10 years.

Deferred collection advantage: delaying by 1 year increases your benefit by 7.2%, and the maximum 5-year delay boosts it by 36%. If you expect good health and longevity, deferral can pay off significantly.

If a spouse dies and you receive survivor's pension, there are limits on collecting both your own old-age pension and the survivor's pension simultaneously. Compare both amounts to make the best choice.
The National Pension Service's 내연금 app or website provides more precise estimated benefits based on your actual contribution record.

items.q: If the pension fund runs out, will I stop receiving payments?
items.a: The fund is projected to be depleted around 2055, but payments would continue from the contributions of active workers at that time. Benefit levels or retirement age may be adjusted, but the system itself would not disappear.

items.q: Can voluntary enrollees (housewives, students, etc.) receive a pension?
items.a: Yes. Anyone aged 27–60 may enroll voluntarily. Premiums start from as low as 90,000 KRW/month, and 10+ years of contributions qualify you for a retirement pension.

items.q: Is pension income taxable?
items.a: Pension amounts corresponding to premiums paid after 2002 are subject to income tax as pension income. After the pension income deduction, the effective tax is minimal for annual pensions under approximately 9 million KRW.

tips.title: Pro Tips
items: The minimum contribution period is 10 years. Below that, you receive a lump-sum refund instead of a monthly pension. You can use voluntary continued enrollment to reach 10 years.

Deferred collection advantage: delaying by 1 year increases your benefit by 7.2%, and the maximum 5-year delay boosts it by 36%. If you expect good health and longevity, deferral can pay off significantly.

If a spouse dies and you receive survivor's pension, there are limits on collecting both your own old-age pension and the survivor's pension simultaneously. Compare both amounts to make the best choice.
The National Pension Service's 내연금 app or website provides more precise estimated benefits based on your actual contribution record.

items.q: If the pension fund runs out, will I stop receiving payments?
items.a: The fund is projected to be depleted around 2055, but payments would continue from the contributions of active workers at that time. Benefit levels or retirement age may be adjusted, but the system itself would not disappear.

items.q: Can voluntary enrollees (housewives, students, etc.) receive a pension?
items.a: Yes. Anyone aged 27–60 may enroll voluntarily. Premiums start from as low as 90,000 KRW/month, and 10+ years of contributions qualify you for a retirement pension.

items.q: Is pension income taxable?
items.a: Pension amounts corresponding to premiums paid after 2002 are subject to income tax as pension income. After the pension income deduction, the effective tax is minimal for annual pensions under approximately 9 million KRW.

q1.question: What is the minimum contribution period?
q1.answer: You need at least 10 years (120 months) of contributions to receive the old-age pension. If less than 10 years, you receive a lump-sum refund.

q2.question: Is early or deferred pension better?
q2.answer: If you live to average life expectancy (~83), total benefits are similar. Deferred is better if you live past 85, early is better if below average.

q3.question: Is inflation adjustment included?
q3.answer: Yes, the national pension adjusts annually based on CPI changes. This calculator shows amounts without inflation adjustment.

howToUse.title: How to Use

tips.title: Pro Tips
items: Daily recommended calories: approximately 2,500 kcal for adult men and 2,000 kcal for adult women. A daily 500 kcal deficit translates to roughly 0.5 kg of weight loss per week.
For unknown food calorie counts, refer to the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety's food nutrition database (식품안전나라). For packaged foods, check the nutrition label.
Consistency is the key. Don't aim for perfection from day one—even if you miss a day or two, just pick up where you left off.
Export to CSV weekly and analyze in a spreadsheet to identify which days and foods are responsible for calorie overruns.

items.q: Can my records disappear unexpectedly?

items.q: Can I track macronutrients (carbs, protein, fat) in addition to calories?

items.q: Can I sync data across multiple devices?
items.a: The current version uses local browser storage, so cross-device sync is not supported. Export your data as CSV and import it on another device to transfer records.

items.q: What year is the data from?

items.q: Can freelancers or self-employed individuals use this for comparison?

items.q: How much do you need to earn to be in the top 1%?

whatIs.title: What is the Stock Calculator?
whatIs.description: Calculates what you actually keep from Korean and US stock trades after broker commissions and the securities transaction tax (0.20% on KOSPI/KOSDAQ in 2026). It also shows the break-even sell price, the sell price needed for a target return, average cost and how many shares to buy when averaging down, and FX gains plus capital gains tax (22%, 2.5M KRW deduction) for US stocks.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Profit/Loss tab: choose the market (KOSPI, KOSDAQ, ETF) and enter buy price, sell price, quantity and commission to see net return and break-even price.
2. Target Price tab: enter a target net return (or stop-loss) to get the required sell price, rounded to the KRX tick size.
3. Average Price tab: enter each purchase to get the average cost and how many shares to buy at the current price to reach a target average.
4. US Stocks tab: enter USD prices and buy/sell FX rates to split price gain and FX gain and see the after-tax KRW result.
5. Inputs are stored in the URL for sharing; the share card can hide amounts and quantities.

tips.title: Key Investment Tips
items: Use the actual commission rate from your broker's fee page. Promotional rates may add separate exchange fees.
If you trade often, check the break-even price first: the 0.20% tax on every KOSPI/KOSDAQ sale means you need roughly 0.2–0.25% above your buy price.
Domestic ETFs have no transaction tax on sale, so switching the market to ETF lowers the break-even price.
A US stock can lose in USD but gain in KRW if the dollar rises, which can still be taxable. Check the FX gain line.
Foreign stock gains are netted over the year, so enter other realized foreign stock P/L to see this trade's real tax.

items.q: What is the securities transaction tax in 2026?
items.a: For sales from Jan 1, 2026: KOSPI 0.05% + rural development tax 0.15% = 0.20%, KOSDAQ 0.20%, KONEX 0.10% (KOSPI/KOSDAQ were 0.15% in 2025). Domestic ETFs are exempt.

items.q: Transaction tax vs capital gains tax?
items.a: Transaction tax is charged on every sale regardless of profit. Korean listed stock gains are taxed only for major shareholders; foreign stock gains are netted annually, 2.5M KRW is deducted and 22% (incl. local tax) is filed and paid the following May.

items.q: What are typical commission rates?
items.a: They vary by broker, account type and promotion. Domestic online trades are often around 0.01–0.015%, US stocks around 0.07–0.25%. The defaults are examples; enter your own rate.

items.q: How is the averaging-down quantity calculated?
items.a: Solving (avg × qty + current × x) ÷ (qty + x) = target gives x = qty × (avg − target) ÷ (target − current). It only works when the current price is below the target average.

items.q: Why does my broker statement differ by a few won?
items.a: Brokers round fees and taxes differently (below 1 or 10 KRW), and split fills are rounded per fill.

howItWorks.title: Rate types and how they are calculated
items: Base rate: the reference rate a bank uses for buying and selling currency. Actual trades use this rate plus or minus the bank's margin (spread).
Cash buy/sell: buying foreign cash uses base × (1 + spread), selling uses base × (1 − spread). Cash costs money to store and ship, so its spread is the largest.
Wire send/receive (telegraphic transfer): used for account transfers, with a smaller spread than cash. Overseas transfers may add transfer, cable and intermediary bank fees on top.
Preferential rate: a discount on the spread. With 90%, you pay only 10% of the spread. E.g. base 1,300 KRW, spread 1.75% → 1,322.75 KRW without discount, 1,302.28 KRW with 90%.
Korean banks quote JPY, VND and IDR per 100 units, so this tool shows them per 100 as well.

comparison.title: Cash vs wire transfer vs card payment
items: Cash exchange: uses the cash buy rate. Ordering through a bank app and picking up at a branch or the airport often gets a high preferential rate. Converting back uses the cash sell rate, so you pay the spread twice on a round trip.
Overseas transfer: the wire rate is better than the cash rate, but check per-transfer fees, cable fees and intermediary bank fees too.

Card payments abroad: the local amount is converted to US dollars by the card network (Visa, Mastercard, etc.), then the card issuer converts it to KRW at the rate on the purchase settlement date and adds network and overseas usage fees. Because the settlement date rate applies, the bill can differ from what you expected at checkout.
Beware of DCC (paying in KRW abroad): the merchant side adds its own conversion fee, so it is usually more expensive. Pay in local currency and turn on your card issuer's overseas KRW payment block.

realWorld.title: When to use it
items: Estimating how much to exchange before a trip and how much a preferential rate saves
Checking overseas shopping prices (USD, JPY, EUR) in KRW
Estimating the KRW needed for overseas transfers such as tuition or living costs
Seeing how much leftover foreign cash is worth when converted back
Splitting a KRW budget across currencies for multi-country trips

whatIs.title: What is this calculator?
whatIs.description: It converts between foreign currencies and Korean won, and shows the rates a bank actually applies (cash buy/sell, wire send/receive) along with the effect of a preferential rate. Market rates come from ExchangeRate-API, updated once a day, and the timestamp is shown.

howToUse.title: How to use
items: Tap a currency button (USD, JPY, EUR, CNY, VND, THB) or pick one from the list.
Type the amount you know in either the foreign or the KRW field; the other is calculated instantly.
Choose your bank's preferential rate (e.g. 90% via app) and adjust the cash/wire spreads to your bank's posted rates for better accuracy.
Compare cash and wire amounts with and without the preferential rate in the bank table.
Enter a KRW budget in the travel table to convert it into many currencies at once, and share the result as an image or link.

tips.title: Tips to cut exchange costs
items: Ordering currency through a bank app often gets a higher preferential rate than exchanging at the counter. Choose the pickup place (branch or airport) in advance.
Exchanging and re-exchanging means paying the spread twice. Convert only the cash you need and use a card for the rest.
Korean banks tend to charge large spreads on minor currencies (dong, baht, peso), so compare with taking US dollars and exchanging locally. Check local exchange rates too.
Many banks do not accept foreign coins or buy them at worse rates than notes, so spend them before you leave.

items.q: Why does this rate differ from my bank's rate?
items.a: This tool uses market rates from ExchangeRate-API, updated once a day. Bank base rates are posted several times a day based on the FX market, so they differ depending on timing. Check your bank's posted rates for exact amounts.

items.q: Does a 90% preferential rate cut the fee by 90%?
items.a: It cuts 90% of the spread (bank margin) built into the rate. With a 1,300 KRW base rate and a 1.75% cash spread, you buy dollars at 1,322.75 KRW without a discount and at 1,302.28 KRW with 90%. Separate fees such as transfer fees are not affected.

items.q: Why do cash and wire rates differ?
items.a: Cash requires storage, transport and insurance, so banks add a larger spread. Wire transfers move between accounts with a smaller spread, though transfer and cable fees may apply separately.

items.q: Why is the yen shown per 100?
items.a: Korean banks quote small-unit currencies such as the yen, Vietnamese dong and Indonesian rupiah per 100 units. If 100 yen is 900 KRW, 1 yen is 9 KRW.

items.q: How often are rates updated?
items.a: Market data is updated once a day, and the timestamp is shown on screen. If loading fails, the calculator uses the last rates saved on this device and tells you so.

whatIs.title: What is a Performance Bonus?
whatIs.description: A performance bonus is additional compensation paid beyond base salary, determined by company profitability or individual performance. In Korean companies, bonuses come in various forms including PS (Profit Sharing), PI (Productivity Incentive), management performance bonuses, and individual incentives. PS distributes a portion of company profits to employees, primarily at large corporations like Samsung and Hyundai, with amounts ranging from 0% to several hundred percent of annual salary. PI is awarded based on department or team-level target achievement. Under Korean tax law, bonuses are classified as earned income, subject to progressive income tax (6-45%), local income tax (10% of income tax), and four types of social insurance (National Pension, Health Insurance, Long-term Care Insurance, and Employment Insurance). When a bonus is added, total annual income increases, potentially pushing the taxpayer into a higher tax bracket with a higher marginal rate, resulting in a greater perceived tax burden. This calculator applies the latest 2025 tax rates and social insurance contribution rates to automatically compute deductions and take-home amounts from your pre-tax salary and bonus inputs. The ratio simulation feature lets you compare scenarios from 50% to 500% bonus ratios at a glance, while the tax structure analysis visually shows how tax brackets and additional tax burdens change with and without the bonus.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Enter your pre-tax annual salary and bonus ratio (or amount)
Enter the number of dependents accurately — it affects income tax calculations
Use the simulation tab to compare different ratios at a glance
Check the tax analysis tab for bracket changes and marginal tax rates

tips.title: Tax-Saving Tips for Bonuses
items: Contribute your bonus to an IRP (Individual Retirement Pension) for up to 9M KRW tax credit
Combined with pension savings, up to 9M KRW annual tax credit (16.5% if salary ≤55M KRW)
Spreading bonus payments across months can lower your marginal tax rate
Maximize non-taxable benefits like meal allowances (200K KRW/month)
Don't miss additional deductions at year-end (medical, education, donations, etc.)

items.q: Are social insurance contributions applied to bonuses?
items.a: In the bonus month only employment insurance (0.9%) and income tax are withheld. National pension uses a fixed monthly base, and health insurance on the bonus is charged at next April's settlement. The 2026 pension monthly cap is 6.59M KRW.

items.q: Why does the tax rate on bonuses seem higher than regular salary?
items.a: The bonus itself isn't taxed at a higher rate. Rather, adding the bonus increases your total annual income, potentially pushing you into a higher progressive tax bracket (6-45% in Korea).

items.q: How much can I save by putting my bonus into a retirement pension?
items.a: You can contribute up to 9M KRW annually to an IRP, with a 16.5% tax credit (salary ≤55M KRW) or 13.2% (>55M KRW). A full 9M KRW contribution saves up to 1.485M KRW in taxes.

items.q: Why do withholding taxes differ from actual taxes?
items.a: Withholding uses simplified tax tables for monthly deductions. Year-end settlement reconciles with actual income and deductions. Even if a large amount is withheld from a bonus month, you may get a refund.

items.q: What's the difference between a bonus and performance pay?
items.a: A regular bonus splits the annual salary into extra payments on specific months (total unchanged). Performance pay is additional income beyond the annual salary. Tax calculation methods are the same.

items.q: Does splitting bonus payments across months reduce taxes?
items.a: Splitting bonus payments across months may lower the withholding rate per month, but since total annual income remains the same, the final tax amount at year-end settlement is identical. However, it can help with cash flow management.

items.q: Are bonuses received after resignation still taxed?
items.a: Yes, bonuses paid after resignation are still classified as earned income and subject to income tax and social insurance contributions. They are processed as earned income (not severance), with taxes withheld before payment.

whatIs.title: What is the Enneagram?
whatIs.description: The Enneagram is a personality typing system categorizing human personality into 9 distinct types, each with a unique worldview, core motivation, and fundamental fear. It's a rich psychological tool used for self-understanding, improving relationships, and guiding personal growth.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Answer all 36 questions honestly, based on actual day-to-day behavior.
2. For each question, select how strongly it applies to you.
3. Once complete, scores for all 9 types are calculated and your primary type is identified.
4. Explore your type's core motivation, fear, wings, and growth direction on the results page.

tips.title: Pro Tips
items: Your core type is stable, but stress and growth situations can shift behavioral patterns.
Considering wing (adjacent type) influence provides a more nuanced self-portrait.
Every type has healthy and unhealthy expressions — consciously work toward the healthy direction.
Understanding others' Enneagram types can dramatically reduce conflict and improve communication.
This is a self-exploration tool and does not replace professional psychological counseling.

items.q: Can your Enneagram type change?
items.a: The core type is generally fixed for life. Under stress or growth, you may exhibit traits of adjacent types or move along integration/disintegration arrows.

items.q: Similar scores across multiple types?
items.a: This often indicates strong wing influence. Read both descriptions to find which resonates more deeply.

items.q: How does it differ from MBTI?
items.a: MBTI focuses on cognitive functions and preferences. The Enneagram centers on core motivations, fears, and desires — exploring the deeper 'why' behind behavior.

items.q: Surprised by my result?
items.a: Read full descriptions of the top types. The one whose core fear and desire resonate most is usually the most accurate.

satVisualizer.description: Separating Axis Theorem — Detect collision between two convex polygons using separating axes

whatIs.title: What is SAT?
whatIs.content: If two convex shapes are not colliding, there must exist an axis (Separating Axis) that separates them. Conversely, if projections overlap on all candidate axes, the shapes are colliding. This is the core of the Separating Axis Theorem.

math.title: Mathematical Principle
math.content: For each edge of both polygons, compute the perpendicular normal. These normals are the separating axis candidates. Project all vertices onto each axis (using dot product) to get 1D intervals, then check if the intervals overlap. If any axis has no overlap, there is no collision.

convex.title: Why Only Convex Polygons?
convex.content: Concave polygons cannot be fully tested with edge normals alone. To apply SAT to concave shapes, you must first perform Convex Decomposition.

optimization.title: Optimization Techniques
optimization.content: Early Exit: Return 'no collision' as soon as one separating axis is found. This makes most non-collision cases very efficient. The MTV (Minimum Translation Vector) is the axis direction with the smallest overlap, used for collision resolution.

stepsGuide.description: Click each axis to see its projection on the canvas.

threeView.explanation: Project two 3D boxes onto X, Y, and Z axes. If shadows overlap on ALL axes, it's a collision. If there's a GAP on even one axis, the shapes are separated. The 4 viewports show projections from each axis direction.

whatIs.title: What is SAT Collision Detection?
whatIs.description: SAT (Separating Axis Theorem) is a key algorithm used in game physics engines, robotics, and CAD to quickly and accurately detect collisions between convex shapes.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Drag the blue (A) or amber (B) polygon on the canvas to move it
Press the play button to run the step-by-step axis checking animation
Check GAP/OVERLAP for each axis in the projection panel
Adjust vertices, size, and rotation in the parameter panel to experiment
View and copy the TypeScript implementation in the Code tab

howItWorks.title: How It Works
items: Extract normals (perpendicular directions) from each edge of both convex polygons to build the list of candidate axes to test.
Project all vertices onto each axis using the dot product to compute each polygon's 1D interval (min~max) along that axis.
Check whether the two intervals overlap on each axis. If any axis shows a gap, immediately return 'no collision' (Early Exit).
If all axes overlap, declare a collision and compute the MTV (Minimum Translation Vector) along the axis with the smallest overlap.

realWorld.title: Real-World Applications
items: Used in 2D/3D game physics engines (Unity, Unreal collision pipelines) for convex shape collision detection.
Applied in robotics path planning to check for obstacle collisions with robot arms and mobile robots.
Used in CAD/manufacturing part interference checks and real-time obstacle avoidance for autonomous vehicles.
Directly applicable to collision detection logic in HTML5 Canvas-based interactive web applications.

comparison.title: Similar Algorithms
items: AABB vs SAT — AABB handles only axis-aligned rectangles at O(1) speed but is inaccurate for rotated shapes. SAT supports any convex polygon.
GJK (Gilbert-Johnson-Keerthi) — More general than SAT and can compute minimum distances between convex shapes, but is more complex to implement.
OBB (Oriented Bounding Box) — A 3D extension of SAT that checks 15 axes for rotated bounding box collisions.

tips.title: Learning Tips
items: Start by placing shapes far apart and observe the first axis projection
Slowly move shapes closer and watch GAP turn into OVERLAP
A triangle (3) and square (4) check 7 axes total (3+4=7)
Two pentagons check 10 axes — more vertices means higher cost

items.q: Can SAT work with circles?
items.a: Yes, circles theoretically need infinite axes, but in practice you only need to add one axis toward the nearest vertex. Commonly used for polygon-circle collision.

items.q: Does SAT work in 3D?
items.a: Yes, in 3D the axis candidates are face normals plus cross products of all edge pairs. Used in OBB (Oriented Bounding Box) collision detection.

items.q: What is SAT's time complexity?
items.a: O(n × m) — where n is the vertex count of polygon A and m is polygon B's. Early Exit makes non-collision cases much faster.

aabbVisualizer.title: AABB Collision Detection Visualizer
aabbVisualizer.description: Axis-Aligned Bounding Box — Detect collision between two rectangles aligned to axes

stepsGuide.description: Check X and Y axis projections to determine collision.
stepsGuide.colliding: Collision! Both X and Y axes overlap

whatIs.title: What is AABB Collision Detection?
whatIs.description: AABB (Axis-Aligned Bounding Box) is the most basic and fastest algorithm for detecting collisions between two axis-aligned rectangles. Widely used in game physics, UI hit testing, and broad phase collision detection.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Drag the blue (A) or amber (B) box to move it
Watch the X and Y axis projection bars update in real time
Adjust box sizes with sliders to experiment with different cases
View and copy the implementation code in the Code tab

howItWorks.title: How It Works
items: Calculate the min/max coordinates (minX, maxX, minY, maxY) of each rectangle.
Compare X-axis intervals: if A.maxX < B.minX or B.maxX < A.minX, the shapes are separated on X.
Compare Y-axis intervals the same way.
If both X and Y axes overlap, it's a collision. If either axis is separated, return no-collision.

realWorld.title: Real-World Applications
items: Used as the broad phase filter in game engines — quickly eliminates obviously non-colliding pairs before precise checks.
The most widely used collision method in 2D scrolling games for enemies, items, and player characters.
Used in map apps for rectangular region POI (point of interest) queries and in web UI drag-and-drop overlap detection.
Ideal for simple hit testing such as selection-area intersection checks in image editors.

comparison.title: Similar Algorithms
items: SAT — A superset of AABB that handles rotated convex polygons, but requires more computation.
OBB — A bounding box that allows rotation, more precise than AABB but loses the axis-alignment advantage.
Circle-circle collision — Compares distance between centers vs sum of radii, equally fast and more accurate for circular objects.

tips.title: Learning Tips
items: AABB doesn't consider rotation — boxes are always axis-aligned
If either X or Y axis is separated, there's no collision (Early Exit)
AABB is a special case of SAT: only 2 axes (X and Y) to check
Games often use AABB for quick filtering before precise detection (SAT, etc.)

items.q: What's the difference between AABB and SAT?
items.a: AABB only handles axis-aligned rectangles and checks 2 axes. SAT handles any convex polygon and checks all edge normals. AABB is much faster but inaccurate for rotated shapes.

items.q: Why use AABB in Broad Phase?
items.a: With hundreds of objects, applying SAT to every pair is slow. AABB quickly filters out obviously separated pairs, greatly reducing the number of precise checks needed.

items.q: How does 3D AABB work?
items.a: Same principle. Compare ranges on X, Y, and Z axes — all three must overlap for a collision.

bfsDfsVisualizer.title: BFS / DFS Search Visualizer
bfsDfsVisualizer.description: Compare Breadth-First Search and Depth-First Search on a grid

stepsGuide.description: Observe which nodes are explored at each step.
stepsGuide.bfsDescription: BFS uses a queue (FIFO) to explore nodes level by level from the start.
stepsGuide.dfsDescription: DFS uses a stack (LIFO) to go deep in one direction before backtracking.

whatIs.title: What are BFS and DFS?
whatIs.description: BFS (Breadth-First Search) and DFS (Depth-First Search) are the two most fundamental graph/tree traversal algorithms. BFS explores nodes closest to the start first, while DFS goes as deep as possible before backtracking.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Click/drag on the grid to draw or erase walls
Set the start point (green) and goal point (red)
Choose BFS, DFS, or side-by-side comparison mode
Press play to watch the search process step by step
Use the random maze button to experiment with different scenarios

howItWorks.title: How It Works
items: BFS — Push the start node onto a queue, then repeatedly dequeue a node and enqueue all unvisited neighbors (marking them visited). This explores nodes level by level.
DFS — Push the start node onto a stack, then repeatedly pop a node and push unvisited neighbors. This dives deep along one path before backtracking (also implementable recursively).
BFS uses a FIFO queue so nodes closest to the start are processed first. DFS uses a LIFO stack so the most recently discovered node is processed first.
Both algorithms have O(V+E) time complexity. On a grid, that's O(rows × columns).

realWorld.title: Real-World Applications
items: BFS — Finding degrees of connection in social networks (LinkedIn 1st/2nd connections) and shortest path navigation in unweighted graphs.
BFS — Web crawlers collecting links level by level, exploring pages in order of distance from the start.
DFS — Maze solving, puzzle solving, compiler syntax tree traversal, and Git commit history exploration.
DFS — Essential for topological sorting (determining build dependency order) and finding strongly connected components (SCC).

comparison.title: Similar Algorithms
items: BFS vs DFS — BFS guarantees the shortest path (unweighted) but requires O(V) memory. DFS is memory-efficient but doesn't guarantee shortest path.
A* — An extension of BFS that uses a heuristic to steer toward the goal, finding shortest paths much faster.
Dijkstra — A weighted version of BFS using a priority queue to find shortest paths in weighted graphs.

tips.title: Learning Tips
items: BFS guarantees the shortest path (in unweighted graphs)
DFS uses less memory but doesn't guarantee the shortest path
Observe the different search patterns in mazes with narrow corridors
Compare visited node counts and path lengths in side-by-side mode

items.q: Is BFS always better than DFS?
items.a: No. BFS is ideal when shortest path is needed, while DFS is better for exhaustive search or topological sorting. DFS also uses less memory.

items.q: What's the time complexity?
items.a: Both are O(V + E) — V is the number of nodes, E is the number of edges. On a grid, that's O(rows × columns).

items.q: How does this relate to A*?
items.a: A* extends BFS by using a heuristic (estimated distance to goal) to guide the search direction. It finds the shortest path much more efficiently than BFS.

insertionSortVisualizer.title: Insertion Sort Visualizer
insertionSortVisualizer.description: Watch elements being picked up and inserted into their correct position in the sorted portion

stepsGuide.description: Observe how each element is inserted into its correct position.

whatIs.title: What is Insertion Sort?
whatIs.description: Insertion Sort works like sorting cards — pick up one element at a time and insert it into its correct position in the sorted portion. It's very efficient for small or nearly-sorted data.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Adjust the array size
Purple bar is the element being inserted
Orange bars are elements shifting right
The lighter area on the left is the sorted portion
Notice how nearly-sorted input finishes much faster

howItWorks.title: How It Works
items: Starting from the second element, save the current element as the 'key'
Shift elements in the sorted portion that are greater than the key one position to the right
Insert the key into the vacated spot
Repeat for every element through to the last one

realWorld.title: Real-World Applications
items: Card sorting — the most natural way people arrange cards in their hand
Keeping a sorted list up to date with small insertions in database systems
Used inside Python's Timsort for sorting small sub-arrays (runs)
Online algorithm — each incoming value can immediately be inserted into its sorted position

comparison.title: Similar Algorithms
items: Bubble Sort — also O(n²), but Insertion Sort makes fewer comparisons and shifts on average, making it the preferred choice in practice
Shell Sort — an extension of Insertion Sort using gaps between comparisons, achieving O(n^1.3–1.5) in practice
Binary Insertion Sort — uses binary search to find the insertion position, reducing comparisons to O(n log n), but shifting is still O(n²)

tips.title: Learning Tips
items: Nearly-sorted arrays run close to O(n)
Reversed arrays show worst case O(n²)
It's both stable and in-place
For small arrays (n<50), it can be faster than Quick Sort

items.q: How does it differ from Bubble Sort?
items.a: Insertion Sort inserts into the sorted portion, Bubble Sort repeatedly swaps adjacent elements. Insertion Sort is faster on average.

items.q: Time complexity?
items.a: Best O(n), average/worst O(n²). Space O(1).

selectionSortVisualizer.title: Selection Sort Visualizer
selectionSortVisualizer.description: Watch the minimum being found and moved to the front at each pass

stepsGuide.description: Observe how the minimum is found and swapped into position.

whatIs.title: What is Selection Sort?
whatIs.description: Selection Sort finds the minimum element in the unsorted portion and places it at the end of the sorted portion. Very simple to implement but always requires O(n²) comparisons.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Adjust the array size
Red bar is the current minimum found so far
Yellow bar is the element being compared
Purple background shows the scan range
Each pass moves exactly one element to its final position

howItWorks.title: How It Works
items: Find the index of the minimum value in the unsorted portion
Swap it with the first element of the unsorted portion
The sorted portion grows by one element
Scan the remaining unsorted portion for the next minimum
Repeat n-1 times — always exactly O(n²) comparisons

realWorld.title: Real-World Applications
items: Useful when swap cost is high — Selection Sort makes at most n-1 swaps total
Flash memory / EEPROM environments where write operations are expensive
Teaching 'find minimum + swap' as a fundamental programming pattern
Small datasets where simplicity of implementation outweighs performance

comparison.title: Similar Algorithms
items: Bubble Sort — more swaps (up to O(n²)) but can exit early with best case O(n). Selection Sort always does exactly O(n²) comparisons
Insertion Sort — faster than Selection Sort in most cases, especially for nearly-sorted data
Heap Sort — improves Selection Sort's 'find minimum' step using a heap, achieving O(n log n)

tips.title: Learning Tips
items: Always performs exactly n(n-1)/2 comparisons regardless of input
Maximum n-1 swaps, very few compared to Bubble Sort
Unstable sort — equal elements may change order
Advantageous when memory writes are expensive (minimal swaps)

items.q: How does it differ from Bubble Sort?
items.a: Selection Sort finds the minimum position first, then swaps once. Bubble Sort repeatedly swaps adjacent elements. Selection Sort makes far fewer swaps.

items.q: Time complexity?
items.a: Always O(n²) comparisons. O(n) swaps. Space O(1).

heapSortVisualizer.title: Heap Sort Visualizer
heapSortVisualizer.description: Watch heap construction and extraction through simultaneous tree and bar chart views

stepsGuide.description: Observe how the binary heap is built and the maximum is extracted at each step.

whatIs.title: What is Heap Sort?
whatIs.description: Heap Sort is a comparison-based sorting algorithm that uses a binary heap data structure. It first builds a max-heap, then repeatedly extracts the root (maximum value) to sort the array. It always guarantees O(n log n) and is an in-place sort requiring no extra memory.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Adjust the array size (max 31 recommended for clear tree visualization)
The tree view and bar chart update simultaneously
In the build phase, watch the heap property being restored bottom-up
In the extract phase, the root (max) moves to the end of the array
Gray nodes are already sorted and removed from the heap

howItWorks.title: How It Works
items: Convert the input array into a max-heap (Build Heap, O(n))
Swap the root (maximum value) with the last element of the heap
Shrink the heap size by 1, then run Heapify (sift-down) from the root
Sift-down: compare the root with its children and swap with the larger child, repeating until heap property is restored
Repeat until heap size reaches 1 — the array is now sorted in ascending order

realWorld.title: Real-World Applications
items: Operating system process schedulers using a priority queue implementation
Real-time systems requiring guaranteed worst-case O(n log n) sorting
Top-K problems — extracting the top K items from a large dataset (news rankings, top-N search results)
Event-driven simulations for managing timer queues
Priority queues in Dijkstra's and A* shortest-path algorithms

comparison.title: Similar Algorithms
items: Quick Sort — faster in practice due to better cache locality, but worst case O(n²). Heap Sort always guarantees O(n log n)
Merge Sort — also O(n log n) guaranteed. Heap Sort is in-place (no extra memory), but Merge Sort is stable and Heap Sort is not
Binary Heap vs Fibonacci Heap — Fibonacci Heaps offer O(1) amortized decrease-key, making Dijkstra theoretically faster, though rarely used in practice

tips.title: Learning Tips
items: In a max-heap, every parent is greater than or equal to its children
Building the heap takes O(n) time (not O(n log n)!)
Each extraction moves the maximum to its correct final position
Reversed arrays build the heap with fewest swaps (already satisfies heap property)

items.q: How does it compare to Quick Sort?
items.a: Heap Sort guarantees worst-case O(n log n) but has worse cache locality, making it slower in practice than Quick Sort. Use it when worst-case guarantees matter.

items.q: Is it a stable sort?
items.a: No. The relative order of equal elements may change during heap extraction.

items.q: How does it relate to priority queues?
items.a: A heap is the standard implementation of a priority queue. The priority queues used in Dijkstra and A* algorithms are binary heaps.

dijkstraVisualizer.title: Dijkstra's Shortest Path Visualizer
dijkstraVisualizer.description: Learn Dijkstra's algorithm for finding shortest paths in weighted grids

stepsGuide.description: Observe how Dijkstra selects the node with the shortest distance.
stepsGuide.dijkstraDescription: Dijkstra always explores the node with the smallest distance from the start. No heuristic — only actual distances.

whatIs.title: What is Dijkstra's Algorithm?
whatIs.description: Dijkstra's algorithm finds the shortest path from one vertex to all other vertices in a weighted graph. Invented by Edsger Dijkstra in 1956, it is widely used in navigation, network routing, and game AI.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Choose a weight type — Uniform (1), Random (1-5), or Terrain
Click/drag to draw walls on the grid
Toggle weight display to see movement costs per cell
Toggle distance display to see shortest distances from start
Use Dijkstra vs A* mode to compare search efficiency

howItWorks.title: How It Works
items: Initialize the start node's distance to 0 and all other nodes to infinity.
Use a greedy strategy: always select the unvisited node with the smallest known distance.
For each neighbor of the selected node, compute the new distance: dist[current] + weight(edge).
If the new distance is smaller, update (relax) it and record the parent. Repeat until all nodes are visited.

realWorld.title: Real-World Applications
items: Core algorithm for road network shortest path in navigation apps (Google Maps, Kakao Maps).
Used in network routing protocols (OSPF) to route packets along minimum-cost paths.
Airline route optimization (weight = cost/time) and logistics delivery route planning.
Finding the shortest connection path (degrees of separation) between two users in social networks.

comparison.title: Similar Algorithms
items: A* vs Dijkstra — A* uses a heuristic to prioritize exploration toward the goal, making it faster. Dijkstra computes all shortest distances without needing a specific destination.
Bellman-Ford — Supports negative edge weights at O(VE), which is slower. Dijkstra only works on graphs with non-negative edge weights.
Floyd-Warshall — Computes shortest paths for all pairs of nodes in O(V³). Dijkstra computes from a single source only.

tips.title: Learning Tips
items: Dijkstra is a special case of A* where h=0
With uniform weights, Dijkstra behaves identically to BFS
In terrain mode, observe how paths detour around heavy (dark) areas
Compare with A* to see Dijkstra exploring more nodes

items.q: What's the difference from A*?
items.a: Dijkstra uses only actual distance from start (g). A* adds a heuristic (h) to guide search toward the goal, making it more efficient.

items.q: What about negative weights?
items.a: Dijkstra cannot handle negative edge weights. Use the Bellman-Ford algorithm for graphs with negative weights.

items.q: What's the time complexity?
items.a: O((V + E) log V) with a binary heap. Can be improved to O(V log V + E) with a Fibonacci heap.

mergeSortVisualizer.title: Merge Sort Visualizer
mergeSortVisualizer.description: Watch the array being split in half and merged back together in sorted order

stepsGuide.description: Observe how the array is split and merged step by step.

whatIs.title: What is Merge Sort?
whatIs.description: Merge Sort is a divide-and-conquer algorithm that splits the array in half, recursively sorts each half, then merges the two sorted halves back together. It guarantees O(n log n) time complexity and is a stable sort that preserves the relative order of equal elements.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Adjust the array size with the slider (5-50)
Generate different inputs with Random, Nearly Sorted, or Reversed buttons
Teal bars are the left sub-array, orange bars are the right sub-array
Yellow means comparing, purple means placing a merged element
Follow the split-merge flow in the Code tab

howItWorks.title: How It Works
items: Split (divide) the array in half
Recursively merge-sort each half
