nQueensVisualizer.description: Watch backtracking place N queens on an N×N board with no mutual attacks

stepsGuide.description: Watch the algorithm place a queen per row, backtracking on conflicts.

whatIs.title: What is N-Queens?
whatIs.description: Place N queens on an N×N chessboard so no two attack each other. A classic backtracking problem.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Select board size 4-12
Press play to watch backtracking
Purple circles are queens, red overlay shows attacks
Yellow is current cell, red marks conflicts
Code tab highlights executing line

howItWorks.title: How It Works
items: Place one queen per row starting from row 0
Check column and diagonal conflicts
No conflict: advance; conflict: try next column
All columns fail: backtrack to previous row
Time: O(N!) with pruning

realWorld.title: Applications
items: Constraint satisfaction — scheduling, resource allocation
VLSI circuit placement
Parallel computing education
AI search strategy benchmarks

comparison.title: Similar Algorithms
items: Backtracking vs Branch and Bound
Sudoku solving — same structure
Graph Coloring — similar constraints

tips.title: Tips
items: Try N=4 first — only 2 solutions
Attempts grow exponentially with N
Red overlay shows why columns are blocked
First queen position affects total search

items.q: Solutions for N=1,2,3?
items.a: N=1: trivial. N=2,3: no solutions. N≥4 has solutions.

items.q: Time complexity?
items.a: Worst O(N!), pruning makes it much faster.

items.q: 8-Queens solutions?
items.a: 92 distinct, 12 fundamental (removing symmetry).

shellSortVisualizer.title: Shell Sort Visualizer
shellSortVisualizer.description: Watch Shell Sort compare and swap elements across diminishing gaps with bar chart and arc visualization

stepsGuide.description: Watch elements gap-apart compared and swapped, reducing gaps to 1.

whatIs.title: What is Shell Sort?
whatIs.description: Shell Sort (1959) improves insertion sort by comparing far-apart elements first, then reducing the gap.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Adjust array size (5-50)
Choose gap sequence: Shell, Knuth, or Hibbard
Generate arrays with Random, Nearly Sorted, Reversed
Press play to watch step by step
Purple arcs show gap distances

howItWorks.title: How It Works
items: Start with largest gap (e.g., n/2)
Compare/swap elements gap positions apart
Insertion sort on each gap-spaced subsequence
Reduce gap and repeat; gap=1 is standard insertion sort
Time: Shell O(n^2), Knuth O(n^{3/2})

realWorld.title: Applications
items: Embedded systems — in-place, non-recursive
uClibc, bzip2 use Shell Sort
Education — gap sequence analysis
Medium-sized data sorting

comparison.title: Similar Algorithms
items: Shell vs Insertion Sort — gaps resolve long-range inversions
Shell vs Quick Sort — non-recursive but slower average
Comb Sort — gap concept applied to bubble sort

tips.title: Tips
items: Compare different gap sequences on same array
Large gaps quickly fix reversed arrays
Gap=1 phase runs fast on nearly-sorted data
Arc length visualizes gap size

items.q: Optimal gap sequence?
items.a: Open problem. Ciura empirical sequence is fastest in practice.

items.q: Is it stable?
items.a: No. Gap-based swaps can change relative order.

items.q: Time complexity?
items.a: Depends on gap sequence. Shell O(n^2), Hibbard O(n^{3/2}).

avlTreeVisualizer.title: AVL Tree Visualizer
avlTreeVisualizer.description: Learn AVL tree insert, delete, and rotations (LL/RR/LR/RL) with step-by-step animations

stepsGuide.description: Observe how the AVL tree maintains balance after each operation.
stepsGuide.hint: Enter a value and press Execute to start.

whatIs.title: What is an AVL Tree?
whatIs.description: An AVL tree is a self-balancing BST where the height difference between left and right subtrees of every node is at most 1. Invented by Adelson-Velsky and Landis in 1962, it guarantees O(log n) operations through automatic rotation rebalancing.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Enter a value and choose Insert or Delete
Watch the balance factor (BF) beside each node — |BF| > 1 means imbalance
Observe the rotation type (LL/RR/LR/RL) when rebalancing occurs
Generate random trees to explore different rotation patterns
Switch between insert code and rotation code in the Code tab

tips.title: Learning Tips
items: LL: left-left insertion → single right rotation
RR: right-right insertion → single left rotation
LR: left-right insertion → double rotation (left then right)
RL: right-left insertion → double rotation (right then left)
AVL is faster than Red-Black for lookups, but Red-Black has less rotation overhead for frequent inserts/deletes

items.q: AVL vs Red-Black tree?
items.a: AVL enforces stricter balance (height diff ≤ 1), making lookups faster. Red-Black uses looser balance, making inserts/deletes faster.

items.q: Rotation time complexity?
items.a: Both single (LL/RR) and double (LR/RL) rotations are O(1). Insert may trigger up to 2 rotations; delete up to O(log n).

items.q: What is the balance factor?
items.a: BF = left subtree height − right subtree height. AVL requires -1 ≤ BF ≤ 1 for all nodes.

heapVisualizer.title: Heap / Priority Queue Visualizer
heapVisualizer.description: Learn min-heap and max-heap insert, extract, and heapify with dual tree+array view

stepsGuide.description: Observe how the heap property is maintained during each operation.
stepsGuide.hint: Enter a value and press Execute to start.

whatIs.title: What is a Heap?
whatIs.description: A heap is a complete binary tree where the parent is always greater (max-heap) or smaller (min-heap) than its children. Efficiently implemented as an array, it is the core data structure behind priority queues.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Select Min/Max Heap, then run Insert, Extract, or Heapify
Compare how the same data appears in tree view vs array view
Check the index mapping formulas: parent, left child, right child
Heapify converts an unsorted array into a heap in O(n)

tips.title: Learning Tips
items: Insert: add at end → bubble up (compare with parent, swap if needed)
Extract: remove root → move last to root → bubble down
Heapify processes only internal nodes (bottom-up), achieving O(n)
Used in priority queues, heap sort, and Dijkstra's algorithm

items.q: Heap vs BST?
items.a: Heap: parent≥children (max) or parent≤children (min), O(1) min/max. BST: left<parent<right, O(log n) arbitrary search.

items.q: Why use an array?
items.a: A heap is a complete binary tree, so parent/children indices can be computed in O(1) without pointers.

items.q: Why is heapify O(n)?
items.a: Bottom-up processing means many deep nodes move little, few shallow nodes move far. The sum is O(n).

linkedListVisualizer.title: Linked List Visualizer
linkedListVisualizer.description: Learn singly and doubly linked list insert, delete, search, and reverse with pointer animations

stepsGuide.description: Watch how pointers (next/prev) change with each operation.
stepsGuide.hint: Select an operation and press Execute to start.

whatIs.title: What is a Linked List?
whatIs.description: A linked list is a linear data structure where each node stores data and a reference (pointer) to the next node. Unlike arrays, it doesn't require contiguous memory, and insertions/deletions are O(1).

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Choose singly or doubly linked, then try various operations
Compare insert/delete at head, tail, and arbitrary index
Watch the reverse operation flip all pointers
Note the dashed prev pointers in doubly linked lists

tips.title: Learning Tips
items: Head insert/delete is O(1); tail insert is O(1) with a tail pointer
Index access is O(n) — arrays offer O(1) but linked lists require traversal
Doubly linked lists allow bidirectional traversal at 2x memory cost
Real-world: browser history, LRU cache, memory allocation

items.q: Array vs Linked List?
items.a: Array: O(1) index access, O(n) insert/delete. Linked List: O(n) access, O(1) insert/delete.

items.q: Singly vs Doubly?
items.a: Singly: less memory, one-way only. Doubly: two-way traversal, O(1) deletion with prev pointer.

items.q: What is a circular linked list?
items.a: The last node's next points to the first node instead of null. Used in round-robin scheduling.

graphReprVisualizer.title: Graph Representation Visualizer
graphReprVisualizer.description: Visualize graphs with synchronized adjacency matrix and adjacency list views in real time

controls.selectedHint: Node {node} selected — click another node to add an edge
controls.instructions: Click empty space: add node | Click node: select/connect | Drag node: move

whatIs.title: What is Graph Representation?
whatIs.description: A graph consists of vertices (nodes) and edges. The same graph can be represented as an adjacency matrix (2D array) or adjacency list (array of lists), each with different trade-offs.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Click empty space to add nodes
Click node A then node B to add an edge
Watch the matrix and list update in real time
Toggle directed/undirected and weighted/unweighted

tips.title: Learning Tips
items: Adjacency matrix: O(V²) space, O(1) edge lookup. Best for dense graphs
Adjacency list: O(V+E) space, O(degree) edge lookup. Best for sparse graphs
Most real-world graphs (social networks, web) are sparse, so adjacency lists are standard
An undirected matrix is symmetric; a directed one is not

items.q: Which representation to use?
items.a: Dense graph → matrix. Sparse graph → list. Most practical graphs are sparse.

items.q: What is graph density?
items.a: Actual edges / maximum possible edges. Close to 1 = dense, close to 0 = sparse.

items.q: What is degree?
items.a: The number of edges connected to a node. In directed graphs, split into in-degree and out-degree.

pathfindingCompareVisualizer.title: Pathfinding Compare (A* vs Dijkstra)
pathfindingCompareVisualizer.description: Run A* and Dijkstra simultaneously on the same map to visually compare search coverage and efficiency

stepsGuide.description: Watch A* (blue) and Dijkstra (orange) search simultaneously.
stepsGuide.comparison: A* uses a heuristic (Manhattan distance) to prioritize exploring toward the goal, reducing unnecessary exploration. Dijkstra explores uniformly in all directions.
stepsGuide.hint: Press Play to start the comparison.

whatIs.title: A* vs Dijkstra
whatIs.description: Both algorithms find shortest paths, but A* uses a heuristic (estimated distance to goal) to explore fewer nodes. Dijkstra expands uniformly from the start.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Draw walls or generate a maze for obstacles
Place start (S) and end (E) points
Press Play to watch both algorithms search simultaneously
Compare visited node counts and path lengths after completion

tips.title: Learning Tips
items: In open space, A* explores far fewer nodes than Dijkstra
In mazes, the difference between the two algorithms shrinks
Compare the shapes of blue (A*) and orange (Dijkstra) search regions
Purple cells were explored by both algorithms

items.q: Is A* always faster?
items.a: Usually yes, but in worst case (all paths similar cost) it matches Dijkstra. Better heuristic = bigger advantage.

items.q: Same path length?
items.a: Yes, both guarantee shortest path (with admissible heuristic). The difference is in explored nodes, not path quality.

items.q: What is a heuristic?
items.a: An estimate of the cost from current position to the goal. This tool uses Manhattan distance (|dx|+|dy|).

redBlackTreeVisualizer.title: Red-Black Tree Visualizer
redBlackTreeVisualizer.description: Learn how a self-balancing BST maintains balance using color rules and rotations on insert/delete

stepsGuide.description: Watch how a Red-Black Tree maintains balance using color rules.
stepsGuide.hint: Enter a value and click Execute to begin.

redBlackTreeVisualizer.rule1: Every node is red or black
redBlackTreeVisualizer.rule3: Red node's children are always black
redBlackTreeVisualizer.rule4: All paths have equal black height

whatIs.title: What is a Red-Black Tree?
whatIs.description: A self-balancing BST that assigns red/black colors to nodes and enforces 5 rules to guarantee O(log n) worst-case search. Used internally by Java TreeMap and C++ std::map.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Enter a value and click Insert
Watch the recoloring and rotation steps
Click a node to delete it
Use Random to quickly add multiple values

howItWorks.title: How It Works
items: New nodes are always inserted as red
If parent is red, violation occurs → recolor or rotate based on uncle's color
Rotations (left/right) restructure the tree to restore balance
Deletion uses double-black handling to maintain black height

realWorld.title: Real-World Applications
items: Java TreeMap/TreeSet, C++ std::map/std::set internals
Linux kernel CFS scheduler
Database in-memory index structures
Java HashMap (8+) bucket tree conversion

comparison.title: Similar Algorithms
items: AVL vs Red-Black — AVL is stricter (faster search) but more rotations on insert/delete
B-Tree — optimized for disk-based storage, Red-Black for memory-based
Skip List — probabilistic, simpler implementation but less cache-efficient

tips.title: Learning Tips
items: Check which rule is violated after insertion first
Uncle node's color is the key to deciding recolor vs rotation
Compare rotation counts with AVL tree

items.q: Why Red-Black over AVL?
items.a: Fewer rotations on insert/delete, making it faster in practice for write-heavy workloads.

items.q: What is black height?
items.a: The number of black nodes on any path from root to leaf. Must be equal for all paths.

bTreeVisualizer.title: B-Tree Visualizer
bTreeVisualizer.description: Learn the core data structure of database indexing — B-Tree insert, delete, and search step by step

stepsGuide.description: Watch how a B-Tree maintains balance through node splitting.
stepsGuide.hint: Enter a value and click Execute to begin.

whatIs.title: What is a B-Tree?
whatIs.description: A self-balancing multi-way search tree that stores multiple keys per node. Designed to minimize disk I/O, it's the standard for database and filesystem indexing.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Set the order (t) — each node stores up to 2t-1 keys
Insert values and observe the split process
Use Search to see the path taken to find a key
When a node overflows, it splits and promotes the median

howItWorks.title: How It Works
items: Insert adds keys to leaf nodes
When a node is full (2t-1 keys), it splits: median goes up, left/right split
Search compares keys at each level and descends to the appropriate child
Delete borrows from siblings or merges nodes when underflowing

realWorld.title: Real-World Applications
items: MySQL InnoDB, PostgreSQL indexes (B+ tree variant)
Filesystems (NTFS, ext4, HFS+) directory indexing
MongoDB, CouchDB NoSQL database indexes
Key-value stores (LevelDB, RocksDB) SSTable indexes

comparison.title: Similar Algorithms
items: B+ Tree — stores all data in leaves with leaf linked list, optimal for range queries
Red-Black Tree — binary tree for memory, B-Tree for disk
LSM Tree — write-optimized, better sequential writes than B-Tree

tips.title: Learning Tips
items: Start with order 2 (2-3-4 tree) to learn split patterns
Explore the correspondence between Red-Black trees and 2-3-4 trees
Focus on how the median promotes upward during splits

items.q: B-Tree vs B+ Tree?
items.a: B+ Tree stores data only in leaves and links them, making range queries faster.

items.q: How is order (t) chosen?
items.a: Based on disk block size. Typically hundreds to thousands, so one I/O reads one node.

segmentTreeVisualizer.title: Segment Tree Visualizer
segmentTreeVisualizer.description: Learn O(log n) range queries for sum, min, and max using a segment tree step by step

stepsGuide.description: Observe the build, query, and update process of the segment tree step by step.
stepsGuide.hint: Select an operation and press Execute to begin.

whatIs.title: What is a Segment Tree?
whatIs.description: A tree that stores range information (sum, min, etc.) of an array, enabling both range queries and point updates in O(log n).

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Enter an array and build the segment tree
Specify a range for sum/min/max queries
Update specific indices and watch the tree update
Switch query types to experiment

howItWorks.title: How It Works
items: Leaves store original array elements
Internal nodes store aggregate of child ranges
Queries visit only relevant nodes for O(log n)
Updates propagate from leaf to root

realWorld.title: Real-World Applications
items: Competitive programming range query problems
Database OLAP range aggregation
Image processing 2D range sums
Game server real-time ranking systems

comparison.title: Similar Algorithms
items: Fenwick Tree (BIT) — simpler, more memory-efficient, but can't do range min/max
Sparse Table — O(1) query but no updates (static arrays only)
sqrt decomposition — simple but O(√n) queries

tips.title: Learning Tips
items: Start with 4-8 elements to understand the tree structure
Observe which nodes are visited during queries
Use this as a foundation for lazy propagation

items.q: Fenwick vs Segment Tree?
items.a: Segment tree is more versatile (supports min/max). Fenwick is more compact for sum queries.

items.q: Memory usage?
items.a: About 4n space for an array of size n.

fenwickTreeVisualizer.title: Fenwick Tree (BIT) Visualizer
fenwickTreeVisualizer.description: Learn O(log n) prefix sum updates and range queries using a Binary Indexed Tree

stepsGuide.description: Observe the update and query process with lowbit operations.
stepsGuide.hint: Select an operation and press Execute to begin.

whatIs.title: What is a Fenwick Tree?
whatIs.description: A compact data structure using bit operations for O(log n) prefix sum updates and queries. Also known as Binary Indexed Tree (BIT).

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Generate an array and the BIT is built automatically
Update a value and watch the BIT update process
Query prefix sums to see the accumulation process
Observe binary representations and lowbit patterns

howItWorks.title: How It Works
items: Each index i is responsible for a range of size lowbit(i) = i & (-i)
Update: add lowbit to index to update parent nodes
Query: subtract lowbit from index to accumulate prefix sums
Range sum [l, r] = prefixSum(r) - prefixSum(l-1)

realWorld.title: Real-World Applications
items: Competitive programming sum/inversion counting
Real-time ranking calculation
2D BIT for rectangular area sum queries
Online judge scoring statistics

comparison.title: Similar Algorithms
items: Segment Tree — more versatile but 2x memory and complex
Prefix Sum Array — O(1) query but O(n) update
sqrt decomposition — simple but O(√n) performance

tips.title: Learning Tips
items: lowbit(i) = i & (-i) is the key — returns the lowest set bit
Convert indices to binary to understand range responsibilities
Compare with Segment Tree to understand trade-offs

items.q: What is lowbit?
items.a: i & (-i) extracts the lowest set bit. This determines the range each index is responsible for.

items.q: Works with 0-indexed arrays?
items.a: BIT is naturally 1-indexed. For 0-indexed, add 1 to all indices.

bloomFilterVisualizer.title: Bloom Filter Visualizer
bloomFilterVisualizer.description: Understand how bloom filters work — fast membership testing with possible false positives
bloomFilterVisualizer.probablyIn: Possibly in set (may be false positive)

stepsGuide.description: Observe how elements are inserted and checked in the bloom filter.
stepsGuide.checkFalsePositive: "{val}" — false positive! (not inserted but all bits are 1)

whatIs.title: What is a Bloom Filter?
whatIs.description: A probabilistic data structure using k hash functions and an m-bit array for fast membership testing. False positives are possible, but false negatives never occur.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Set bit array size and number of hash functions
Insert values — k bit positions are set to 1
Check values — all k positions must be 1
Watch false positive rate increase with fill rate

howItWorks.title: How It Works
items: Insert: pass element through k hash functions, set k bit positions to 1
Check: if all k positions are 1 → 'possibly in set'; any 0 → 'definitely not'
False positive: bits set by other elements coincidentally match the pattern
Optimal k = (m/n) × ln(2), where m=bits, n=elements

realWorld.title: Real-World Applications
items: Chrome Safe Browsing malicious URL pre-filtering
Cassandra/HBase SSTable existence checks to avoid unnecessary disk I/O
Medium's recommendation system to filter already-read articles
Bitcoin SPV node transaction filtering

comparison.title: Similar Algorithms
items: Hash Table — exact but uses 10-50x more memory
Counting Bloom Filter — supports deletion but 3-4x memory
Cuckoo Filter — supports deletion + better space efficiency, modern alternative

tips.title: Learning Tips
items: Insert few elements and verify no false positives
Add many elements to increase fill rate and experience false positives
Experiment with different hash function counts to find the optimum

items.q: Can elements be deleted?
items.a: Not in basic Bloom filters. Use Counting Bloom Filters for deletion support.

items.q: False negatives?
items.a: Never occur. Inserted elements always test positive.

primVisualizer.title: Prim's MST Visualizer
primVisualizer.description: Learn Prim's algorithm building minimum spanning trees by expanding from vertices step by step

stepsGuide.description: Watch Prim's algorithm expand from a start vertex to build the MST.
stepsGuide.addEdges: Add edges from {node} to priority queue

whatIs.title: What is Prim's Algorithm?
whatIs.description: A greedy algorithm that builds a minimum spanning tree by starting from any vertex and repeatedly selecting the minimum weight edge connecting to an unvisited vertex.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Generate a graph and select a start vertex
Run to watch the MST construction step by step
Distinguish candidate edges (yellow) from selected edges (green)
Compare results with Kruskal's algorithm

howItWorks.title: How It Works
items: Add start vertex to MST and insert adjacent edges into priority queue
Extract minimum weight edge; if opposite vertex is unvisited, add to MST
Insert new vertex's adjacent edges into the queue
Repeat until all vertices are in MST — O(E log V)

realWorld.title: Real-World Applications
items: Network design — minimum cost cabling to connect all nodes
Road/pipeline design for minimum construction cost
Clustering algorithms (Single-linkage) foundation
VLSI circuit routing optimization

comparison.title: Similar Algorithms
items: Kruskal — edge-based MST, better for sparse graphs. Prim is better for dense graphs
Boruvka — parallel MST construction, suited for distributed environments
Dijkstra — similar structure but for shortest paths, not MST

tips.title: Learning Tips
items: Run Kruskal on the same graph to verify identical total weight
Observe priority queue behavior to understand greedy selection
Change start vertex to confirm MST weight remains the same

items.q: Prim vs Kruskal?
items.a: Prim is vertex-based (better for dense graphs), Kruskal is edge-based (better for sparse graphs).

items.q: Does start vertex matter?
items.a: Edge selection may differ but total weight is always the same.

floydWarshallVisualizer.title: Floyd-Warshall Visualizer
floydWarshallVisualizer.description: Learn all-pairs shortest paths using dynamic programming with an interactive distance matrix

whatIs.title: What is Floyd-Warshall?
whatIs.description: A DP algorithm computing shortest paths between all pairs of vertices in O(V³). It iteratively adds intermediate vertices k and updates the distance matrix.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Generate a graph and click Run
Watch the distance matrix update as intermediate vertex k increases
Updated cells are highlighted
Select vertex pairs to see shortest paths on the graph

howItWorks.title: How It Works
items: Initial matrix: direct edge weights, ∞ for non-connected pairs
For k = 0..V-1: dist[i][j] = min(dist[i][j], dist[i][k] + dist[k][j])
After iteration k, shortest paths using vertices 0..k as intermediates are found
Negative diagonal means negative cycle exists

realWorld.title: Real-World Applications
items: Network routing table computation
Social network degrees of separation
Transportation all-pairs shortest time calculation
Transitive closure computation

comparison.title: Similar Algorithms
items: Dijkstra V times — O(V·E log V), no negative weights but faster for sparse graphs
Bellman-Ford V times — O(V²·E), handles negative weights but slower
Johnson's — O(V·E log V) for sparse all-pairs, faster than Floyd for sparse graphs

tips.title: Learning Tips
items: Start with 4-5 vertices to trace matrix changes
Observe which paths improve as k increases
Add negative weights to test negative cycle detection

items.q: Isn't O(V³) slow?
items.a: For dense graphs with all-pairs shortest paths, it's the simplest and most efficient. Practical for V ≤ 500.

items.q: Path reconstruction?
items.a: Maintain a next[i][j] matrix to track intermediate vertices for path recovery.

stepsGuide.description: Watch the distance matrix update as intermediate vertex k increases.

tarjanSccVisualizer.title: Tarjan's SCC Visualizer
tarjanSccVisualizer.description: Learn how to find Strongly Connected Components in directed graphs using DFS-based Tarjan's algorithm

whatIs.title: What is Tarjan's SCC?
whatIs.description: An algorithm that finds all Strongly Connected Components (SCCs) in a directed graph using a single DFS pass. An SCC is a maximal subgraph where every vertex pair is mutually reachable.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Generate a directed graph and run the algorithm
Watch DFS traversal order and discovery/low-link value changes
Observe when SCCs are extracted from the stack
Nodes of the same color belong to one SCC

howItWorks.title: How It Works
items: DFS visits vertices, assigning discovery time and low-link values
Visited vertices are pushed onto a stack; low-link is updated from descendants
When low-link == discovery, vertex is SCC root → pop SCC members from stack
Runs in O(V + E) with a single DFS pass

realWorld.title: Real-World Applications
items: Compiler dependency analysis for circular dependency detection
Social network community/group detection
Web crawler link structure analysis
Core subroutine for solving 2-SAT problems

comparison.title: Similar Algorithms
items: Kosaraju — uses 2 DFS passes, more intuitive but needs graph transpose
Gabow — uses 2 stacks, same complexity as Tarjan
Topological Sort — DAG only, applicable after SCC condensation

tips.title: Learning Tips
items: Understand the meaning of discovery and low-link values first
Manually trace values on small graphs before using the visualizer
Connect with SCC condensation graph concept

items.q: Why are SCCs important?
items.a: They're fundamental for circular dependency analysis, 2-SAT, and graph condensation.

items.q: Works for undirected graphs?
items.a: Undirected graphs use simpler Connected Components (DFS/BFS suffices).

stepsGuide.description: Watch DFS traverse vertices, tracking discovery/low-link values and extracting SCCs.

eulerPathVisualizer.title: Euler Path Visualizer
eulerPathVisualizer.description: Learn how to find paths and circuits that visit every edge exactly once in a graph
eulerPathVisualizer.stepsDescription: Watch Hierholzer's algorithm traverse edges and build the Euler path/circuit.
eulerPathVisualizer.stepCheckDegrees: Check degrees — determine Euler path/circuit existence
eulerPathVisualizer.stepNoEuler: No Euler path — conditions not met
eulerPathVisualizer.stepStuck: Stuck at vertex {node} — no unused edges

whatIs.title: What is an Euler Path?
whatIs.description: A path visiting every edge exactly once. If it returns to the start, it's an Euler Circuit. Famous from the Königsberg Bridge Problem.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Generate a graph — Euler path/circuit existence is auto-detected
Run to see Hierholzer's algorithm find the path
Odd-degree vertices are highlighted for intuitive condition understanding
Toggle directed/undirected modes

howItWorks.title: How It Works
items: Existence check: undirected — 0 (circuit) or 2 (path) odd-degree vertices
Directed: all in-degree == out-degree (circuit), or exactly one ±1 difference (path)
Hierholzer: start from any vertex, traverse edges until stuck, add to circuit
Return to vertex with unused edges and extend

realWorld.title: Real-World Applications
items: Garbage collection/mail delivery route optimization (Chinese Postman Problem)
DNA sequencing using De Bruijn graphs
PCB circuit board test routing
Network equipment testing — check every link once

comparison.title: Similar Algorithms
items: Hamiltonian Path — visits every 'vertex' once (NP-complete vs Euler which is P)
Chinese Postman — minimizes edge duplication when Euler path doesn't exist
DFS — foundation for Euler path algorithms

tips.title: Learning Tips
items: Practice counting degrees to determine Euler path/circuit existence
Focus on Hierholzer's circuit merging process
Model the Königsberg Bridge Problem as a graph

items.q: Euler vs Hamiltonian path?
items.a: Euler visits every edge once, Hamiltonian visits every vertex once. Euler is polynomial, Hamiltonian is NP-complete.

items.q: Disconnected graph?
items.a: The subgraph with edges must be connected. Isolated vertices are ignored.

editDistanceVisualizer.title: Edit Distance Visualizer
editDistanceVisualizer.description: Learn minimum edit operations (insert, delete, replace) between two strings using a DP table
editDistanceVisualizer.stepsDescription: Watch the DP table fill and backtrack to determine edit operations.
editDistanceVisualizer.stepInit: Initialize DP table — set base cases

whatIs.title: What is Edit Distance?
whatIs.description: The minimum number of insert/delete/replace operations to transform one string into another. Also known as Levenshtein Distance, widely used for spell checking and similarity measurement.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Enter two strings and click Calculate
Watch the DP table fill step by step
Backtrack path shows actual edit operations
Try various string pairs

howItWorks.title: How It Works
items: dp[i][j] = min cost to convert first i chars of A to first j chars of B
If A[i]==B[j]: dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1] (free)
Else: dp[i][j] = 1 + min(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1], dp[i-1][j-1]) — delete, insert, replace
Time and space O(m×n)

realWorld.title: Real-World Applications
items: Search engine 'Did you mean?' typo correction
Git diff text comparison algorithms
Bioinformatics — DNA/protein sequence alignment (Needleman-Wunsch)
NLP string similarity measurement

comparison.title: Similar Algorithms
items: LCS — finds common subsequence; ED = m + n - 2×LCS
Damerau-Levenshtein — also allows transposition of adjacent characters
Hamming Distance — counts different positions in equal-length strings only

tips.title: Learning Tips
items: Start with 3-4 character strings and fill the table by hand
Trace the backtrack path to understand each cell's choice
Verify the ED-LCS relationship directly

items.q: Space optimization possible?
items.a: Yes, keeping only the previous row gives O(min(m,n)) space, but backtracking is lost.

items.q: Different operation weights?
items.a: Yes, assigning different costs for insert/delete/replace gives generalized edit distance.

coinChangeVisualizer.title: Coin Change Visualizer
coinChangeVisualizer.description: Learn how to find minimum coins for a target amount using dynamic programming

stepsGuide.description: Click on each step to jump to that point.
stepsGuide.hint: Press the run button to start.

whatIs.title: What is Coin Change?
whatIs.description: A classic DP problem: find the minimum number of coins to make a target amount. Greedy doesn't guarantee optimal solutions, so DP is needed.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Set available coin types and target amount
Run to watch the DP array fill
Backtrack to see which coins were selected
Change coin types for different scenarios

howItWorks.title: How It Works
items: dp[i] = minimum coins to make amount i, dp[0] = 0
For each amount i: dp[i] = min(dp[i - coin] + 1) for each coin ≤ i
dp[amount] is the answer; ∞ means impossible
Time O(amount × coins), Space O(amount)

realWorld.title: Real-World Applications
items: Vending machine/ATM change optimization
Payment system minimum bill/coin combination
Resource allocation problem modeling
Coding interview essential — top-down/bottom-up DP practice

comparison.title: Similar Algorithms
items: Knapsack — weight limit + value maximization; coin change is unbounded special case
Greedy change — optimal only for specific coin systems (1, 5, 10, 50...)
Coin combination count — counting total ways instead of minimum count

tips.title: Learning Tips
items: Try coins [1,3,4] for amount 6 — greedy gives 3 (4+1+1), DP gives 2 (3+3)
Fill the dp array by hand and compare with visualization
Implement both top-down (memoization) and bottom-up approaches

items.q: Can't greedy work?
items.a: Only for specific coin systems (like Korean won). Generally DP is required.

items.q: Limited coin supply?
items.a: Extends to Bounded Knapsack problem.

lisVisualizer.title: LIS (Longest Increasing Subsequence) Visualizer
lisVisualizer.description: Learn how to find the longest increasing subsequence using DP and binary search

stepsGuide.description: Click on each step to jump to that point.
stepsGuide.hint: Press the run button to start.

whatIs.title: What is LIS?
whatIs.description: The longest subsequence maintaining original order with increasing values. Two approaches: O(n²) DP and O(n log n) binary search (patience sorting).

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Enter a sequence or generate randomly
Switch between DP and binary search methods
Watch DP array or Tails array updates
LIS elements are highlighted

howItWorks.title: How It Works
items: DP: dp[i] = LIS length ending at arr[i], dp[i] = max(dp[j]+1) for j < i where arr[j] < arr[i]
Binary Search: maintain tails array; if new element > last tail, append; else replace at lower_bound
Binary search achieves O(n log n) for large inputs
Backtrack to reconstruct the actual LIS

realWorld.title: Real-World Applications
items: Git patience diff algorithm uses LIS-based matching
Network packet reordering
Genomics — gene sequence similarity analysis
Stock price analysis — longest rising period

comparison.title: Similar Algorithms
items: LCS — common subsequence of two sequences; LIS is within one sequence
Edit Distance — related string DP problem to LCS/LIS
Patience Sorting — same idea as the binary search LIS solution

tips.title: Learning Tips
items: Master the O(n²) DP first before moving to binary search
Think about why the tails array always stays sorted
Implement backtracking yourself

items.q: Is LIS unique?
items.a: Length is unique, but multiple subsequences of that length may exist.

items.q: Non-decreasing instead of strictly increasing?
items.a: Use upper_bound instead of lower_bound for non-decreasing (≤) LIS.

rabinKarpVisualizer.title: Rabin-Karp Visualizer
rabinKarpVisualizer.description: Learn string pattern matching using rolling hash step by step

stepsGuide.description: Click a step to jump to that point.
stepsGuide.hint: Press Search to start.

whatIs.title: What is Rabin-Karp?
whatIs.description: Uses rolling hash to compare substring hashes with the pattern hash in O(1), enabling efficient pattern matching. Especially powerful for multi-pattern search.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Enter text and pattern, then search
Watch hash computation at each position
Hash collisions (false positives) trigger actual character comparison
Change base and modular to see collision frequency changes

howItWorks.title: How It Works
items: Compute pattern hash
Slide window one position at a time, updating hash in O(1) using rolling hash
If hashes match, verify with actual character comparison (spurious hit prevention)
Average O(n+m), worst O(nm) but nearly linear with good hash function

realWorld.title: Real-World Applications
items: Plagiarism detection — searching multiple documents simultaneously
Virus scanner signature multi-pattern matching
Text editor find/replace functionality
Network IDS packet pattern matching

comparison.title: Similar Algorithms
items: KMP — worst-case O(n+m) guaranteed for single pattern; Rabin-Karp excels at multi-pattern
Aho-Corasick — standard for simultaneous multi-pattern search, trie-based
Boyer-Moore — fastest single-pattern matching in practice, compares from right

tips.title: Learning Tips
items: Understand rolling hash math (polynomial hash) first
Create examples that intentionally cause collisions
Compare comparison counts with KMP on the same input

items.q: Better than KMP?
items.a: For multi-pattern search, yes. For single patterns, KMP has better worst-case guarantees.

items.q: Too many hash collisions?
items.a: Use larger modular or double hashing to reduce collisions.

suffixArrayVisualizer.title: Suffix Array Visualizer
suffixArrayVisualizer.description: Learn how to sort all suffixes and analyze LCP (Longest Common Prefix) step by step

stepsGuide.description: Click a step to jump to that point.
stepsGuide.hint: Press Build to start.

whatIs.title: What is a Suffix Array?
whatIs.description: A sorted array of all suffix starting indices. More memory-efficient than suffix trees while solving equivalent problems.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Enter a string and build to create suffix array and LCP array
Watch suffixes being sorted
Search patterns using binary search
Analyze LCP array patterns

howItWorks.title: How It Works
items: Sort all suffix starting indices lexicographically
O(n log²n) or SA-IS O(n) algorithms for efficient construction
LCP array: common prefix length between adjacent suffixes, O(n) via Kasai's algorithm
Pattern search: binary search in O(m log n)

realWorld.title: Real-World Applications
items: Bioinformatics — genome repeat pattern search
Data compression (BWT/bzip2) core preprocessing
Full-text search index construction
String similarity/repeat analysis

comparison.title: Similar Algorithms
items: Suffix Tree — O(n) construction, more powerful but 20x+ memory
Trie — good for prefix search of multiple strings; suffix array better for single string
FM-index — suffix array + BWT based, compressed index for memory savings

tips.title: Learning Tips
items: Start with short strings (5-8 chars) and manually list/sort suffixes
Practice finding repeated substrings using the LCP array
Trace the binary search pattern matching process by hand

items.q: Better than suffix tree?
items.a: Much better memory efficiency and practical. Functionally equivalent when combined with LCP array.

items.q: Construction time?
items.a: SA-IS achieves O(n), but O(n log²n) approach is more intuitive.

huffmanCodingVisualizer.title: Huffman Coding Visualizer
huffmanCodingVisualizer.description: Learn the greedy algorithm for optimal prefix codes — the basis of data compression

stepsGuide.description: Click on any step to jump to that point.
stepsGuide.hint: Press Encode to start.

whatIs.title: What is Huffman Coding?
whatIs.description: A greedy algorithm generating optimal prefix codes based on character frequencies. Frequent characters get short codes, rare ones get long codes, minimizing total bits.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Enter text and character frequencies are auto-analyzed
Encode to watch Huffman tree construction step by step
Check each character's bit code in the code table
Compare compression ratios with different texts

howItWorks.title: How It Works
items: Count character frequencies and insert into priority queue (min-heap)
Extract two lowest-frequency nodes, merge into new parent
Repeat until one tree remains
Left=0, Right=1 determines each character's code

realWorld.title: Real-World Applications
items: ZIP, GZIP compression core algorithm
JPEG, PNG image compression entropy coding stage
MP3/AAC audio compression
HTTP/2 header compression (HPACK) uses Huffman tables

comparison.title: Similar Algorithms
items: Arithmetic Coding — better compression than Huffman but more complex
LZW — dictionary-based compression, used in GIF format
Deflate — LZ77 + Huffman combination, core of ZIP/GZIP

tips.title: Learning Tips
items: Start with skewed frequency text (e.g., 'aaaaabbc') for clear tree structure
Understand prefix codes — no code is a prefix of another
Compare compression ratio with fixed-length coding (ASCII)

items.q: Always optimal compression?
items.a: Optimal among prefix codes, but arithmetic coding achieves closer to theoretical limit.

items.q: How is decoding done?
items.a: Read bits and traverse the Huffman tree. When a leaf is reached, output that character.

slidingWindowVisualizer.title: Sliding Window Visualizer
slidingWindowVisualizer.description: Learn to efficiently solve subarray/substring problems by moving a fixed or variable-size window

stepsGuide.description: Click on any step to jump to that point.
stepsGuide.hint: Press Run to start.

whatIs.title: What is Sliding Window?
whatIs.description: A technique solving contiguous subarray/substring problems in O(n) by sliding a window across data. Two types: fixed-size and variable-size.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Enter array and set window size or target value
Fixed mode: find max sum window of size k
Variable mode: find minimum length window with sum ≥ target
Watch left/right pointer movements

howItWorks.title: How It Works
items: Fixed: slide window one position, subtract front element, add back element — O(n)
Variable: expand right to satisfy condition, shrink left to optimize
Key insight: reuse previous computation instead of recalculating from scratch
Closely related to two-pointer technique

realWorld.title: Real-World Applications
items: Network monitoring — average packet throughput over last N seconds
Stock analysis — moving average calculation
TCP flow control sliding window protocol
String processing — longest substring without repeats

comparison.title: Similar Algorithms
items: Two Pointers — generalization of sliding window, window may not be contiguous
Prefix Sum — O(1) range sum but not suitable for dynamic windows
Segment Tree — versatile range queries but sliding window is simpler and faster

tips.title: Learning Tips
items: Start with fixed-size max sum — most intuitive
For variable-size, clearly understand left/right pointer movement conditions
Practice with 'longest substring without repeats' for real-world application

items.q: vs Two Pointers?
items.a: Sliding window is a special case of two pointers, always maintaining a contiguous range.

items.q: When to use?
items.a: When finding max/min/specific condition over contiguous subarrays or substrings.

whatIs.title: What is the Government Subsidy Calculator?
whatIs.description: A tool that checks your eligibility for 12+ Korean government subsidy programs at once by entering household income, assets, and member information. Covers Basic Living Security, EITC, Child Tax Credit, Basic Pension, Youth Rent Subsidy, and more.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Enter household size, monthly income, and total assets
Select applicant age and housing type (jeonse/rent/owned)
Check applicable options: children, single parent, disability
Click 'Check Eligibility' to see results for 12+ programs with estimated amounts
Review application methods and official website links for each program

tips.title: Useful Tips
items: Income should be pre-tax (earned + business + property income)
Assets = real estate market value + financial assets + vehicle value
You can receive multiple subsidies simultaneously if eligible
For borderline results, visit your local community center for accurate assessment
Online applications available at bokjiro.go.kr

items.q: What is median income?
items.a: The income level at the exact middle when all households are ranked by income. The 2026 median income for a 4-person household is approximately ₩6.09M.

items.q: Can I receive multiple subsidies?
items.a: Yes, since each program has different criteria, you can qualify for multiple programs. However, some programs restrict overlapping benefits.

items.q: How are assets calculated?
items.a: Real estate (market value) + financial assets (savings, stocks) + vehicle value + other assets. Some debts may be deducted.

whatIs.title: What is the Youth Rent Subsidy?
whatIs.description: A Korean government program supporting ages 19-34 who live independently without home ownership, providing up to ₩200K/month for up to 12 months (total ₩2.4M). Both parent household income and personal income/assets are verified.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Enter your age and independent living status
Enter personal income/assets and parent household income
Enter current rent and deposit amounts
Click 'Check Eligibility' to see pass/fail for each of 7 conditions
Review any failed conditions to see if they can be resolved

tips.title: Useful Tips
items: If rent is below ₩200K, only the actual rent amount is supported
Deposit must be ₩50M or less and rent ₩700K or less
Living at the same address as parents does not count as independent
Income is calculated based on health insurance premiums
Results are typically notified within 1-2 months after application

items.q: Can I reapply if I received it before?
items.a: You can apply for the remaining period only. Total support cannot exceed 12 months.

items.q: Are gosiwon/dormitories eligible?
items.a: Gosiwon with lease agreements are eligible, but school dormitories are generally excluded.

items.q: Why is parent income checked?
items.a: To assess the youth's actual economic situation, parent household income is also verified. Parent income must be below 100% of median income.

evSubsidy.title: EV Subsidy Calculator
evSubsidy.description: Calculate national and local government subsidies for electric vehicle purchases by model and region.
evSubsidy.resultPlaceholder: Enter vehicle info and click Calculate

whatIs.title: What are EV Subsidies?
whatIs.description: Korean national (government) and local subsidies cover part of an EV's price. In 2026 the national subsidy for passenger EVs is up to ₩5.8M (mid/large) or ₩5.3M (small), plus a conversion bonus of up to ₩1M when you sell or scrap a combustion car (max ₩6.8M). Local subsidies range from about 30% of the national amount (Seoul etc.) to over 150% in some rural counties.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Pick a model to load the national and local amounts published on ev.or.kr (or enter/estimate them for unlisted cars)
Enter your quoted price and manufacturer discount to get the net price
Choose your province and district to apply that area's local subsidy
Tick conversion, young first-time buyer, low-income or multi-child if they apply
Share the result by link or image, and check the area/model comparisons and 5-year energy cost

tips.title: Useful Tips
items: National = [(performance + battery safety) × battery coefficients + supply target + charging infra + innovation] × price factor. Performance depends on efficiency and range (25% cold weather)
Base price under ₩53M gets 100%, ₩53M–85M gets 50%, ₩85M or more gets nothing
Young first-time and low-income buyers each get +20% of the national amount; multi-child households get ₩1M/2M/3M for 2/3/4+ kids (stackable)
The conversion bonus is ₩1M when the national subsidy is ₩5M or more, prorated below that (e.g. ₩3M → ₩0.6M)
Local budgets run out, so check remaining slots on ev.or.kr first

items.q: Can I sell the car right after receiving the subsidy?
items.a: Passenger EVs must be kept for 2 years. Selling or exporting earlier requires repaying part of the subsidy depending on how long you kept it.

items.q: Can I combine the young first-time buyer and low-income add-ons?
items.a: Yes. Percentage add-ons (20% of national each) are added first, then fixed amounts such as the multi-child bonus.

items.q: Why do local subsidies differ so much?
items.a: The guideline requires local governments to add at least 30% of the national amount; anything above depends on their budget. Seoul and Busan pay about 30%, while many counties in Chungbuk, Chungnam, Jeonbuk and Gyeongbuk match or exceed the national amount.

items.q: What changes in 2027?
items.a: Price thresholds are expected to drop to ₩50M (100%) and ₩80M (50%), and a bill to cut the EV acquisition tax relief cap from ₩1.4M to ₩0.7M is in pre-announcement.

whatIs.title: What are Parent Pay & Child Allowance?
whatIs.description: Cash benefits provided by the Korean government to families raising children. Includes Parent Pay (₩1M/month for age 0, ₩500K/month for age 1), Child Allowance (₩100K/month for ages 0-8), and Childcare Allowance (for home care). A ₩2M First Meeting Voucher is also available at birth.

howToUse.title: How to Use

tips.title: Useful Tips
items: Parent Pay and Childcare Allowance cannot be received together (difference only)
Child Allowance is universal — all families qualify regardless of income
Use the 'Happy Birth One-Stop Service' at birth registration for convenient batch application
Daycare attendees get fee support instead of childcare allowance
First Meeting Voucher must be used within 1 year of birth

items.q: Can fathers receive parent pay?
items.a: Yes, parent pay is based on the caregiver, so fathers who are the primary caregiver can receive it.

items.q: Do dual-income families qualify?
items.a: Yes, parent pay is available to all families with children aged 0-1 regardless of income.

items.q: How long does child allowance last?
items.a: Until the month before the child turns 8 (96 months), paid monthly.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Enter property address and jeonse deposit amount

Mark each item as checked, unchecked, or not applicable

Save or share results for professional consultation

tips.title: Useful Tips
items: Deposit insurance (HUG) eligibility is the most important safety measure
Jeonse-to-sale ratio over 80% indicates high underwater risk
Register residence and get confirmation date on move-in day for opposing power

items.q: Is deposit insurance mandatory?
items.a: Not legally required, but strongly recommended. If the landlord fails to return the deposit, the insurer pays instead. Choose from HUG, SGI, or HF.

items.q: What is underwater jeonse?
items.a: When the jeonse deposit approaches or exceeds the property's sale value. If the property goes to auction, you risk not recovering your deposit.

items.q: What's the difference between residence registration and confirmation date?
items.a: Residence registration reports your address to the government. Confirmation date is an official date stamp on your lease. Both must be done on move-in day to secure opposing power and priority repayment rights.

items.q: Should juniors prepare for system design?

items.q: How to allocate time in a 45-min interview?

items.q: What order should I study?
items.a: Easy (Two Pointers, HashMap, Tree Traversal) → Medium (BFS/DFS, Binary Search, Sliding Window) → Hard (DP, Topological Sort).

From this year the computer sign pen is provided on site (bringing your own is also allowed), and recording answers for self-scoring is permitted.

dayBefore.title: The day before
items: On the preliminary gathering day (the day before the exam in previous years), pick up your admission ticket and check the test site location, route and travel time.
Put your admission ticket and ID in your bag in advance.
Make sure your analog watch works and has no prohibited features.
Pack a lunch you usually eat and digest easily.
Go to bed at your usual time.

examDay.title: On exam day
items: Be seated by 8:10 AM. Leave early to allow for traffic.
Hand prohibited items such as phones to the proctor before Period 1 starts.
Keep the order of your Period 4 electives.
Lunch is 12:10–13:00. Even if a subject went badly, focus on the next period.

tips.title: Making the most of the time left
items: Use the practice run button to take mock exams on the real timetable.
The exam starts at 8:40 AM, so start shifting your wake-up time now.
The checklist is saved in this browser, so reopen it the night before.
After the exam, copy your answers into the answer sheet and check estimated grades with the grade calculator.

items.q: When is the 2027 CSAT?
items.a: Thursday, November 19, 2026. Scores are released on Friday, December 11, 2026. You must be seated by 8:10 AM.

items.q: Can I bring my own computer sign pen?
items.a: From the 2027 CSAT the pen is provided at the test site, but you may also use your own. Mechanical pencils and correction tape are provided too.

items.q: What if I brought my phone?
items.a: Hand it to the proctor before Period 1 starts. Merely having a prohibited item such as a phone or smartwatch during the exam counts as cheating.

items.q: I lost my admission ticket.
items.a: Bring one photo and your ID to the test site's management office to have it reissued (based on previous years' guidelines).

items.q: How do I self-score?
items.a: During the exam, record your answers the way KICE instructs (e.g. the back of the admission ticket), then copy them into this page's answer sheet afterwards. Once the answer key is out, check estimated grades in the CSAT grade calculator.

guide.title: IOU essentials
guide.intro: A Korean IOU (차용증) has no fixed format. It is valid if it clearly states who lent how much to whom, until when and on what terms, and the debtor signs or seals it. Keep it together with records of the money actually transferred.

sections.title: Validity
items: A printed document is valid once signed or sealed.
Include both parties, the amount (in words and figures), loan date, due date and interest.
Make two copies, sign both and keep one each.
If anything is corrected, both parties should seal next to the correction.

sections.title: Stronger evidence
items: Transfer money by bank rather than cash to leave a record.
The debtor should use a registered seal and attach a seal certificate.
Pay interest and installments to the account on the agreed dates.
Write the full resident registration number by hand after printing.

sections.title: When to notarize
items: For large or long-term loans, make a notarial deed for a loan for consumption.
With a consent-to-execution clause, you can enforce without a lawsuit.
A simple notarial certification proves the signing only and is not enforceable.
Notary fees depend on the amount; ask the notary office.

sections.title: Interest and tax
items: The maximum rate between individuals is 20% a year; the excess is void.
Interest received is subject to 27.5% withholding.
For family loans, gift tax applies if the gap against 4.6% is 10 million KRW or more a year.
Interest-free, that threshold is a principal of about 217.39 million KRW.

sections.title: If you aren't repaid
items: Personal loan claims expire 10 years after the due date (Civil Act Art. 162).
Send a certified letter demanding repayment first.
Small claims (up to 30 million KRW) or a payment order are fast and cheap.
If assets may disappear, consider a provisional attachment first.

sections.title: Joint guarantors
items: A joint guarantor can be claimed against directly, without the debtor first.
A guarantee must be in writing signed by the guarantor (Civil Act Art. 428-2).
Guarantors should also use a registered seal and certificate.

items.q: Is a printed IOU valid?
items.a: Yes. An IOU has no required format, so a printed one is valid when it lists the parties, amount, loan date, due date and interest and the debtor signs or seals it. Bank transfer records strengthen it.

items.q: What is the maximum interest rate between individuals?
items.a: 20% a year under the Interest Limitation Act (contracts from July 7, 2021). The excess is void and must be applied to principal or returned. The same cap applies to late damages.

items.q: Does an IOU avoid gift tax on family loans?
items.a: Only with records of actually paying the agreed interest and principal. For interest-free or low-rate loans, gift tax applies when the gap against the deemed rate of 4.6% is 10 million KRW or more a year — about 217.39 million KRW of principal when interest-free.

items.q: Is interest income taxed?
items.a: Yes. Interest between individuals is non-business lending income, subject to 27.5% withholding (25% income tax + 2.5% local tax), withheld by the payer and filed by the 10th of the following month.

items.q: Do I need to notarize it?
items.a: Not required, but a notarial deed with a consent-to-execution clause lets you enforce without a lawsuit. Recommended for large or long-term loans.

items.q: How long can I claim repayment?
items.a: 10 years from the due date for personal loans (Civil Act Art. 162); 5 years for commercial claims. Interrupt the period with a payment order, lawsuit or attachment.

guide.title: How to Write a Resignation Letter
guide.intro: A resignation letter expresses your intent to end the employment contract. There is no mandatory form; name, department, desired last day, reason, date and signature are enough. Getting the dates and reason right matters more than the format.

sections.title: Procedure & timing
items: Usually tell your direct manager in person first, then submit the letter.
Check the notice rule in your work rules or contract. 30 days is common practice.
If accepted, you leave on the agreed date; if not, under Civil Act Art. 660 it takes effect one month after notice (end of the next month for monthly pay).
Keep a copy or photo, and keep sent records if submitted by email or messenger.
Make sure your last day does not overlap with your new job's start date (social insurance).

sections.title: Handover
items: Document your tasks, status and deadlines of ongoing work, and key contacts.
Transfer accounts, passwords and shared-drive access per company process; back up personal files beforehand.
Get a checklist signed for returning laptop, access card, corporate card, etc.
Agree in advance whether you will use remaining leave during handover.

sections.title: Leaving checklist
items: Severance and remaining wages: within 14 days of leaving (Labor Standards Act Art. 36, Retirement Benefit Act Art. 9). Severance goes to an IRP account.
Social insurance: the company reports loss of coverage as of the day after your last day. Check regional health insurance or voluntary continued coverage.
Year-end tax settlement: done mid-year on leaving; claim missed deductions in the May income tax filing.
Get a certificate of employment, withholding receipt and retirement income withholding receipt.
If eligible for unemployment benefits, check the separation reason and apply on Work24 within 12 months after leaving.

sections.title: Writing the reason
items: For voluntary resignation, a short 'personal reasons' is enough.
If the company's circumstances apply (recommended resignation, contract end, unpaid wages, harassment), state them factually so unemployment benefits are not affected.
Do not sign if the company asks you to rewrite it as 'personal reasons' when that is untrue.
Leave out emotional wording or criticism of the company; it may surface in reference checks.

items.q: What if the company refuses to accept my resignation?
items.a: For an open-ended contract, under Civil Act Art. 660 resignation takes effect one month after notice even without acceptance. If pay is set by period (e.g., monthly), it takes effect after the next pay period following the notice (usually the end of next month). Keep working until then to be safe.

items.q: Is a resignation sent by email or messenger valid?
items.a: Yes. Resignation is a declaration of intent with no required form. You must be able to prove it reached the company and when, so keep sent records and ideally attach a signed PDF letter.

items.q: Must I use the company's own form?
items.a: No form is required by law, so any form has the same effect. Using the company form is fine, but if asked to write something untrue (e.g., 'personal reasons' for a recommended resignation), write the actual reason; it affects unemployment benefits.

items.q: Can I withdraw my resignation?
items.a: In principle yes, before the company accepts it. Once accepted, or if withdrawal would cause unforeseen harm to the company, the company's consent is needed.

items.q: When do I receive severance pay?
items.a: With 1+ year of continuous service (15+ hours/week), within 14 days of leaving. The date can be extended by agreement, and severance is in principle transferred to an IRP account.

sources.label: Civil Act Art. 660 (termination notice of employment without fixed term) — Korea Law Information Center
Labor Standards Act Art. 36 (settlement of money and valuables)
Employee Retirement Benefit Security Act Art. 9 (payment of severance)
Enforcement Rule of the Employment Insurance Act, Annex 2 (justified reasons for leaving)
Work24 — unemployment benefit application

guide.title: Power of attorney essentials
guide.intro: A power of attorney records that you are entrusting a task to someone else. What the agent does within that authority binds you as if you did it yourself (Civil Act Art. 114). So keep who, what and until when narrow and clear.

sections.title: Must-have items
items: Name, date of birth (first 6 digits of resident number), address and phone of principal and agent
Delegated matters, one by one (e.g. apply for and receive 1 resident registration copy)
Target and recipient: account, vehicle, property address, and which office
Period, date written, principal's signature or seal

sections.title: Documents by purpose
items: Community center certificates: POA + agent's ID + principal's ID (copy)
Seal certificate: official handwritten POA form + original IDs of both
Vehicle: POA (registered seal) + principal's seal certificate + agent's ID + vehicle registration etc.
Bank: check bank's own form + registered seal + seal certificate + both IDs
Real estate: POA (registered seal) + seal certificate (real estate sale use for selling) + agent's ID
Company: POA (corporate seal) + corporate seal certificate + agent's ID/employment certificate

sections.title: Registered seal vs signature
items: A general POA is valid with a signature alone. Any stamp is also fine.
Property matters (bank, real estate, vehicle) often require the registered seal plus a seal certificate.
A signature verification certificate can replace the seal; sign the POA with the same signature.
The signature verification certificate cannot be issued to an agent — the principal must visit in person.

sections.title: For the agent
items: The agent's own original ID is always required (resident card, driver's license, passport).
Only those aged 17+ can obtain a seal certificate as agent.
Offices may call the principal to confirm, so make sure they can answer.
Many offices keep the original. Print and sign one per office if needed.

sections.title: Avoid blanket authority
items: 'All rights' or 'any and all acts' with no scope can be abused to sell property or take on debt.
An agent with undefined authority may only preserve and manage property (Civil Act Art. 118), so banks and registries ask for specific delegation.
Keep the period short and take back or revoke the POA when done.
Handing over your seal and seal certificate together is like a blank check.

items.q: Does a family member need a POA to get documents for me?
items.a: It depends. Household members can get resident registration copies without one. Spouses and lineal relatives (parents, children, grandparents) can request family relation certificates without a POA, but siblings need a POA and a copy of the principal's ID. A seal certificate always requires the official POA form and the principal's original ID, even for family.

items.q: How long is a power of attorney valid?
items.a: A general POA has no statutory validity period: it lasts until the stated end date, or until the task is done or revoked. Only the seal certificate POA is fixed at 6 months from delegation (Enforcement Decree of the Certification of Seal Imprints Act Art. 13). Banks and offices usually want one written within 1–3 months.

items.q: Can I just sign without a seal?
items.a: For ordinary tasks like community center documents, the principal's handwritten signature is enough. Property matters often require the registered seal and seal certificate, but you may submit a signature verification certificate and sign the POA identically instead.

items.q: Can I use this form to have someone get my seal certificate?
items.a: No. You must use the official 'Seal Certificate Issuance POA' (Form No. 13), handwritten by the principal. It is available at community centers and on Gov24. Choose the seal certificate purpose here to see what to bring.

items.q: Is a typed and printed POA valid?
items.a: Yes. A general POA has no fixed format, so a printed one is valid. The principal should sign or stamp it by hand after printing. Only official forms that require handwriting, like the seal certificate POA, are exceptions.

insight.smallClaimsOver: Small claims covers only monetary claims up to KRW 30M. Use a regular lawsuit or payment order for this amount.
insight.wage: Wages and severance must be paid within 14 days of leaving; after that 20% annual late interest applies (Labor Standards Act Art. 37). Wage claims expire after 3 years.

guide.title: Certified letters in a nutshell
guide.intro: A certified letter (naeyong jeungmyeong) is registered mail where the post office certifies what was sent, by whom, to whom and when. It cannot force payment by itself, but it records your demand and its date as solid evidence and is the first step before legal action.

sections.title: What it does
items: The post office certifies the content and sending date (Postal Act Enforcement Rules Art. 25).
It is not enforceable by itself; ignoring it does not allow seizure.
It is strong evidence of your demand and signals that legal action may follow.
Ideal for notices that take effect on arrival, such as termination or non-renewal. Add proof of delivery to certify the arrival date.

sections.title: Interrupting the limitation period
items: Demanding performance by certified letter is a 'peremptory notice' under the Civil Act.
It only interrupts the period if you file a lawsuit, payment order, attachment or injunction within 6 months (Civil Act Art. 174).
If the period is about to end, follow up with a payment order or lawsuit within 6 months.
Typical periods: personal loans 10 years, goods/construction payments 3 years, wages and severance 3 years.

sections.title: Writing tips
items: State when, what and how much with exact dates and amounts.
State the demand and deadline clearly; 7–14 days after arrival is typical.
Avoid insults, threats or exaggeration; they can backfire legally.
Use an address where the recipient actually gets mail; returned mail is hard to prove as delivered.

sections.title: Sending and cost
items: Prepare 3 identical copies: recipient, post office and you.
Submit at a post office counter or upload the file on ePost.
2026 rates: postage KRW 500 + registered KRW 2,400 + certification KRW 1,300 (KRW 650 per extra page). About KRW 4,200 for one page.
Add proof of delivery (KRW 1,600). The post office keeps its copy for 3 years and can re-certify within that time.

sections.title: If it still is not resolved
items: Payment order: when the other party is unlikely to contest. Paper-only, stamp duty 1/10 of a lawsuit.
Small claims: monetary claims up to KRW 30M, quick hearings.
Lease registration order: when moving out without the deposit; keeps priority rights (Housing Lease Protection Act Art. 3-3).
Unpaid wages: file a labor office complaint and apply for substitute payment.

sections.title: Lease non-renewal deadlines
items: Landlord: from 6 months to 2 months before expiry (Housing Lease Protection Act Art. 6(1)).
Tenant: by 2 months before expiry.
Without notice the lease renews on the same terms; the tenant can then terminate with 3 months' notice (Art. 6-2).
If the tenant exercises the renewal right, the landlord needs a statutory reason such as moving in (Art. 6-3). Commercial leases use 6 to 1 month.

items.q: What happens if the recipient ignores it?
items.a: A certified letter is not enforceable by itself, so ignoring it has no immediate penalty. But the demand and its date remain as evidence, and the sender can proceed with a payment order, lawsuit or lease registration order. If you disagree, reply with your own certified letter.

items.q: Does it stop the limitation period?
items.a: It counts as a peremptory notice under the Civil Act, which only interrupts the period if you file a lawsuit, payment order, attachment or injunction within 6 months (Civil Act Art. 174).

items.q: Can I send it before my lease ends?
items.a: Yes. Before expiry, combine a non-renewal notice with a demand to return the deposit on the end date. A tenant's notice must arrive by 2 months before expiry; a landlord's between 6 and 2 months before (Housing Lease Protection Act Art. 6). If you must move out without the deposit, apply for a lease registration order first.

items.q: How much does it cost?
items.a: Under 2026 Korea Post rates, one A4 page costs about KRW 4,200: postage KRW 500, registered fee KRW 2,400 and certification fee KRW 1,300. Each extra page adds KRW 650, and proof of delivery adds KRW 1,600.

items.q: Can I send it online?
items.a: Yes. Upload the document on ePost and the post office prints, sends it by registered mail and keeps a copy. The final fee is shown on the submission screen. Otherwise bring 3 copies and an envelope to a post office counter.

items.q: What if the recipient does not accept it?
items.a: Keep returned mail unopened. Courts may treat an unjustified refusal as delivery. Resend to another address or also send the content by text or email; in court, the court's service procedures can be used.

items.q: Does it need to come from a lawyer?
items.a: The legal effect is the same either way. Clear facts, demands, a deadline and consequences are enough in your own name. For large or complex disputes, consult a lawyer.

guide.title: Employment contract essentials
guide.intro: Every Korean employer — including those hiring part-timers, trainees or short-term staff — must issue a written employment contract to the employee. This generator follows the Ministry of Employment and Labor's standard form and flags minimum wage, break and working-hour violations as you type.

sections.title: Required terms (LSA Art. 17)
items: Wages: components, calculation and payment method
Contractual working hours and breaks
Weekly paid holiday
Annual paid leave
Workplace, duties and contract term (fixed-term)
Wages, hours, holidays and leave must be given in writing; electronic documents are allowed.

sections.title: Penalties
items: Failure to state and issue terms in writing: fine up to 5 million KRW (LSA Art. 114)
For fixed-term/part-time workers, an administrative fine up to 5 million KRW per worker may also apply (Fixed-term Act Art. 24)
If wages or hours change, the new terms must be issued in writing again
Issue a copy even if not requested, and keep a signed receipt

sections.title: Part-time workers
items: Working days and hours per day must be stated (Fixed-term Act Art. 17)
15+ hours/week earns weekly holiday pay and annual leave; under 15 earns neither
Work beyond contractual hours needs consent, max 12 h/week, 50% premium (5+ employees)
2026 minimum wage 10,320 KRW/h; 2,156,880 KRW/month for 40 h/week (209 h)

sections.title: Workers under 18
items: Max 7 h/day and 35 h/week, +1 h/day and +5 h/week by agreement (LSA Art. 69)
Keep a family relation certificate and parental consent on file (Art. 66)
Parents cannot sign on the minor's behalf; the minor claims wages directly (Arts. 67–68)
Night (10 pm–6 am) and holiday work require consent and MOEL authorization (Art. 70)
Under 15 requires an employment permit (Art. 64)

items.q: Do part-time jobs need a written contract?
items.a: Yes. One-day jobs, trainees and all employees must receive a written contract. Not issuing wages, hours, holidays and leave in writing can lead to a fine up to 5 million KRW (LSA Art. 114), and part-time workers can also trigger an administrative fine up to 5 million KRW under the Fixed-term Act.

items.q: When must the contract be signed?
items.a: When the employment begins, before work starts, with a copy handed to the employee right away. If wages or hours change, issue the new terms in writing again.

items.q: How do I check minimum wage for monthly pay?
items.a: Divide base pay plus regular monthly allowances by monthly contractual hours plus weekly holiday hours. For 40 h/week that is 209 hours, so the 2026 monthly minimum is 10,320 × 209 = 2,156,880 KRW. This tool calculates it from the hours you enter.

items.q: Should weekly holiday pay be written in the contract?
items.a: With 15+ contractual hours a week and full attendance, a paid weekly holiday arises. For hourly pay it is often paid separately, so stating the amount prevents disputes; for monthly pay it is usually stated as included. This tool fills it in automatically.

items.q: Do workplaces with fewer than 5 employees need contracts?
items.a: Yes. The written contract duty, minimum wage, weekly holidays and breaks apply. Overtime/night/holiday premiums, annual leave and the 52-hour cap do not.

items.q: What documents are needed to hire a student under 18?
items.a: The young worker standard contract, a family relation certificate and parental consent. Hours are limited to 7 h/day and 35 h/week, and under-15s need an employment permit. Choosing 'Under 18' generates the consent form as page 2.

brokerageFee.disclaimer: For reference based on legal maximums. The actual fee depends on negotiation, local ordinances and expense claims.

amount.title: Transaction amount
items: Sales use the price; jeonse uses the deposit.
Monthly rent uses deposit + rent × 100, or deposit + rent × 70 if that is under 50M KRW (Enforcement Rule Art. 20(5)).
Exchanges use the higher-valued property; pre-sale rights use payments made plus premium.
If the same broker handles a sale and a lease between the same parties, only the sale fee applies.

pay.title: When to pay
items: Paid as agreed with the broker, or on the day the balance is paid if there is no agreement (Enforcement Decree Art. 27-2).
In practice each party pays its share on the balance payment day.
Write the fee and payment date in the contract to avoid disputes.

doc.title: Property confirmation statement
items: Brokers must explain the property and hand over a confirmation statement with the contract (Licensed Real Estate Agents Act Art. 25).
The statement lists the fee, expenses and how they were calculated — compare them with this result.
Charging more than the legal cap is prohibited (Art. 33(1)4), punishable by up to 1 year in prison or a 10M KRW fine.

receipt.title: Cash receipts and tax invoices
items: Brokerage is a mandatory cash-receipt business: cash payments of 100,000 KRW or more must be receipted even without a request.
Businesses can receive a tax invoice (general taxpayer) and deduct input VAT.
VAT is 10% for general and about 4% for simplified taxpayers. Check the business registration.

cancel.title: If the contract is cancelled
items: No fee is owed if the contract is void, cancelled or rescinded due to the broker's intent or negligence (Art. 32(1) proviso).
If a party walks away after paying the down payment, the fee may still be claimed, though courts sometimes reduce it.
If it falls through at the provisional deposit stage, a claim is difficult without a fee agreement. Consult the local district office in a dispute.

region.title: Regional differences and expenses
items: Housing fees are set by provincial ordinances within the ministry ordinance; since October 2021 all provinces use the same rates.
Officetel, commercial and land rates are set nationwide by the Enforcement Rule (Art. 20(4)).
Brokers may also charge documented actual expenses for title checks and deposit protection (Art. 32(2)).

items.q: What is the brokerage fee for a home sale?
items.a: Under the 2021 rates: under 50M 0.6% (cap 250K), 50M–200M 0.5% (cap 800K), 200M–900M 0.4%, 900M–1.2B 0.5%, 1.2B–1.5B 0.6%, 1.5B and over 0.7%. Seller and buyer each pay.

items.q: How are jeonse and monthly rent fees calculated?
items.a: Leases: under 50M 0.5% (cap 200K), 50M–100M 0.4% (cap 300K), 100M–600M 0.3%, 600M–1.2B 0.4%, 1.2B–1.5B 0.5%, 1.5B and over 0.6%. Monthly rent uses deposit + rent × 100, or × 70 if under 50M.

items.q: Is VAT added to the brokerage fee?
items.a: Yes. Legal rates and caps exclude VAT. General-taxpayer brokers add 10%, simplified taxpayers about 4%.

items.q: Can I negotiate the fee?
items.a: Yes. The legal rate is a ceiling. Agree on the rate before signing; on a 600M sale, 0.1%p lower saves 600K KRW per party (before VAT).

items.q: What is the officetel fee?
items.a: Residential officetels (85㎡ or less with kitchen, toilet and bath): 0.5% for sales, 0.4% for leases. Others are negotiated within 0.9%.

items.q: What is the fee for commercial property or land?
items.a: Non-residential property is negotiated within 0.9% of the transaction amount.

items.q: When do I pay the fee?
items.a: As agreed, or on the day the balance is paid if there is no agreement — usually the balance payment day.

items.q: Do I pay if the contract falls through?
items.a: Not if it is due to the broker's intent or negligence. If a party cancels, the fee may be claimed, though courts may reduce it.

items.q: Can I get a cash receipt?
items.a: Yes. Brokerage is a mandatory cash-receipt business for payments of 100,000 KRW or more, including bank transfers.
