lump.title: How to pay in a lump sum
items: Apply and pay between the 16th and month-end in January, March, June or September. Applying without paying gets no discount.
Use Wetax (wetax.go.kr) or the Smart Wetax app; Seoul residents can use ETAX. District tax offices also accept it.
Auto-debit for regular installments does not cover lump-sum payment.
After one January lump-sum payment, a January bill may be sent in following years. The 2026 rate is 5%, same as 2024-2025.

age.title: Vehicle age reduction
items: Age counts from the first registration date, not the model year.
Registered Jan-Jun: tax year − registration year + 1.
Registered Jul-Dec: June installment uses the year difference, December adds 1.
5% from year 3, +5% each year, up to 50% from year 12. Applies only to cc-based passenger cars.

refund.title: Selling, scrapping, moving
items: After a lump-sum payment, selling or deregistering refunds the unowned days pro rata.
When you buy a used car, you owe the share from the transfer date to year-end.
Moving to another district after paying does not trigger a new charge that year.
Regular bills go to the owner as of June 1 and December 1, split by ownership period.

tips.title: Good to know
items: Car tax is an annual property-type tax. The one-time acquisition tax on purchase is calculated in the car acquisition tax calculator.
Compact cars get no car tax exemption; they simply pay 80 KRW/cc. Their perks are acquisition tax relief and fuel tax refunds.
Hybrids are taxed by engine displacement, not at the EV flat rate.
Late payment adds a 3% penalty plus monthly late-payment interest; unpaid tax can lead to plate seizure.

items.q: What is the 2026 lump-sum discount?
items.a: The rate is 5%, applied only to the period after the payment month, so January saves about 4.58% of the annual tax, March ~3.77%, June ~2.52% and September ~1.26%. Education tax falls too.

items.q: How do I apply for lump-sum payment?
items.a: Between the 16th and month-end in January, March, June or September, look up your car on Wetax/Smart Wetax (ETAX in Seoul) and pay. Auto-debit does not apply.

items.q: Do I get a refund if I sell or scrap the car?
items.a: Yes. Tax for the period after the transfer or deregistration date is refunded pro rata (Enforcement Decree Art. 126). Moving districts does not trigger a new charge.

items.q: Are compact cars exempt?
items.a: No car tax exemption. Up to 1,000cc is 80 KRW/cc, so a 998cc car pays about 100,000 KRW a year including education tax.

items.q: How much is car tax on an EV?
items.a: Non-commercial EVs and hydrogen cars pay 100,000 KRW plus 30,000 KRW education tax = 130,000 KRW. Commercial: 20,000 KRW. No age reduction.

items.q: How is vehicle age calculated?
items.a: From the first registration date. Jan-Jun registrations: tax year − registration year + 1. Jul-Dec: June uses the difference, December adds 1. 5% off from year 3, up to 50% from year 12.

items.q: Are company cars taxed as commercial?
items.a: No. Commercial means licensed transport businesses such as taxis, rental cars and freight carriers. Company passenger cars usually pay non-commercial rates.

items.q: How is this different from acquisition tax?
items.a: Acquisition tax is paid once when you buy a car; car tax is paid every June and December while you own it.

guide.title: Pay slips: what you need to know
guide.intro: If you employ even one person in Korea, you must issue a wage statement every payday. This tool fills in every legally required item and calculates overtime, night and holiday pay, social insurance and income tax for 2026. Your input stays in this browser.

sections.title: Obligation and fines
items: Required every payday since Nov 19, 2021 (Labor Standards Act Art. 48(2))
Applies to businesses of any size, including part-time and daily workers
Not issued: KRW 300,000 / 500,000 / 1,000,000 per worker for the 1st / 2nd / 3rd+ violation (max 5 million)
Missing or false items: KRW 200,000 / 300,000 / 500,000

sections.title: Mandatory items (Decree Art. 27-2)
items: Name, date of birth or employee number
Pay date and total wages
Amount of each item: base pay, allowances, bonus
Calculation method for hour-based items, including overtime, night and holiday hours
Each deduction and the total

sections.title: Tax-free items (2026)
items: Meal allowance up to KRW 200,000/month (when no free meals are provided)
Car allowance up to KRW 200,000/month (own car used for work)
Childbirth/childcare allowance up to KRW 200,000/month (children aged 6 or under)
Amounts above the limit are taxable for tax and insurance

sections.title: Premium pay
items: Ordinary hourly wage = monthly ordinary wage ÷ 209 hours (40h week)
Overtime: hourly × hours × 1.5
Night (10pm-6am): hourly × hours × 0.5 premium
Holiday: 1.5x up to 8 hours, 2x beyond
Businesses with 4 or fewer workers pay 1x (Decree Annex 1)

sections.title: Insurance and tax (employee share, 2026)
items: National pension 4.75% (base KRW 410,000-6,590,000)
Health insurance 3.595%, long-term care = health premium × 13.14%
Employment insurance 0.9%
Income tax: simplified withholding table (revised Feb 27, 2026); local tax 10% of income tax
3.3% contractors: 3% income tax + 0.3% local tax

sections.title: How to deliver
items: Print it, or send the PDF by email, KakaoTalk or text (electronic documents are valid)
Keep proof of delivery (sent log or signature)
Keep wage records for 3 years (Labor Standards Act Art. 42)
2026 minimum wage: KRW 10,320/hour, 2,156,880/month (209 hours)

items.q: What happens if an employer doesn't issue a pay slip?
items.a: Since November 19, 2021, Korean employers must issue a wage statement (paper or electronic) every time wages are paid (Labor Standards Act Art. 48(2)). Failure is subject to a fine of up to KRW 5 million; under Enforcement Decree Annex 7 it is KRW 300,000 / 500,000 / 1,000,000 per worker for the 1st / 2nd / 3rd+ violation. Missing or false items start at KRW 200,000.

items.q: Do businesses with fewer than 5 workers or part-timers need one?
items.a: Yes. The obligation applies to every employer with at least one worker, including part-time and daily workers. Businesses with 4 or fewer regular workers are exempt only from the 50% overtime/night/holiday premium, so extra hours are paid at 1x.

items.q: Can I send it via KakaoTalk or email?
items.a: Yes. Electronic documents are allowed, so email, text, KakaoTalk or an intranet are fine. Save a PDF here and send it, and keep the sent record as proof.

items.q: What items are mandatory?
items.a: Under Enforcement Decree Art. 27-2: name and date of birth or employee number, pay date, total wages, amount of each item (base pay, allowances, bonus), the calculation method for items that depend on days or hours worked (including overtime, night and holiday hours), and each deduction and the total.

items.q: Is the KRW 200,000 meal allowance also excluded from social insurance?
items.a: A qualifying meal allowance up to KRW 200,000 a month is excluded from income tax and from the pension, health and employment insurance base. The excess is taxable. Car allowances and childcare allowances (children aged 6 or under) are also tax-free up to KRW 200,000 each.

items.q: How is income tax calculated?
items.a: It is looked up in the NTS simplified withholding table (Income Tax Enforcement Decree Annex 2, revised Feb 2026) using monthly taxable pay and the number of dependents, minus KRW 20,830 for one child aged 8-20 or KRW 45,830 for two. Workers may choose 80% or 120%. Local income tax is 10% of income tax. You can override any amount, e.g. in bonus months.

receiptGenerator.title: Receipt Generator
receiptGenerator.description: Rent, club dues, second-hand sales or money received between individuals: fill in the blanks and get a simple Korean receipt with the amount in Korean words, two copies with a cut line, a seal and PDF export.

sectionHint.purpose: Pick a purpose to prefill the description, wording and items. Edit freely afterwards.
sectionHint.buyer: The person who takes the receipt. Printed as 'To: ○○○'.
sectionHint.issuer: The person who received the money and signs the receipt (supplier). Add a business registration number if you are a business.

receiptGenerator.subject: Description
receiptGenerator.subjectPlaceholder: e.g. October rent, club dues, repair fee
receiptGenerator.amountOverrideHint: Leave empty to use the item total of {sum} KRW. Enter only if the money actually received differs.
receiptGenerator.issuerBizHint: Leave empty if you are an individual.
receiptGenerator.bizValid: Format and check digit are valid.
receiptGenerator.bizInvalid: Invalid number. Check the 10 digits and the final check digit.
receiptGenerator.notePlaceholder: e.g. bank account, item condition, balance due
receiptGenerator.copiesHint: Prints the same receipt twice on one A4 sheet with a cut line. Cut and keep one each.

insight.mismatch: The item total is {sum} KRW but the amount received is {total} KRW. Make them match.
insight.bizInvalid: The business registration number is invalid. Leave it empty if you are an individual.
insight.vatNoBiz: Only registered businesses may charge VAT. For transactions between individuals, set VAT to 'None'.
insight.cashReceipt: If your business is in a mandatory cash-receipt industry, you must issue a cash receipt for cash or bank-transfer payments of {min} KRW or more even if the customer does not ask. This receipt does not replace it, and the penalty is 20% of the unissued amount.
insight.tooMany: With 2 copies, more than {n} items may not fit on half a page. Group items or turn off 2-copy printing.
insight.card: For card payments, the card sales slip is the official proof. Use this receipt for confirmation only.
insight.proof: If the payer is a business claiming this as an expense, transactions over {limit} KRW need a tax invoice, card slip or cash receipt. With only a simple receipt, a 2% penalty applies.
insight.notSubstitute: A simple receipt confirms that money changed hands. It does not replace a tax invoice or cash receipt.

guide.title: Receipt essentials
guide.intro: A receipt is a document in which the recipient confirms 'I received this amount for this purpose'. There is no fixed format: the amount, purpose, date and the recipient's signature or seal are enough. For business tax purposes, however, statutory proof such as tax invoices or cash receipts is required separately.

sections.title: Receipts between individuals
items: The payer may demand a receipt from the person who received the payment (Civil Act Article 474).
For rent, club dues or second-hand sales between non-businesses, a receipt prevents disputes about whether payment was made.
Write the amount in both Korean words and digits to make alteration difficult.
Make two copies and keep one each.

sections.title: Simple receipts and expenses (30,000 KRW rule)
items: For business expenses of 30,000 KRW or less per transaction (VAT included), a simple receipt is acceptable proof (Corporate Tax Act Enforcement Decree Art. 158).
Above 30,000 KRW, you must obtain a tax invoice, invoice, card sales slip or cash receipt.
With only a simple receipt, the expense may still be deductible but a 2% penalty on the amount applies (Corporate Tax Act Art. 75-5, Income Tax Act Art. 81-6).
Business entertainment expenses over 30,000 KRW per transaction without a card slip or tax invoice are not deductible at all (200,000 KRW for congratulatory/condolence gifts).

sections.title: Tax invoice vs cash receipt vs simple receipt
items: Tax invoice: issued between businesses. Counts for input VAT credit and expense proof.
Card sales slip: the card payment itself is official proof. No separate receipt needed.
Cash receipt: reported to the National Tax Service for cash or transfer payments. Individuals get an income deduction; businesses use it as expense proof.
Simple receipt (this form): confirms payment. Valid as expense proof up to 30,000 KRW and as evidence between individuals; no VAT credit.

sections.title: Mandatory cash-receipt industries
items: Clinics, academies, professionals such as lawyers and tax accountants, restaurants and lodging, real-estate brokers, interior work and other designated industries must issue a cash receipt for cash transactions of 100,000 KRW or more even without a request (Income Tax Act Art. 162-3).
Bank transfers count as cash transactions for tax purposes.
If you do not know the customer's details, self-issue within 5 days using the NTS designated number 010-000-1234.
Failure to issue incurs a penalty of 20% of the unissued amount. A simple receipt cannot replace it.

sections.title: Proof tips for personal money transfers
items: Use bank transfers when possible and put the purpose (e.g. October rent) in the memo.
If you paid in cash, get a receipt on the spot.
A receipt only proves payment was received. For a loan, write a separate IOU with repayment terms.
For second-hand sales, note the item's condition and any disclosed defects in the note field.

sections.title: How to fill it in
items: Numbering receipts makes it easy to match them with your ledger or bank statement.
Be specific in the description, e.g. 'October rent and maintenance'.
The recipient must sign or seal it. Seal any corrections too.
Only registered businesses may charge VAT. Set VAT to 'None' for transactions between individuals.

items.q: Is there a required receipt format?
items.a: No. A receipt needs the amount, purpose, date, the payer, and the recipient's signature or seal. Write the amount in Korean words and digits, and make two copies so each side keeps one.

items.q: Up to what amount is a simple receipt accepted as an expense?
items.a: Business expenses of 30,000 KRW or less per transaction (VAT included) can be proven with a simple receipt. Above that, you need a tax invoice, card slip or cash receipt; otherwise a 2% penalty applies.

items.q: Do individuals need receipts when trading with each other?
items.a: It is not mandatory but it is safer. Under Civil Act Article 474, the payer may demand a receipt, and for cash payments a receipt is often the only evidence.

items.q: Can I give this receipt instead of a cash receipt?
items.a: No. Businesses in mandatory cash-receipt industries must issue a cash receipt for cash or transfer payments of 100,000 KRW or more. A simple receipt cannot replace it, and the penalty is 20% of the unissued amount.

items.q: Can an individual add VAT to a receipt?
items.a: VAT is collected and filed by registered taxable businesses. In transactions between non-business individuals, do not add VAT; just write the amount.

items.q: How is a receipt different from an IOU?
items.a: A receipt only confirms that money was received. If the money was lent, write a separate IOU with the repayment date and interest so you have grounds to get it back.

leaseContract.title: Housing Lease Agreement Generator
leaseContract.description: Create a Korean jeonse or monthly-rent lease based on the official Standard Housing Lease Agreement (rev. 2023-10-06). Add anti-fraud special terms and save as an A4 PDF.

sectionHint.money: The down payment is usually 10% of the deposit. The balance is calculated as deposit minus down payment and interim payment.
sectionHint.property: Copy exactly what the property register and building ledger say.
sectionHint.notice: Under Article 3-7 of the Housing Lease Protection Act, the landlord must show prior fixed-date records and a tax payment certificate when signing.
sectionHint.lessor: Check the landlord's ID against the owner on the property register. All co-owners must sign.
sectionHint.specials: Checking an item adds its clause to the special terms. You can edit the text freely below.

contractTypeHint.agreed: A new contract by agreement has no 5% cap, and the tenant's one-time renewal right remains.
contractTypeHint.renew: A renewal under Article 6-3 runs 2 years, and deposit/rent increases are capped at 5%.

leaseContract.middleHint: Without an interim payment, either party can cancel until the balance is paid by forfeiting or returning double the down payment.
leaseContract.mgmtItemsToggle: Itemize (required on the standard form for fixed fees of {min} KRW or more)
leaseContract.mgmtNotePlaceholder: e.g. as billed by the management office (common + household usage)
leaseContract.startHint: Usually the same day as the balance payment.
leaseContract.areaHint: For apartments, land area is usually the land-right share and building area the exclusive area. For part of a multi-household house, describe the unit precisely.
leaseContract.repairHint: Agreeing on what to fix and by when prevents disputes.
leaseContract.repairWhatPlaceholder: e.g. bathroom leak, living room wallpaper
leaseContract.repairDeduct: If not repaired by the deadline, deduct the cost from the deposit or rent
leaseContract.specialHint: Numbered after the standard printed terms (move-in registration, cancellation for undisclosed info, etc.).

rights.label: No changes to title until the day after the balance date
rights.hint: Tenant protection starts at 00:00 the day after move-in registration. This blocks a mortgage in that gap.

ownerAccount.label: Pay only to the registered owner's account
ownerAccount.hint: Requests to pay an agent's or relative's account are a classic fraud sign.

tax.label: Landlord declares no unpaid taxes
tax.hint: Unpaid taxes can be paid out before your deposit in an auction.

prior.label: Cancel if prior-tenant disclosures are false
prior.hint: In multi-household houses, large earlier deposits put yours at risk.

loan.label: Void and refund if the jeonse loan is refused
loan.hint: Covers refusals caused by the property or landlord (illegal building, mortgage, etc.).

insurance.label: Landlord cooperates with deposit insurance (cancel if refused)
insurance.hint: HUG/HF/SGI deposit return guarantee. Check eligibility before signing.

returnDeposit.label: Return the deposit on the end date regardless of a new tenant
returnDeposit.hint: Prevents 'I'll pay when the next tenant moves in'.

settle.label: Settle maintenance fees, utilities and long-term repair reserve
settle.hint: Avoid inheriting unpaid fees from before move-in.

restore.label: Restoration scope (based on move-in photos)
restore.hint: Normal wear and nail holes excluded. Take photos together on move-in day.

pet.label: Pets allowed
pet.hint: States permission and responsibility for damage.

earlyExit.label: Tenant pays brokerage fee on early exit
earlyExit.hint: Sets when the deposit is returned and who pays the broker if the tenant leaves early.

leaseContract.mediation: Agree to mediation by the Housing Lease Dispute Mediation Committee before suing
leaseContract.mediationHint: Mediation is faster and almost free compared with litigation.
leaseContract.addressConsent: Owner consents to the tenant applying for a detailed address
leaseContract.addressConsentHint: Without a unit number, the registered address may be inaccurate and weaken tenant protection.
leaseContract.brokeredHint: Adds the brokerage fee and disclosure clauses and a broker signature block. Leave unchecked for a direct deal.

insight.noAmount: Enter a deposit or monthly rent.
insight.endBeforeStart: The end date is before the handover date.
insight.payGap: Down + interim + balance ({sum} KRW) is {diff} KRW {dir} the deposit ({deposit} KRW). Please match them.
insight.middleAfterBalance: The interim payment date is after the balance date.
insight.balanceBeforeContract: The balance date is before the contract date.
insight.shortTerm: Even with a term under 2 years, the tenant may claim 2 years (Housing Lease Protection Act Art. 4(1)). The landlord cannot.
insight.renewCap: For a renewal under the renewal right, increases are capped at 5% (Art. 7(2)): deposit up to {maxDeposit} KRW, rent up to {maxRent} KRW. When converting between deposit and rent, compare using the conversion rate.
insight.agreedCap: This is more than {pct}% above the previous terms. No cap applies to a re-signed contract, but if the tenant uses the renewal right the maximum is {maxDeposit} KRW deposit / {maxRent} KRW rent.
insight.taxArrears: Unpaid taxes can be paid out before your deposit at auction. Add a term requiring full payment before the balance.
insight.priorLease: With prior tenants, check that their deposits plus mortgages are safe relative to the property value.
insight.noSpecials: No special terms yet. Anti-fraud terms such as no title changes and tax disclosure are recommended.
insight.moveIn: On {date}, when you pay the balance, register your move-in and get a fixed date the same day. Protection starts at 00:00 the next day.
insight.report: This lease must be reported (deposit over {deposit} KRW or rent over {rent} KRW). Report by {deadline} at a community center or RTMS; a fixed date is granted automatically.
insight.reportMaybe: Deposit over {deposit} KRW or rent over {rent} KRW: if the property is in the capital area, a metropolitan city, Sejong, Jeju or a city in a province, report by {deadline}.
insight.mgmtGap: Itemized fees ({sum} KRW) differ from the total ({total} KRW).
insight.mgmtDetail: Fixed fees of 100,000 KRW or more must be itemized on the standard form (rev. 2023-10). Open 'Itemize' and fill in the items.

guide.title: Lease essentials
guide.intro: Follows the clause structure of the Ministry of Justice / MOLIT Standard Housing Lease Agreement (rev. 2023-10-06). For direct deals without a broker, checks before signing and special terms matter more than the form. Housing only; commercial leases fall under a separate act.

sections.title: Documents to check first
items: Property register (iros.go.kr): owner, seizures and trusts in section A; mortgage amounts in section B.
Building ledger (gov.kr / eais.go.kr): illegal buildings or neighborhood-facility use can block loans and insurance.
Resident registration check: see whether earlier tenants or the owner's family are registered.
Tax certificate: for deposits over 10 million KRW you can view unpaid national taxes without the landlord's consent after signing.
If mortgage maximum + earlier deposits + your deposit exceed 70-80% of market value, be careful.

sections.title: Signing day
items: Re-issue the property register and compare the owner with their ID.
For an agent, get a power of attorney with the owner's seal certificate and call the owner.
Pay the down payment only to the owner's account.
Sign two copies, seal across pages, and keep one each.

sections.title: Balance and move-in day
items: Check the register again right before paying the balance.
Receive the keys with the balance and register your move-in and fixed date that day.
Protection starts at 00:00 the next day, which is why the 'no title changes' term matters.
Settle fees and photograph any defects.

sections.title: Move-in registration, fixed date, lease report
items: Register within 14 days of moving. Handover + registration = opposability.
Get a fixed date at a community center, iros.go.kr or gov.kr. Opposability + fixed date = priority repayment.
Deposits over 60 million KRW or rent over 300,000 KRW must be reported within 30 days (capital area, metro cities, Sejong, Jeju, cities in provinces).
Late reports incur fines. Renewals with unchanged amounts need no report.

sections.title: Deposit insurance
items: HUG, HF and SGI offer deposit return guarantees.
Eligibility depends on the deposit-to-value ratio and building status, so check before signing.
Add a term allowing cancellation if insurance is refused.

sections.title: During and at the end of the lease
items: The tenant may request renewal 6 to 2 months before the end (once, for 2 years).
Renewal increases are capped at 5%, and no further increase within a year.
Without notice the lease renews automatically; the tenant may then terminate with 3 months' notice.
If the deposit isn't returned, apply for a lease registration order before moving out.

items.q: Is a lease signed without a broker valid?
items.a: Yes. A lease is formed by agreement, and a contract you draft and sign yourself is equally valid. Without a broker's checks and insurance, verify the register, building ledger and tax certificate yourself and pay only to the owner's account.

items.q: If I sign for 1 year, must I leave after a year?
items.a: No. Under Article 4 of the Housing Lease Protection Act a term under 2 years is deemed 2 years. The tenant may leave after a year or stay 2 years; the landlord cannot insist on less than 2.

items.q: When should I register my move-in and get a fixed date?
items.a: On the day you pay the balance and move in. Protection starts at 00:00 the next day, so a mortgage registered the same day ranks ahead. Hence the 'no title changes until the day after the balance date' term.

items.q: Who reports the lease and by when?
items.a: Leases with a deposit over 60 million KRW or rent over 300,000 KRW must be reported within 30 days of signing at a community center or RTMS (one party submitting the contract counts as a joint report). Applies in the capital area, metro cities, Sejong, Jeju and cities in provinces, and a fixed date is granted automatically.

items.q: How much can the deposit rise on renewal?
items.a: If the tenant uses the renewal right, deposit and rent may rise by at most 5%. A new contract by agreement has no cap, but the renewal right then remains unused.

items.q: Can I cancel after paying only the down payment?
items.a: Until the interim payment (or balance) is paid, the tenant can cancel by forfeiting the down payment and the landlord by returning double (standard form Art. 5, Civil Act Art. 565). If a cancellation event in the special terms occurs, the down payment is refunded.

items.q: Can I make a commercial lease?
items.a: This tool covers housing jeonse and monthly rent only. Shops and offices fall under the Commercial Building Lease Protection Act; use the Ministry of Justice commercial standard lease.

greetingGenerator.title: Greeting Message Generator
greetingGenerator.description: Pick the occasion, the recipient and the tone to get several ready-to-send greetings.
greetingGenerator.koreanNote: Messages are written in Korean, composed from hand-written sentences. Names you enter stay on this screen and are not added to the link.
greetingGenerator.toneHint: Changing the recipient picks a matching tone first. You can still change it.
greetingGenerator.nameHint: Names are added at the start and the end of each message. In casual messages to a friend, the name gets the vocative ending (민수야).
greetingGenerator.imageAria: Save message {n} as a card image
greetingGenerator.smsHint: With Korean bulk-texting services, up to 90 bytes (about 45 Korean characters) goes as SMS; longer messages or messages with emoji go as LMS. Pick Short when sending to many people.

guide.title: How to write a good greeting

whatIs.title: What is this?
whatIs.description: A tool that writes Korean greetings for year-end, New Year, Seollal, Chuseok, thanks, birthdays, promotions and farewells, matched to the recipient and the tone. Hand-written sentences are combined per relationship and tone, so honorific and casual speech never mix. New Year messages automatically include the coming year and its sexagenary name (e.g. 2027, 정미년).

howToUse.title: How to use
items: Choose the occasion and the recipient. A matching tone is selected first.
Change the tone and length. Short messages fit in a single SMS for group texts.
Enter the recipient and sender names to add '김 부장님,' or '홍길동 드림' automatically.
Copy a message or save it as a card image. 'Show other messages' gives new combinations.
Star the messages you like to keep them in favorites on this device.

tips.title: Avoid the mass-text feel
items: Put the recipient's name first. A name alone makes it feel personal.
Add one sentence about something you did together. A specific memory carries the sincerity.
When sending to many people, use 'Show other messages' to vary the text per person.
Use emoji only with friends and colleagues; leave them out for clients and seniors.

realWorld.title: When to send
items: Year-end: mid to late December. For clients, around the third week of December, a few days before the last workday.
New Year: within the first week of January. Messages sent at midnight get buried.
Seollal and Chuseok: 2 to 3 days before the holidays start.
Birthdays and promotions: on the day you hear the news.
Leaving a job: on your last afternoon or the day before. Tell clients who takes over.

comparison.title: Etiquette with clients
items: Formal speech is the default. Polite (haeyo) is fine if that is how you usually talk.
Sign with your company and name so they know who sent it.
Keep business out of it: thanks and good wishes only.
For new or formal relationships, a text or email is safer than KakaoTalk.

items.q: When should I send year-end greetings?
items.a: Mid to late December. Messages pile up around Christmas and the last week, so for clients the third week of December works best. New Year greetings can go out within the first week of January.

items.q: When should I send Seollal or Chuseok greetings?
items.a: Two to three days before the holidays begin. During the holidays people are with family, and the first morning is flooded with messages. For clients, send before noon on the last workday.

items.q: How do I keep it from looking like a mass text?
items.a: Start with the recipient's name and add one sentence about something you shared. Names you enter here are added automatically, and 'Show other messages' gives each person a different text.

items.q: Is KakaoTalk okay for clients?
items.a: Yes, if you already talk about work there. For new or formal relationships, a text message or email is safer, without emoji.

items.q: What is the difference between SMS and LMS?
items.a: With Korean bulk-texting services, SMS carries up to 90 bytes (about 45 Korean characters); longer messages become LMS. Emoji often prevent sending as SMS too. LMS may cost more, so choose Short when texting many people.
